title: 一切皆有源
blurb: F2 豪华版小说：完整电影故事，深入阿塔霍兰与四灵的设定。

paras.en: INTRODUCTION Dry Banana Hippy Hat!
paras.zh: 引言　干香蕉嬉皮帽！

paras.en: (Or… Happy Birthday, Frozen!) It’s still hard to believe it’s been ten years since Queen Elsa fled Arendelle, throwing her crown into the snow and accidentally creating an eternal winter (and bonus ice palace!).
paras.zh: （又或者……《冰雪奇缘》生日快乐！）很难相信，距离艾莎女王逃离阿伦黛尔、把王冠抛进雪中、意外创造出永恒寒冬（还附赠一座冰宫殿！）已经过去十年了。

paras.en: I’ll never forget watching that scene in theaters for the first time, mesmerized by the music and lyrics as well as the empowering message on the importance of accepting ourselves for who we are, despite whether others will understand.
paras.zh: 我永远不会忘记第一次在影院看到那一幕时的情景，音乐的旋律与歌词让我如痴如醉，而那句振奋人心的话语更让我铭记：无论别人能否理解，都要接纳真实的自己。

paras.en: The film was packed with action, adventure, and snowmen, both scary… and silly.
paras.zh: 这部电影充满了动作、冒险，还有雪人——既有吓人的……也有傻乎乎的。

paras.en: And, to top it all off, an unexpected fairy-tale ending where the love of two sisters could thaw a frozen heart.
paras.zh: 而最妙的是，它还有一个出人意料的童话式结局：姐妹二人之间的爱，足以融化一颗冰冻的心。

paras.en: Frozen fever was real, and we all caught it that winter of 2013.
paras.zh: “冰雪热”是真的，在2013年的那个冬天，我们全都中了招。

paras.en: Soon store shelves were as barren of Frozen merchandise as Oaken’s Trading Post and Sauna was of winter apparel.
paras.zh: 很快，商店货架上《冰雪奇缘》的周边就被抢购一空，那情形就像奥肯的杂货桑拿店缺了冬装一样空荡荡。

paras.en: Families would stand in line over six hours at the theme parks for a chance to meet the two sisters in person.
paras.zh: 在主题乐园里，一家人会排上六个多小时的队，只为能亲眼见上两姐妹一面。

paras.en: And the music began to feel like a soundtrack to our lives, playing wherever we went—often sung by enthusiastic children dressed as their favorite magical Snow Queen or her feisty younger sister.
paras.zh: 那些音乐渐渐成了我们生活的原声带，走到哪儿都能听到——常常是那些热情的孩子唱出来的，他们打扮成自己最爱的魔法雪宝女王，或是她那活泼的小妹妹。

paras.en: No one, it seemed, was able to “let it go.” And this was just the beginning.
paras.zh: 似乎没有人能真的“随它吧”。而这，仅仅只是个开始。

paras.en: Over the years the film spawned several animated shorts and a feature animation sequel that broke box office records.
paras.zh: 这些年来，这部电影衍生出好几部动画短片，还有一部打破票房纪录的长篇续集动画。

paras.en: Olaf kept us laughing on Instagram through the depths of the pandemic; and books, comics, and even video games and virtual reality deepened the lore, introducing new characters and entertaining us with side stories set in our favorite Frozen ’verse.
paras.zh: 在疫情最艰难的日子里，雪宝在Instagram上逗得我们哈哈大笑；而书籍、漫画，甚至电子游戏和虚拟现实，都让这个世界观更加深厚，带来了新角色，也用我们最爱的“冰雪宇宙”里的支线故事陪伴着我们。

paras.en: And now we have a third feature film to look forward to!
paras.zh: 而现在，我们又有了一部值得期待的第三部长片！

paras.en: In the meantime, to celebrate the original film’s tenth birthday, we’ve put together a brand-new anthology for you to enjoy.
paras.zh: 在此期间，为了庆祝原版电影十周年，我们为你准备了一本全新的故事集。

paras.en: Ten original stories, one for each year, written by ten talented authors (who are also Frozen fans).
paras.zh: 十个原创故事，一年一个，由十位才华横溢的作者（他们也都是《冰雪奇缘》的粉丝）共同写就。

paras.en: You’ll enjoy sweet, nostalgic, never-before-told stories of Anna’s and Elsa’s childhoods and brand-new adventures taking place after the events of Frozen 2 .
paras.zh: 你会读到甜蜜而怀旧的、从未讲述过的安娜与艾莎的童年故事，以及发生在《冰雪奇缘2》之后的全新冒险。

paras.en: You’ll spend time with beloved side characters (Mattias!
paras.zh: 你会和深受喜爱的配角共度时光（马提亚斯！

paras.en: Oaken!) and learn a new Northuldra legend.
paras.zh: 奥肯！），还会了解到一则全新的北地人传说。

paras.en: You’ll encounter deadly beasts of Nordic folklore and get to relive Elsa’s coronation day—with a rather unexpected time-slippery twist.
paras.zh: 你会遇见北欧民间传说中致命的怪兽，还能重温艾莎加冕那一天的情景——不过会有一个相当出人意料的“时间错位”式反转。

paras.en: Some stories may make you laugh.
paras.zh: 有些故事会让你发笑。

paras.en: Others may make you cry.
paras.zh: 有些会让你落泪。

paras.en: But we hope all of them will remind you of why Frozen has remained so close to our hearts for these last ten years.
paras.zh: 但我们希望，所有故事都能让你想起，为什么这十年来《冰雪奇缘》始终贴近我们的心。

paras.en: And why it will continue to do so as we journey “into the unknown” for the next decade to come.
paras.zh: 以及为什么，在即将到来的下一个十年里，当我们一同迈向“未知的远方”时，它仍会如此。

paras.en: With the warmest of hugs, Mari Mancusi Author of Dangerous Secrets: The Story of Iduna and Agnarr and Polar Nights: Cast Into Darkness
paras.zh: 送上最温暖的拥抱，玛丽·曼库西（《危险秘密：伊杜娜与安格瑞的故事》及《极地之夜：坠入黑暗》作者）

chapters.title: Anna of Arendelle and the Silver Skates

paras.en: The first freeze in Arendelle was a beautiful and terrible thing.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔的初寒，是一件美丽又可怕的事。

paras.en: Princess Elsa could always sense it coming.
paras.zh: 艾莎公主总能感觉到它的到来。

paras.en: Her fingers would tingle, and a deep, starving something would cry out in her heart.
paras.zh: 她的手指会发麻，一种深沉而渴望的东西会在她心底呐喊。

paras.en: She couldn’t seem to silence it.
paras.zh: 她似乎无法让它安静下来。

paras.en: Something inside her yearned to go out into the frigid air, to cast her magic down into the snow and up into the crisp wintry sky.
paras.zh: 她体内的某种东西渴望冲进凛冽的寒风里，把魔法洒向雪地，送入清冷冬日的天空。

paras.en: Those nights, she’d bury her fingers into her covers, trying to hide the cold that would inevitably burst forth, turning her pillows and bedsheets as frosty by morning as the ground outside.
paras.zh: 那些夜晚，她会把手指埋进被子里，试图藏起那股必然会迸发出来的寒意——到了清晨，她的枕头和床单就会像外面的地面一样结满霜。

paras.en: It was proof that she hadn’t yet learned to control her magic, as Grand Pabbie had long ago advised.
paras.zh: 这证明她还没学会控制自己的魔法，就像皮比很久以前告诫过的那样。

paras.en: It was proof that she was still unprepared to enter Arendelle society.
paras.zh: 这也证明，她还没准备好踏入阿伦黛尔的上流社会。

paras.en: And the reason that the castle gates remained shut and she remained locked inside.
paras.zh: 而这，正是城堡大门紧闭、她被关在里面的原因。

paras.en: And then, by midmorning at the latest, would come the worst part of all—the inevitable soft knock on her chamber door. “Elsa?” Anna’s voice, plaintive and filled with an unquenchable hope.
paras.zh: 然后，最迟到了上午，最糟糕的时刻总会降临——那不可避免、轻轻叩响她房门的声音。“艾莎？”是安娜的声音，带着哀怨，也满是无法被浇灭的希望。

paras.en: It had been years, and yet her little sister never gave up. “Do you want to build a snowman?” Elsa sat on the richly brocaded chair in her richly furnished chamber, her gloved hands clasped tightly in her lap.
paras.zh: 好几年过去了，可她的小妹妹从不放弃。“你想堆个雪人吗？”艾莎坐在自己那间陈设华丽的房间里、一张织锦精美的椅子上，戴着连指手套的双手紧紧交握在膝上。

paras.en: Outside, the ice called to her.
paras.zh: 窗外，寒冰在呼唤着她。

paras.en: At the door, her little sister did the same. “It doesn’t have to be a snowman,” Anna went on, wheedling. “We could go sledding.
paras.zh: 在门外，她的小妹妹做着同样的事。“不一定要堆雪人呀，”安娜继续软磨硬泡，“我们可以去滑雪橇。

paras.en: Or… skating?” Elsa winced.
paras.zh: 或者……去滑冰？”艾莎皱了皱眉。

paras.en: In the Before Times, she and Anna had loved to build snowmen, and sled, and even skate.
paras.zh: 在“从前那段时光”里，她和安娜曾那么喜欢堆雪人、滑雪橇，甚至滑冰。

paras.en: They’d wake up in the middle of the night and sneak down into the Great Hall of the castle.
paras.zh: 她们会在半夜醒来，偷偷溜下楼，跑到城堡的大厅里去。

paras.en: Elsa would use her magic to freeze the floor and send big drifts of snow up against the columns and corners of the room, and they’d have their own winter wonderland.
paras.zh: 艾莎会用魔法把地板冻住，让一大堆雪涌到房间的柱子和角落边，于是她们就有了属于自己的冬日奇境。

paras.en: Anna didn’t remember any of that anymore.
paras.zh: 安娜再也记不起那些了。

paras.en: The troll had seen to that.
paras.zh: 那是地精的功劳。

paras.en: All she knew was that she and Elsa would play in the ice and snow together.
paras.zh: 她只知道，自己和艾莎曾一起在冰雪里玩耍。

paras.en: He should have erased her memories entirely, and maybe Elsa’s, too, for good measure.
paras.zh: 他本该把她的记忆彻底抹去，或许也该把艾莎的干脆一起抹掉，才算妥当。

paras.en: That way, they wouldn’t miss each other so much.
paras.zh: 那样的话，她们就不会如此思念彼此了。

paras.en: If only Elsa could learn to control her powers!
paras.zh: 要是艾莎能学会控制自己的力量就好了！

paras.en: Then she could play with her sister again.
paras.zh: 那样她就能再和妹妹一起玩了。

paras.en: They could even build snowmen or go ice-skating. “Elsa?” Anna tried again, always hopeful.
paras.zh: 她们甚至还能堆雪人、去滑冰。“艾莎？”安娜又试了一次，依然满怀希望。

paras.en: Elsa bit her lip.
paras.zh: 艾莎咬了咬嘴唇。

paras.en: Inside her gloves, the frost spread. “Okay,” her sister said at last, her voice filled with a sadness as deep as the fjord. “Bye.” Long after she was gone, Elsa remained glued to her seat, worried that she’d lose her nerve and open the door.
paras.zh: 手套里，寒霜蔓延开来。“好吧，”妹妹最后说道，声音里满是如同峡湾般深沉的悲伤。“再见。”安娜离开很久之后，艾莎仍黏在座位上，担心自己会泄了气，把门打开。

paras.en: It was a good thing that Arendelle Castle’s grounds were so expansive, or Princess Anna might have gotten bored years ago.
paras.zh: 幸好阿伦黛尔城堡的庭院如此广阔，否则安娜公主恐怕几年前就无聊坏了。

paras.en: As it was, she felt like she’d memorized every brick in the walls and each tree in the royal gardens.
paras.zh: 即便如此，她觉得自己都快把围墙上的每一块砖、皇家花园里的每一棵树都记熟了。

paras.en: In the spring, she’d given names to every fluffy yellow duckling that hatched in the royal duck pond, and in the autumn, she’d watched tearfully as each duck, now grown and wearing its green-and-black plumage, flew south for the winter, on adventures Anna herself could barely imagine.
paras.zh: 春天时，她给皇家鸭塘里孵出的每一只毛茸茸的小黄鸭都起了名字；秋天时，她含泪看着每一只鸭子——如今都已长大，披着绿黑相间的羽毛——向南飞去越冬，去经历安娜自己几乎无法想象的冒险。

paras.en: One day, perhaps she too would venture beyond these confining walls.
paras.zh: 也许有一天，她也会鼓起勇气，走出这些束缚她的围墙。

paras.en: Now that very same duck pond was frozen solid, though, and Anna had plans.
paras.zh: 不过，眼下这个鸭塘已经冻得结结实实，而安娜已经有了打算。

paras.en: Even if her sister once again had no interest in playing with her, it didn’t mean Anna herself had to be stuck inside all winter.
paras.zh: 即便妹妹再次对和她玩耍毫无兴趣，也不意味着安娜自己就得整个冬天都困在屋里。

paras.en: She pulled on her warmest fur-lined cape and her thickest stockings and boots.
paras.zh: 她穿上了最暖和的皮里斗篷，还有最厚的长袜和靴子。

paras.en: Once upon a time—Anna remembered it well—she and Elsa had run all over the castle grounds in the winter, building snowmen in the gardens, sledding off the hills near the courtyard, and, yes, skating on this duck pond.
paras.zh: 曾几何时——安娜记得清清楚楚——她和艾莎冬天曾在城堡庭院里到处奔跑，在花园里堆雪人，从庭院旁的小山上滑雪橇，没错，还在这片鸭塘上滑过冰。

paras.en: It had been years since Anna had skated, but it couldn’t be that hard to pick up again, right?
paras.zh: 安娜已经好几年没滑过冰了，但重新捡起来应该没那么难吧？

paras.en: Earlier she’d heard two kitchen maids whispering about a festival the village was holding this weekend in celebration of the first frost.
paras.zh: 早些时候，她听见两个厨房女仆在低声议论，说村里这个周末要办一场庆祝初霜的节日。

paras.en: There would be food and games and fun, and it sounded like a total fantasy.
paras.zh: 会有吃的、有游戏、有好玩的，听起来简直像一场美梦。

paras.en: Ice-sculpting contests and ice-skating races, a winter market and a hot chocolate stand… Outside the castle it seemed like everyone was always having fun.
paras.zh: 冰雕比赛、滑冰比赛、冬日集市，还有热巧克力摊位……城堡外面，似乎每个人永远都在乐个不停。

paras.en: She had no idea why her parents never let her go.
paras.zh: 她完全想不通，父母为什么从不让她去。

paras.en: She also had no idea where her old skates were hidden.
paras.zh: 她同样不知道，自己那双旧冰鞋被藏到了哪里。

paras.en: She doubted the ones she’d had when she was little would fit anymore, but Elsa’s probably would, and Elsa obviously wasn’t using them.
paras.zh: 她怀疑自己小时候那双现在肯定穿不下了，但艾莎的应该还能穿，而且艾莎显然根本没在用。

paras.en: Anna searched high and low to no avail.
paras.zh: 安娜上上下下找了个遍，却一无所获。

paras.en: It was very strange.
paras.zh: 这真是太奇怪了。

paras.en: She knew they’d often gone skating.
paras.zh: 她知道她们以前常去滑冰。

paras.en: But Anna had never been one to let a little adversity stop her.
paras.zh: 不过，安娜可不是那种会被一点小挫折拦住的人。

paras.en: She grabbed a bit of twine and some smooth lengths of cloth to tie over her boots and tromped out into the snow.
paras.zh: 她抓了一截细绳和一些平整的长布条，准备绑在靴子上，然后踩着雪大步走了出去。

paras.en: The air was cold and clear, and some castle servant had helpfully shoveled the walk down to the duck pond.
paras.zh: 空气清冷而澄澈，某个城堡仆人好心地把通往鸭塘的小路铲过了雪。

paras.en: The ice over the surface was frosty but clear, and it seemed thick enough to hold her weight, especially if she stayed near the edges of the pond.
paras.zh: 水面上结的冰覆着白霜却很透亮，看上去厚得足以承受她的体重，尤其是如果她待在池塘边缘的话。

paras.en: Fortunately, the servants had also swept the frozen pond clean of snow that might have blown or fallen on the ice, keeping the surface as flat as glass.
paras.zh: 幸好，仆人们还把冻住的池塘上可能吹落或飘落的雪扫得干干净净，让冰面平得像玻璃一样。

paras.en: She sat down on a rock and began to tie the cloth over her shoes.
paras.zh: 她坐到一块石头上，开始把布绑在鞋上。

paras.en: It would have been so much better if she’d had real skates.
paras.zh: 要是她有真正的冰鞋，那该好多了。

paras.en: It would have been so much better if she’d had a lot of things.
paras.zh: 要是她拥有很多东西，那都会好得多。

paras.en: She cast one last look back at the castle wall, where, far up, she could see the tall windows that belonged to her sister’s chamber.
paras.zh: 她回头最后望了一眼城堡的墙，在高处，她能看见属于妹妹房间的高窗。

paras.en: For a second, she thought she saw a shadow in the window. “Elsa!” she called, and waved furiously.
paras.zh: 有那么一瞬，她以为自己看见窗里有个影子。“艾莎！”她喊道，使劲挥手。

paras.en: But if that really was her sister, the shadow didn’t wave back.
paras.zh: 可如果那真是她妹妹，那影子并没有挥手回应。

paras.en: Typical.
paras.zh: 果然。

paras.en: Anna tied the final knot.
paras.zh: 安娜打上了最后一个结。

paras.en: She was so tired of waiting.
paras.zh: 她已经等得厌倦了。

paras.en: She wanted to skate, even if Elsa didn’t.
paras.zh: 她想滑冰，哪怕艾莎不想。

paras.en: She nodded firmly, pushed her red braids behind her shoulders, and took a step out onto the ice.
paras.zh: 她坚定地点点头，把红色麻花辫甩到肩后，迈步踏上了冰面。

paras.en: Elsa watched from the window of her chamber, just like always.
paras.zh: 艾莎像往常一样，从自己房间的窗口望着。

paras.en: Far below, Anna was trying—and failing—to skate on the duck pond.
paras.zh: 在下方远处，安娜正试着在鸭塘上滑冰——却滑不好。

paras.en: Elsa supposed it couldn’t properly be called skating, not really.
paras.zh: 艾莎心想，那恐怕称不上是真正的滑冰。

paras.en: What her little sister was doing was sliding around on a bit of cloth or something tied to her boots.
paras.zh: 她小妹妹所做的，不过是在绑在靴子上的布片之类东西上打滑。

paras.en: Actually, what she was mostly doing was slipping a few feet on the ice, then falling.
paras.zh: 其实，她大多是在冰上滑出几英尺，然后摔倒。

paras.en: Honestly, it seemed painful, and it had been going on for over half an hour.
paras.zh: 说实话，这看着都疼，而且已经持续半个多小时了。

paras.en: Elsa imagined Anna’s entire backside was covered in bruises at this point, and she was probably freezing.
paras.zh: 艾莎想象着，到这会儿安娜的整个后背恐怕青一块紫一块，而且她大概冻坏了。

paras.en: Any minute, her sister would give up.
paras.zh: 妹妹随时都会放弃的。

paras.en: Any minute.
paras.zh: 随时。

paras.en: Another half hour went by.
paras.zh: 又一个半小时过去了。

paras.en: Slip, slip, thunk.
paras.zh: 滑，滑，咚。

paras.en: Slip, slip, whoosh.
paras.zh: 滑，滑，呼。

paras.en: Slip, slip, bonk.
paras.zh: 滑，滑，嘭。

paras.en: Elsa groaned.
paras.zh: 艾莎叹了口气。

paras.en: Frost crept up the glass from the ends of her frustrated fingers.
paras.zh: 寒霜从她沮丧的手指尖爬上了玻璃。

paras.en: She wished she could help.
paras.zh: 她真希望自己能帮上忙。

paras.en: She knew how.
paras.zh: 她知道该怎么做。

paras.en: Despite years of focusing solely on not using her magic, she still remembered exactly what it was like to make smooth sheets of ice, to make shapes from snow.
paras.zh: 尽管多年来她只专注于不使用魔法，却仍清楚地记得，造出平整冰面、用雪捏出形状是什么感觉。

paras.en: She could magic up a set of icy blades for the bottom of her sister’s boots that would make this entire process so much easier.
paras.zh: 她可以用魔法给妹妹的靴底变出一副冰刀，让整个过程轻松许多。

paras.en: She could… but she wouldn’t.
paras.zh: 她可以……但她不会那么做。

paras.en: She’d promised to keep her magic secret from her sister.
paras.zh: 她答应过，要对妹妹保守魔法的秘密。

paras.en: To control it, to not let it show.
paras.zh: 要控制它，不让它显露。

paras.en: Outside, on the ice, Anna kept trying.
paras.zh: 外面，冰面上，安娜还在不断尝试。

paras.en: Slip, slip… crash.
paras.zh: 滑，滑……哗啦。

paras.en: Elsa straightened and pressed her hands against the windowpane.
paras.zh: 艾莎挺直身子，把手按在窗玻璃上。

paras.en: The air in the room dropped twenty degrees.
paras.zh: 房间里的气温骤降了二十度。

paras.en: Down by the duck pond, all she could see of her sister was two stockinged legs waving in the air from deep in a snowbank, under a weeping willow.
paras.zh: 在鸭塘边，她能看见的妹妹，只有从深雪堆里、在一棵垂柳下朝空中乱蹬的两条穿着长袜的腿。

paras.en: Frantically, Elsa checked the area around the pond, but she saw no servants, no stable hands.
paras.zh: 艾莎慌乱地扫视着池塘四周，却没看见任何仆人，也没看见马夫。

paras.en: No one to help her sister.
paras.zh: 没人能帮她的妹妹。

paras.en: No one… but her.
paras.zh: 没人……除了她自己。

paras.en: Elsa couldn’t take it anymore.
paras.zh: 艾莎再也受不了了。

paras.en: She went over to her closet, pushing aside the fancy fur coats she never wore, the warm velvet cloaks she found stifling both inside and outdoors.
paras.zh: 她走到自己的衣柜前，把那些从不见她穿的华丽皮草外套、还有那些在室内外都让她觉得闷得慌的温暖天鹅绒斗篷推开。

paras.en: Far in the back was a trunk.
paras.zh: 最里面有一个旧木箱。

paras.en: It had once been her mother’s, back when Queen Iduna was nothing more than a common girl in love with a king.
paras.zh: 那曾是她母亲的东西，那时伊杜娜女王还只是个爱上国王的普通姑娘。

paras.en: Inside were plenty of plain, simple clothes.
paras.zh: 箱子里是许多朴素、简单的衣物。

paras.en: Anna probably didn’t remember it now, but the girls had used to play dress-up with them.
paras.zh: 安娜现在大概不记得了，但姐妹俩从前常拿这些衣服玩换装游戏。

paras.en: In the old days.
paras.zh: 在从前那些日子里。

paras.en: When they’d played.
paras.zh: 在她们还一起玩的时候。

paras.en: Elsa dug through the stack of rough-knit sweaters and thick boiled-wool caps.
paras.zh: 艾莎翻找着那一叠粗糙针织的毛衣和厚实的缩绒羊毛帽。

paras.en: From the very bottom, she pulled out a pair of skates.
paras.zh: 在最底下，她抽出了一双冰鞋。

paras.en: They were fancier than most of the stuff in her mother’s trunk, with sharp silver blades.
paras.zh: 它比母亲箱子里的大多数东西都精致，还带着锋利的银色冰刀。

paras.en: A gift, the queen had said, from someone who should have known better at the time.
paras.zh: 女王说过，这是一份礼物，来自当时本应更懂事的一个人。

paras.en: And then she’d always smiled that goofy grin at their father.
paras.zh: 然后她总会冲着她们的父亲露出那种傻乎乎的笑。

paras.en: The one that made the girls blush and groan.
paras.zh: 就是那种让姐妹俩又脸红又叹气的笑。

paras.en: Elsa hadn’t ever used the skates, and neither had Anna.
paras.zh: 艾莎从没用过这双冰鞋，安娜也没用过。

paras.en: Why bother, when she could have just magicked up a set of ice blades and gone careening around the ballroom?
paras.zh: 既然她可以直接用魔法变出一副冰刀、在舞厅里横冲直撞，又何必费那劲呢？

paras.en: But that was then.
paras.zh: 但那是从前。

paras.en: And this?
paras.zh: 而现在呢？

paras.en: This was now.
paras.zh: 这是现在。

paras.en: There was just one problem.
paras.zh: 只是有一个问题。

paras.en: She could never let Anna know.
paras.zh: 她绝不能让安娜知道。

paras.en: Anna dug her body out of the snowdrift, feeling something very akin to despair.
paras.zh: 安娜从雪堆里把自己刨出来，心里涌起一种近乎绝望的感觉。

paras.en: This was impossible!
paras.zh: 这根本不可能！

paras.en: Around her, the wind blew cold and harsh.
paras.zh: 她周围，寒风凄冷而刺骨地吹着。

paras.en: Her skin stung where her clothes were soaked through.
paras.zh: 衣服湿透的地方，她的皮肤刺痛着。

paras.en: She could hardly even feel her fingers anymore.
paras.zh: 她几乎连手指都感觉不到了。

paras.en: All this time, all this work, and she’d barely even made it a few feet across the ice.
paras.zh: 这么长时间，这么一番折腾，她却连冰面都没能横着滑出几英尺。

paras.en: How had it been so much easier when she was a child?
paras.zh: 小时候怎么就那么容易呢？

paras.en: So much easier… with Elsa?
paras.zh: 那么容易……因为有艾莎在？

paras.en: Out of nowhere, something cold and soft and wet smacked her right in the back of her head.
paras.zh: 不知从哪儿飞来一样又冷又软又湿的东西，正中她后脑勺。

paras.en: A snowball!
paras.zh: 一个雪球！

paras.en: Stunned, Anna whirled around, her hand going by instinct to her head.
paras.zh: 安娜愣住了，猛地转过身，手本能地摸向自己的头。

paras.en: Bits of fresh snow encrusted her braids.
paras.zh: 新鲜雪花黏在了她的辫子上。

paras.en: Someone had thrown a snowball at her!
paras.zh: 有人朝她扔了雪球！

paras.en: But there was no one lurking by the trunk of the willow tree, or hiding behind its drooping branches.
paras.zh: 可柳树干旁没有藏着谁，垂下的枝条后也没有人躲着。

paras.en: In fact, all she saw was a glint of… Wait, what was that?
paras.zh: 事实上，她只看见一道闪光……等等，那是什么？

paras.en: Anna’s eyes narrowed as she peered more closely.
paras.zh: 安娜眯起眼睛，凑近仔细看。

paras.en: There, resting in a tangle of willow branches Anna could have sworn had not existed a second ago, was a pair of ice skates.
paras.zh: 在那里，搁在一团柳枝间——安娜发誓那一秒前那里还没有枝条——竟是一双冰鞋。

paras.en: Bright white ice skates, with silver blades.
paras.zh: 亮白色的冰鞋，配着银色冰刀。

paras.en: She squealed with delight and went closer.
paras.zh: 她欢喜地叫了一声，凑近了些。

paras.en: To the touch, the skates were ice cold, which was probably not surprising given they were out in this freezing weather.
paras.zh: 摸上去，冰鞋冰凉刺骨，考虑到它们就放在这冰天雪地里，这倒也不足为奇。

paras.en: She pulled them down from the branches, still looking to see where they could have come from.
paras.zh: 她把冰鞋从枝条上取下，仍在四处张望，想看清它们到底从哪儿来。

paras.en: But there was no one around.
paras.zh: 可四周空无一人。

paras.en: There was never anyone around.
paras.zh: 从来都没有人在附近。

paras.en: And the skates were here, in her castle courtyard.
paras.zh: 而这双冰鞋就在这儿，在她城堡的庭院里。

paras.en: Could they be meant for her? “Hello?” she asked the winter wind. “Anyone there?” There was no answer.
paras.zh: 会不会是给她的？“有人吗？”她问冬日里的风，“有人在吗？”没有回答。

paras.en: In fairy tales, princesses had fairy godmothers.
paras.zh: 童话里，公主都有仙女教母。

paras.en: Maybe that was what this was.
paras.zh: 也许这就是其中之一吧。

paras.en: Or a troll.
paras.zh: 要么，是地精。

paras.en: Could always be a troll, right?
paras.zh: 总有可能是地精，对吧？

paras.en: Before she could talk herself out of it, Anna untied the cloths from her shoes, pulled off her boots, and slipped her feet inside the skates.
paras.zh: 安娜还没来得及说服自己放弃，就解下鞋上的布，脱掉靴子，把脚套进了冰鞋里。

paras.en: They fit perfectly.
paras.zh: 它们正合适。

paras.en: The blades cut firmly but minutely into the ice at her feet as she took her first steps out onto the duck pond.
paras.zh: 当她迈出第一步踏上鸭塘时，冰刀稳稳地、微微地切入脚下的冰里。

paras.en: She wasn’t slipping!
paras.zh: 她没有打滑！

paras.en: She felt… powerful.
paras.zh: 她感到……充满力量。

paras.en: She pushed off, arms held out for balance, expecting at any moment for her feet to slide out from beneath her as they had so many times before.
paras.zh: 她蹬地出发，张开双臂保持平衡，等待着自己的脚随时像以往那么多次一样从身下溜走。

paras.en: But they didn’t!
paras.zh: 可它们没有！

paras.en: The skates slid through the ice with a satisfying schewp-schewp sound.
paras.zh: 冰鞋在冰上滑过，发出令人满足的“唰——唰——”声。

paras.en: That was the problem!
paras.zh: 问题就在这儿！

paras.en: That was it the whole time.
paras.zh: 一直以来都是这个原因。

paras.en: She hadn’t forgotten how to skate.
paras.zh: 她并没有忘记怎么滑冰。

paras.en: She just needed real skates.
paras.zh: 她只是需要真正的冰鞋。

paras.en: Beautiful ones, like these.
paras.zh: 像这样漂亮的。

paras.en: She circled the pond, tentatively at first, and then—as she got the feel for the blades, for the ice, for the wind on her face—with far more confidence.
paras.zh: 她绕着池塘滑，起初小心翼翼，而后——随着她渐渐摸熟了冰刀、冰面，还有拂面的风——便自信了许多。

paras.en: Schewp schewp schewp.
paras.zh: 唰唰唰。

paras.en: Anna grinned from ear to ear.
paras.zh: 安娜笑得合不拢嘴。

paras.en: Could she go faster?
paras.zh: 她能滑得更快吗？

paras.en: Oh, yes, she could.
paras.zh: 噢，她当然能。

paras.en: Elsa slammed the door to her bedroom behind her, panting.
paras.zh: 艾莎“砰”地关上卧室门，气喘吁吁。

paras.en: That was close!
paras.zh: 好险！

paras.en: She was sure that Anna might have seen her, lurking beyond the willow.
paras.zh: 她确信安娜可能看见她了，就藏在柳树后面。

paras.en: She felt hot all over, her face flushed, probably from running through the castle and sprinting across the grounds.
paras.zh: 她浑身发烫，脸涨得通红，大概是因为跑过城堡、又冲过庭院的缘故。

paras.en: It had been years since she’d thrown a snowball.
paras.zh: 她已经好多年没扔过雪球了。

paras.en: She was afraid she’d forgotten how.
paras.zh: 她怕自己已经忘了怎么扔了。

paras.en: But even without the magic, the snow obeyed her perfectly, smacking her sister right in the back of the head.
paras.zh: 可即便没有用魔法，雪也完美地听她指挥，正中妹妹的后脑勺。

paras.en: Elsa hoped it had worked.
paras.zh: 艾莎希望这招奏效了。

paras.en: Tentatively, she approached the window, her gloved hands covering her face.
paras.zh: 她小心翼翼地走近窗边，用戴着手套的双手捂住脸。

paras.en: Somehow, Elsa felt as if peeking through her gloved fingers made it just the tiniest bit better.
paras.zh: 不知为何，艾莎觉得从手套指缝里偷看，能让心情好上那么一点点。

paras.en: She wasn’t supposed to go near Anna until she learned how to control her magic.
paras.zh: 在学会控制魔法之前，她不该靠近安娜。

paras.en: She certainly shouldn’t have played in the snow.
paras.zh: 她当然更不该在雪里玩耍。

paras.en: But she’d done it, for her sister.
paras.zh: 可她这么做了，为了妹妹。

paras.en: Elsa looked.
paras.zh: 艾莎看去。

paras.en: Down on the duck pond, Anna skated around on their mother’s old ice skates.
paras.zh: 下方的鸭塘上，安娜正穿着她们母亲那双旧冰鞋绕圈滑行。

paras.en: She shouted for joy, her red braids flying out behind her like a streak as she went faster and faster with every loop.
paras.zh: 她欢喜地喊着，红色麻花辫在身后如一道流光般飞扬，每一圈都滑得越来越快。

paras.en: And Elsa had done that, too.
paras.zh: 而这一切，艾莎也出了一份力。

paras.en: The next time Anna approached Elsa’s door, she was hopeful in a way she hadn’t been in a long time.
paras.zh: 下一次安娜走到艾莎门前时，她带着许久未有的期待。

paras.en: She knocked, as usual, and waited to see if her sister would open the door.
paras.zh: 她像往常一样敲了门，等着看妹妹会不会开门。

paras.en: Of course, she did not. “Want to go skating?” she asked the door’s painted panels. “Come on, Elsa, the weather is perfect.
paras.zh: 当然，妹妹没有开。“想去滑冰吗？”她对着门上的彩绘木板问道，“来嘛，艾莎，天气再好不过了。

paras.en: Remember how much we used to like skating together?
paras.zh: 还记得我们以前多喜欢一起滑冰吗？

paras.en: The duck pond isn’t far.…” No answer.
paras.zh: 鸭塘离这儿不远……”没有回答。

paras.en: She took a breath. “Okay,” she continued, her voice a bit lower. “But listen, I have a secret.
paras.zh: 她吸了口气。“好吧，”她继续道，声音低了些，“不过你听，我有个秘密。

paras.en: I found these skates, out by the pond.
paras.zh: 我在池塘边找到了这双冰鞋。

paras.en: I’ve been skating on them every day.
paras.zh: 我每天都穿着它滑冰。

paras.en: They’re amazing, Elsa.
paras.zh: 它太棒了，艾莎。

paras.en: So smooth, so fast, so beautiful.
paras.zh: 那么顺滑，那么快，那么美。

paras.en: And skating on them—wow, it’s just like magic!” Was that a noise?
paras.zh: 穿着它滑冰——哇，简直像魔法一样！”那是不是有什么声音？

paras.en: Had Elsa made some kind of sound there on the other side of the door?
paras.zh: 是艾莎在门的那一侧发出了什么动静吗？

paras.en: Anna pressed her forehead against the door.
paras.zh: 安娜把额头抵在门上。

paras.en: It was cool to the touch—no, cold, even.
paras.zh: 摸上去凉凉的——不，甚至是冰冷的。

paras.en: How very strange. “Elsa,” she wheedled. “Please?
paras.zh: 真奇怪。“艾莎，”她软声央求，“求你了？

paras.en: Please at least come watch me skate?
paras.zh: 至少来看看我滑冰好不好？

paras.en: You won’t believe how fast I am!
paras.zh: 你都不敢信我滑得多快！

paras.en: I’ve only been practicing a few days.…” Sometimes, Anna wondered if Elsa was really in there at all.
paras.zh: 我才练了几天而已……”有时，安娜会怀疑艾莎到底是不是真的在里面。

paras.en: They saw each other at formal events, of course, nodded to one another across a lavish dinner table or from a castle balcony.
paras.zh: 她们当然会在正式场合见到彼此，隔着奢华的餐桌或站在城堡阳台上互相点头致意。

paras.en: Her sister was so tall and elegant now, so distant.
paras.zh: 妹妹如今那么高挑、优雅，那么疏远。

paras.en: So silent.
paras.zh: 那么沉默。

paras.en: It was hard to remember that they’d ever played together at all.
paras.zh: 简直难以记起她们曾经一起玩耍过。

paras.en: The door was so cold!
paras.zh: 这扇门好冷！

paras.en: Did Elsa have the window open in there?
paras.zh: 艾莎是不是把里面的窗打开了？

paras.en: She must have been freezing.
paras.zh: 她肯定冻坏了。

paras.en: If only her sister would answer.
paras.zh: 要是妹妹肯应一声就好了。

paras.en: Even talking would be better than this cold, quiet closed door.
paras.zh: 哪怕说句话，也比这扇冰冷、安静的紧闭之门要好。

paras.en: Then Anna had an idea.
paras.zh: 这时安娜有了个主意。

paras.en: A delightful idea.
paras.zh: 一个妙极了的主意。

paras.en: A wicked idea. “Want to hear a secret?” she blurted out. “Want to hear my plan?
paras.zh: 一个淘气的主意。“想听个秘密吗？”她脱口而出，“想听我的计划吗？

paras.en: It’s crazy, really.
paras.zh: 说真的，这很疯狂。

paras.en: But these skates are so great, and I’m skating so fast, and really, it’s a shame that I never get to try them out on anything but the old duck pond.…” Was that a sound behind the door?
paras.zh: 可这双鞋太棒了，我滑得又那么快，说真的，我从来只能在老鸭塘上试它们，真是太可惜了……”门后是不是有声响？

paras.en: Was Elsa even listening? “Anyway, I heard there’s a festival down in the village square today.
paras.zh: 艾莎到底有没有在听？“反正，我听说今天村子广场上有个节日。

paras.en: A winter festival with games and contests… and a skating race—and I’m going to enter it!” Anna finished triumphantly.
paras.zh: 一个冬日的节日，有游戏、有比赛……还有一场滑冰赛——而我要去参加！”安娜得意地收了尾。

paras.en: Was that a gasp?
paras.zh: 那是一声倒吸凉气吗？

paras.en: Was her sister going to say something at last?
paras.zh: 妹妹终于要开口了吗？

paras.en: Anna didn’t care.
paras.zh: 安娜才不在乎。

paras.en: The moment the words passed her lips she realized that she was actually going to do it.
paras.zh: 话一出口，她就意识到自己是真的要去做这件事了。

paras.en: Not just say so to tease Elsa to get her to open this door.
paras.zh: 不单是为了逗艾莎、让她打开这扇门才这么说。

paras.en: Actually go. “Mama and Papa would be so upset… but they wouldn’t stop me,” she insisted.
paras.zh: 是真要去。“爸爸妈妈会很不高兴……但他们拦不住我，”她坚持道。

paras.en: Her brow furrowed, her jaw clenched. “And neither will you—will you, Elsa?
paras.zh: 她皱起眉头，咬紧牙关。“你也拦不住我——对吧，艾莎？

paras.en: You won’t tell me not to do it.
paras.zh: 你不会叫我别去的。

paras.en: You won’t even open.
paras.zh: 你连门都不肯开。

paras.en: This.
paras.zh: 这扇。

paras.en: Door.” She put her hand up to touch the knob, then pulled it back.
paras.zh: 门。”她抬起手想去碰门把，又缩了回来。

paras.en: The metal was so cold it almost burned. “Elsa?” she said again, forgetting for a moment her years of frustration.
paras.zh: 那金属冷得几乎像在灼人。“艾莎？”她又唤了一声，一时忘了这些年的沮丧。

paras.en: Her sister was sitting in there, all alone and apparently freezing.
paras.zh: 她妹妹就坐在里面，孤零零的，显然冻得要命。

paras.en: Anna had no idea what she did for fun anymore.
paras.zh: 安娜再也不知道她现在拿什么找乐子了。

paras.en: Certainly nothing like Anna was about to do. “Are you all right in there?” But, as always, there was no answer.
paras.zh: 肯定不像安娜即将要做的这样。“你一个人在里面还好吗？”可像往常一样，没有回答。

paras.en: It was official: Elsa had created a monster.
paras.zh: 这下定了：艾莎养出了一个“小魔王”。

paras.en: Every protective older-sister instinct she’d ever had warred with her resolve.
paras.zh: 她曾有的每一个保护妹妹的姐姐本能，都在与她的决心交战。

paras.en: She was moments from flinging open the door and telling Anna under no circumstances was she to go down to the village alone.
paras.zh: 她差点就要一把拉开房门，告诉安娜无论如何都不准她独自下村去。

paras.en: But surely Anna would only use that as an excuse to ask Elsa to come along.
paras.zh: 可安娜多半只会借此央求艾莎陪她一起去。

paras.en: Which she couldn’t do.
paras.zh: 而那是她做不到的。

paras.en: Ever.
paras.zh: 永远。

paras.en: No matter how much she might want to.
paras.zh: 无论她多想这么做。

paras.en: When she was sure the coast was clear, Elsa cracked open the door to her room.
paras.zh: 确认四下无人后，艾莎把房门开了一条缝。

paras.en: The hallway was empty, as usual.
paras.zh: 走廊空荡荡的，一如往常。

paras.en: The castle’s skeleton staff must be working in some other wing today.
paras.zh: 城堡里那点仅剩的仆人今天一定在别的厢房干活。

paras.en: She crept down the hall to her sister’s chambers.
paras.zh: 她蹑手蹑脚沿走廊走向妹妹的房间。

paras.en: Anna—possibly in protest—hardly ever closed her door completely.
paras.zh: 安娜——也许是为了表示抗议——几乎从不完全关上门。

paras.en: From inside, Elsa could hear her grumbling. “The problem with being a princess,” Anna complained to no one in particular, “is that all of your clothes look like you’re a princess.
paras.zh: 从门里，艾莎能听见她在嘟囔。“当公主的麻烦，”安娜不知在对谁抱怨，“就在于你所有的衣服都让你像个公主。

paras.en: Ugh!
paras.zh: 唉！

paras.en: I have nothing to wear !” Elsa peered through the crack between the door and the threshold.
paras.zh: 我根本没衣服可穿！”艾莎从门与门槛之间的缝隙里张望。

paras.en: If Anna looked out, Elsa could pretend she was just walking down the hall for something else.
paras.zh: 如果安娜往外看，艾莎可以假装自己只是路过走廊、有别的事。

paras.en: After all, it was a free hall.
paras.zh: 毕竟，那是条公共走廊。

paras.en: Her jaw dropped as she glanced in the room.
paras.zh: 她朝屋里瞥了一眼，惊得张开了嘴。

paras.en: Elsa’s little sister had created an enormous mess.
paras.zh: 艾莎的小妹妹把房间弄得一团糟。

paras.en: Piles of gowns lay all over the bed and the floor.
paras.zh: 一堆堆礼服散落在床上和地上。

paras.en: The maids would have a fit when they saw it. “What am I supposed to skate in!” Anna groaned, and flopped onto the bed.
paras.zh: 女仆们见了非疯掉不可。“我到底该穿什么去滑冰！”安娜哀叹，一屁股瘫倒在床上。

paras.en: For a moment all was silent.
paras.zh: 有那么一会儿，四周静悄悄的。

paras.en: Elsa bit her lip and listened harder.
paras.zh: 艾莎咬着嘴唇，更仔细地听。

paras.en: Was that—was that crying?
paras.zh: 那是不是——是不是在哭？

paras.en: Protective older-sister instincts reared up again, but this time, there was a very different goal in mind.
paras.zh: 保护妹妹的姐姐本能再次涌起，可这一次，心里怀着全然不同的目标。

paras.en: Elsa hurried back down the hall to her own room.
paras.zh: 艾莎赶紧沿走廊跑回自己房间。

paras.en: To Iduna’s trunk.
paras.zh: 奔向伊杜娜的木箱。

paras.en: A cap to hide those wild red braids.
paras.zh: 一顶能遮住那狂野红辫子的帽子。

paras.en: A thick sweater to keep her warm.
paras.zh: 一件能让她暖和的厚毛衣。

paras.en: Peasant-boy pants—the kind made to move in.
paras.zh: 一条农夫男孩式的裤子——那种方便活动的。

paras.en: These weren’t just dress-up clothes in her mother’s old trunk.
paras.zh: 这些不只是母亲旧木箱里的换装衣服。

paras.en: They were perfect for skating.
paras.zh: 它们简直是为滑冰量身定做的。

paras.en: But how to get them to her sister without giving it all away?
paras.zh: 可怎么才能把它们送到妹妹手里，又不露馅呢？

paras.en: Elsa bundled the clothes in her arms and headed back toward Anna’s room.
paras.zh: 艾莎把衣服抱在怀里，朝安娜的房间走去。

paras.en: There she saw her sister waist deep in her royal closet, rejecting every item in her wardrobe as being far too fancy for the festival.
paras.zh: 在那里，她看见妹妹正埋首在皇家衣橱里，把每件衣服都嫌太过华贵、不适合节日而否决掉。

paras.en: Talk about princess problems.
paras.zh: 这才叫公主的烦恼。

paras.en: Elsa shook her head.
paras.zh: 艾莎摇了摇头。

paras.en: Then, before her sister could turn around, she raised the bundle of clothes in her arms and lobbed them into the middle of the biggest pile of rejects.
paras.zh: 接着，趁妹妹还没转身，她举起怀里的那包衣服，朝最大那堆被否决的衣服中央一抛。

paras.en: There was a loud woompf as the clothing pile toppled over.
paras.zh: 衣服堆被砸倒时发出“嘭”的一声闷响。

paras.en: Elsa didn’t look to see if Anna noticed.
paras.zh: 艾莎没有去看安娜有没有注意到。

paras.en: She just ran.
paras.zh: 她拔腿就跑。

paras.en: Anna was ready to give up entirely.
paras.zh: 安娜已经准备彻底放弃了。

paras.en: No way could she sneak into the village dressed like Princess Anna of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 她绝不可能穿着阿伦黛尔安娜公主的行头溜进村子。

paras.en: Her skirts were all embroidered with the royal crest, her vests all had golden buttons up the front.
paras.zh: 她的裙子全都绣着皇家纹章，马甲前面全是一排排金纽扣。

paras.en: She sat back in a pile of ball gowns and sighed.
paras.zh: 她向后靠在一堆舞会礼服上，叹了口气。

paras.en: Just then, her eye caught on something unfamiliar.
paras.zh: 就在这时，她的目光被一样不熟悉的东西吸引了。

paras.en: Unfamiliar and very brown.
paras.zh: 不熟悉，而且很棕。

paras.en: She cocked her head at the trousers now lying among the piles of silk and satin.
paras.zh: 她歪着头，看向此刻躺在丝绸与缎子堆里的那条裤子。

paras.en: Where had those come from?
paras.zh: 那是从哪儿来的？

paras.en: They were dark and rough, like somehow the gardener’s laundry had gotten mixed up with her own.
paras.zh: 它们又深又粗，仿佛是园丁的衣物不知怎的和她的混在了一起。

paras.en: And nearby lay a sweater she didn’t recognize in a drab olive green, and a boiled-wool cap in dishwater gray.
paras.zh: 旁边还躺着一件她没见过的暗橄榄绿毛衣，和一顶灰扑扑的缩绒羊毛帽。

paras.en: Had those things been in her closet?
paras.zh: 这些东西本来就在她衣橱里吗？

paras.en: A costume?
paras.zh: 是戏服？

paras.en: A mistake?
paras.zh: 是弄错了？

paras.en: No!
paras.zh: 不是！

paras.en: She sat up straight.
paras.zh: 她坐直了身子。

paras.en: It was another gift from that invisible fairy godmother, that magical troll who’d left her the skates!
paras.zh: 那是那位隐形的仙女教母、那位留下冰鞋的神奇地精送来的又一份礼物！

paras.en: Anna got dressed in the new clothes at once.
paras.zh: 安娜立刻换上了这身新衣服。

paras.en: They were a bit big on her, but they’d do the job.
paras.zh: 它们穿在她身上有点大，但够用了。

paras.en: She dug up her thickest pair of mittens and the warmest socks as well, then stuffed her red braids inside the cap and admired her reflection in the mirror.
paras.zh: 她翻出最厚的一副连指手套和最暖的袜子，然后把红色麻花辫塞进帽子里，欣赏起镜子里的自己。

paras.en: There.
paras.zh: 好了。

paras.en: Now she looked just like any random village boy.
paras.zh: 现在她看起来就和随便哪个村子里的小男孩一样。

paras.en: She was doing this.
paras.zh: 她要这么干了。

paras.en: She was really sneaking out!
paras.zh: 她是真的要溜出去了！

paras.en: It was easier than she’d expected to sneak through the empty halls of the castle in her getup and out the door.
paras.zh: 穿着这身行头，溜过城堡空荡的走廊、再出门，比她预想的容易得多。

paras.en: Easy to grab her skates from their hiding place by the old willow and creep along the wall until she found a drift of snow firm and high enough to scrabble up the side, and another, far more obligingly soft drift to hop into on the other.
paras.zh: 她轻而易举地从老柳树旁的藏身处抓起冰鞋，沿墙潜行，直到找到一处够硬够高、能让她扒着爬上去的雪堆，又在对面找到另一处更“配合”的松软雪堆，正好跳进去。

paras.en: She took one look back at the castle, at its high towers and cold, empty leaded glass windows.
paras.zh: 她回头望了一眼城堡，望向它高耸的塔楼和冰冷、空荡的铅条玻璃窗。

paras.en: It was impossible to see from here if anyone had watched her escape.
paras.zh: 从这里没法看清有没有人看到了她逃跑。

paras.en: If anyone even cared.
paras.zh: 也没人知道是否有人在意。

paras.en: Well, she didn’t care, either.
paras.zh: 嗯，她也不在乎。

paras.en: She was sick of waiting around inside.
paras.zh: 她受够了关在里面的等待。

paras.en: She was going to have an adventure if it was the last thing she ever did.
paras.zh: 就算这是她这辈子做的最后一件事，她也要去冒险。

paras.en: Nodding firmly, she straightened her cap, adjusted her scarf over her face, and set off down toward the town square.
paras.zh: 她坚定地点点头，扶正帽子，把围巾拉到脸上，朝村镇广场出发了。

paras.en: Once Anna had clambered over the castle wall, Elsa could no longer see her from her window.
paras.zh: 安娜刚翻过城堡墙，艾莎就从窗口看不见她了。

paras.en: But still she didn’t leave, remaining seated by the glass and staring out, as if wishing she could watch what was happening in the village would somehow make it so.
paras.zh: 可她仍没有离开，坐在窗边凝望着外面，仿佛只要她许愿能看见村里发生的事，愿望就会成真似的。

paras.en: If she closed her eyes, she could almost feel it—the freezing wind nipping at Anna’s face, turning her cheeks red and her eyes bright, swirling around the streets down to the village— “Elsa!” Elsa’s eyes popped open and she whirled around to see her mother, Queen Iduna, standing at the door.
paras.zh: 她若闭上眼，几乎能感觉到——凛冽的寒风轻咬安娜的脸颊，冻得她双颊通红、两眼发亮，风打着旋儿掠过街道，一直吹向村子——“艾莎！”艾莎猛地睁眼，转过身，看见母亲伊杜娜女王正站在门口。

paras.en: And then she saw the rest of it.
paras.zh: 接着，她看到了其余的一切。

paras.en: The frost over the windowpane, the icicles dangling in crystal majesty from the curtains.
paras.zh: 窗玻璃上的霜花，以及从窗帘上悬垂而下、如水晶般华美的冰柱。

paras.en: Elsa tightened her hands into fists in horror. “Oh, Mother, I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 艾莎惊恐地攥紧了拳头。“噢，母亲，对不起。

paras.en: I had no idea!
paras.zh: 我完全没注意！

paras.en: I—I wasn’t paying attention.” “Sweetheart…” The queen came closer, but Elsa shied away.
paras.zh: 我——我没留神。”“乖孩子……”女王走近了些，可艾莎躲开了。

paras.en: She didn’t want to hurt her.
paras.zh: 她不想伤到母亲。

paras.en: It was always like this.
paras.zh: 向来都是如此。

paras.en: She’d spent so many years trying desperately to control her magic, to not feel, and yet it felt so much more powerful than any mastery she’d managed to achieve over it in all this time.
paras.zh: 她花了那么多年拼命想控制魔法、想不去感受，可它却比她这些年来勉强掌握的一切都强大得多。

paras.en: Using it was easy—not using it was what was hard.
paras.zh: 使用它很容易——难的是不用它。

paras.en: Just like every other part of her life.
paras.zh: 就像她生活中的其他一切。

paras.en: Loving her sister was so much easier than avoiding Anna for her own safety.
paras.zh: 爱妹妹远比为了她的安全而避开安娜要容易。

paras.en: But, as Elsa’s father said, just because a thing was hard did not mean it wasn’t worth doing.
paras.zh: 但是，正如艾莎的父亲所说，一件事难，不代表就不值得去做。

paras.en: Ruling Arendelle was no picnic, and as heir, Elsa needed to learn everything there was about doing that, too. “Oh, Elsa,” her mother said. “And here I thought things had been going so well lately.” They had been.
paras.zh: 治理阿伦黛尔绝非易事，而作为继承人，艾莎也得把相关的方方面面都学到手。“噢，艾莎，”母亲说，“我还以为最近一切都挺顺利呢。”本来是挺顺利的。

paras.en: At least, they had until Elsa had started letting her guard down.
paras.zh: 至少，在艾莎开始放松警惕之前是。

paras.en: Helping Anna with this skating quest.
paras.zh: 帮安娜实现这趟滑冰之旅。

paras.en: Playing with snowballs.
paras.zh: 玩雪球。

paras.en: She hung her head in shame.
paras.zh: 她羞愧地垂下头。

paras.en: Elsa could not afford to slip up. “I know it’s hard in the wintertime,” Iduna said gently. “It’s so very, very beautiful.” She came to stand beside Elsa anyway. “Is that my old trunk?
paras.zh: 艾莎冒不起出差错的风险。“我知道冬天很难熬，”伊杜娜温柔地说，“它又那么、那么美。”她还是走到艾莎身旁站定。“那是我的旧木箱吗？

paras.en: What do you have that out for?” “Nothing,” Elsa said quickly, making a decision.
paras.zh: 你把它翻出来做什么？”“没什么，”艾莎飞快地答道，心里做了个决定。

paras.en: No more risks. “It was silly.” And it was over.
paras.zh: 不能再冒险了。“都是傻事。”于是就到此为止了。

paras.en: Anna had always loved going into town the few times she’d accompanied her parents on visits.
paras.zh: 安娜向来喜欢进城，那几次跟着父母去拜访时尤其如此。

paras.en: Even through the windows of some stuffy carriage, the village of Arendelle had been filled with wondrous sights and sounds and smells.
paras.zh: 即便隔着某辆闷热马车的车窗，阿伦黛尔村也满是奇妙的景象、声响和气味。

paras.en: The seafood market with its pungent odors and sharp cries of fishmongers hawking their wares.
paras.zh: 海鲜市场里刺鼻的气味，鱼贩叫卖货色时尖锐的吆喝。

paras.en: The ice sellers with their massive sleds and their majestic reindeer.
paras.zh: 卖冰人赶着巨大的雪橇和威风凛凛的驯鹿。

paras.en: Her mother, Iduna, would sometimes point out the windmills on the hills beyond the fjord and explain how, long ago, she was apprenticed to an inventor who built such amazing machines.
paras.zh: 母亲伊杜娜有时会指着峡湾对岸山丘上的风车，讲起很久以前，她曾给一位发明家当学徒，而那人就造出过如此神奇的机器。

paras.en: Anna would always beg to visit the windmills, but it never seemed to be the right time, at least according to her parents.
paras.zh: 安娜总缠着要去参观风车，可似乎总不是合适的时机，至少她父母是这么说的。

paras.en: Today she had better things to do as well.
paras.zh: 今天她也有更要紧的事要做。

paras.en: She slipped in with the crowds and followed the decorations through the winding streets of the market to where the winter festival was already under way.
paras.zh: 她混入人群，顺着装饰，穿过市场蜿蜒的街道，来到冬日节庆已经热闹开场的地方。

paras.en: The smells of roasting meat and spiced cider filled the air, and Anna was pleased she’d remembered to stuff a handful of coins in her pocket before she’d taken off.
paras.zh: 烤肉与香料热苹果酒的香气弥漫在空气中，安娜很庆幸自己在出发前记得往口袋里塞了一把硬币。

paras.en: She was looking at the golden, flaky pastries piled high in a cart when she noticed two other children also enjoying the scent of baked goods and chocolate.
paras.zh: 她正望着推车里高高堆起的金黄酥皮点心，这时注意到另外两个孩子也在享受烘焙食品和巧克力的香气。

paras.en: It was a small girl and a tall boy, about the same ages as herself and Elsa, dressed simply but warmly.
paras.zh: 那是个小女孩和一个高个子男孩，年纪和她与艾莎相仿，穿得朴素却暖和。

paras.en: Both had battered brown skates slung across their shoulders and worn blue caps on their heads.
paras.zh: 两人肩上都斜挎着一双磨损的棕色冰鞋，头上戴着旧的蓝帽子。

paras.en: All at once, the girl noticed Anna staring at them. “Hello,” she said, and nudged the boy. “Look, Trygve.
paras.zh: 忽然，女孩注意到安娜正盯着他们。“你好，”她说着，用胳膊肘捅了捅男孩，“看，特里格维。

paras.en: Our competition.” The boy eyed her up and down. “Seems so.
paras.zh: 我们的对手。”男孩把她上下打量了一番。“好像是。

paras.en: Look at those fancy skates!” “Uh, hi,” Anna said shyly. “Are you in line for pastries?” “No,” said the girl bluntly. “We’re saving our money to enter the skating race.” “Me too!” Anna blurted, even though she hadn’t had any idea there was an entry fee at all, let alone how much it was. “Do you know where to go?” “Of course,” said the girl. “You’re not from around here, are you?” Oh no, was it that obvious? “I’m visiting,” she said quickly.
paras.zh: 瞧那双讲究的冰鞋！”“呃，嗨，”安娜羞怯地说，“你们在排队买点心吗？”“不，”女孩直截了当地说，“我们在攒钱报名滑冰赛。”“我也是！”安娜脱口而出，尽管她根本不知道还要交报名费，更别提多少了。“你知道去哪儿报吗？”“当然，”女孩说，“你不是这附近的人吧？”噢不，有那么明显吗？“我是来串门的，”她赶紧说。

paras.en: She racked her brain for the names of her father’s trading partners. “From, uh… Weselton.
paras.zh: 她绞尽脑汁回想父亲那些贸易伙伴的名字。“从，呃……威斯尔顿。

paras.en: We don’t have skating races there.
paras.zh: 我们那儿没有滑冰比赛。

paras.en: We have, um… weasel races.…” “Weird,” said the girl, possibly tired of Anna’s blathering. “I’m Nora.
paras.zh: 我们有，嗯……鼬鼠比赛……”“怪事，”女孩说，大概听烦了安娜的胡咧咧，“我叫诺拉。

paras.en: This is my brother, Trygve.” “I’m Ann—” Oh no, she really should have thought of a name.
paras.zh: 这是我弟弟，特里格维。”“我叫安——”噢不，她真该先想好一个名字。

paras.en: A boy’s name. “Anders.
paras.zh: 一个男孩的名字。“安德斯。

paras.en: Anders Anderson.
paras.zh: 安德斯·安德森。

paras.en: That’s me.” Was this what it was like, making friends?
paras.zh: 就是我。”交朋友，原来就是这种感觉吗？

paras.en: She liked it.
paras.zh: 她挺喜欢。

paras.en: A lot. “Nice skates, Anders,” said Trygve, though his arms were still crossed.
paras.zh: 很喜欢。“好鞋，安德斯，”特里格维说，尽管他仍抱着胳膊。

paras.en: Anna was glad to have some companions as they made their way to the racing area.
paras.zh: 能有几个伴儿一起去赛区，安娜很高兴。

paras.en: They wandered past stalls selling embroidered shawls and some with painted sleds.
paras.zh: 他们闲逛着经过卖刺绣披肩的摊位，还有卖彩绘雪橇的。

paras.en: A man in a cart was selling reindeer bridles studded with golden, jingling bells.
paras.zh: 一个坐在车上的男人在卖驯鹿缰绳，上面缀着叮当作响的金铃铛。

paras.en: Nora chattered about the race and about their cottage on the slopes near the fjord.
paras.zh: 诺拉喋喋不休地说着比赛，还有他们在峡湾附近山坡上的小屋。

paras.en: Their parents worked in the mill, and they kept their own sheep.
paras.zh: 他们的父母在磨坊干活，自家还养着羊。

paras.en: Anna was amazed by the stories. “What are they like?” she asked. “The sheep?” “Smelly,” answered Trygve.
paras.zh: 安娜听得入了迷。“它们什么样？”她问，“羊？”“臭烘烘的，”特里格维答道。

paras.en: The race itself began at a canal that ran up a street at the edge of the market, all the way to the mill.
paras.zh: 比赛本身从一条运河开始，它顺着市场边缘的街道延伸，一直通到磨坊。

paras.en: Trygve and Nora walked with Anna.
paras.zh: 特里格维和诺拉陪着安娜走。

paras.en: They signed in together at a little booth where Anna discovered that the money she had brought would have covered not only the entrance fee for all three of them, but pastries for half the crowd as well. “I guess I don’t know the exchange rate,” she said sheepishly, but her new friends seemed skeptical.
paras.zh: 他们一起在一个小摊前登记报名，安娜这才发现自己带的钱不光够三人报名，连给半场人买点心都够了。“我想我是不懂汇率吧，”她不好意思地说，可新朋友们似乎将信将疑。

paras.en: No matter what country’s currency it was, she’d accidentally brought a fortune to the race.
paras.zh: 不管那是哪国的钱，她都是阴差阳错带了一笔巨款来比赛。

paras.en: Still, all that faded away once they strapped on their skates and hit the ice to warm up.
paras.zh: 不过，等他们绑上冰鞋、踏上冰面热身，这一切就都抛到脑后了。

paras.en: Anna thrilled at the wind in her face as she circled the little practice area with the other skaters.
paras.zh: 安娜和其他滑冰者一起绕着小练习区滑，风拂过脸庞，让她兴奋不已。

paras.en: The silver skates on her feet were just as smooth here as they’d been on the duck pond.
paras.zh: 脚上的银色冰鞋在这里和鸭塘上一样顺滑。

paras.en: She glided and skimmed over the ice, taking in the gaily painted banners and flags that spectators were waving around the paths above the canal.
paras.zh: 她在冰上滑行、掠过，欣赏着运河上方小径边观众挥舞的鲜艳彩旗横幅。

paras.en: How much you missed by staying inside the castle gates!
paras.zh: 待在城堡门里，你错过了多少东西！

paras.en: Around her, the competition was skating, too.
paras.zh: 她周围，其他选手也在滑。

paras.en: There was a girl in a graceful purple gown who seemed as interested in leaps and spins as she was in speed.
paras.zh: 有个穿优雅紫裙的女孩，似乎对跳跃旋转和对速度一样感兴趣。

paras.en: A trio of young men in the furs and leathers of the ice cutters from the North Mountain raced past, their moves in perfect unison.
paras.zh: 三个穿着北山采冰人皮毛皮装的年轻男子飞驰而过，动作整齐划一。

paras.en: A cluster of kids younger than Anna were falling all over themselves and one another every few strokes of their skates.
paras.zh: 一小群比安娜还小的孩子，每滑几下就把自己和别人摔成一团。

paras.en: Trygve was steady and focused as a skater.
paras.zh: 作为滑冰者，特里格维稳健而专注。

paras.en: Each stroke was precise, moving him efficiently across the ice.
paras.zh: 每一次蹬冰都精准利落，让他在冰上高效前进。

paras.en: Nora was more playful, scissoring her feet in and out and squatting to glide beneath the struts sticking out of the canal wall. “Wow,” said Anna.
paras.zh: 诺拉更爱玩，她两脚像剪刀般开合，还蹲下身子从运河壁伸出的撑柱下滑过。“哇，”安娜说。

paras.en: Trygve skated up beside her and slowed to match her pace. “Don’t be fooled by her size.
paras.zh: 特里格维滑到她身旁，放慢速度配合她的节奏。“别被她个子小骗了。

paras.en: Nora’s going to give all of us a challenge.” “It must be nice,” she said, “skating with your sister.
paras.zh: 诺拉会给我们所有人制造麻烦的。”“那一定很好，”她说，“和妹妹一起滑冰。

paras.en: My sister never comes out with me.” “Sorry to hear that,” he replied. “Does she only like playing with other girls?” “What?” Anna said, and then caught herself.
paras.zh: 我妹妹从不愿和我一起出来。”“听到这个挺遗憾，”他答道，“她只喜欢和别的女孩玩吗？”“什么？”安娜说，随即反应过来。

paras.en: That was right, she was supposed to be a boy. “Oh, yeah.
paras.zh: 对了，她该是个男孩。“噢，对。

paras.en: That’s it.
paras.zh: 就是那样。

paras.en: Actually, she never even comes out of her room.” By now Nora had circled the starting area and come up behind them. “What?
paras.zh: 其实，她连房间都不出来。”这时诺拉已绕到起点区、从后面追上他们。“什么？

paras.en: When there’s this whole winter wonderland out here?” She spread her arms and spun around on the ice.
paras.zh: 外面明明有一整座冬日奇境？”她张开双臂，在冰上转了一圈。

paras.en: Anna laughed. “I don’t know.
paras.zh: 安娜笑了。“我也不知道。

paras.en: I guess she doesn’t like the cold very much.” On her feet the silver skates gleamed.
paras.zh: 我想她不太喜欢冷吧。”她脚上的银色冰鞋闪闪发亮。

paras.en: She sped across the ice, more than ready to race.
paras.zh: 她飞掠过冰面，早已迫不及待要比赛了。

paras.en: Elsa tamped down her fear as her mother stood by her side at the window.
paras.zh: 母亲站在窗边，艾莎强压下心中的恐惧。

paras.en: There was no way that the queen could know that even now, her younger daughter had snuck out of the castle and was walking down to the village. “I love this time of year,” Iduna said, gazing out at the frost.
paras.zh: 女王绝不可能知道，即便此刻，她的小女儿已经溜出城堡、正往村子走去。“我喜欢一年里的这个时候，”伊杜娜望着霜花说。

paras.en: Elsa did not say that it was her favorite, too.
paras.zh: 艾莎没有说自己也最爱这时节。

paras.en: But she was sure her mother knew anyway. “There’s a winter festival down in the village today,” her mother went on. “I was planning on making a brief appearance.” “Wait… what?” Elsa started.
paras.zh: 但她确信母亲反正也知道。“今天村子里有个冬日节庆，”母亲接着说，“我正打算去露个面。”“等等……什么？”艾莎一惊。

paras.en: She had not considered that.
paras.zh: 她没料到这一点。

paras.en: Though no one in the village had seen either of the princesses in years, her mother would not be fooled by Anna’s disguise.
paras.zh: 尽管村里人已经多年没见过两位公主，母亲却不会被安娜的伪装骗到。

paras.en: Especially since they were her old clothes.
paras.zh: 尤其那还是她旧衣服。

paras.en: Iduna placed a hand comfortingly on Elsa’s shoulder. “Perhaps you would like to come with me?” No, because she could not control her magic.
paras.zh: 伊杜娜安慰地把手放在艾莎肩上。“也许你想跟我一起去？”不行，因为她控制不了魔法。

paras.en: She could not leave her room.
paras.zh: 她不能离开房间。

paras.en: She could not act like Arendelle’s crown princess and make appearances at festivals, because she might accidentally ice the whole parade. “But—but—” She gestured helplessly with her gloved hands.
paras.zh: 她无法像阿伦黛尔的王储公主那样去节庆上露面，因为她可能会不小心把整个游行都冻住。“可——可——”她用戴手套的手无助地比划着。

paras.en: Her mother waved that off. “You’re just getting what we used to call cabin fever.
paras.zh: 母亲把这话挥开了。“你只是得了我们以前常说的幽闭症。

paras.en: Castle fever, in this case.
paras.zh: 这回该叫城堡症。

paras.en: I would be willing to bet that getting outside in a real winter wonderland for a few hours will keep you from bringing one indoors.” She smiled, as if she was telling a little joke.
paras.zh: 我敢打赌，到真正的冬日奇境里待上几个小时，就能让你不再把一座奇境搬进屋里。”她笑了，像在讲个小笑话。

paras.en: Elsa did not find it funny. “You don’t even have to get out of the carriage, if you’re not comfortable,” her mother went on. “No one will know you are there.
paras.zh: 艾莎觉得一点不好笑。“你要是不自在，甚至不用下马车，”母亲接着说，“没人会知道你在那儿。

paras.en: You can just look through the windows.
paras.zh: 你只需从车窗往外看。

paras.en: We won’t bring Anna.
paras.zh: 我们不带安娜。

paras.en: It’ll be just you and me.” Elsa caught her breath.
paras.zh: 就你和我。”艾莎屏住了呼吸。

paras.en: Perhaps this would be best.
paras.zh: 也许这样最好。

paras.en: She could keep her mother from wondering where Anna was in the castle all afternoon, and then, down at the festival, she might steer the queen away from the skating race.
paras.zh: 她能让母亲不至于整个下午都在奇怪安娜在城堡里哪儿，然后到了节庆上，她还能把女王从滑冰比赛那儿引开。

paras.en: Though it would be a thrill to see her sister in action.
paras.zh: 虽说能亲眼看到妹妹上场会让人激动。

paras.en: Her mother looked at her for a long, long time.
paras.zh: 母亲久久地望着她。

paras.en: Long enough for ice crystals to blossom under every fingertip inside her gloves. “I suppose so,” said Elsa at last. “As long as no one sees me.” Her mother leaned in her head to touch her daughter’s, a secret smile on her face. “No one will ever know.
paras.zh: 久到她手套里的每个指尖下都绽出了冰晶。“我想可以吧，”艾莎终于说，“只要没人看见我。”母亲把头凑过去贴上女儿的头，脸上带着一个秘密的微笑。“没人会知道。

paras.en: It’s like we’re in disguise.” Elsa closed her eyes.
paras.zh: 就像我们化了妆一样。”艾莎闭上了眼。

paras.en: If she only knew!
paras.zh: 要是她知道就好啦！

paras.en: Soon enough, all the skaters—including Anna—gathered at the starting area of the ice.
paras.zh: 很快，所有滑冰者——包括安娜——都聚到了冰面的起点区。

paras.en: The race official, a large man with a red beard, spelled out the rules. “The race will begin at my mark.
paras.zh: 裁判是个留红胡子的壮汉，他把规则说了一遍。“比赛以我的口令开始。

paras.en: The course consists of three loops around the canal.
paras.zh: 赛道是绕运河三圈。

paras.en: Start here and skate counterclockwise, all the way down to the flags at the far end.
paras.zh: 从这里出发，逆时针滑行，一直滑到远端的旗子处。

paras.en: All skaters must pass the flags three times on their left-hand side or they will be disqualified.
paras.zh: 所有选手必须从左侧经过旗子三次，否则将被取消资格。

paras.en: There are prizes for the first three skaters to complete the race.” Anna adjusted her hat down over her braids and got into starting position.
paras.zh: 前三名完成比赛的选手有奖品。”安娜把帽子拉下来盖住辫子，摆出起跑姿势。

paras.en: Nearby, her new friends Trygve and Nora were jockeying for position at the front of the pack.
paras.zh: 不远处，她的新朋友特里格维和诺拉正在人群前方抢占位置。

paras.en: People crowded the paths above the canal, leaning on the railings and looking out below to cheer on their friends in the race.
paras.zh: 人们挤在运河上方的小径上，倚着栏杆朝下方张望，为自己参赛的朋友加油。

paras.en: She wished her own family could be there to see her.
paras.zh: 她希望自己的家人也能在那儿看她。

paras.en: Just then a whistle blew, and the race began.
paras.zh: 就在这时哨声响起，比赛开始了。

paras.en: The scrape of blades on ice filled the air, and racers began to jostle and move around her.
paras.zh: 冰刀刮过冰面的声音充斥空中，选手们开始推挤、从她身边掠过。

paras.en: Anna quickly realized that this was nothing like the duck pond.
paras.zh: 安娜很快意识到，这和在鸭塘上完全不同。

paras.en: There, she had all the space in the world to move precisely as she wanted to, but here, she dodged elbows and feet, nowhere near able to set the pace she wanted as she fought for any space at all on the crowded ice.
paras.zh: 在那里，她有全世界那么大的空间随心所欲地滑，可在这里，她得躲开手肘和脚，在拥挤的冰面上拼命挤出一点空间，根本没法按自己想要的速度滑。

paras.en: A skater went down in front of her and she swerved wildly to miss running over their fingers.
paras.zh: 一个选手在她前面摔倒，她猛地急转，免得碾到对方手指。

paras.en: Unfortunately, the move sent her in the path of the ice cutters, who had formed a solid wall across the course.
paras.zh: 不巧，这一转让她撞上了采冰人的路线，他们正横在赛道上，组成一道密实的墙。

paras.en: Anna’s arms wheeled wildly in the air. “Watch out!” one of the ice cutters barked at her.
paras.zh: 安娜的胳膊在空中乱舞。“小心！”一个采冰人对她喝道。

paras.en: As one, they swerved to miss her.
paras.zh: 他们齐刷刷地一转，避开了她。

paras.en: She overcorrected her stride and caught the edge of her left blade on an imperfection in the ice, tripping and spinning off course in an attempt to keep from wiping out.
paras.zh: 她纠正过度，左脚冰刀的刀刃卡在冰面一处不平上，为了不摔个四脚朝天，她踉跄着转出了赛道。

paras.en: The crowd gasped.
paras.zh: 人群倒吸一口凉气。

paras.en: After a moment, Anna managed to regain control of herself.
paras.zh: 过了一会儿，安娜总算重新稳住自己。

paras.en: She patted the hat on her head, making sure it was still secure, and got her bearings.
paras.zh: 她拍了拍头上的帽子，确认还戴得牢，然后辨明了方向。

paras.en: The racers had all moved on.
paras.zh: 选手们都已经滑远了。

paras.en: She was dead last! “Come on, skates!” she called between gritted teeth and started after the others.
paras.zh: 她是彻彻底底的最后一名！“加油啊，冰鞋！”她咬着牙喊，追着其他人出发了。

paras.en: The silver skates did not fail her.
paras.zh: 银色冰鞋没让她失望。

paras.en: Cleared of those who were blocking her before, Anna was able to pick up speed easily.
paras.zh: 摆脱了之前挡路的人，安娜轻易就提了速。

paras.en: By the time the first skaters were passing the flags at the far end of the course, she had reached the back of the pack.
paras.zh: 等最前面的选手滑到赛道远端旗子处时，她已经追到了队伍末尾。

paras.en: The others had spread out some at this point, and she was able to pass the flailing children as she might have avoided a boulder in the duck pond or a fallen willow branch.
paras.zh: 这会儿其他人已拉开些距离，她能超过那些乱挥乱舞的孩子，就像在鸭塘里避开一块石头或一根落下的柳枝那样轻松。

paras.en: Looking ahead, Anna spotted the girl in the purple gown.
paras.zh: 望向前方，安娜发现了那个穿紫裙的女孩。

paras.en: She had given up on her twirls and was now trying to focus on speed, but her form was all off.
paras.zh: 她已经放弃了旋转，转而专注速度，可姿势全乱了。

paras.en: Anna raced by her.
paras.zh: 安娜从她身边超了过去。

paras.en: By the time the leaders had completed the first loop, Anna had managed to catch up to the three ice cutters, who were still skating in perfect unison, blocking the course for anyone who might want to pass.
paras.zh: 等领先者完成第一圈时，安娜已经追上了那三个采冰人，他们仍以完美的一致动作滑行，挡住任何想超车者的去路。

paras.en: The three came closer and closer to the starting gate, where another flagpole marked their turn.
paras.zh: 三人越来越接近起点门，那里另一根旗杆标着他们的转弯处。

paras.en: Anna did not think she could pass them on the outside, but she could also tell by their moves that the leftmost skater was sure to cut as close to the pole as possible as they turned.
paras.zh: 安娜觉得自己没法从外侧超，但从他们的动作能看出，最左边的那个滑冰者转弯时一定会尽可能贴着旗杆切过去。

paras.en: She skated behind them, unsure, as they all turned together.
paras.zh: 她跟在他们身后，犹疑着，和他们一同转弯。

paras.en: Anna knew she had the speed to pass them, but they wouldn’t let her through.
paras.zh: 安娜知道自己有速度超过他们，可他们不会放她过去。

paras.en: She dithered, skating up on one side, then another, the entire length of the canal.
paras.zh: 她犹豫不决，在运河全程一会儿滑到这边，一会儿滑到那边。

paras.en: She was still stuck behind them as they made their second turn around the flags at the far end of the course.
paras.zh: 等他们完成远端旗子处的第二次转弯时，她仍被堵在后面。

paras.en: She’d never get past them at this rate!
paras.zh: 照这速度，她永远也超不过去！

paras.en: Anna glanced across the course to where she could see Nora in the lead, the pom-pom on her blue hat bobbing with every stroke.
paras.zh: 安娜朝赛道对面望去，看见诺拉正领先，她蓝帽上的绒球随着每一次蹬冰上下跳动。

paras.en: She was already so far ahead she was circling around behind the slowest racers.
paras.zh: 她已经领先那么多，正绕到最慢选手的身后了。

paras.en: Remembering Nora’s antics during practice, Anna got an idea.
paras.zh: 想起诺拉练习时的那些花招，安娜有了主意。

paras.en: She skated close to the three ice cutters, set her silver skates one before the other in a straight line, then swiftly got down low, holding her hands out for balance, and zipped underneath the ice cutters’ arms.
paras.zh: 她滑近三个采冰人，把银色冰鞋一前一字排开成直线，随即迅速压低身子，张开双手保持平衡，从采冰人的胳膊底下嗖地钻了过去。

paras.en: The crowd went wild.
paras.zh: 人群沸腾了。

paras.en: Anna smiled and straightened, and didn’t notice for half a length that her hat had been knocked clean off her head. “Well!” cried Queen Iduna from her carriage seat.
paras.zh: 安娜笑着直起身，滑出半程都没注意到帽子已被整个撞飞了。“哎呀！”伊杜娜女王从马车座位上叫道。

paras.en: She had been peering out the window down at the skating race in the canal below, but now sat back in her seat, an expression very much like shock across her features. “I don’t know what to say.” Elsa clasped her gloved hands in her lap, and a chill wind seemed to blow about the carriage walls. “Elsa, darling, do look out the window and tell me if I’m seeing things.” Obediently, Elsa looked.
paras.zh: 她本一直从窗里俯看下方运河里的滑冰比赛，此刻却靠回座位，脸上是一副近乎震惊的表情。“我不知该说什么。”艾莎把戴手套的手交握在膝上，一阵寒风似乎在马车四壁间吹过。“艾莎，亲爱的，你看看窗外，告诉我我是不是看错了。”艾莎顺从地看去。

paras.en: It did not take long to catch sight of her sister, her auburn braids streaming behind her, flying around the racecourse in her commoner’s clothes. “I…” She didn’t know what to say. “I had no idea your sister could skate like that.
paras.zh: 没多久她就看到了妹妹，她红褐色的辫子在身后飘扬，穿着平民衣服在赛道上飞驰。“我……”她不知该说什么。“我没想到你妹妹能滑成这样。

paras.en: Did you?” Miserably, she nodded. “I’ve, um, been watching her.
paras.zh: 你呢？”她痛苦地点点头。“我，嗯，一直看着她。

paras.en: On the duck pond.” “The duck pond?” The queen shook her head in disbelief. “My goodness.” “Wait,” Elsa said. “You’re not mad?” Her mother chuckled. “Well, sneaking around the castle isn’t what I’d want my children to do.
paras.zh: 在鸭塘上。”“鸭塘上？”女王难以置信地摇头，“我的天。”“等等，”艾莎说，“你不生气？”母亲轻笑，“嗯，溜进溜出城堡不是我希望孩子们做的事。

paras.en: But I’m forced to admit you aren’t the only Arendellian royal children to have done it.
paras.zh: 但我不得不承认，你们不是唯一这么干过的阿伦黛尔王室孩子。

paras.en: I do wish she had asked me, though.” A cheer went up from the crowd.
paras.zh: 不过我倒真希望她先问过我。”人群中爆发出一阵欢呼。

paras.en: The race was over. “Is Anna in trouble?” Her mother looked sad. “We’re all in a bit of trouble, I think.
paras.zh: 比赛结束了。“安娜有麻烦吗？”母亲神色忧伤。“我想我们都有点麻烦。

paras.en: Anna for sneaking around, and your father and I for making her think she had to sneak.” And Elsa, too.
paras.zh: 安娜是因为溜进溜出，你父亲和我是因为让她觉得非溜不可。”艾莎也是。

paras.en: Elsa always, for her uncontrollable magic that was making the rest of it so very necessary. “I left her the skates, you know,” she confessed. “They’re from your old trunk.” Her mother nodded. “I see.
paras.zh: 艾莎永远都是，为了那不可控的魔法，才让其余一切都如此必要。“是我把冰鞋留给她的，你知道，”她坦白道，“就来自你的旧木箱。”母亲点点头。“我明白了。

paras.en: Well, I suppose we’ll have to have a talk with her when she gets back.
paras.zh: 嗯，我想等她回来，我们得和她谈谈。

paras.en: But for now, let her have her fun.” She notified the driver of the carriage that they wanted to return to the castle.
paras.zh: 不过现在，就让她玩个痛快吧。”她吩咐车夫，他们要回城堡了。

paras.en: Elsa took one final look out the window at the festival.
paras.zh: 艾莎最后一次从窗口望向节庆。

paras.en: Down on the ice, she saw the winner of the skating race—a young girl in a blue hat—but no sign of her own sister.
paras.zh: 冰面上，她看到滑冰赛的冠军——一个戴蓝帽子的年轻女孩——却不见自己妹妹的踪影。

paras.en: Knock knock! “Elsa?” Anna’s voice echoed down the hall. “Please, I know you’re in there.
paras.zh: 叩叩！“艾莎？”安娜的声音在走廊里回荡，“求你了，我知道你在里面。

paras.en: Don’t you want to hear about my day?” No answer, as usual.
paras.zh: 你不想听听我今天的事吗？”没有回答，一如往常。

paras.en: But Anna was too excited to care.
paras.zh: 可安娜太兴奋了，顾不上在意。

paras.en: She started telling Elsa’s door the entire story.
paras.zh: 她开始对着艾莎的门讲起整件事。

paras.en: The shepherd children she’d met, the trick she’d learned to pass the racers who were blocking her, the loss of her hat.
paras.zh: 她遇见的牧羊孩子，她学来超过挡路选手的窍门，还有她丢了帽子的事。

paras.en: She told her sister all about it. “Oh, Elsa, it was amazing.
paras.zh: 她全讲给妹妹听了。“噢，艾莎，太了不起了。

paras.en: I wish you could have seen it.” It would have been like the old days, when the two of them had run all over the castle without a care in the world.
paras.zh: 真希望你当时能看到。”那会像从前那些日子，她俩满城堡乱跑，无忧无虑。

paras.en: Like Trygve and Nora did, up the fjord on their little sheep farm.
paras.zh: 就像特里格维和诺拉在峡湾上游的小羊场上那样。

paras.en: Like siblings were supposed to. “Anyway…” Anna went on. “I… um… I brought you something.
paras.zh: 就像兄弟姐妹本该有的样子。“总之……”安娜接着说，“我……嗯……我给你带了点东西。

paras.en: From the festival.” She put her skates down by the door and, from her pocket, drew out a little packet wrapped in brown paper.
paras.zh: 从节庆上带的。”她把冰鞋放在门边，又从口袋里掏出一个用牛皮纸包着的小包。

paras.en: Delicious smells wafted up from the contents. “It’s a little squashed now,” she admitted. “But… oh, Elsa, won’t you please open the door?” And there was still no answer.
paras.zh: 里面飘出诱人的香气。“现在有点压扁了，”她承认，“可是……噢，艾莎，你开开门好不好？”依然没有回答。

paras.en: None at all.
paras.zh: 一点都没有。

paras.en: Anna bit her lip, and her eyes stung with unshed tears.
paras.zh: 安娜咬住嘴唇，眼中噙着未落的泪。

paras.en: Just for once, she wanted her sister to play with her.
paras.zh: 哪怕就这一次，她想让妹妹陪她玩。

paras.en: Just for once, she wanted them to be happy together, like sisters. “It’s chocolate,” she said weakly.
paras.zh: 哪怕就这一次，她想让她们像姐妹一样一起快乐。“是巧克力，”她无力地说。

paras.en: Nothing.
paras.zh: 没有回应。

paras.en: All at once, her anger flared.
paras.zh: 忽然，她的怒火窜了上来。

paras.en: Maybe Elsa didn’t care.
paras.zh: 也许艾莎根本不在乎。

paras.en: Down below, in the Great Hall, the doors to the castle opened.
paras.zh: 下方的大厅里，城堡的门开了。

paras.en: From far away, the voice of a royal guard called, “Her Majesty, Queen Iduna.” Anna startled.
paras.zh: 远处传来一名皇家卫兵的声音：“伊杜娜女王陛下驾到。”安娜吓了一跳。

paras.en: Oh no, her mother couldn’t see her like this!
paras.zh: 噢不，母亲不能看到她这副模样！

paras.en: She dashed back down the hall to her room—forgetting entirely that her skates and the pastry were still on the floor by the door.
paras.zh: 她沿走廊冲回自己房间——完全忘了冰鞋和点心还放在门边的地板上。

paras.en: The first thing Elsa saw when she returned to her room was the pair of skates and the crumpled pastry lying outside her door.
paras.zh: 艾莎回到房间时，第一眼看到的就是门外地上那双冰鞋和压皱了的点心。

paras.en: Her mother pursed her lips. “It’s possible your sister understands what happened far more than you are giving her credit for.” “Chocolate,” Elsa said wistfully, picking up the items.
paras.zh: 母亲抿起嘴唇。“你妹妹对发生的事，可能比你想的明白得多。”“巧克力，”艾莎若有所思地拿起那些东西。

paras.en: Anna had even remembered that it was her favorite.
paras.zh: 安娜甚至还记得那是她的最爱。

paras.en: Nevertheless, a crown princess of Arendelle could hardly eat floor pastry.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，阿伦黛尔的王储公主可不能去吃地上的点心。

paras.en: She opened the door to her bedroom and dropped the pastry into the waste bin.
paras.zh: 她打开卧室门，把点心丢进了废纸篓。

paras.en: Such a disappointment.
paras.zh: 真叫人失望。

paras.en: Like so many other things.
paras.zh: 就像那么多别的事一样。

paras.en: Her mother followed her inside, holding the skates. “Oh, what to do,” she said, shaking her head ruefully. “Mother,” Elsa said. “Don’t punish Anna.
paras.zh: 母亲拿着冰鞋跟了进来。“噢，该怎么办呢，”她懊恼地摇头说。“母亲，”艾莎说，“别罚安娜。

paras.en: I feel responsible.
paras.zh: 我觉得我有责任。

paras.en: If I’d never given her the skates—” “Acting like a queen already?” Iduna replied. “You remind me so much of your father.
paras.zh: 要不是我给了她冰鞋——”“已经做起女王派头了？”伊杜娜答道，“你真像你父亲。

paras.en: You are not responsible for every choice another person makes, whether it’s your subject or your sister.
paras.zh: 你不必为别人做的每个选择负责，无论是你的臣民还是你妹妹。

paras.en: Anna chose to sneak into the village.
paras.zh: 安娜是自己选择溜进村子的。

paras.en: That was not your idea.” “But she never would have had to if…” Elsa trailed off and clasped her gloved hands behind her back.
paras.zh: 那不是你的主意。”“可要不是……她根本不必这样……”艾莎声音低下去，把戴手套的手背到身后。

paras.en: They all knew why.
paras.zh: 他们都心知肚明为什么。

paras.en: Her mother got that patient, sad look on her face again.
paras.zh: 母亲脸上又浮现出那种耐心而忧伤的神情。

paras.en: The one Elsa felt like the cold in her bones. “Perhaps our rules have been a little too harsh,” her mother said. “Neither of you girls should be spending so much time alone.” It was true.
paras.zh: 那种神情让艾莎从骨子里感到冷。“也许我们的规矩太严了些，”母亲说，“你们两个女孩都不该独处这么久。”的确如此。

paras.en: Elsa could not stop smiling at the memory of her sister racing around that canal on the silver skates.
paras.zh: 一想起妹妹穿着银色冰鞋绕运河飞驰的模样，艾莎就忍不住微笑。

paras.en: The sight was the most delightful thing she’d seen in—well—years.
paras.zh: 那景象是她多年来——嗯——见过最叫人欢喜的事。

paras.en: It warmed her heart like spring.
paras.zh: 它像春天一样温暖了她的心。

paras.en: She had done that.
paras.zh: 那是她带来的。

paras.en: She had brought that joy to her sister’s life.
paras.zh: 是她把这份欢乐带进了妹妹的生活。

paras.en: It was like the old days, when she and Anna would run all over the castle, delighting in her magic without a care in the world.
paras.zh: 就像从前那些日子，她和安娜满城堡乱跑，沉浸在她的魔法里，无忧无虑。

paras.en: She wished it could always be this way.
paras.zh: 她希望永远能这样。

paras.en: She wished she would learn to master her magic.
paras.zh: 她希望自己能学会驾驭魔法。

paras.en: Then she and Anna could always be together.
paras.zh: 那样她和安娜就能永远在一起。

paras.en: Her mother seemed to understand that, too.
paras.zh: 母亲似乎也明白这一点。

paras.en: She reached her hand out and cupped Elsa’s cheek. “I’ll talk to your father and find a way,” she promised Elsa. “Soon.” Iduna turned to go, and as she opened the door to Elsa’s bedroom she saw Anna lurking in the hall.
paras.zh: 她伸出手，捧住艾莎的脸颊。“我会和你父亲谈谈，想个办法，”她向艾莎许诺，“很快。”伊杜娜转身要走，打开艾莎卧室门时，看见安娜正鬼鬼祟祟地站在走廊里。

paras.en: Elsa peeked out around her mother’s form.
paras.zh: 艾莎从母亲身侧探出头去。

paras.en: Anna’s braids were still a mess.
paras.zh: 安娜的辫子还是乱糟糟的。

paras.en: Her gown was buttoned all wrong. “Mother!
paras.zh: 她的礼服扣得乱七八糟。“母亲！

paras.en: You’re home!” Anna exclaimed in a tone that wouldn’t have fooled a particularly dim reindeer. “I’ve been alone in my room all day.
paras.zh: 你回来啦！”安娜用一种连最迟钝的驯鹿都骗不过的语气惊叫，“我一整天都独自待在房间里。

paras.en: Reading.” “Oh, really,” her mother said. “I’m just back from the winter festival.
paras.zh: 看书呢。”“噢，真的吗，”母亲说，“我刚从冬日节庆回来。

paras.en: There was an exhilarating skating race.” She gave one last knowing glance back at Elsa.
paras.zh: 那有场激动人心的滑冰赛。”她回头意味深长地看了艾莎最后一眼。

paras.en: Elsa wanted to sink into the floorboards.
paras.zh: 艾莎恨不得钻进地板缝里。

paras.en: She felt the temperature drop around her.
paras.zh: 艾莎感到周围的气温降了下去。

paras.en: But across the threshold she met Anna’s eyes, brilliant green, defiant.
paras.zh: 可隔着门槛，她迎上了安娜那双明亮的绿眼睛，眼里满是倔强。

paras.en: If there was one thing to know about Anna, it was that she never gave up. “I wouldn’t know anything about that,” Anna said. “You know I can’t skate.”
paras.zh: 若说安娜有一点最该让人记住，那就是她永不放弃。“那种事我可一点都不知道，”安娜说，“你知道的，我不会滑冰。”

paras.en: Please join us for a ROYAL ENGAGEMENT PARTY* honoring Queen Anna of Arendelle & Kristoff Bjorgman o f Troll Valley Given, with Love, by Queen Elsa and Olaf & Bulda and Cliff This Saturday at Sunset the Arendelle Castle Courtyard Psst… it’s a surprise!
paras.zh: 诚邀您参加一场皇家订婚派对*，致敬阿伦黛尔的安娜女王与巨魔谷的克里斯托夫·比约格曼。由艾莎女王、雪宝、以及布达与克利夫满怀爱意呈献。本周六日落时分，阿伦黛尔城堡庭院。嘘……这是个惊喜！

paras.en: Don’t tell Anna and Kristoff! *Throwing a party?
paras.zh: 千万别告诉安娜和克里斯托夫！*要办派对吗？

paras.en: Hire Oaken’s Hearty Party-Planning Service… and Sauna—we’re here for all your party-planning (and sauna) needs!
paras.zh: 请聘用奥肯的“热忱派对策划服务……兼桑拿”——您所有的派对策划（及桑拿）需求，我们统统包办！

paras.en: FOUR HOURS BEFORE THE PARTY “I can’t believe you’re here!” Anna yelled to Elsa, rushing down the castle hallway.
paras.zh: 派对前四小时 “真不敢相信你来了！”安娜冲着艾莎大喊，沿着城堡走廊飞奔而去。

paras.en: She held her tiara with one hand and her skirt with the other, revealing the sensible boots she was wearing underneath a green-and-cream silk ball gown. “This is such a nice surprise.” “That’s me—full of surprises,” Elsa said softly, maintaining a small smile—one that she hoped didn’t appear too excited yet didn’t make it seem like she wasn’t happy to see her sister, either.
paras.zh: 她一只手扶着王冠，另一只手提起裙摆，露出了绿色与米色相间的丝绸礼服下那双实用的靴子。“这真是个好惊喜。”“这就是我嘛——满身惊喜。”艾莎轻声说道，保持着一丝微笑——她希望那笑容既不过于激动，又不至于让人觉得她见到妹妹不高兴。

paras.en: Her fingers tingled. “I thought you weren’t coming till the Yule Bell celebration next week,” Anna cheered, running faster to meet her. “I thought we could start the holiday celebrations early,” Elsa said simply. “Early sounds good to me!” Anna ran at Elsa full force, practically knocking her over with the weight of her hug.
paras.zh: 她的指尖微微发麻。“我还以为你要到下周的尤尔钟庆典才回来呢，”安娜欢呼着，跑得更快去迎接她。“我想我们不妨提早开始过节，”艾莎淡淡地说。“提早挺好！”安娜全力冲向艾莎，那一抱几乎把她撞倒。

paras.en: Elsa and Anna agreed: Arendelle was never more beautiful than it was during the holidays.
paras.zh: 艾莎和安娜一致认为：阿伦黛尔最美的时候，莫过于节日期间。

paras.en: The ceremonial ringing of the Yule Bell kicked off the festivities that included everything from families putting out the porridge for the tomte and rolling lefse for their parties to knitting socks for presents.
paras.zh: 尤尔钟的鸣响拉开了庆祝活动的序幕，内容包罗万象——从各家各户为“小地精”摆出粥食、为派对擀制薄饼，到织袜子当礼物，应有尽有。

paras.en: A highlight was always the Polar Nights Festival, which seemed to get bigger every year.
paras.zh: 其中的重头戏永远是极夜节，而且似乎一年比一年盛大。

paras.en: But this year the kingdom had another reason to celebrate—Anna and Kristoff’s engagement.
paras.zh: 但今年王国还有另一桩喜事要庆祝——安娜与克里斯托夫的订婚。

paras.en: Elsa knew that, after so many years of closed gates and lonely milestones, Anna would love a party.
paras.zh: 艾莎知道，在经历了多年闭门谢客与形单影只的过往后，安娜一定会喜欢一场派对。

paras.en: Kristoff maybe not so much, but he’d survive.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫或许没那么热衷，但他总能撑过去。

paras.en: He’d do anything for her sister.
paras.zh: 为了妹妹，他什么都愿意做。

paras.en: And so Elsa had decided to throw a surprise party, inviting Bulda and the rest of the trolls to help her.
paras.zh: 于是艾莎决定办一场惊喜派对，并邀请布达和其他地精来帮忙。

paras.en: The details had been coming together beautifully.
paras.zh: 各项细节都安排得美轮美奂。

paras.en: The only issue?
paras.zh: 唯一的问题呢？

paras.en: Keeping the happy couple from finding out.
paras.zh: 就是别让这对幸福的恋人发现。

paras.en: Elsa had an idea on how to keep Kristoff in the dark, but Anna was the tricky one.
paras.zh: 艾莎已有办法瞒住克里斯托夫，可安娜才是难对付的那个。

paras.en: Her sister—how did she put it delicately?—could be a bit curious?
paras.zh: 她妹妹——该怎么委婉地说呢？——是不是有点好奇心太重？

paras.en: Intuitive?
paras.zh: 太敏锐？

paras.en: Nosy? “You said you had too much work this week to get back to the castle early to help us decorate,” Anna said, squeezing Elsa tight. “Those were your exact words.” In a nearby open doorway, Elsa saw a distinct shadow—one that consisted of an oval-shaped snowball head and a blocky snowball body—watching them. “I got done early,” Elsa murmured into Anna’s hair, which smelled like chocolate and pine needles and reminded her of home. “I couldn’t miss hanging ornaments on all the trees.” Anna pulled away, still beaming. “I told everyone to leave the big tree in our parlor bare so we could decorate it together with Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf.” She bit her lip. “The rest of the castle is decorated, though.
paras.zh: 多管闲事？“你说过这周工作太忙，没法提前回城堡帮我们布置，”安娜紧紧搂着艾莎说，“你原话就是这么说的。”在旁边一扇敞开的门洞里，艾莎看到一个清晰的影子——一个鹅蛋形雪球脑袋配上方块状雪球身子的影子——正望着她们。“我提前忙完了，”艾莎把脸埋进安娜的头发里低声说，那发丝带着巧克力和松针的香气，让她想起家的味道。“我可不能错过给所有树上挂装饰。”安娜抽身退开，依旧笑逐颜开。“我让大家都别动客厅那棵大树，好让咱们和克里斯托夫、斯文、雪宝一起装饰它。”她咬了咬嘴唇。“不过城堡其他地方都已经布置好了。”

paras.en: If I had known you were coming, I would have waited.” Elsa had been hoping decorations would be up.
paras.zh: “要是我知道你要来，我就等你也一起了。”艾莎其实正盼着装饰已经布置好。

paras.en: She looked around the hallway: boughs of garland were draped over windows, and wreaths hung on every door.
paras.zh: 她环顾走廊：窗台上垂挂着花环枝条，每扇门上都挂着花圈。

paras.en: Elsa knew when she walked through each room, including her own bedroom, she’d find a tree decorated with handmade ornaments, some of which she and Anna had made as small children before… well, she didn’t like to think about “after” that much.
paras.zh: 艾莎知道，当她走过每个房间——包括自己的卧室——都会看到一棵装饰着手工艺品的小树，其中一些是她与安娜幼年时所做，在那……嗯，她不太愿意多想“那之后”的事。

paras.en: The present was much happier, and she was determined to pull out all the stops to celebrate this new chapter in her sister’s life.
paras.zh: 当下要快乐得多，她下定决心要全力以赴，庆祝妹妹人生中崭新的这一章。

paras.en: She knew Bulda, who adored “her boy” Kristoff, felt the same way. “It looks beautiful, which is good, because… well…” Elsa hesitated.
paras.zh: 她知道，宠爱“自家小伙子”克里斯托夫的布达，也有着同样的感受。“真漂亮，这很好，因为……那个……”艾莎犹豫了一下。

paras.en: Anna picked up on her tone right away, firing off a slew of thoughts all at once. “I knew you had a reason for being here early!
paras.zh: 安娜立刻听出了她的语气，一股脑儿倒出了一连串想法。“我就知道你提前来是有原因的！”

paras.en: What’s going on?
paras.zh: 到底怎么回事？

paras.en: You can talk to me about anything, you know.” Elsa looked around before leaning in close. “I’m here because the trolls have a surprise for Kristoff and need our help pulling it off.” Anna squeezed Elsa’s hand, making the tingling sensation stop. “A surprise for Kristoff?
paras.zh: “什么事你都可以跟我说，你知道的。”艾莎左右张望后凑近低语。“我来是因为地精们要给克里斯托夫一个惊喜，需要咱们帮忙办成。”安娜攥紧艾莎的手，那阵发麻的感觉也随之消失。“给克里斯托夫的惊喜？”

paras.en: What is it?
paras.zh: 是什么惊喜？

paras.en: How do you know about this?
paras.zh: 你怎么会知道这事？

paras.en: Why don’t I know about this?
paras.zh: 怎么我一点都不知道？

paras.en: Tell me everything!
paras.zh: 全都告诉我！

paras.en: How can I help?” Elsa spoke in a conspiratorial tone. “I stopped in to see the trolls in the Valley of the Living Rock the other day, and Bulda and Cliff told me today is the tenth anniversary of Kristoff starting his official ice harvesting business.” Anna gasped. “Kristoff didn’t tell me that.
paras.zh: “我能帮什么忙？”艾莎用神秘兮兮的语气说。“前两天我顺道去看了生命之石山谷里的地精，布达和克利夫告诉我，今天是克里斯托夫正式经营采冰生意十周年的日子。”安娜倒吸一口凉气。“克里斯托夫可没告诉过我。”

paras.en: Neither did Sven!
paras.zh: 斯文也没说！

paras.en: I mean, it makes sense—I know Kristoff started delivering ice in his teens, but I had no idea he had a big anniversary coming up.” She frowned. “Now I feel terrible.
paras.zh: “我是说，这也说得通——我知道克里斯托夫十几岁就开始送冰了，但我完全没料到他还有个大纪念日临近。”她皱起眉头。“现在我觉得糟透了。”

paras.en: I must be the worst fiancée ever.” This was taking a turn Elsa had not prepared for. “Not true!
paras.zh: “我一定是史上最差劲的未婚妻。”这走向可不在艾莎的预料之中。“才不是！”

paras.en: You’re the best fiancée!
paras.zh: “你是最棒的未婚妻！”

paras.en: You know how Kristoff is.
paras.zh: “你又不是不了解克里斯托夫。”

paras.en: He’d never brag about himself like that.” She thought for a moment. “Although Sven might.” “Sven would,” Anna agreed. “We have to do something.” “I knew you’d say that, which is why I told Bulda and the trolls you’d throw a small party here.
paras.zh: “他绝不会那样自夸。”她想了想。“不过斯文也许会。”“斯文会说的，”安娜表示同意。“我们得做点什么。”“我就知道你会这么说，所以才告诉布达和地精们，你会在城堡里办一场小派对。”

paras.en: At the castle.
paras.zh: “就在城堡里。”

paras.en: Tonight.” Anna looked panicked, as Elsa knew she would. “But not to worry.
paras.zh: “今晚。”安娜露出艾莎预料中的惊慌神色。“不过别担心。”

paras.en: I’ve taken care of all the details already.
paras.zh: “所有细节我都已经安排妥当了。”

paras.en: All you need to do is keep Kristoff busy this afternoon so we can set up.
paras.zh: “你只需要今天下午拖住克里斯托夫，好让我们布置现场。”

paras.en: You can bring him back around sunset.” “I can do that,” Anna said excitedly. “Elsa, you’re the best sister ever.
paras.zh: “日落时分你再带他回来就行。”“这我能做到，”安娜兴奋地说，“艾莎，你真是全世界最好的姐姐。”

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: “谢谢你。”

paras.en: How did you have the time to plan a whole party?” Elsa saw the snowman shadow start to dance. “Oh, I had some help.
paras.zh: “你哪来的时间策划一整场派对？”艾莎看到那个雪人影子开始手舞足蹈。“噢，我有人帮忙。”

paras.en: Do you think you can get away from your duties to keep Kristoff distracted?” “Not a problem,” Anna told her, fixing her eyes on Elsa. “All my meetings today were canceled.
paras.zh: “你觉得你能从公务中抽身，去拖住克里斯托夫吗？”“没问题，”安娜盯着艾莎说，“我今天所有的会议都取消了。”

paras.en: Apparently, there is a cold going around.
paras.zh: “显然，最近好像在流行感冒。”

paras.en: Even the Vesterland dinner we were supposed to host tonight had to be postponed because Mari was under the weather, too.” “You don’t say.” Elsa predicted they’d all have a miraculous recovery right around the time printed on the invitation. “It’s a shame, because Olina has been cooking and baking all morning.” Anna sniffed the air. “I can smell the chocolate and butter from here.” She brightened. “Hey.
paras.zh: “就连我们今晚本该主办的维斯特兰晚宴也不得不推迟，因为玛丽也身体不适。”“不会吧。”艾莎料到，他们大概都会在请柬上印的时辰前后奇迹般康复。“真可惜，因为奥丽娜一上午都在做饭烘焙。”安娜嗅了嗅空气。“我在这儿都能闻到巧克力和黄油的香味。”她眼睛一亮。“嘿。”

paras.en: Maybe you can use whatever Olina made for the party.” Elsa suppressed the urge to laugh. “Great idea.
paras.zh: “也许你能把奥丽娜做的东西用在派对上。”艾莎强忍住笑意。“好主意。”

paras.en: I’ll ask her.” Anna thought for a moment. “I just need to think of a reason to get Kristoff out of the castle.” Elsa tried to play it cool. “I already thought of one.
paras.zh: “我去问问她。”安娜想了想。“我只需要想个理由把克里斯托夫弄出城堡。”艾莎故作淡定。“我已经想好一个了。”

paras.en: Tell him you need to pick up some cookies for a special holiday-themed game night we’re going to have since I’m here early.” Elsa pulled a list out of her pocket.
paras.zh: “告诉他，因为我提前回来了，我们要办一场特别的节日主题游戏之夜，你需要去取些饼干。”艾莎从口袋里掏出一张单子。

paras.en: Anna read it over and paused. “You ordered seven different types of cookies and pastries from seven different bakeries and villagers?” “Having the seven cookies of Arendelle at a gathering is a holiday tradition,” Elsa reminded her. “The more stops you make, the longer you keep Kristoff busy.
paras.zh: 安娜把单子看了一遍，顿了顿。“你从七家不同的面包店和村民那里订了七种不同口味的饼干和糕点？”“聚会上备齐阿伦黛尔的七款饼干是节日传统，”艾莎提醒她，“你跑的店越多，拖住克里斯托夫的时间就越长。”

paras.en: Plus, I knew you wouldn’t want to leave any of the kingdom’s bakers off the list.” “True.
paras.zh: “而且我知道，你肯定不想把王国里任何一位面包师漏在名单外。”“没错。”

paras.en: Guess we’ll be doing a lot of taste-testing along the way,” Anna said resolutely as the clock in the village began to toll. “You can count on us.” The snowman shadow around the corner continued to dance around.
paras.zh: “看来这一路上咱们得好好试吃一番了，”安娜坚定地说，这时村中的钟声敲响。“交给我们吧。”角落里的雪人影子继续转着圈跳舞。

paras.en: Anna started to walk backward. “I’ll just go change out of this gown, get Kristoff, and then we’ll be out of your hair.” The shadow stopped dancing. “Don’t change!” Elsa blurted out, and Anna faltered. “I mean, you look lovely.
paras.zh: 安娜开始倒退着走。“我去换掉这身礼服，叫上克里斯托夫，就不打扰你了。”影子停下了舞步。“别换！”艾莎脱口而出，安娜踉跄了一下。“我是说，你这样很好看。”

paras.en: And besides, cookie taste-testing is kind of official queen business.
paras.zh: “再说了，试吃饼干也算得上半桩女王公务。”

paras.en: You want to look your best.” Anna grinned. “What would I do without you?
paras.zh: “你当然得保持最佳形象。”安娜咧嘴一笑。“没有你，我可怎么办？”

paras.en: I’ll go call on Kristoff and be right back!” As Anna ran in one direction, Elsa realized Kristoff was making his way down the hall from the other direction with Sven.
paras.zh: “我去找克里斯托夫，马上回来！”安娜朝一个方向跑去，艾莎却发现克里斯托夫正带着斯文从走廊另一头走来。

paras.en: Elsa tried to block Anna’s retreating figure from view.
paras.zh: 艾莎试图挡住安娜离去的身影，不让对方看到。

paras.en: Kristoff had on a blue dress coat and a white shirt that he seemed to find too tight around the collar.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫穿着一件蓝色礼服外套和一件白衬衫，那衬衫的领口似乎让他觉得太紧了。

paras.en: His hair was even slicked back and tamed.
paras.zh: 他的头发甚至被抹平梳到了脑后，服服帖帖。

paras.en: Elsa tried not to laugh at the sight of her sister’s fiancé all dressed up. “Can’t believe all our deliveries were canceled today,” Kristoff said in his Sven voice. “Good thing Olina took all our ice deliveries for that Vesterland dinner she said we’re having tonight,” Kristoff told Sven. “There’s nothing worse than wasted ice.” Kristoff saw Elsa and smiled. “Elsa, hi!
