paras.zh: 艾莎看着妹妹的未婚夫这身盛装，差点笑出声。“真不敢相信今天所有的配送都取消了，”克里斯托夫用他扮斯文的嗓音说。“还好奥丽娜接手了咱们所有送冰的活儿，好让她说的今晚那场维斯特兰晚宴用得上，”克里斯托夫对斯文说，“没有比糟蹋冰更糟的事了。”克里斯托夫看到艾莎，笑了。“艾莎，嗨！”

paras.en: I thought you weren’t coming back till next week.” “Surprise,” Elsa said, and saw the snowman shadow in the doorway start to boogie. “You’re just the person I was looking for, too.” “Me?” Kristoff looked surprised. “I was hoping you could help me with a surprise for Anna,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: “我还以为你要到下周才回来呢。”“惊喜吧，”艾莎说，同时看到门口的雪人影子开始摇摆起舞。“你正好也是我在找的人。”“我？”克里斯托夫一脸惊讶。“我正希望你能帮我给安娜准备一个惊喜呢，”艾莎说。

paras.en: Kristoff’s cheeks reddened at the name of his fiancée. “I’d do anything for Anna.
paras.zh: 一听到未婚妻的名字，克里斯托夫的脸就红了。“为了安娜，我什么都愿意做。”

paras.en: What do you need?” “I was hoping you and Sven could keep her away from the castle this afternoon so I can set up a spa retreat for her,” Elsa told him, putting a cool hand on his shoulder. “She’s been working so hard, I thought she could use some pampering.” “That’s a great idea,” Kristoff said. “I knew you’d agree.” Elsa smiled. “The stewards are going to set up a room for her to relax in with lots of aromatherapy and a massage treatment.
paras.zh: “需要我做什么？”“我希望你和斯文今天下午能把她带离城堡，好让我为她布置一处水疗休憩所，”艾莎说着，把一只凉凉的手搭在他肩上。“她工作太辛苦了，我想她该好好享受一番宠爱。”“这主意太棒了，”克里斯托夫说。“我就知道你会同意。”艾莎微笑。“侍从们会布置一个房间让她放松，有好多芳香疗法和按摩护理。”

paras.en: All we need is some time to set everything up.
paras.zh: “我们只需一些时间来布置好一切。”

paras.en: Do you think you can keep Anna distracted?” “Sure,” Kristoff said without hesitation, “if she doesn’t have meetings.” Elsa cut him off. “All canceled.
paras.zh: “你觉得你能拖住安娜吗？”“当然，”克里斯托夫毫不犹豫地说，“只要她没有会议。”艾莎打断他。“全取消了。”

paras.en: There’s a cold going around.” She pulled another slip of paper out of her pocket. “All you need to do is tell Anna you guys have to make seven stops this afternoon to seven bakeries to—” “Pick up the traditional seven holiday cookies and pastries?” Kristoff guessed. “One of Sven’s and my favorite Arendelle traditions.” He nudged the reindeer. “Am I right?” “I just wish one of the baked goods was carrot cake,” Kristoff said for Sven, and the reindeer nodded. “Well, you can make that suggestion this afternoon when you visit all the shops and homes in the village,” Elsa said. “Tell Anna the cookies are for a taste-testing we’re all going to do at the Vesterland dinner tonight.
paras.zh: “最近在流行感冒。”她从口袋里又抽出一张纸条。“你只需要告诉安娜，你们今天下午得跑七家面包店、停七站去——”“去取传统的七款节日饼干和糕点？”克里斯托夫猜道。“这是我和斯文最喜欢的阿伦黛尔传统之一。”他轻轻碰了碰驯鹿。“我没猜错吧？”“我只希望其中一款点心是胡萝卜蛋糕，”克里斯托夫替斯文说道，驯鹿点了点头。“嗯，今天下午你们逛遍村里的店铺和人家时，可以提这个建议，”艾莎说，“告诉安娜这些饼干是用在今晚维斯特兰晚宴上大家一起试吃的。”

paras.en: The dinner will be right at sunset, so afterward, it’s all about pampering Anna.” “Great diversion,” Kristoff said confidentially. “She’ll jump at the chance to show off Arendelle’s baked goods.
paras.zh: “晚宴正好在日落时分，所以之后就全是宠爱安娜的时间了。”“绝妙的调虎离山，”克里斯托夫神神秘秘地说，“她一定会抓住机会炫耀阿伦黛尔的烘焙。”

paras.en: She and Mari seem to have some sort of competition going about the best cookie in the world.” “I’ve heard them debate that.” Elsa nodded. “So take your time.
paras.zh: “她和玛丽似乎在为‘世界上最好吃的饼干’较着劲。”“我听她们争辩过这个。”艾莎点了点头。“所以你们慢慢来。”

paras.en: Enjoy the village!
paras.zh: 好好逛逛村子！

paras.en: Sample some sweets!
paras.zh: 尝尝那些甜点！

paras.en: You can bring Anna back around sunset for the Vesterland dinner and then it’s on to her spa day.” Kristoff scratched his head. “Spa day ?” Elsa paused.
paras.zh: “日落时你带安娜回来参加维斯特兰晚宴，之后就进入她的水疗日。”克里斯托夫挠了挠头。“水疗日？”艾莎顿了顿。

paras.en: The snowman shadow stopped dancing again. “It’s more like a spa night.
paras.zh: 雪人影子又停下不跳了。“更像是水疗夜。”

paras.en: The evening is more relaxing anyway.” “That’s true,” Kristoff agreed. “I’ll just go change.
paras.zh: “反正晚上更让人放松。”“说得对，”克里斯托夫表示同意，“我去换身衣服。”

paras.en: Kai left this outfit out for me this morning.
paras.zh: “今天早上凯给我留了这身衣服。”

paras.en: Something about looking nice today.
paras.zh: “大概是说今天要穿得体面些。”

paras.en: The shirt is pretty constricting.” He pulled at the tight collar around his neck. “You know what?
paras.zh: “这衬衫实在勒得慌。”他扯了扯勒着脖子的紧领口。“你知道吗？”

paras.en: I think you should stay in that outfit,” Elsa said quickly. “Anna will be all dressed up since cookie sampling is official business.
paras.zh: “我觉得你就穿这身吧，”艾莎连忙说，“安娜会盛装出席，毕竟试吃饼干是公务。”

paras.en: You are her consort, after all.” Kristoff sighed and pulled at his shirt again. “Fine.
paras.zh: “毕竟你是她的配偶嘛。”克里斯托夫叹了口气，又扯了扯衬衫。“好吧。”

paras.en: But only because this is for Anna.
paras.zh: “只因为这是为了安娜。”

paras.en: She could use a relaxing night off.” He looked around. “I just have to find her.” “No need,” Elsa said, as Anna came running back around the corner. “There you are!” Anna said to Kristoff, eyeing Elsa as if the two were in on a big secret.
paras.zh: “她正需要这样一个放松的夜晚歇一歇。”他四下张望。“我得先找到她。”“不用了，”艾莎说，这时安娜正好从拐角跑回来。“你在这儿！”安娜对克里斯托夫说，同时用眼角瞟着艾莎，仿佛两人正共守着一个大秘密。

paras.en: Kristoff, ironically, gave Elsa the same look. “I was just coming to find you.” “Really?
paras.zh: “我正要去找你呢。”“真的？”

paras.en: I was coming to find you ,” Anna said with a laugh. “I need you to help me—” “Pick up cookies from all the Arendelle shops and bakers?” Kristoff supplied. “Elsa already told me.
paras.zh: “我正要去找你呀，”安娜笑着说，“我需要你帮我去——”“去阿伦黛尔各家店铺和面包师那儿取饼干？”克里斯托夫接茬道，“艾莎已经跟我说了。”

paras.en: I am at your service.” Sven snorted and his ears perked up.
paras.zh: “听候差遣。”斯文喷了喷鼻息，耳朵竖了起来。

paras.en: He seemed to be looking right at Elsa as if he just knew something was going on.
paras.zh: 他似乎直直盯着艾莎，仿佛刚刚察觉到有什么不对劲。

paras.en: Elsa maintained her innocence and glanced out the nearest window at the clock in the square.
paras.zh: 艾莎装出一副无辜的样子，望向最近的窗户，看着广场上的大钟。时间正一分一秒地流逝。

paras.en: Time was ticking. “Well, now that you’re both here, and you both know what you need to do, you should get going.” Elsa pushed Anna and Kristoff toward each other and clasped their hands together. “See you both tonight!” Sven seemed to give Elsa a questioning look as the three headed down the hallway, with Kristoff and Anna debating the best cookie on their list.
paras.zh: “好了，既然你们俩都在这儿，也知道自己该干什么，就该出发了。”艾莎把安娜和克里斯托夫往彼此那边推了推，将他们的手合在一起。“今晚见！”三人沿着走廊走去，克里斯托夫和安娜还在争论单子上哪款饼干最好，斯文则似乎给了艾莎一个疑问的眼神。

paras.en: Olaf waited till the pair disappeared to pop his head out from the doorway. “I think Sven is on to you.” “You might be right, but the important thing is, Anna and Kristoff bought it.” Elsa opened the nearest window and called for Gale.
paras.zh: 雪宝等到那两人消失，才从门洞里探出脑袋。“我觉得斯文看穿你了。”“也许你说得对，但重要的是，安娜和克里斯托夫信了。”艾莎推开最近的窗户，呼唤盖尔。

paras.en: She held up a note that the Wind Spirit took. “Please let Bulda, Cliff, and the other trolls know we’re ready for them.
paras.zh: 她举起一张便条，风灵接了过去。“请转告布达、克利夫和其他地精，我们已经准备好了。”

paras.en: We have a lot to set up and not a lot of time to do it.” The Wind Spirit carried the note away. “Thanks, Gale!
paras.zh: “我们要布置的东西很多，时间却不多。”风灵带着便条飞走了。“谢谢你，盖尔！”

paras.en: Come along, everyone!” Olaf shouted. “Operation Anna and Kristoff’s Engagement Party is a Go!
paras.zh: “大家快跟上！”雪宝喊道，“‘安娜与克里斯托夫订婚派对行动’正式启动！”

paras.en: Go!
paras.zh: 出发！

paras.en: Go!” A flurry of castle staff and villagers came out of every closed door in the hallway.
paras.zh: 出发！走廊里每扇紧闭的门后，都涌出一拨城堡仆人和村民。

paras.en: Two stewards were carrying an ice sculpture of their queen and her ice man.
paras.zh: 两名侍从抬着一尊冰雕，雕的是他们的女王和她那位“冰人”。

paras.en: Several others had bouquets of crocuses, the official flower of Arendelle, while another group from Blodget’s Bakery carried trays of eplekake (apple cake was a favorite of both Anna’s and Kristoff’s, especially when served with caramel sauce and vanilla ice cream) and a chocolate cake she knew her sister would flip for.
paras.zh: 另一些人捧着阿伦黛尔的国花——番红花束；还有一队来自布洛杰特面包店的人，端着托盘装着苹果蛋糕（安娜和克里斯托夫都最爱苹果蛋糕，尤其配上焦糖酱和香草冰淇淋时）和一块巧克力蛋糕，她知道妹妹见了准会欣喜若狂。

paras.en: Olina was making King Agnarr’s favorite dry-rubbed roasted pork tenderloin, which Anna would love as a nod to their parents being part of the day.
paras.zh: 奥丽娜正在烹制安格瑞国王最爱的干腌烤猪里脊，安娜会喜欢这道菜，因为它也算是让父母参与了这一天。

paras.en: As far as Elsa could tell, everything was going as planned.
paras.zh: 在艾莎看来，一切都在按计划进行。

paras.en: She hoped. “Come on, Olaf.
paras.zh: 她希望如此。“快点儿，雪宝。”

paras.en: Let’s start decorating the courtyard.” “Ready!” Olaf clapped his stick arms together. “I love engagement parties!
paras.zh: “咱们开始布置庭院吧。”“准备好啦！”雪宝啪地拍了拍他的小树枝手臂。“我超爱订婚派对！”

paras.en: I don’t think I’ve ever been to one before, but I already know I’m going to like them.
paras.zh: “我想我以前从没参加过订婚派对，但我已经知道自己会喜欢上它们。”

paras.en: Especially since this one is a surprise.” “Olaf, it is still a surprise, right?” Elsa asked gently. “Anna doesn’t know anything, does she?” “Nope!” Olaf said. “You only told me an hour ago.” An hour, Elsa had learned, was still a long time for a snowman to keep a secret. “Just checking,” Elsa said. “Remember: your job is to be on the lookout for Anna and Kristoff.” “I will keep my eyes peeled!” Olaf promised. “For now, all I see is our party planner.” “Hoo-hoo!” said someone with a familiar accent.
paras.zh: 尤其这场还是惊喜派对。“雪宝，这还是个惊喜，对吧？”艾莎温和地问，“安娜什么都不知道，是吧？”“不知道！”雪宝说，“你才一个小时前告诉我。”艾莎已经领教到，对雪人来说，一个小时守住秘密也够漫长了。“我只是确认一下，”艾莎说，“记住：你的任务就是留意安娜和克里斯托夫的动向。”“我会瞪大眼睛盯着！”雪宝保证道。“眼下我看到的只有咱们的派对策划人。”“嗬——嗬！”一个带着熟悉口音的声音响起。

paras.en: The giant of a man approaching had red hair and was wearing a green beanie and a matching green sweater that had the word ENGAGED knitted on the front along with images of Anna and Kristoff. “We don’t have much time, ja?
paras.zh: 走过来的是个巨人般的汉子，一头红发，戴着绿色毛线帽，穿着配套的绿色毛衣，胸前织着“订婚”二字，还有安娜和克里斯托夫的图案。“咱们时间不多了，是吧？”

paras.en: We have to move quick.” It was Oaken, or in this case, Oaken of Oaken’s Hearty Party-Planning Service… and Sauna.
paras.zh: “得动作快。”来者是奥肯，或者更准确地说，是“奥肯热忱派对策划服务……兼桑拿”的奥肯。

paras.en: Elsa had no idea Oaken even did party planning, but when she and Kristoff’s family had started thinking about how to toast the happy couple, Oaken had appeared out of nowhere.
paras.zh: 艾莎根本不知道奥肯还干派对策划这行，但当她和克里斯托夫的家人开始琢磨如何为这对新人庆贺时，奥肯凭空冒了出来。

paras.en: So had his sauna.
paras.zh: 他的桑拿房也是。

paras.en: In fact, right at that moment, two men came around a corner rolling a rectangular sauna that was no bigger than a closet. “Oaken, why would we need a sauna at the party?” Elsa asked. “Everyone likes a good schvitz,” Oaken said. “I love a good schvitz!” Olaf agreed. “Although a schvitz doesn’t always agree with me.” Elsa held her head.
paras.zh: 事实上就在此刻，两名男子推着一只矩形桑拿房从拐角转出来，那玩意儿还没个壁橱大。“奥肯，派对上为什么需要桑拿？”艾莎问。“谁都爱痛快地蒸一把，”奥肯说。“我就爱痛快地蒸一把！”雪宝附和。“虽说蒸桑拿并不总是对我胃口。”艾莎扶住了额头。

paras.en: This was going to be a long four hours.
paras.zh: 看来这四个小时会很难熬。

paras.en: THREE AND A HALF HOURS TILL THE PARTY “Let’s go eat some cookies!” Anna cheered as Sven pulled their sled out of the castle and into the snowy streets. “Where should we go first?” “Maybe the farthest location?” Kristoff suggested.
paras.zh: 距派对还有三个半小时 “去吃饼干啦！”安娜欢呼着，斯文把雪橇拉出城堡，驶上积雪的街道。“咱们先去哪家？”

paras.en: He was starting to sweat at the thought of keeping Anna distracted for hours without letting anything slip. “No need to rush back to the castle when it’s such a nice day.” They both looked up.
paras.zh: “去最远的怎么样？”克里斯托夫提议。

paras.en: The Arendelle sky was its typical wintry self: gray and a bit windy.
paras.zh: 一想到要拖住安娜好几小时还不能露馅，他已经开始冒汗了。“这么好的天气，不必急着回城堡嘛。”两人一起抬头望去。

paras.en: Neither acknowledged the lack of sunshine. “Let me look at the list Elsa gave me and see where the farthest bakery is,” Anna said, pulling her paper out at the same time as Kristoff pulled out his list. “Elsa made you a list, too?” “Yeah.” Kristoff looked confused. “She gave you one, too?” “Maybe in case one of us lost one?” Anna guessed.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔的天空一如往常的冬日模样：灰蒙蒙的，还带着点风。

paras.en: They put their heads together and looked at their stops.
paras.zh: 谁也没去提没有阳光这回事。“我看看艾莎给我的单子，最远的面包店在哪，”安娜说着，和克里斯托夫同时掏出了自己的纸条。“艾莎也给你列了单子？”“嗯。”克里斯托夫一脸茫然，“她也给你一份了？”“也许怕咱俩谁弄丢了一张？”安娜猜道。

paras.en: Pick up COOKIES AND BAKED GOODS today! 1.
paras.zh: 两人凑到一起，研究起各自的站点。

paras.en: Krumkaker from Blodget’s Bakery 2.
paras.zh: 今日领取饼干与烘焙点心！1.

paras.en: Bordstabelbakkels from Waffle Brothers 3.
paras.zh: 布洛杰特面包店的脆卷饼 2.

paras.en: Fattigmann from the Olsens 4.
paras.zh: 华夫兄弟的棋盘小饼 3.

paras.en: Sandkaker from the Haugens 5.
paras.zh: 奥尔森家的穷人饼 4.

paras.en: Sirupssnipper from Tomally’s Baked Goods 6.
paras.zh: 豪根家的沙饼 5.

paras.en: Berlinerkranser from the Bergs 7.
paras.zh: 托马利烘焙店的糖浆脆饼 6.

paras.en: Smultringer from Gerda “Wow, Arendelle has a lot of bakers,” Anna realized. “Tell me about it.
paras.zh: 伯格家的柏林花环饼 7.

paras.en: And they’re all over Arendelle.” He pointed to the last one on the list. “Our last stop is the castle.
paras.zh: 格尔达的炸面圈 “哇，阿伦黛尔的面包师真多，”安娜感叹，“可不是嘛。”

paras.en: Not that we should rush to get back,” Kristoff said. “Absolutely not,” Anna agreed hurriedly. “Taste-testing cookies takes time.” “Lots of time,” Kristoff agreed.
paras.zh: “而且遍布阿伦黛尔各地。”他指着单子上最后一家。“咱们最后一站就是城堡。”

paras.en: Sven made a strange noise, and Kristoff looked at him over the top of the sled. “Did you say something, buddy?” “Nope!” Kristoff said in his Sven voice.
paras.zh: “当然不是催咱们赶回去，”克里斯托夫说。“绝对不是，”安娜连忙附和，“试吃饼干很费时间的。”“很费时间，”克里斯托夫认同。

paras.en: Kristoff and Anna glanced at each other, then looked away.
paras.zh: 斯文发出一声怪响，克里斯托夫从雪橇上头探看过去。“你说话了，老伙计？”“没啊！”克里斯托夫用他的“斯文腔”说。

paras.en: Neither saw the other one gulp. “Tomally’s is the farthest stop,” Anna said, pointing to one of the bakeries on the list. “That’s all the way up in the mountains.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫和安娜对视一眼，又各自移开目光。

paras.en: How does Elsa even know about that place?” “I don’t know,” Kristoff realized. “Is that the one that makes the syrup snap snowman cookies?
paras.zh: 谁都没注意到对方咽了口唾沫。“托马利家是最远的一站，”安娜指着单子上一家面包店说，“那家在山里头。”

paras.en: I love those.” Anna heard Sven lick his lips. “Yep!
paras.zh: “艾莎怎么会知道那家店？”“我也不知道，”克里斯托夫这才反应过来，“那是不是做糖浆脆饼雪人饼干的那家？”

paras.en: It’s pretty far, though,” Anna observed. “Like maybe too far.
paras.zh: “我超爱那个。”安娜听到斯文咂了咂嘴。“没错！”

paras.en: It could take two hours to get there and back, and we need to stop at all seven places on this list and be home by sunset.” “Sunset?” Kristoff froze. “Who said anything about sunset?” “I didn’t say anything about sunset.
paras.zh: “不过那可真够远的，”安娜评论道，“远得有点过头了。”

paras.en: Did I say sunset?” Anna asked, her voice getting squeaky. “Well, I didn’t say anything about sunset.
paras.zh: “来回得两小时，可咱们还要在单子上七家全停下来，而且得在日落前回家。”“日落？”克里斯托夫僵住了，“谁提日落了？”“我可没提日落。”

paras.en: Nope!
paras.zh: “我说日落了吗？”安娜问，声音都变尖了，“反正我也没提日落。”

paras.en: Although sunset is a good time to get home.
paras.zh: 没有！

paras.en: For dinner.
paras.zh: “虽说日落回家是个好时辰。”

paras.en: Not that we’re having dinner.
paras.zh: “回去吃晚饭。”

paras.en: Maybe we’re relaxing or getting a massage, or not.
paras.zh: “虽说我们也没在吃晚饭。”

paras.en: Who needs a massage?” Kristoff swallowed hard and pulled at his collar. “Let’s just get to Tomally’s and go from there.” “Good idea.
paras.zh: “也许我们在放松，或做按摩，又或者没有。”克里斯托夫用力咽了口唾沫，扯了扯衣领。“先去托马利家，到那儿再说。”“好主意。”

paras.en: Go slow, but not too slow, Sven.” Anna glanced at the clock in the village as they passed it. “We have plenty of time… I think.” THREE HOURS BEFORE THE PARTY Gale was helping Elsa and Olaf hang a large banner across the courtyard that read CONGRATULATIONS, ANNA AND KRISTOFF! when there was a sound like rolling thunder.
paras.zh: 慢点走，但别太慢，斯文。经过村子时，安娜瞥了眼大钟。“咱们时间绰绰有余……我想是吧。”距派对还有三小时 盖尔正帮艾莎和雪宝在庭院上方拉起一条大横幅，上面写着“恭喜，安娜与克里斯托夫！”，这时忽然传来一阵滚雷般的声响。

paras.en: Oaken stopped placing his hand-carved wooden business calling cards on each chair and looked up.
paras.zh: 奥肯停下往每张椅子上放他手雕木质名片，抬起头来。

paras.en: Every table and chair in the courtyard began to shake. “Here they come!” Olaf cheered.
paras.zh: 庭院里每一张桌子和椅子都开始震动。“他们来了！”雪宝欢呼。

paras.en: All eyes went to the gates of the castle as a few dozen boulders rolled quickly down the path that connected the village to the castle and came to a stop in the courtyard.
paras.zh: 所有人的目光都投向城堡大门——几十块巨石顺着连接村庄与城堡的小路飞快滚下，停在庭院里。

paras.en: One of the boulders leading the pack bounced into the air and unfurled in front of Elsa. “My Kristoff is getting married!” Bulda sounded both teary and elated at the same time. “I can’t believe my boy is all grown up and finally marrying a girl!
paras.zh: 领头的那块巨石弹到半空，在艾莎面前舒展开来。“我家克里斯托夫要成亲啦！”布达的声音里又含泪又欣喜，“真不敢相信我家小子都长大成人，终于要娶媳妇啦！”

paras.en: And not just any girl—Anna!” Olaf cheered. “I’m happy, too.
paras.zh: “而且不是别人——是安娜！”雪宝欢呼，“我也很高兴。”

paras.en: For a while, I thought Kristoff might be marrying Sven.” “Thank you for coming a bit early.” Elsa glanced at the sky, which was just starting to darken.
paras.zh: “有一阵子，我还以为克里斯托夫要娶斯文呢。”“谢谢你们提前过来。”艾莎瞥了眼天空，天色刚要暗下来。

paras.en: With the winter solstice around the corner, daylight hours were shorter—perfect, since the trolls usually only awoke at night. “Of course!
paras.zh: 冬至将近，白昼变短——这正合适，因为地精通常只在夜里醒来。“当然啦！”

paras.en: Of course!
paras.zh: “当然啦！”

paras.en: We’re so excited!” Bulda said as, all around her, trolls began unfurling and moving in the courtyard to check out what Elsa and Olaf had already done with the help of the staff of the castle, who watched the trolls with interest.
paras.zh: “我们太激动了！”布达说，她四周的地精纷纷舒展开身体，在庭院里走动，打量艾莎和雪宝在城堡仆从帮助下已经布置好的东西，而那些仆从也饶有兴致地望着地精们。

paras.en: Elsa had to admit—hiring Oaken’s party-planning service had been the right move.
paras.zh: 艾莎不得不承认——雇用奥肯的派对策划服务是个正确的决定。

paras.en: The courtyard had been outfitted with the traditional holiday decor, with wreaths, boughs of holly, and festive tablescapes making the castle look like a winter wonderland.
paras.zh: 庭院已布置起传统节日装饰，花圈、冬青枝条和节庆餐桌摆设，把城堡装点成了冬日仙境。

paras.en: Lanterns hung on ropes over the tables and were placed strategically around the courtyard, giving the whole area a romantic glow, and in the center of everything was an ice sculpture of Anna and Kristoff.
paras.zh: 灯笼挂在桌面之上的绳索上，又精心地摆在庭院各处，让整片区域笼罩在浪漫的光晕中，而在正中央，则是一尊安娜与克里斯托夫的冰雕。

paras.en: For a finishing touch, Elsa had planned to create a very light snowfall as the party started.
paras.zh: 作为收尾，艾莎还打算在派对开始时降一场很轻的雪。

paras.en: It was elegant.
paras.zh: 一切优雅至极。

paras.en: It screamed Arendelle.
paras.zh: 处处透着阿伦黛尔的韵味。

paras.en: This party was fit for her sister and her future brother-in-law.
paras.zh: 这场派对配得上她妹妹和未来的妹夫。

paras.en: She sighed with happiness.
paras.zh: 她幸福地叹了口气。

paras.en: There was the sound of a crash across the courtyard, and Elsa and Bulda looked over.
paras.zh: 庭院另一头传来一声碰撞的巨响，艾莎和布达循声望去。

paras.en: The Kristoff and Anna ice sculpture had been knocked onto its side. “Oh no!” Elsa cried. “Sorry!” yelled a troll, righting the sculpture that was now missing something important. “Don’t worry!
paras.zh: 那尊克里斯托夫与安娜的冰雕被撞倒在一边。“噢不！”艾莎惊呼。“抱歉！”一个地精喊道，把冰雕扶正，可它现在少了样要紧的东西。“别担心！”

paras.en: I made it better-looking.” Olaf gasped and held his twig arms up to his face. “Anna and Kristoff have lost their heads!” Bulda chuckled. “No, no!
paras.zh: “我把它弄得更好看了。”雪宝倒吸一口气，把小树枝手臂举到脸前。“安娜和克里斯托夫丢了脑袋！”布达咯咯笑了。“不不不！”

paras.en: We’re just replacing them with traditional troll heads.
paras.zh: “我们只是换上传统的地精脑袋。”

paras.en: It’s custom to have rock sculptures in a couple’s likeness at a wedding ceremony.
paras.zh: “婚礼上摆一对新人模样的石雕是咱们的习俗。”

paras.en: Look how beautiful these are!” Several trolls had piled on one another to reach the top of the sculpture, where they stuck small troll heads with grass hair on the top.
paras.zh: “瞧瞧多好看！”几只地精叠罗汉爬到冰雕顶端，把长着草发的小地精脑袋安在上面。

paras.en: All the trolls cheered.
paras.zh: 所有地精都欢呼起来。

paras.en: Elsa guessed this was fine—she wanted Bulda and the trolls to feel comfortable at the party, too.
paras.zh: 艾莎觉得这也无妨——她也想让布达和地精们在派对上自在些。

paras.en: But when she looked closer, she had to hide her surprise at the Anna and Kristoff doppelgängers.
paras.zh: 可当她凑近细看，不得不把对那对“安娜与克里斯托夫替身”的惊讶藏起来。

paras.en: Apparently, the trolls thought her future brother-in-law was a lot hairier than he appeared.
paras.zh: 显然，地精们觉得她未来的妹夫比本人毛多得多。

paras.en: Moss and grass were sticking out of his ears and his nostrils.
paras.zh: 他的耳朵和鼻孔里都伸出苔藓和草。

paras.en: Anna, on the other hand, had hair that was long and wild, which, to be fair, Elsa had to admit was the way her sister’s hair looked when she woke up.
paras.zh: 而安娜的头发则又长又乱——平心而论，艾莎不得不承认，这确实是她妹妹刚睡醒时头发的模样。

paras.en: At that very moment, two trolls walked by carrying a wooden canopy festooned with fungus, moss, and dandelions.
paras.zh: 就在那时，两只地精抬着一顶木制华盖走过，华盖上缀满了菌菇、苔藓和蒲公英。

paras.en: The smell was overpowering. “Ooh!
paras.zh: 那气味扑鼻而来。“噢！”

paras.en: What’s that?” Olaf asked, following the trolls. “The traditional wedding canopy,” Bulda said proudly. “We made it for our Kristoff.” “Bulda, you realize they aren’t getting married today, right?” Elsa said, feeling her fingers begin to tingle again.
paras.zh: “那是什么？”雪宝跟着地精们问。“传统的婚礼华盖，”布达骄傲地说，“这是我们为自家克里斯托夫做的。”“布达，你清楚他们今天不是真结婚，对吧？”艾莎说，感到指尖又开始发麻。

paras.en: She wrinkled her nose and held in the need to sneeze for fear a few snowgies might appear.
paras.zh: 她皱了皱鼻子，强忍着喷嚏的冲动，生怕冒出几只小雪人。

paras.en: Things were already a bit hectic as it was. “Yes, yes, but they should pose under it, as we’ll want to bless it before their actual wedding in the valley,” Bulda said. “The valley?” Elsa repeated.
paras.zh: 眼下场面已经够手忙脚乱了。“知道知道，不过他们该在华盖下拍个照，等谷里真正办婚礼时我们还得为它祈福呢，”布达说。“谷里？”艾莎重复道。

paras.en: Anna needed to get married here, at the castle, but she kept her mouth shut, or rather, half shut as she gaped at the canopy being placed over the head table.
paras.zh: 安娜是要在城堡这儿结婚的，可艾莎闭紧了嘴——或者更确切地说，是半张着嘴，傻看着那顶华盖被安到主桌上方。

paras.en: The trolls’ movements knocked over two unlit lanterns, which sent several plates crashing to the floor. “My tablescape!” Oaken said, running over in a panic. “You don’t need those!
paras.zh: 地精们的走动撞翻了两盏没点的灯笼，几只盘子哗啦摔在地上。“我的餐桌摆设！”奥肯惊慌地跑过来。“那些用不着！”

paras.en: We brought nicer plates,” Bulda told Elsa. “They’re carved out of wood.
paras.zh: “我们带了更好的盘子，”布达对艾莎说，“是木雕的。”

paras.en: We even have moss tablecloths.” A few trolls began unrolling one. “Umm…” Elsa started to say.
paras.zh: “我们还有苔藓桌布呢。”几只地精开始展开一块。“嗯……”艾莎刚要开口。

paras.en: She wasn’t sure how to put this delicately. “Wow, that smells just like Kristoff after an ice delivery!” Olaf said with glee. “And now it’s going on the table.
paras.zh: 她不知该怎样委婉表达。“哇，这味道简直像克里斯托夫送完冰回来的味儿！”雪宝乐滋滋地说，“现在还要铺到桌上。”

paras.en: With food.” Oaken rushed in to stop the trolls. “Hoo-hoo!
paras.zh: “还放吃的。”奥肯冲过来拦住地精们。“嗬——嗬！”

paras.en: I’ve already set the table.
paras.zh: “桌子我已经摆好了。”

paras.en: It looks nice.
paras.zh: “挺好看的。”

paras.en: Ja?” “It will look better with the moss tablecloth,” said Cliff, Kristoff’s troll dad, somewhat indignantly. “No, no,” said Oaken. “This table is fit for the queen.” “So is this tablecloth,” said Cliff. “It’s a present from Grand Pabbie, and it needs to be with Anna and Kristoff.
paras.zh: “是吧？”“铺上苔藓桌布会更好看，”克里斯托夫的地精爸爸克利夫有点不满地说。“不不不，”奥肯说，“这桌子是配女王的。”“这桌布也配，”克利夫说，“这是皮比长老送的礼物，得陪着安娜和克里斯托夫。”

paras.en: It’s tradition!” “It’s tradition,” Bulda echoed, looking at Elsa pleadingly. “We have to use it for our boy.
paras.zh: “这是传统！”“这是传统，”布达跟着说，恳切地望着艾莎，“咱们得为自家小子用上它。”

paras.en: We’re just so happy for the couple and thankful you’ve made us part of the party planning.” Her eyes began to fill with tears again.
paras.zh: “我们就是替这对新人高兴，也谢谢你让我们参与了派对策划。”她的眼眶又泛起泪光。

paras.en: Elsa bit her tongue.
paras.zh: 艾莎忍住了没说话。

paras.en: If Kristoff and Anna wanted to eat on a bed of moss, who was she to stop them? “Of course.
paras.zh: 如果克里斯托夫和安娜愿意在苔藓堆上吃饭，她又有什么资格拦着呢？“当然可以。”

paras.en: We wouldn’t have it any other way.” Bulda smiled, revealing her teeth, and rolled away to help Cliff. “Nice save,” Olaf whispered in Elsa’s ear. “Elsa!” Oaken frantically rushed over. “They’re changing all my work!” Elsa looked around.
paras.zh: “我们就这么办。”布达露出牙齿笑了，滚去帮克利夫。“救场漂亮，”雪宝在艾莎耳边低语。“艾莎！”奥肯慌慌张张地冲过来，“他们把我布置的都改了！”艾莎环顾四周。

paras.en: In just a few minutes, the trolls had taken down the holly and replaced it with boughs of grass.
paras.zh: 才几分钟工夫，地精们就撤下了冬青，换上了草枝。

paras.en: The whole courtyard suddenly smelled like earth.
paras.zh: 整个庭院忽然一股泥土味。

paras.en: This was not at all the party she had been picturing for Anna and Kristoff’s engagement. “Wow, this is different,” Olaf said, as if hearing her thoughts. “Feels like we’re back in the Enchanted Forest.” “The only difference is we’re in Arendelle and we’re celebrating the queen as well as Kristoff,” Elsa murmured worriedly. “What are Anna and Kristoff going to think of all this?” TWO HOURS BEFORE THE PARTY “That took longer than expected, but it was delicious,” Kristoff said, licking his fingers as they sledded back into the village.
paras.zh: 这完全不是她心目中安娜与克里斯托夫订婚派对的样子。“哇，这可不一样，”雪宝仿佛听到了她的心声，“感觉像回到了魔法森林。”“唯一的不同是，咱们在阿伦黛尔，庆祝的是女王和克里斯托夫两个人，”艾莎忧心忡忡地低语，“安娜和克里斯托夫会怎么看这一切？”距派对还有两小时 “比预想的要久，不过真好吃，”克里斯托夫舔着手指说，雪橇滑回了村子。

paras.en: He burped. “I think I had too much sirupssnipper, though.
paras.zh: 他打了个嗝。“不过我想我是糖浆脆饼吃多了。”

paras.en: And jelly rings.” He patted his stomach, not noticing that jelly caked the front of his white shirt.
paras.zh: “还有果冻圈。”他拍了拍肚皮，没注意到果冻糊白衬衫前襟上。

paras.en: Anna dusted off her dress, which had white powder all over the front. “I think I got a little too close to the powdered sugar.
paras.zh: 安娜拍掉裙子上的粉，前襟沾满了白粉末。“我好像离糖粉靠太近了。”

paras.en: It was yummy, but I’m going to have to change before tonight.” Kristoff looked at her strangely. “Tonight?
paras.zh: “是挺好吃，不过今晚之前我得换身衣服。”克里斯托夫奇怪地看她。“今晚？”

paras.en: You’re probably just going to be wearing your robe.
paras.zh: “你大概也就穿件睡袍。”

paras.en: I mean, not just your robe, uh…” Kristoff gulped. “Why do I need a robe?” Anna asked. “You don’t!
paras.zh: “我是说，不光是睡袍，呃……”“我干嘛要穿睡袍？”安娜问。“你不用！”

paras.en: I meant pajamas.” “Pajamas?
paras.zh: “我说的是睡衣。”“睡衣？”

paras.en: For a party?
paras.zh: “去参加派对？”

paras.en: I mean game night,” Anna said, and covered her mouth. “What game night?” Kristoff asked. “I meant you don’t have to look nice tonight, even though you always look nice.
paras.zh: “我是说游戏之夜，”安娜说着捂住了嘴。“什么游戏之夜？”克里斯托夫问。“我是说你今晚不必穿得体面，虽说你向来都体面。”

paras.en: Always!” He ran a hand through his hair and sighed. “Sven?
paras.zh: “一向都体面！”他伸手理了理头发，叹了口气。“斯文？”

paras.en: Help, please?” Sven seemed to groan.
paras.zh: “帮帮忙行吗？”斯文似乎哼了一声。

paras.en: Anna bit her lip. “I meant clean up, you know, before our next stop.
paras.zh: 安娜咬了咬嘴唇。“我是说收拾干净，你知道的，在下一站之前。”

paras.en: A queen shouldn’t be covered in powdered sugar in front of her future in-laws.” Sven snorted.
paras.zh: “女王不该在准公婆面前一身糖粉。”斯文喷了喷鼻息。

paras.en: Kristoff sat up straighter. “Did you say ‘in-laws’?” Anna was still going. “Maybe I can have Gerda help me change quick, and you, too.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫坐直了身子。“你刚说‘公婆’？”安娜还在说。“也许我能让格尔达帮我快点换身衣服，也帮你换。”

paras.en: You should look nice for… wait.” She did a double take. “You already look nice.
paras.zh: “你该穿得体面点去……等等。”她愣了一下，“你已经够体面了。”

paras.en: Why are you dressed up, anyway?
paras.zh: “话说回来，你穿这么正式干嘛？”

paras.en: The Vesterland dinner was canceled.” “Elsa said I should look nice on official business,” Kristoff said with a shrug. “Even if it’s uncomfortable.
paras.zh: “维斯特兰晚宴取消了。”“艾莎说公务在身就该穿得体面，”克里斯托夫耸耸肩，“哪怕不舒服。”

paras.en: Wait.
paras.zh: 等等。

paras.en: Did you say the Vesterland dinner was canceled?
paras.zh: “你刚说维斯特兰晚宴取消了？”

paras.en: No it’s not.
paras.zh: “没取消啊。”

paras.en: It got moved up so that Elsa could plan the—” “Plan what?
paras.zh: “是提前了，好让艾莎策划——”“策划什么？”

paras.en: Game night?” Anna asked, confused. “I thought that’s why you looked so nice.
paras.zh: “游戏之夜？”安娜困惑地问，“我还以为这就是你穿这么体面的原因。”

paras.en: Not that you don’t always look nice, too.
paras.zh: “虽说你向来也都体面。”

paras.en: You look nicer.
paras.zh: “你更体面些。”

paras.en: Nicer-er?” She started to perspire and wiped her brow, getting powdered sugar from her sleeve onto her nose. “Sven?
paras.zh: “更体面点？”她开始冒汗，擦了擦额头，把袖口的糖粉蹭到了鼻子上。“斯文？”

paras.en: Help.” Sven groaned again.
paras.zh: “救命。”斯文又哼了一声。

paras.en: Kristoff wiped the powder off Anna’s nose. “Forget everything we both just said!
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫擦掉安娜鼻子上的糖粉。“刚才咱俩说的全当没说！”

paras.en: The point is we are not going back to the castle to change.” “Good,” Anna said, relieved.
paras.zh: “重点是，咱们不回城堡换衣服了。”“好，”安娜如释重负。

paras.en: Kristoff glanced at the clock in the village as they passed it. “We still have six stops.
paras.zh: 经过村子时，克里斯托夫瞥了眼大钟。“咱们还有六站。”

paras.en: Let’s continue on to the Olsens’.” “Yes!
paras.zh: “接着去奥尔森家吧。”“好！”

paras.en: The Olsens’.” Anna looked at her list. “It’s time for fattigmann.” ONE AND A HALF HOURS BEFORE THE PARTY “Wreaths!” “Moss garland!” “Wreaths!” “Moss garland!” Cliff and Oaken were currently in a standoff over the superior engagement party decor, and the party’s start time was only an hour and a half away.
paras.zh: “奥尔森家。”安娜看着单子。“该吃穷人饼了。”距派对还有一个半小时 “花圈！”“苔藓花环！”“花圈！”“苔藓花环！”克利夫和奥肯正为哪种订婚派对装饰更好僵持不下，而派对开场只剩一个半小时了。

paras.en: Or less if Kristoff and Anna came back early.
paras.zh: 若安娜和克里斯托夫提前回来，时间就更少了。

paras.en: Now the party looked less put together than it had an hour ago.
paras.zh: 此刻的派对比一小时前更显凌乱了。

paras.en: Bulda was debating with one of Oaken’s workers the better seating option—rock or actual chair.
paras.zh: 布达正和奥肯的一名手下争论哪种座位更好——石头还是真正的椅子。

paras.en: The stewards kept removing moss tablecloths, and the trolls kept putting them back on.
paras.zh: 侍从们不断撤下苔藓桌布，地精们又不断铺回去。

paras.en: The troll choir and the children’s choir, who had agreed to team up to serenade the happy couple, had since decided they couldn’t agree on a song.
paras.zh: 地精唱诗班和儿童唱诗班本说好联手为新人唱小夜曲，这会儿却发现自己连选哪首歌都达不成一致。

paras.en: An argument had even broken out over the punch bowl—the trolls wanted to add lichen, and Oaken had gagged at the thought. “Olaf,” said Elsa, surveying the chaos. “This party is turning into a disaster.
paras.zh: 就连潘趣酒碗也吵了起来——地精想加地衣，奥肯一想到就反胃。“雪宝，”艾莎审视着这一片混乱说，“这派对要变成灾难了。”

paras.en: What are we going to do?” “About the decor or the fact that Anna and Kristoff are back in the village and getting closer?” Olaf pointed with a stick finger toward the open gates where Anna, Kristoff, and Sven were gliding by.
paras.zh: “咱们怎么办？”“是指装饰，还是指安娜和克里斯托夫已经回村、正越走越近这件事？”雪宝用小树枝手指指向敞开的大门，安娜、克里斯托夫和斯文正从那儿掠过。

paras.en: The two appeared to be talking animatedly.
paras.zh: 两人似乎正聊得热火朝天。

paras.en: Did they know she’d tricked them both?
paras.zh: 他们知道她把两人都骗了吗？

paras.en: Elsa used her ice magic to close the gates so they couldn’t see inside the courtyard.
paras.zh: 艾莎用冰魔法关上大门，好让他们看不到庭院里面。

paras.en: Then she turned to Olaf. “You need to tell whoever is next to last on that list to stall them,” she said. “Even if Anna and Kristoff have already figured out that you created an elaborate ruse to trick them both and they somehow both let slip to each other what they think is actually going on even if that’s not what’s happening, but they decide to come back here anyway?” Olaf asked. “Wow, that was a lot of words to say in one breath.” He held his stomach by the center coal.
paras.zh: 然后她转向雪宝。“你得去告诉单子上倒数第二家的人拖住他们，”她说。“你是说，就算安娜和克里斯托夫已经猜到你设了个精密圈套把两人都骗了，而且不知怎么彼此都漏了嘴、说出各自以为的实情——尽管那并不是真相——但他们还是决定回来？”雪宝问。“哇，一口气说了那么多词。”他按着肚子上的那块中心煤。

paras.en: Elsa felt her panic rising. “Just make up something to keep them out there.
paras.zh: 艾莎的慌乱感升了起来。“随便编点什么，把他们拖在外面就行。”

paras.en: Please?” “On it!” Olaf said, toddling toward the gates.
paras.zh: “行吗？”“交给我！”雪宝说，摇摇摆摆朝大门走去。

paras.en: ONE HOUR TILL THE PARTY “I feel kind of bad we rushed through all those stops,” said Kristoff, eyeing the stacks of boxes of cookies now nestled in the sled behind them. “We had to.
paras.zh: 距派对还有一小时 “咱们急吼吼跑完所有站点，我有点过意不去，”克里斯托夫看着雪橇后头码着的几摞饼干盒说。“没办法。”

paras.en: We’re running out of time,” Anna said, staring at the almost darkened sky. “We’ve made it to Blodget’s, the Waffle Brothers’, the Olsens’, and the Haugens’.
paras.zh: “时间不够了，”安娜盯着几乎全黑的天色说，“咱们已经跑完布洛杰特、华夫兄弟、奥尔森家和豪根家了。”

paras.en: All that’s left before Gerda is the Bergs’.” Anna eyed a house all lit up with candles in the windows and a wreath on the front door that brought out the green painted trim. “We’re in luck!
paras.zh: “离格尔达家还差伯格家。”安娜看中一栋房子，窗里烛光通明，前门挂着花圈，衬出绿色的描边。“咱们运气不错！”

paras.en: They’re on this very street.” Kristoff pulled to a stop out front, jumped out of the sled, and then helped Anna out, too.
paras.zh: “他们就在这条街上。”克里斯托夫在门前停下，跳下雪橇，又扶安娜下来。

paras.en: They’d just made it to the door when it flew open.
paras.zh: 他们刚走到门口，门就猛地开了。

paras.en: A dozen finely dressed people were standing in the doorway, looking gobsmacked to see them. “Queen Anna!
paras.zh: 十几个盛装的人站在门里，看到他们一脸惊呆。“安娜女王！”

paras.en: What are you doing here?” said the woman in front, hiding a bouquet of crocuses behind her back. “We’re here to pick up the cookies Elsa ordered for…” Anna wasn’t sure how to finish that sentence.
paras.zh: “您怎么会在这儿？”前面的女子说，背后藏着一束番红花。“我们是来取艾莎订的饼干，给……”安娜不知该怎么把这句话说完。

paras.en: She kept messing it up. “For game night, or maybe it’s the dinner with Vesterland,” Kristoff said.
paras.zh: “给游戏之夜，或者也许是和维斯特兰的晚宴，”克里斯托夫说。

paras.en: A small girl handed Kristoff the cookies and then began to giggle. “No, sillies!
paras.zh: 一个小女孩把饼干递给克里斯托夫，然后咯咯笑起来。“不对，傻瓜们！”

paras.en: The cookies are for the party!” Everyone in the house turned and shushed her. “Party?” Anna started to laugh. “We’re not having a party to celebrate anything, like, say, a certain anniversary or career choice.” Kristoff laughed awkwardly, too. “No!
paras.zh: “饼干是给派对的！”屋里所有人都转过身去嘘她。“派对？”安娜笑了起来，“我们可没在庆祝什么，比如某个纪念日或职业选择之类的。”克里斯托夫也尴尬地笑了。“没有！”

paras.en: Not a party!
paras.zh: “没有派对！”

paras.en: Not a spa day, either!” They looked at each other suspiciously. “Spa day?” Anna asked. “Anniversary party?” Kristoff questioned. “Hi there!” Olaf pushed his way to the door. “Olaf, what are you doing here?” Anna asked. “Elsa had a feeling you two were taking too long, so she asked me to find you!” “So she wants us to come back early?” Kristoff asked.
paras.zh: “也没有水疗日！”两人狐疑地对看。“水疗日？”安娜问。“纪念日派对？”克里斯托夫反问。“嗨！”雪宝挤到门前。“雪宝，你在这儿干嘛？”安娜问。“艾莎觉得你们俩磨蹭太久了，就派我来找你们！”“那她是想让我们早点回去？”克里斯托夫问。

paras.en: In front of the house, Sven seemed to be grunting and snorting a lot.
paras.zh: 房子前面，斯文似乎一个劲儿地哼哼喷鼻。

paras.en: Olaf looked at the reindeer warily. “Um… well, no.
paras.zh: 雪宝警惕地看着驯鹿。“呃……嗯，不是。”

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: “不是。”

paras.en: That’s not it.
paras.zh: “不是那样。”

paras.en: Elsa asked me to…” Olaf looked like he wanted to melt. “Elsa told me to come help with all the cookies.
paras.zh: “艾莎是让我……”雪宝一副想融化的样子。“艾莎让我来帮忙搬这些饼干。”

paras.en: With you!
paras.zh: “和你们一起！”

paras.en: Because… because…” Sven was snorting madly. “Don’t say it, Olaf,” the little girl whispered. “So neither of you ruined the surprise.” Olaf exhaled. “Oh, good.
paras.zh: “因为……因为……”斯文发疯似的喷鼻。“别说了，雪宝，”小女孩低声道，“这样你们俩谁都没毁了惊喜。”雪宝舒了口气。“噢，还好。”

paras.en: I didn’t actually say that the surprise was for the both of you, just that it was a surprise.
paras.zh: “我其实没说惊喜是给你们俩的，只说了是个惊喜。”

paras.en: See?

I can keep a secret.” “Surprise for both of us?” Anna and Kristoff questioned at the same time. “Excuse me,” Olaf said, rushing past them to the reindeer and taking a cookie with him along the way. “Sven and I have to go.” “Wait!” Kristoff called as Olaf jumped on the reindeer’s back and unhooked him from the sled. “Sven is our ride!” FORTY-FIVE MINUTES BEFORE THE PARTY Olaf rushed through the gates on Sven’s back and faced Elsa. “The jig is up.
paras.zh: “我守得住秘密。”“给咱们俩的惊喜？”安娜和克里斯托夫同时发问。“失陪，”雪宝说着从他们身边冲向驯鹿，顺手抓了块饼干。“我和斯文得走了。”“等等！”克里斯托夫喊，雪宝已跳上鹿背，把他从雪橇上解下。“斯文是我们的坐骑！”距派对还有四十五分钟 雪宝骑着斯文冲进大门，面对艾莎。“露馅了。”

paras.en: They know.” “How?” Elsa groaned. “They had a lot of questions,” Olaf told her. “It was stressful.” In the background was a lot of yelling. “Never mind that,” Elsa said. “We have bigger problems.
paras.zh: “他们知道了。”“怎么知道的？”艾莎叹道。“他们问了一堆问题，”雪宝告诉她，“压力好大。”背景里是一片大喊大叫。“先别管这个，”艾莎说，“我们有更大的麻烦。”

paras.en: Look at the courtyard!” Everywhere Elsa looked, trolls and stewards, Oaken and his workers, were arguing over the decor!
paras.zh: “看看庭院！”艾莎目光所及，地精和侍从、奥肯和他的手下，正为装饰吵作一团！

paras.en: The menu!
paras.zh: “菜单！”

paras.en: Where to put the sauna!
paras.zh: “桑拿房放哪儿！”

paras.en: Footwear! “Why are people shouting about shoes?” Olaf asked. “Bulda feels it would be nice if everyone was barefoot, while Oaken said it would be improper to show the queen’s feet unless she was wearing someone’s hand-knit socks—or ones you could buy at the trading post,” Elsa said, sounding exasperated. “Apparently it’s troll tradition to not wear socks at a party.” Olaf held up a snowball foot. “No complaints here.
paras.zh: “鞋履！”“大家干嘛为鞋子吵？”雪宝问。“布达觉得大家都光脚挺好，奥肯却说，除非女王穿了谁手织的袜子——或者在贸易站能买到的那种——否则露出女王的脚不成体统，”艾莎无奈地说，“显然地精的传统是派对上不穿袜子。”雪宝举起雪球脚。“我这儿没意见。”

paras.en: But, um, why is the sauna smoking?” Elsa looked up. “Oh no.” The sauna had steam billowing out its top, and several trolls were dancing around it singing some sort of gathering song.
paras.zh: “不过，嗯，桑拿房怎么冒烟了？”艾莎抬头。“噢不。”桑拿房顶喷着蒸汽，几只地精围着它跳舞，唱着某种聚会歌。

paras.en: Oaken’s workers were trying to shoo them away so they could fix whatever was wrong, but the trolls wouldn’t leave. “Hoo-hoo, Queen Elsa!
paras.zh: 奥肯的手下想把他们轰走好修理故障，可地精们不肯走。“嗬——嗬，艾莎女王！”

paras.en: I need your help here!” Oaken yelled over. “Queen Elsa!” Bulda did the same. “So do I!” “Coming!” Elsa looked at Olaf. “The question is: Who is going to help me?” THIRTY MINUTES BEFORE THE PARTY “Do you think Elsa is lying to both of us?” Anna pressed Kristoff as the two trudged by foot through the village streets with as many boxes of cookies as they could carry.
paras.zh: “我这儿需要你帮忙！”奥肯喊过来。“艾莎女王！”布达也喊。“我也需要！”“来了！”艾莎看着雪宝，“问题是：谁来帮我？”距派对还有三十分钟 “你觉得艾莎是不是在骗咱俩？”安娜紧逼克里斯托夫，两人尽可能多拎着饼干盒，步行穿过村中街道。

paras.en: The Bergs and the rest of the people at their house had said something about somewhere they needed to be and left them behind. “Elsa?” Kristoff asked. “Lie?
paras.zh: 伯格一家和屋里的其他人说要去个什么地方，把他们撇下了。“艾莎？”克里斯托夫问，“骗人？”

paras.en: I don’t see it.” He paused. “Although, she did keep Ahtohallan from you at first by not telling you about the voice she was hearing.” “Exactly!” Anna said, trying to balance three boxes of cookies in her arms. “All I know is that she told you to keep me busy this afternoon, but you won’t say why.” “Lips are sealed,” Kristoff commented as he held on to four boxes of cookies from the Bergs. “And she told you to keep me busy, but you won’t tell me what’s going on, either.” “I’m a vault!” Anna declared.
paras.zh: “我看不出来。”他顿了顿，“虽说，她一开始确实瞒着你阿塔霍兰的事，没告诉你她听到了那个声音。”“就是嘛！”安娜说，怀里勉强平衡着三盒饼干。“我只知道她让你今天下午拖住我，可你不肯说原因。”“嘴严得很，”克里斯托夫攥着从伯格家拿的四盒饼干说，“她也让你拖住我，可你也一句不透露。”“我像保险箱！”安娜宣布。

paras.en: She watched a bunch of villagers sneak out of their homes and down the street, much like the Bergs had done after pushing cookies into Anna’s and Kristoff’s hands. “She’s up to something, though.” “Maybe she’s preoccupied with work,” Kristoff guessed. “Being the fifth spirit comes with lots of responsibility, you know.” He gently nudged her with his shoulder. “Just like being queen of Arendelle does.” “True, but I don’t want her to hide things from me,” Anna said. “I hate secrets.
paras.zh: 她看着一群村民悄悄溜出家门沿街而去，就像伯格一家把饼干塞给安娜和克里斯托夫后那样。“不过她肯定在搞什么名堂。”“也许她忙着公务，”克里斯托夫猜道，“毕竟身为第五精灵，责任重大，你知道的。”他轻轻用肩膀碰了碰她。“就像当阿伦黛尔女王一样。”“没错，可我不想让她对我藏着掖着，”安娜说，“我讨厌秘密。”

paras.en: I’m bad at them.” “Me too,” Kristoff admitted. “Good and bad secrets.
paras.zh: “我对秘密很不在行。”“我也是，”克里斯托夫承认，“好的坏的秘密都算。”

paras.en: Wanting to ask you to marry me was a hard secret to keep, even though I had trouble asking you.” “I can imagine,” said Anna, as the clock began to chime. “At least the secrets we both tried to keep today—badly—are almost up.
paras.zh: “想向你求婚是个很难守住的秘密，尽管我开口求你都费劲。”“我可以想象，”安娜说，这时钟声敲响，“至少咱们今天都勉强想守住、却守得很糟的秘密，快到头了。”

paras.en: Let’s get to the castle.
paras.zh: “咱们去城堡吧。”

paras.en: No matter what’s happening, we both know we need to be there at sunset, and that time is now.” PARTY TIME (AT LEAST IT’S SUPPOSED TO BE) The sound of everyone yelling was hurting Elsa’s ears.
paras.zh: “不管发生什么，咱俩都知道得在日落时到那儿，而此刻就是日落时分了。”派对时间（至少本该是） 所有人吵闹的声音吵得艾莎耳朵疼。

paras.en: She looked at Olaf. “What are we going to do about everyone?
paras.zh: 她看着雪宝。“咱们该怎么对付这些人？”

paras.en: They can’t agree on anything!” “I don’t know,” Olaf said, looking worried himself. “It’s a shame everyone can’t just stop and remember why we’re here—to give Anna and Kristoff a warm hug.
paras.zh: “他们什么事都谈不拢！”“我也不知道，”雪宝自己看起来也忧心，“真遗憾大家不能停下来，想想咱们为什么来这儿——是为了给安娜和克里斯托夫一个温暖的拥抱。”

paras.en: Isn’t that what an engagement party is?
paras.zh: “这不就是订婚派对的意义吗？”

paras.en: A celebration because we’re happy they found each other?” Elsa looked at Olaf in surprise before leaning down to give him a hug. “You, my friend, always know the right thing to say.
paras.zh: “因为咱们高兴他俩走到一起而庆祝？”艾莎又惊又喜地看着雪宝，俯身给了他一个拥抱。“我的朋友，你总是知道该说什么。”

paras.en: This group needs a reminder.” She turned to the others. “Everyone?
paras.zh: “这群人需要被提醒一下。”她转向其他人。“各位？”

paras.en: Could I have your attention for a moment?” Slowly Cliff, Bulda, the trolls, the stewards, Oaken and his party planners, the troll and children’s choirs, and Olaf gathered round. “We’re all here because we love Anna and Kristoff and want what’s best for them,” Elsa began, “but I’m afraid that’s not really showing with all the arguments going on.” Behind Elsa, as if for effect, the engagement banner, which was now covered in moss, crashed to the ground. “We just want to include some troll traditions,” Bulda explained. “So our boy knows how much we love him.” “And Anna deserves a party fit for a queen, ja?” Oaken countered, and the stewards nodded. “Why can’t this party be both?” Elsa asked. “A mix of both worlds, just like Anna and Kristoff?
paras.zh: “能听我说一句吗？”克利夫、布达、地精们、侍从们、奥肯和他的策划团队、地精与儿童唱诗班，还有雪宝，慢慢围拢过来。“我们聚在这里，是因为都爱安娜和克里斯托夫，都希望他们好，”艾莎开口道，“可吵成这样，这份心意怕是看不出来了。”艾莎身后，仿佛配合演出般，那面如今覆满苔藓的订婚横幅哗啦落地。“我们只是想加点地精传统，”布达解释，“好让自家小子知道我们有多爱他。”“而安娜配得上女王级别的派对，对吧？”奥肯反驳，侍从们点头。“这场派对为什么不能两者兼得？”艾莎问，“两个世界的融合，就像安娜和克里斯托夫那样？”

paras.en: They should see the best of each of our traditions.” Olaf leaned into Elsa. “Nicely put.” The entire group was quiet for a moment.
paras.zh: “他们该看到咱们各自传统里最好的部分。”雪宝靠向艾莎。“说得好。”全场安静了片刻。

paras.en: Slowly they started to approach one another. “I guess we don’t have to have moss on every table,” Cliff said begrudgingly, and looked at Oaken. “Not every table, ja?
paras.zh: 慢慢地，他们开始走近彼此。“我想咱们不必每张桌上都铺苔藓，”克利夫勉强地说，看着奥肯，“不是每张桌，对吧？”

paras.en: But the moss does look nice on some—like where you’re all going to sit.
paras.zh: “不过苔藓铺在有些桌上确实好看——比如你们要坐的那几张。”

paras.en: And I like the canopy over Kristoff’s and Anna’s seats.” “It is lovely, isn’t it?
paras.zh: “而且我喜欢罩在克里斯托夫和安娜座位上的华盖。”“是很美，不是吗？”

paras.en: As are the bouquets of crocuses on each table,” said Bulda, walking off with Oaken. “Now that I think about it, the straw grass I added might be overkill.” “We could sing two songs,” Elsa heard Little Rock, a small troll Kristoff was close to, say to a choir girl named Hedda. “Good idea!
paras.zh: “每张桌上的番红花束也美，”布达和奥肯边走边说，“现在想想，我加的稻草可能有点多余了。”“我们可以唱两首歌，”艾莎听到和小克里斯托夫亲近的小地精小石头，对一位叫海达的唱诗班女孩说。“好主意！”

paras.en: Two songs are better than one anyway,” said Hedda.
paras.zh: “反正两首歌总比一首好，”海达说。

paras.en: Within minutes, everyone was discussing what should stay and what should go and how they could help one another.
paras.zh: 几分钟内，大家就哪些该留、哪些该撤、如何互相帮忙，讨论起来。

paras.en: Elsa smiled at Olaf. “Thanks to your wisdom, I have a feeling Anna and Kristoff are going to think this is the best engagement party ever.” Olaf peered out a hole in the castle gates. “That’s good, because it looks like everyone is already here!” PARTY TIME (FOR REAL) “I cannot believe the gates are closed,” Anna said, standing in front of the castle on her tippy-toes trying to peer through a small gate window in indignation. “This feels wrong on so many levels, and not just because I’m queen.” She could hear a lot of movement and talking, including laughter from inside the castle courtyard.
paras.zh: 艾莎对雪宝笑了。“多亏你的智慧，我预感安娜和克里斯托夫会认为这是史上最棒的订婚派对。”雪宝从城堡大门的缝隙往外瞄。“那正好，因为看样子大家都已经到了！”派对时间（真开始了） “真不敢相信大门关着，”安娜站在城堡前踮起脚尖，愤愤地想从门上的小窗往里窥视，“这怎么看都不对劲，而且不只因为我是女王。”她能听见里头许多动静和说话声，还有城堡庭院里传来的笑声。

paras.en: Kristoff put his boxes of cookies down on the ground, next to Anna’s boxes, and walked over to her.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫把饼干盒放在地上，挨着安娜的盒子，然后走到她身边。

paras.en: Anna felt a warm hand on her shoulder. “All right, Ms.
paras.zh: 安娜感到一只温暖的手搭在肩上。“好了，暴脾气小姐。”

paras.en: Feisty Pants, let’s give Elsa a minute.
paras.zh: “咱们给艾莎一点时间。”

paras.en: Maybe whatever this surprise is for you… or for me… or for us, it’s still coming together.” For you or for me.
paras.zh: “不管这惊喜是给你的……还是给我的……或是给咱俩的，都还在筹备中。”“给你的还是给我的。”

paras.en: Olaf’s slipup followed by Kristoff’s words made Anna wonder: Could Elsa have tricked them because the surprise was for both of them?
paras.zh: 雪宝的失言，加上克里斯托夫这话，让安娜纳闷：艾莎会不会正因为惊喜是给两人共同的，才把他们都骗了？

paras.en: Anna looked up at him. “I’m not sure you know this about me, fiancé, but I have a hard time sitting out on things.
paras.zh: 安娜抬头看他。“未婚夫，我不确定你知不知道，我这人最受不了被晾在一边。”

paras.en: I’m a doer.” Kristoff pulled her into his arms. “Oh, I know, and I love that about you.
paras.zh: “我是个行动派。”克里斯托夫把她揽入怀中。“噢，我知道，而且我爱你的这一点。”

paras.en: But maybe—just this once—Elsa is keeping us both busy because she doesn’t need either of our help on this one.
paras.zh: “但也许——就这一次——艾莎把咱俩都支开，是因为这事她不需要咱俩帮忙。”

paras.en: She wants to do this on her own.
paras.zh: “她想自己来完成。”

paras.en: So let’s let her.
paras.zh: “所以咱们就让她来吧。”

paras.en: All right?” Anna beamed up at him. “All right.
paras.zh: “好吗？”安娜抬头朝他粲然一笑。“好。”

paras.en: We’ll wait—quietly, without protesting—for her to tell us she’s ready.” She kissed him.
paras.zh: “我们就安静地、不抗议地等着，等她告诉我们她准备好了。”她吻了他。

paras.en: By the time the kiss was over, the gates were opening and there were Elsa and Bulda waiting. “Surprise!” Bulda shouted before anyone else could. “Happy engagement!” “Happy engagement!” The trolls, Oaken, the villagers, and the stewards cheered.
paras.zh: 等这个吻结束，大门开了，艾莎和布达正等着。“惊喜！”布达抢在所有人前头喊，“订婚快乐！”“订婚快乐！”地精、奥肯、村民和侍从们齐声欢呼。

paras.en: More townsfolk—the Bergs, the Olsens, Mrs.
paras.zh: 更多镇民——伯格一家、奥尔森一家、

paras.en: Blodget, the Waffle Brothers—came streaming in from all sides of the castle courtyard.
paras.zh: 布洛杰特太太、华夫兄弟——从城堡庭院四面涌了进来。

paras.en: Anna and Kristoff watched in wonder as the whole world, troll and human, seemed to appear to celebrate them. “It’s our engagement party,” Anna said, looking at Kristoff in surprise. “I can’t believe it.” When all was said and done, Elsa had to admit the mix of earthy touches and castle elegance came together in a truly inspired way that was distinctly Anna and Kristoff.
paras.zh: 安娜和克里斯托夫惊奇地看着，仿佛整个世界——地精和人类——都冒出来为他们庆祝。“这是我们的订婚派对，”安娜惊讶地看着克里斯托夫说，“真不敢相信。”事到如今，艾莎不得不承认，泥土气息与城堡典雅的混搭，以真正别具匠心的方式融合在一起，满满都是安娜与克里斯托夫的味道。

paras.en: Looking at General Mattias chatting with Grand Pabbie, Elsa couldn’t imagine it any other way.
paras.zh: 看着马蒂亚斯将军和皮比长老闲聊，艾莎想象不出还能有别的样子。

paras.en: This was the party they were meant to have. “This place looks amazing!” Kristoff gushed, bending down to give Bulda a hug. “I love the ice slash troll sculptures.
paras.zh: 这正该是他们该有的派对。“这地方太棒了！”克里斯托夫滔滔不绝，弯腰给了布达一个拥抱，“我超爱这些冰雕混搭地精的雕塑。”

paras.en: I’m not sure you got my hair right, though.” “It’s beautiful!
paras.zh: “不过我可不敢说你把我头发雕对了。”“真美！”

paras.en: You pulled all this off in the last four hours?” Anna asked Elsa. “Yep,” Elsa said, smiling at Oaken, who was showing Mrs.
paras.zh: “这些都是你四小时内搞定的？”安娜问艾莎。“没错，”艾莎微笑着说，这时奥肯正给

paras.en: Olsen and Cliff the personal sauna he’d brought for the evening. “But I was lucky.
paras.zh: 奥尔森太太和克利夫展示他今晚带来的私人桑拿房。“不过我运气好。”

paras.en: I had a lot of help.
paras.zh: “我有很多帮手。”

paras.en: I couldn’t have done it without Bulda and the others.
paras.zh: “没有布达和其他人，我可做不到。”

paras.en: This was a team effort.” Kristoff smiled and Bulda blew her nose into a moss handkerchief. “We’re just so happy for you two lovebirds!
paras.zh: “这是团队的努力。”克里斯托夫笑了，布达用苔藓手帕擦了擦鼻子。“我们替你们这对小情侣高兴坏了！”

paras.en: I knew this day would come the moment we saw our Anna for the first time.” “ Our Anna,” Anna repeated softly. “I’m really part of the family now.” “That you are!” Cliff agreed. “And family,” Elsa reminded Anna, “works together.
paras.zh: “从第一次见到咱家安娜那一刻起，我就知道这天会来。”“‘咱家安娜’，”安娜轻声重复，“我现在真成家里人了。”“可不是嘛！”克利夫认同。“而家人，”艾莎提醒安娜，“是要一起努力的。”

paras.en: I’m sorry I shut you out.
paras.zh: “抱歉我之前把你关在门外。”

paras.en: I just thought you two both deserved a surprise, and pulling that off took some creative thinking.
paras.zh: “我只是觉得你们俩都该有个惊喜，而要把这事办成，得动点脑筋。”

paras.en: I knew I had to make you both believe you were helping the other one if I was going to keep you away from the castle for a few hours.
paras.zh: “我知道，要想把你们支开城堡几小时，就得让你们都以为自己在帮对方。”

paras.en: Plus, I worried Kristoff would stress if he knew the scale of this party.” “You know me so well, Elsa,” Kristoff said.
paras.zh: “而且我担心，克里斯托夫要是知道派对规模，会紧张。”“你太了解我了，艾莎，”克里斯托夫说。

paras.en: They all laughed. “You know the best part?
paras.zh: 大家都笑了。“你们知道最棒的是什么吗？”

paras.en: Now we have lots of cookies for everyone!” said Olaf, balancing a tower of cookie boxes in his arms.
paras.zh: “现在我们有好多饼干给大家吃！”雪宝说，怀里稳稳抱着一摞饼干盒。

paras.en: The rest were atop Sven’s back.
paras.zh: “剩下的都在斯文背上。”

paras.en: Kristoff quickly helped unload the boxes while Bulda and Cliff each took them over to several of the tables where trolls and the people of Arendelle sat together, toasting the happy couple, just as Elsa envisioned they would.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫赶紧帮忙卸下盒子，布达和克利夫各自把它们端到几张桌子旁，地精与阿伦黛尔百姓围坐在一起，为新人举杯——正如艾莎所设想的那样。

paras.en: Anna took Elsa’s hand in her own. “I love what you did here—it’s our world and Kristoff’s, and you pulled off the perfect surprise.” “You didn’t figure out what I was up to?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: 安娜握住艾莎的手。“我爱你所做的一切——这是我的世界和克里斯托夫的世界，而你成就了完美的惊喜。”“你没猜到我在忙什么？”艾莎问。

paras.en: Anna just smiled. “Didn’t have a clue.” Elsa squeezed Anna’s hand and looked at Kristoff. “Congratulations, you two.
paras.zh: 安娜只是微笑。“一点都没猜到。”艾莎攥了攥安娜的手，看向克里斯托夫。“恭喜你们俩。”

paras.en: I’m so happy for you both.” “I’m happy for all of us,” Olaf said, jumping on Sven’s back and coming in close so that they could share Elsa’s favorite thing of all: a group hug.
paras.zh: “我真替你们俩高兴。”“我替咱们所有人高兴，”雪宝说着跳上斯文背，凑近过来，好让他们一起分享艾莎最爱的东西：一个集体拥抱。

paras.en: The day was balmy and blue, the sea a deep, sparkling emerald flecked with white.
paras.zh: 那天风和日丽，天空湛蓝，海水是深邃闪亮的祖母绿，点缀着点点白光。

paras.en: Some of that white was playful foam that billowed up each time waves bashed the neat frigate cutting across the water, and some of that white was courtesy of a certain seasick snowman. “You didn’t tell us you got motion sickness,” Anna said, patting Olaf on the back. “Ask Elsa.
paras.zh: 那白光中，一部分是顽皮的浪沫，每次浪头拍向劈波而行的小帆船便翻涌而起；另一部分则来自某位晕船的雪人。“你又没说你会晕船，”安娜拍着雪宝的背说，“去问艾莎。”

paras.en: She’s the one who made me this way!” Olaf moaned. “Look at the horizon,” suggested a canny old sailor named Frode, who stroked his long gray beard as he watched Olaf heave snowballs over the side of the ship. “That should settle ye.” “I don’t even know what ‘ye’ is,” Olaf said. “But I don’t think I have one.” Everyone else, at least, seemed to have proper sea legs.
paras.zh: “是她把我造成这样的！”雪宝哀哼。“看地平线，”一位精明的老水手弗罗德建议道，他捋着灰色长须，看着雪宝往船舷外吐雪球。“那样能让你稳下来。”“我连‘ye’是什么都不知道，”雪宝说，“不过我觉得我也没有那个。”至少其他人似乎都站稳了脚跟。

paras.en: Sven had to brace himself on the slick deck, hooves spread wide, but he enjoyed the brisk air and stood near the bow with Kristoff as the ship dipped up and down in the waves.
paras.zh: 斯文不得不在湿滑的甲板上叉开蹄子站稳，但他享受着凉爽的空气，和克里斯托夫一起站在船头，随船在浪间起伏。

paras.en: Anna was excited by the adventure and wanted nothing more than to run from one end of the ship to the other so she could see everything, but Olaf was currently demanding all her attention.
paras.zh: 安娜对这趟冒险兴奋不已，恨不得从船头跑到船尾看个遍，可雪宝这会儿正独占她的全部注意力。

paras.en: Elsa, of course, was more than happy to be so near the wild water, smiling each time a breaking wave hit the ship.
paras.zh: 艾莎自然乐得离野性的海水这么近，每次碎浪拍打船身都报以微笑。

paras.en: As for General Mattias, he had brought his sweetheart, Halima, along to enjoy the diplomatic mission to the province of Liljeby.
paras.zh: 至于马蒂亚斯将军，他带了心上人哈利玛同行，好一起享受这趟前往利耶比省的外交任务。

paras.en: The crossing was expected to be calm and uneventful, and the two lovebirds sat side by side on a couple of barrels, enjoying the breeze as his guards kept watch.
paras.zh: 这趟横渡本该风平浪静、无事发生，这对恋人并排坐在几只木桶上，吹着微风，他的卫兵在旁警戒。

paras.en: Of course, the only thing to watch at the moment was a nauseated talking snowman. “Look!
paras.zh: 当然，眼下唯一值得看的，就是那位想吐的会说话的雪人。“看！”

paras.en: Dolphins!” Elsa called, pointing off to the side of the ship, where sleek gray bodies arced in and out of the rippling sea. “I always wanted to see a— urghblah! ” Olaf cried. “Dunno what an urghblah is,” Frode said, “but I’ve been at sea for fifty years and ne’er heard o’ one.” Captain Jens kept a tight ship, and he’d been scouting this area for years and claimed to know every inch of the sea’s fathomless depths.
paras.zh: “海豚！”艾莎喊，指向船侧，光滑的灰色身躯在涟漪起伏的海面忽隐忽现。“我一直想看一头——呃啊呸！”雪宝叫道。“不知道‘呃啊呸’是个啥，”弗罗德说，“不过我出海五十年，从没听过这玩意儿。”延斯船长治船甚严，多年来一直在这一带巡弋，自称摸透了这片深海的每一寸。

paras.en: A few of the older sailors fished off the side, pulling in the occasional cod or haddock, while the younger deckhands moved around the ship with cheerful confidence, doing their duties and sidestepping the little white snowballs that rolled here and there with the pitching deck.
paras.zh: 几名老水手在船边垂钓，偶尔钓上鳕鱼或黑线鳕；年轻的水手们则乐呵呵又利落地在船上穿梭，履行本职，还不忘避开随着甲板颠簸到处乱滚的小雪球。

paras.en: A young deckhand stepped in one and muttered, “Ugh,” as he scraped it off on a rail. “Sorry,” Olaf said, sitting up and wiping his mouth with a branch. “Hopefully, they’ll melt soon.
paras.zh: 一名年轻水手踩到一个，喃喃“呃”了一声，在栏杆上把它刮掉。“抱歉，”雪宝坐起来，用树枝擦了擦嘴，“希望它们很快就能化掉。”

paras.en: Kinda wish water didn’t have memory, just now.” Anna stood and put her arm around Elsa’s waist. “I still can’t believe it.
paras.zh: “这会儿真希望水没有记忆。”安娜站起身，揽住艾莎的腰。“我还是不敢相信。”

paras.en: Our first time on a big ship!
paras.zh: “我们头一回坐大船！”

paras.en: Well, you’re no stranger to the sea, of course, but I’m just so excited.
paras.zh: “当然，你对大海并不陌生，可我实在太激动了。”

paras.en: I’ve always wanted to see dolphins!” Elsa moved a lock of windblown red hair out of Anna’s face. “You’re not scared at all?
paras.zh: “我一直想看海豚！”艾莎把安娜被风吹乱的一缕红发拨开。“你一点都不怕？”

paras.en: After what happened to Mother and Father, I wondered if you’d ever go on a sea voyage.…” “Maybe a little scared,” Anna admitted. “But I have you with me.
paras.zh: “想到父母当年的遭遇，我还在想你会不会愿意出海呢……”“也许有点怕，”安娜承认，“但有你在。”

paras.en: And Kristoff and Sven.” “And Olaf!” the snowman muttered. “Even if I’m more of an emotional support snowman than a protector at this point.” “And Olaf,” Anna said with a fond smile. “I wonder what it will be like in Liljeby.” Elsa fussed with the ties of her cape. “I know word of my powers has spread, and the stories have sometimes grown in the telling.…” “That ridiculous diplomat from the Southern Isles thought you were made of ice, remember?” Anna chuckled. “He brought a fur coat, just in case.
paras.zh: “还有克里斯托夫和斯文。”“还有雪宝！”雪人嘟囔，“虽说这会儿我更像是个情感支持雪人，而非守护者。”“还有雪宝，”安娜宠溺地笑着说，“不知利耶比会是什么样。”艾莎摆弄着披风的系带。“我知道我的魔力已经传开，故事有时还越传越神……”“南境群岛那个荒唐的外交官以为你是冰做的，记得吗？”安娜扑哧一笑，“他还带了件皮草大衣，以防万一。”

paras.en: I’m glad you came along for the trip, though.
paras.zh: “不过我很高兴你陪我来这趟。”

paras.en: The people of Liljeby will see you for what you are: a princess of Arendelle.” “With superpowers!” Olaf piped up. “A super princess!
paras.zh: “利耶比的人们会看到你本来的样子：一位阿伦黛尔公主。”“还自带超能力！”雪宝插嘴，“超能公主！”

paras.en: Suprincess?
paras.zh: “超主？”

paras.en: No, that sounds too much like soup.” “I suppose I’ll never be normal.…” Elsa trailed off. “Normal is overrated,” Sven said in what sounded a little bit like Kristoff’s voice. “Of course a talking reindeer would say that.
paras.zh: “不行，那听着太像汤了。”“我想我永远正常不了了……”艾莎声音渐弱。“正常被高估了，”斯文用有点像克里斯托夫的嗓音说。“会说话的驯鹿当然会这么说。”

paras.en: You’re perfect, Elsa, and we wouldn’t have you any other way.” Anna squeezed her sister’s waist and went to join her fiancé and his four-legged best friend.
paras.zh: “你就是完美的，艾莎，我们谁都不想换掉你。”安娜紧了紧揽着姐姐腰的手，去加入未婚夫和他那位四条腿的好友。

paras.en: Standing at the rail, she looked out to the horizon, the world divided into clear blue above and deep green below.
paras.zh: 她站在船舷边，望向地平线，世界被分成上方澄澈的蓝与下方深邃的绿。

paras.en: They were far enough from Arendelle now that there was nothing visible but water and sky in any direction.
paras.zh: 此刻他们离阿伦黛尔够远了，四面八方除了海水与天空再无他物。

paras.en: If her magically gifted sister hadn’t felt such a kinship with the water, and if Captain Jens hadn’t been so capable and the ship so new and sturdy, Anna might’ve been a little worried.
paras.zh: 若非她那位天赋魔力的姐姐对水如此亲近，若非延斯船长如此能干、船又新又结实，安娜或许会有些担忧。

paras.en: After seeing her parents’ ship, she could never forget the unexpected things that could happen at sea.
paras.zh: 见过父母那艘船后，她永远忘不了海上可能发生的种种意外。

paras.en: But as it was, the day was beautiful and she was with the people—and reindeer, and snowman—she loved best in the world.
paras.zh: 但眼下，天气明媚，她身边都是这世上她最爱的人——还有驯鹿和雪人。

paras.en: She couldn’t believe she was the queen of Arendelle now, and that it was up to her to make an appearance at the Liljeby summer festival.
paras.zh: 她不敢相信自己如今已是阿伦黛尔女王，而且得由她出面参加利耶比夏日节庆。

paras.en: She had an exquisite new gown of spring green, embroidered with lilies and bluebells and a delicate tiara that didn’t squeeze her head quite as much as her diadem back home.
paras.zh: 她身着一袭绝美的春绿色新礼服，绣着百合与蓝铃花，头戴一顶精致小冠，不像在家的王冠那样勒得脑袋发疼。

paras.en: Elsa’s powder-blue dress shared the same flowers along the hem, though her tiara was much smaller.
paras.zh: 艾莎的粉蓝色衣裙下摆也绣着同样的花朵，不过她的冠更小巧。

paras.en: Anna often wondered if Elsa minded that she was no longer queen, but as she watched her older sister gaze out into the sea, laughing at the antics of the dolphins racing their ship, she knew that what Elsa wanted most of all was freedom—the freedom to be herself and explore her powers and the world around her.
paras.zh: 安娜常想，艾莎会不会介意自己不再是女王；可当她望着姐姐凝望大海，为与船竞速的海豚的调皮模样而笑时，她明白艾莎最渴望的其实是自由——做自己、探索自己的力量与周遭世界的自由。

paras.en: There was a deep sigh and a depressed squelching, and Olaf appeared at her side. “As someone who’s mostly made of water, I’m disappointed in myself,” he said with that newfound maturity he’d been gaining. “You can’t help what you are,” Anna said with a chuckle. “Besides, you’re probably the first snowman to ever set foot on a boat,” Kristoff added. “And I hope I’ll be the last.
paras.zh: 一声深深的叹息伴着泄气的吧唧声，雪宝出现在她身边。“作为一个基本由水做成的人，我对自己很失望，”他带着近来新长的那份成熟说。“你是什么样由不得自己，”安娜笑着说，“再说了，你大概是头一个踏上船的雪人，”克里斯托夫补充，“而我真希望我是最后一个。”

paras.en: My permafrost is all jiggly.
paras.zh: “我的永冻层全晃悠了。”

paras.en: This must be what middle age feels like.” Anna reached down and rearranged his hair twigs. “Discomfort is just the middle of the journey,” she reminded him. “We’ve got to be halfway there.
paras.zh: “这一定就是中年的感觉。”安娜俯身理了理他的头发树枝。“不适只是旅程的中段，”她提醒他，“咱们肯定走了一半了。”

paras.en: Right, Frode?” The old sailor looked up from his fishing pole and gazed out into the brisk air, squinting. “Not quite halfway,” he said. “You’ll get used to it, me icy lad.
paras.zh: “对吧，弗罗德？”老水手从钓竿上抬起头，眯眼望向清冽的空气。“还差得远呢，”他说，“你会习惯的，我的冰小子。”

paras.en: Sea’s not even that choppy today.
paras.zh: “今儿海面都不算太颠。”

paras.en: No fish without bones, as my farfar always told me.” “A fish without bones would be way too floppy.
paras.zh: “没有无骨头的鱼，我爷爷总这么说。”“没有骨头的鱼也太软趴趴了。”

paras.en: Even I, without bones, understand that,” Olaf said sniffily. “It’s a proverb,” Anna told him. “He just means that even the nicest things aren’t perfect.” “I’m glad you have bones, Anna.” Olaf looked into her eyes, smiling, before running to the rail and letting loose another volley of snowballs. “Anna, come see!” Elsa called, and Anna kissed Kristoff on the cheek and patted Sven on the head before moving to the rear of the boat, where Elsa was looking down. “There’s a rainbow, see?” Elsa pointed to where the mist made by leaping dolphins shimmered in pastel hues. “I didn’t know water could do that.” “The sea is so—” But Anna couldn’t finish her sentence, because the ship juddered suddenly, throwing her to the ground as the wood creaked and groaned.
paras.zh: “连我这个没骨头的都懂，”雪宝自傲地说。“那是句谚语，”安娜告诉他，“他只是说，再好的东西也不完美。”“真高兴你有骨头，安娜。”雪宝望着她的眼睛笑着，然后跑到船舷边，又喷出一阵雪球。“安娜，来看！”艾莎喊，安娜吻了吻克里斯托夫的脸颊，拍了拍斯文的脑袋，走到船尾，艾莎正朝下望。“有道彩虹，看到了吗？”艾莎指着海豚跃起激起的水雾在柔和色彩中闪烁的地方。“我不知道水还能这样。”“大海真是太——”可安娜的话没说完，因为船猛地一震，把她摔在地上，木头发出了吱嘎呻吟。

paras.en: Elsa was able to stay upright since she had a hand on the railing, and as she helped Anna stand, the ship fell into absolute chaos. “To the harpoons!” Captain Jens called. “To the crossbows!” “Are we being attacked?” General Mattias asked, running over without Halima, his guards behind him. “Not by people,” Frode told him, swiftly pulling up his fishing line. “But the sea hides many things, twisted and hideous, full of sharp teeth and treacherous claws.” “Is that true?” Elsa asked Captain Jens, who had hurried over to her and Anna and cut a dashing but strained bow. “Depends on what you consider hideous, I suppose, but sharks have teeth and crabs have claws, so technically, he’s correct.” The young captain grinned gallantly, but there was fear in his eyes. “Your Majesties, might I persuade you to join Halima and take shelter in the cabins below?
paras.zh: 艾莎因为手扶着栏杆才站稳，她扶安娜起身时，船陷入了彻底混乱。“拿鱼叉！”延斯船长喊，“拿弩！”“我们被攻击了？”马蒂亚斯将军问，丢下哈利玛跑了过来，卫兵跟在身后。“不是人，”弗罗德边利落地收起钓线边说，“但海里藏着许多东西，扭曲而可怖，满口利齿与阴毒的利爪。”“真的吗？”艾莎问延斯船长，他匆匆赶到她与安娜跟前，行了个潇洒却显紧绷的礼。“要看你怎么定义‘可怖’了，不过鲨鱼有牙、螃蟹有钳，所以严格说他说得对。”年轻船长殷勤一笑，眼里却有恐惧。“两位陛下，可否请你们去和哈利玛一起，到下层舱室避险？”

paras.en: Now is no time to be on the deck.
paras.zh: “此刻绝不是待在甲板上的时候。”

paras.en: Whatever we’ve hit will want a fight.” “We never back down from a fight,” Anna said. “I do,” Olaf moaned from the railing. “Look at my arms.
paras.zh: “不管咱们撞上的是什么，它都会想干一仗。”“我们从不临阵退缩，”安娜说。“我退，”雪宝在栏杆边哀哼，“看看我的胳膊。”

paras.en: If I was supposed to fight, they’d be much sturdier.
paras.zh: “若真要我打架，它们该结实得多。”

paras.en: I’m a willow, not an oak.” Kristoff and Sven joined the crew as the sailors scurried down the stairs into the ship and returned carrying sinister harpoons and heavy crossbows.
paras.zh: “我是柳树，不是橡树。”水手们匆匆跑下舷梯钻进船舱，再出来时扛着阴森的鱼叉和沉重的弩，克里斯托夫和斯文也加入了船员队伍。

paras.en: Fearlessly, the sailors launched rowboats into the foaming waves, paddling away from the ship and searching the water for their prey. “How can we help?” Kristoff asked, although Sven’s eyes flew wide with alarm.
paras.zh: 水手们无畏地放下划艇，冲进翻涌的浪里，划离大船，在水面搜寻猎物。“我们能帮什么？”克里斯托夫问，尽管斯文的眼睛因警觉瞪得溜圆。

paras.en: Captain Jens looked at each of them in turn. “First of all, stay out of the way.
paras.zh: 延斯船长挨个看了看他们。“首先，别挡道。”

paras.en: The crew will attempt to strike whatever hit the boat.
paras.zh: “船员会去攻击撞船的东西。”

paras.en: That should drive the beast away, and if not, we might wound it enough to weaken it.” “But what is it?” Anna asked. “Most likely a whale,” Captain Jens said. “If you’ll excuse me, I need to direct my crew.
paras.zh: “那样应能把它赶走，就算不行，也能把它伤得够重、失了力气。”“可那到底是什么？”安娜问。“多半是鲸鱼，”延斯船长说，“失陪，我得去指挥船员了。”

paras.en: Frode, stay with our guests and keep them as safe as can be, if they’ll not go belowdecks.” Frode nodded as the captain ran off. “Terrible, hungry things whales be.
paras.zh: “弗罗德，留下来陪客人，尽量护他们周全，只要他们不下去。”弗罗德点头，船长跑开了。“鲸鱼可是又可怕又贪吃的东西。”

paras.en: Why, my friend has been hunting a particularly vicious one for years, a vast white beast that hungers for the blood o’ men.
paras.zh: “唉，我朋友多年来一直在猎一头特别凶残的，那是个渴求人血的巨大白兽。”

paras.en: The hideous things that live in the depths of the sea are consumed by rage and hunger, monsters of bristling maw and dread with sea-beating tails.
paras.zh: “栖居深海的那些可怖之物，被愤怒与饥饿吞噬，是利齿森森、甩尾拍海的骇人怪物。”

paras.en: Should the whale open his mouth—” “I’ll be in the hold, trying not to become a puddle,” Olaf said, swiftly toddling off to the stairs. “Maybe we just hit a rock?” Kristoff asked. “Rocks aren’t always terrible.” “Or a sunken shipwreck?” Anna asked, an old sadness in her eyes.
paras.zh: “万一鲸鱼张嘴——”“我去底舱，尽量不让自己化成一滩，”雪宝说，摇摇摆摆快步走向楼梯。“也许咱们只是撞了块石头？”克里斯托夫问，“石头也不总是坏事。”“或者撞上沉船？”安娜问，眼里闪过一丝旧日的哀伤。

paras.en: As if in answer, the ship heaved again, the deck boards thudding and creaking as everyone struggled to stay on their feet. “’Tis no rock, nor any shipwreck,” Frode said darkly. “’Tis a behemoth sent from the deepest fathoms who wishes only to drown us all.” He paused and stroked his beard. “Good eatin’, though, if you can manage to best such a thing.” “I don’t like this,” Elsa said softly. “Whatever it is, this is its home.
paras.zh: 仿佛作答，船又猛地一晃，甲板木板砰砰作响、吱呀呻吟，所有人努力站稳。“既不是石头，也不是沉船，”弗罗德阴沉沉地说，“是来自最深海底的巨兽，只想把咱们全淹死。”他顿了顿，捋了捋胡子。“不过真要能降住它，倒是好吃的。”“我不喜欢这样，”艾莎轻声说，“不管它是什么，这儿是它的家。”

paras.en: We’re the intruders here, and it seems wrong for us to—” “Kill it, lads!” Captain Jens shouted. “Double rations for whoever gets the first shot!” The crew in the rowboats cheered and aimed their harpoons, howling as they heaved the giant hooks into the dark, unknowable waters.
paras.zh: “我们是闯入者，我们去——似乎不对——”“宰了它，伙计们！”延斯船长喊，“谁先下手，双份口粮！”划艇上的船员欢呼，瞄准鱼叉，嚎叫着把巨大的钩子掷进黑暗莫测的水中。

paras.en: The sailors still on the frigate held heavy crossbows, waiting for a beast to appear. “I don’t like it, either,” Anna said, her face stony. “It seems cruel.” “The sea is cruel.” Frode took a shining knife from the sheath at his belt and picked his teeth with the blade. “What you don’t kill first here will gladly kill you.
paras.zh: 仍留在帆船上的水手端着沉重的弩，等着怪物现身。“我也不喜欢，”安娜板着脸说，“这太残忍了。”“大海就是残忍。”弗罗德从腰间刀鞘抽出一把锃亮的刀，用刀尖剔牙。“在这儿，你不先下手，它就乐得要你的命。”

paras.en: The sea ain’t soft, like the land.
paras.zh: “大海不像陆地那样温柔。”

paras.en: There, you build walls and streets and buildings to protect yourself from beasts, but here in the ocean, there is no protection.
paras.zh: “在陆地，你筑墙、修路、盖房来抵御野兽；可在海里，毫无遮蔽。”

paras.en: You’re either faster than what wants to eat you, or you’re meaner, or you get eaten.
paras.zh: “你要么比想吃你的东西更快，要么比它更狠，要么就被吃掉。”

paras.en: It may not be ideal, but if’n you don’t like it, why, you might as well stay on land.” He shrugged. “If we live through it, whatever this is.” As the harpoons rained down, Elsa and Anna linked their arms and watched. “They said this part of the sea was safe,” Anna murmured. “I guess we know better than anyone that almost anything can suddenly turn dangerous.” Elsa leaned over, looking down at the roiling water. “I got it!” one of the sailors called.
paras.zh: “也许不完美，可你若不喜欢，干脆待在陆上得了。”他耸耸肩。“只要咱们能活过这一劫，管它是什么。”鱼叉如雨点落下，艾莎和安娜挽着手臂观望。“他们说这片海域很安全，”安娜低语，“我想我们比谁都清楚，几乎任何东西都可能突然变得危险。”艾莎俯身，盯着翻腾的水面。“上钩了！”一名水手喊。

paras.en: When the sisters looked over, they saw his line had gone taut, pulling the rowboat along.
paras.zh: 姐妹俩看过去，只见他的钓线绷得笔直，拽着划艇往前走。

paras.en: But the beast didn’t swim away from the ship; it pulled the rowboat directly into the side, causing the wood to shudder yet again. “Your Majesties, your safety is of the utmost importance,” Captain Jens said urgently, now looking far more worried than a seasoned captain should. “Please seek shelter, I beg you.
paras.zh: 可那怪物没有游离大船，反而把划艇直接拽向船身，木头再次震颤。“两位陛下，你们的安全最为要紧，”延斯船长急切地说，此刻的担忧远超一位老练船长应有的程度，“求你们去避险吧。”

paras.en: This part of the process can be messy and dangerous.” “I agree,” General Mattias said. “Halima is already in the captain’s quarters, where everything is nailed down.
paras.zh: “这环节可能又乱又危险。”“我同意，”马蒂亚斯将军说，“哈利玛已经在船长室里，那里一切都钉死了。”

paras.en: I can’t keep you safe if you remain on deck.” He put his hand on his sword. “Whatever is under the boat, my crew and I can fight it.
paras.zh: “你们若留在甲板，我护不住你们。”他把手按在剑上。“不管船下是什么，我和我的部下都能对付。”

paras.en: Our utmost duty is to keep you safe.” “You should go,” Elsa said, taking Anna’s hands. “I’m staying with you,” Anna told her sister, squeezing her hands. “I go where Anna goes.” Kristoff turned and slung an arm around his reindeer friend’s neck. “But you should go shelter with Halima, Sven.
paras.zh: “我们的最高职责就是护你们周全。”“你该下去，”艾莎握住安娜的手说。“我留下陪你，”安娜紧了紧姐姐的手，“安娜去哪儿我去哪儿。”克里斯托夫转过身，一条胳膊搂住驯鹿朋友的脖子。“不过你该和哈利玛一起去避险，斯文。”

paras.en: It’s probably going to get slippery up here.
paras.zh: “这儿上面恐怕要变得很滑。”

paras.en: And even if you’re an excellent swimmer”—Sven snorted his pride—“we wouldn’t be able to get you back up on the deck if you fell overboard.” With a honk of realization, Sven trotted toward the stairs and disappeared into the lower decks with an awkward clatter of hooves. “Whew.
paras.zh: “再说你游泳虽棒——”斯文骄傲地喷了喷鼻——“可你若落水，我们也没法把你弄回甲板。”斯文恍然鸣叫一声，小跑向楼梯，蹄声杂乱地消失在下层舱。“呼。”

paras.en: Okay.

Now I only have to worry about one person.” Anna jerked her head toward Elsa and cleared her throat. “I mean, I worry about Elsa,” Kristoff hurried to assure her, “but if it involves nature, she seems more than capable of taking care of herself.” The ship creaked with another hit, and Captain Jens shook his head in frustration. “I can’t order royalty around, but I hope you all understand the grave risk you’re taking.
paras.zh: “现在我只需担心一个人了。”安娜朝艾莎方向一扬头，清了清嗓子。“我是说，我担心艾莎，”克里斯托夫连忙向她保证，“可只要关乎自然，她似乎完全能照顾好自己。”船又撞了一下，吱呀作响，延斯船长懊恼地摇头。“我命令不动王室，但希望你们明白自己冒了多大风险。”

paras.en: Whales are a challenge for even the most seasoned sailor.” “So it’s a whale?” Elsa asked. “It doesn’t feel like—” “Definitely a whale.” He nodded coolly. “They’re the biggest things in the sea, after all, and—” Something enormous shot out of the water just beyond him—a curling, glistening white tentacle covered in suckers.
paras.zh: “对最老练的水手来说，鲸鱼也是难题。”“所以是鲸鱼？”艾莎问，“感觉不像——”“绝对是鲸鱼。”他冷静地点头，“毕竟它们是海里最大的东西，而且——”他身后不远的水面猛地窜出个庞然大物——一条蜷曲、泛着光泽、布满吸盘的白色触手。

paras.en: It rose as tall as the highest flag of Arendelle Castle, pausing as if assessing the situation.
paras.zh: 它升起得和阿伦黛尔城堡最高的旗帜一般高，悬停片刻，仿佛在估量局势。

paras.en: They watched it, stunned into silence, as it shot down toward the ship like a seeking hand.
paras.zh: 他们目瞪口呆地望着它，像一只搜寻的手般朝大船猛扎下来。

paras.en: Before anyone could react, before Elsa could even scream, the tentacle wrapped around Anna’s waist.
paras.zh: 还没等谁反应过来，连艾莎都来不及尖叫，触手已缠住安娜的腰。

paras.en: Kristoff grabbed her hands, then her skirt, but the fine new cloth was torn out of his grip as the tentacle jerked her into the air. “Anna!” Elsa shouted.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫抓住她的手，又抓住她的裙摆，可那精致的衣料从他手中被扯断，触手猛地把她拽向空中。“安娜！”艾莎大叫。

paras.en: She flung her fingers outward, aiming blasts of ice at the tentacle, but it was too fast.
paras.zh: 她手指向外一挥，朝触手射出冰刃，可它太快了。

paras.en: With Anna struggling in its grasp, it slipped underwater with a powerful splash. “Careful, crew!” Captain Jens shouted. “Aim your harpoons well.
paras.zh: 安娜在它掌控中挣扎，它带着巨大的水花沉入水下。“小心，伙计们！”延斯船长喊，“瞄好你们的鱼叉。”

paras.en: Take down the beast, but don’t hit the queen!” Kristoff immediately dove over the railing and into the water as the sailors maneuvered their rowboats to the spot where Anna had disappeared.
paras.zh: “放倒那怪物，但别伤到女王！”克里斯托夫立刻翻过栏杆跃入水中，水手们也操控划艇驶向安娜消失的地方。

paras.en: But Elsa turned to the captain. “That’s no whale, so what is it?” she asked him, frantic. “It doesn’t seem hungry.…” “The Kraken,” Captain Jens said, face twisted in a snarl. “And hunger it does.
paras.zh: 可艾莎转向船长。“那不是鲸鱼，那到底是什么？”她急切地问，“它似乎并不饿……”“北海巨妖，”延斯船长龇牙咧嘴地说，“而且它确实饥饿。”

paras.en: It’s a colossal octopus the size of an island, known for pulling ships into the deep.
paras.zh: “它是座岛屿般巨大的章鱼，以把船拖进深海而闻名。”

paras.en: Should it be allowed to fully rise to the surface, it will create a whirlpool that will suck down the ship and all souls upon it.” “So you’ve fought it before?” He shook his head. “No one who encounters the Kraken has lived to tell the tale.” “Then how is there a tale to tell?” The captain looked momentarily flummoxed before taking up a harpoon and returning to the rail. “If you’ve a plan, best put it into motion.
paras.zh: “若任它完全浮出水面，会掀起漩涡，把船和船上所有生灵一并吸入海底。”“那么你以前和它交过手？”他摇头。“遇见北海巨妖的人，从无生还者能讲出故事。”“那这故事是怎么传下来的？”船长一时语塞，随即抓起一支鱼叉回到栏杆边。“你若有计划，最好赶紧施行。”

paras.en: We’ve heard stories of your powers, and you may be your sister’s only hope.” Elsa joined him at the railing right as Kristoff surfaced, sucking in a huge breath. “I can’t see her,” he called. “This thing is huge, and it’s down too deep, and there are too many arms.
paras.zh: “我们听过你魔力的传说，你或许是你妹妹唯一的希望。”艾莎在他身边来到栏杆旁，正赶上克里斯托夫浮出水面，大口喘息。“我看不见她，”他喊，“这东西太大，潜得太深，而且手臂太多。”

paras.en: I can’t—” He, too, disappeared, pulled down into the water.
paras.zh: “我没法——”他也消失了，被拽入水下。

paras.en: Elsa looked down at her heavy traveling dress and tall boots.
paras.zh: 艾莎低头看了看自己厚重的旅行裙和高筒靴。

paras.en: There wasn’t time. “No more harpoons,” she warned the enraged captain. “We don’t want to make it any angrier.” With a running start, she arced over the railing and dove, bracing herself for the hard slap of the freezing water.
paras.zh: 没时间了。“别再投鱼叉了，”她警告怒不可遏的船长，“我们可不想惹它更恼。”她助跑几步，越过栏杆划出弧线跃入水中，准备好迎接刺骨海水狠狠的一击。

paras.en: It hit her like a bad dream, salt and spray battering her as the Kraken churned the waters.
paras.zh: 海水像噩梦般击中她，盐与浪花拍打着她，北海巨妖搅动着水域。

paras.en: But Elsa—she was made for this.
paras.zh: 可艾莎——她本就是为这而生。

paras.en: She’d fought the Dark Sea, eventually made peace with it.
paras.zh: 她曾与暗海搏斗，最终与它和解。

paras.en: She knew Ahtohallan like an old friend.
paras.zh: 她熟悉阿塔霍兰，如老友一般。

paras.en: With a huge, gasping breath and a mighty kick, she swam under the waves and opened her eyes.
paras.zh: 她深深喘息一口，猛地一蹬，潜入浪下，睁开了眼睛。

paras.en: Her gaze followed the sailor’s taut rope down into the darkness, where the rope quivered with the mighty creature’s movement.
paras.zh: 她的目光顺着水手绷紧的绳索探入黑暗，绳索随那巨兽的动静而颤动。

paras.en: Elsa swam a few strokes before remembering—she wasn’t alone here.
paras.zh: 艾莎划了几下，才想起——她在这儿并不孤单。

paras.en: She had an ally.
paras.zh: 她有个盟友。

paras.en: With a silent plea and a beckoning motion, she called the Water Nokk to her.
paras.zh: 她无声地恳求着，招了招手，唤来水马。

paras.en: The sleek water horse took form, tossing its mane and twirling, glad to be with her in the churning waves.
paras.zh: 那光滑的水马凝成形，甩动着鬃毛转了个圈，欣喜能与她同在这翻腾的浪里。

paras.en: With a smile of welcome, Elsa mounted the horse’s back and tangled her hands in its flowing mane, urging it downward.
paras.zh: 艾莎含笑相迎，跨上马背，双手缠进它飘扬的鬃毛，催它下潜。

paras.en: The Water Nokk happily swam, whinnying its joy.
paras.zh: 水马欢快地游着，嘶鸣着喜悦。

paras.en: Flashes of movement disturbed the murk.
paras.zh: 游动的闪光搅动了幽暗。

paras.en: There, a white tentacle waved.
paras.zh: 那儿，一条白色触手在摆动。

paras.en: There, a flash of gold—Kristoff’s hair.
paras.zh: 那儿，一抹金色闪过——是克里斯托夫的头发。

paras.en: Elsa nudged the Water Spirit with her knees, and it galloped toward where Kristoff fought the tentacle, trying to push his way out of the muscular curl of pale flesh.
paras.zh: 艾莎用膝盖轻碰水之精灵，它便向克里斯托夫挣扎的那条触手飞驰而去，他正试图从那苍白肌肉的蜷曲中挣脱。

paras.en: Elsa took aim and unleashed a volley of ice at the tentacle, below Kristoff so he wouldn’t be struck.
paras.zh: 艾莎瞄准，朝触手射出一阵冰刃，落点在克里斯托夫下方，免得伤到他。

paras.en: The Kraken’s tentacle jerked open and retreated as if in pain, releasing Kristoff, who gave a mighty kick toward the surface.
paras.zh: 北海巨妖的触手像吃痛般猛地张开、缩了回去，放开了克里斯托夫，他奋力一蹬朝水面游去。

paras.en: As he swam upward, cheeks round with held breath, Elsa continued to battle the tentacle, distracting it from reclaiming its catch.
paras.zh: 他鼓着腮帮憋气向上游，艾莎继续与那条触手缠斗，引开它，不让它重新抓回猎物。

paras.en: Once Kristoff surfaced, Elsa watched from far below as sailors pulled him into their boat.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫一浮出水面，艾莎在深处望着水手们把他拉上划艇。

paras.en: Now that Kristoff was safe, she had to be quick.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫既已安全，她必须快。

paras.en: Not only would Anna be out of air soon, but if Elsa didn’t save her, courageous Kristoff would dive right back down to fight for his love, a fight he couldn’t win on his own.
paras.zh: 安娜很快就要撑不住气了，而且若艾莎不救她，勇敢的克里斯托夫会再次潜下，为爱而战——一场他独自赢不了的战斗。

paras.en: But for all of Elsa’s powers, she still couldn’t breathe underwater.
paras.zh: 可尽管艾莎魔力无边，仍不能在水下呼吸。

paras.en: She could last a long time when riding the Water Nokk because of how quickly they could surface, but she wasn’t indomitable.
paras.zh: 骑着水马时她能撑很久，因为它们上浮极快，可她并非无坚不摧。

paras.en: She swiftly asked the Water Spirit to swim upward, where she broke the surface and sucked in a breath. “Is she okay?” Kristoff asked her, soaked and shivering as he peered down from the rowboat, where the sailors held him back by his shoulders. “She will be.
paras.zh: 她急忙让水之精灵上游，破水而出，深吸一口气。“她还好吗？”克里斯托夫问她，浑身湿透、瑟瑟发抖，从划艇上往下望，水手们按着他的肩不让他动。“她会的。”

paras.en: Stay here.” Elsa inflated her lungs and dove back underwater, urging the Water Nokk downward with all its speed and power.
paras.zh: “待在这儿。”艾莎吸足肺里的气，再次潜入水下，催水马以全速全力下潜。

paras.en: Seen from far below the surface, the Kraken was more enormous than Elsa ever could’ve believed, a mass of heaving white skin that shivered with lavender and gray speckles as it moved in the darkness, its colors seeming to shift and shimmer like a butterfly in the sunlight.
paras.zh: 从水面下极深处望去，北海巨妖比艾莎想象中更庞大，一团起伏的白色皮肤在黑暗中游动，泛着淡紫与灰色的斑点微微颤动，其色彩仿佛阳光下蝴蝶般流转闪烁。

paras.en: She hunted for a sign of Anna against the deep greenish black before catching a flash of something red billowing—Anna’s hair.
paras.zh: 她在深绿近黑的水中搜寻安娜的踪迹，终于捕捉到一抹飘动的红——是安娜的头发。

paras.en: Anna wasn’t moving; she looked like a doll waved in the reckless hand of a child.
paras.zh: 安娜一动不动，像被孩子胡乱挥舞手中的玩偶。

paras.en: With renewed determination, Elsa urged the Water Nokk to dive deeper and deeper still.
paras.zh: 艾莎决心更坚，催水马一沉再沉。

paras.en: The pressure pushed all around Elsa, a headache beginning to build behind her eyes.
paras.zh: 压力从四面挤压艾莎，她眼后开始隐隐作痛。

paras.en: She hadn’t been this deep underwater since she’d first faced the Dark Sea.
paras.zh: 自第一次直面暗海以来，她还没潜过这么深。

paras.en: Her fingers tightened in the Water Spirit’s mane as they approached the Kraken.
paras.zh: 接近北海巨妖时，她的手指在精灵鬃毛中攥得更紧。

paras.en: Elsa couldn’t find anything about the beast that was familiar or friendly, no face or eyes or even a body; it seemed to be all tentacles, a swarming, curling mass of suckers probing and churning in darkness as thick as ink.
paras.zh: 艾莎在这巨兽身上找不到任何熟悉或友善之处，没有脸、没有眼、甚至没有身体；它仿佛全是触手，一团蠕动蜷曲的吸盘在浓墨般的黑暗中探触翻搅。

paras.en: She could sense its turmoil, though—curiosity and hurt and an ancient, innocent anger at the alien ship that had struck its tender head.
paras.zh: 不过她能感到它的纷乱——好奇、受伤，以及对撞疼它柔嫩脑袋的异类船只，那份古老而天真的愤怒。

paras.en: It held Anna close to its center, where all its tentacles originated, and one great, round eye opened to regard Elsa with a flat black pupil the size of the fountain in the town square back home.
paras.zh: 它把安娜紧贴在身体中央——所有触手发源之处，一只巨大浑圆的眼睛睁开，用如家乡镇上喷泉般大小的扁平黑瞳注视着艾莎。

paras.en: Once she was close enough that she was completely certain of her aim, Elsa unwrapped her hands from the Water Nokk’s mane and used both of her arms to throw a massive burst of ice water at the Kraken’s tentacle, just under where it held Anna.
paras.zh: 等近到全然确信能瞄准时，艾莎从水马鬃毛中松开手，双臂齐发，朝北海巨妖抓着安娜下方的触手，喷出一大股冰水。

paras.en: As the sharp, sheeting daggers of ice slammed into the tender flesh, the eye squeezed shut in pain and the tentacle uncurled, pulled back into the nest of writhing appendages.
paras.zh: 尖锐如刃的冰片扎进柔嫩的皮肉，那只眼痛苦地紧闭，触手舒展开来，缩回那团蠕动的附肢之中。

paras.en: Elsa fought the desperate instinct to call out to her sister, knowing she needed every bit of air in her body.
paras.zh: 艾莎压下心底拼命想呼唤妹妹的冲动，知道自己体内的每一口气都至关重要。

paras.en: Urging the Water Spirit forward, she leaned into the flow of water and stretched out her hand.
paras.zh: 她催水之精灵向前，顺势融入水流，伸出手去。

paras.en: The moment her fingertips brushed the wet velvet of Anna’s dress, relief flowed through Elsa.
paras.zh: 指尖触到安娜衣裙那湿润的天鹅绒般质感的一瞬，艾莎心中涌起一阵释然。

paras.en: She pulled the fabric close, and Anna floated, unconscious and listless, toward her.
paras.zh: 她拉近衣料，安娜毫无知觉、绵软无力地朝她漂来。

paras.en: With a sharp jerk, the Water Nokk spun around, reared with an echoing call, and galloped straight up toward the surface so very far above.
paras.zh: 水马猛地一扭身，扬蹄长嘶一声，朝着极遥远的上方水面直冲而上。

paras.en: Elsa wanted to cradle her sister’s body to her chest and weep.
paras.zh: 艾莎想将妹妹的身体拥入怀中，放声痛哭。

paras.en: She wanted to beg Anna to open her eyes, to move, to do anything reassuring, but she knew their best bet was to get her sister out of the water as quickly as possible.
paras.zh: 她想恳求安娜睁开眼、动一动、做任何令人安心的事，可她知道最要紧的是尽快把妹妹带离水面。

paras.en: She clutched the wad of Anna’s skirts so hard that her fist began to go numb and focused her prayers on the nearest sunlight dappling the shifting waters above.
paras.zh: 她死死攥着安娜的裙摆，攥得拳头发麻，把祈祷投向头顶晃动的水面上最近的那片阳光。

paras.en: Anna billowed behind them, her hair trailing in the water like a paintbrush.
paras.zh: 安娜在他们身后漂荡，头发如画笔般拖在水中。

paras.en: Come on , Elsa thought, her knees pressing against the Water Spirit’s sides.
paras.zh: 快呀，艾莎想着，膝盖紧抵着水之精灵的两侧。

paras.en: Run like you’ve never run before.
paras.zh: “像你从未跑过那样奔跑。”

paras.en: The Water Nokk, as if hearing her plea, put on an extra burst of speed, and Elsa’s head and ribs ached with pressure as she began to go dizzy from lack of air.
paras.zh: 水马仿佛听到了她的恳求，又猛地加速，艾莎的头和肋骨因压力作痛，缺氧让她开始发晕。

paras.en: They were so close.
paras.zh: 他们如此接近了。

paras.en: So close— Finally the Water Spirit’s nose broke the surface, and Elsa pushed up from its back and clawed her way past the waves with one hand, so desperate to taste sweet air that she all but forgot her powers.
paras.zh: 如此接近——终于，水之精灵的鼻子破水而出，艾莎从它背上撑起，一只手扒开波浪，急切地想尝一口甜美的空气，几乎忘了自己的魔力。

paras.en: The moment her head was above the water, she sucked in a huge, burning breath, even as she pulled her sister up to the surface.
