paras.zh: 头一露出水面，她便猛吸一口灼烫的气息，同时把妹妹也拉出水面。

paras.en: Kristoff was there, and he and the sailors lifted Anna into the rowboat.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫就在那儿，他和水手们把安娜抬进划艇。

paras.en: Elsa clung to the side of the boat, watching as they laid her beloved sister on her side and smacked her back, trying to get the water out. “She was under a long time,” one of the sailors said apologetically. “Not too long,” Kristoff said fiercely. “It wasn’t too long.” Elsa’s body was numb, her feet limply kicking.
paras.zh: 艾莎扒着船舷，看他们把亲爱的妹妹侧放，拍着她的背，想把她肺里的水拍出来。“她在水下太久了，”一名水手歉疚地说。“不久，”克里斯托夫激烈地说，“不算久。”艾莎浑身麻木，双脚无力地踢着水。

paras.en: The Water Nokk floated beside her, mane spread out in the water.
paras.zh: 水马浮在她身旁，鬃毛在水中散开。

paras.en: The men turned Anna over, trying to force the water out of her lungs as Kristoff watched, feeling helpless, his heart in his eyes. “Let me have her,” he said, laying her down on the bottom of the rowboat as he pressed his mouth to Anna’s blue-tinged lips.
paras.zh: 男人们把安娜翻过来，想逼出她肺里的水，克里斯托夫望着，满眼无助、满眼心疼。“让我来，”他说，把她平放在艇底，嘴贴向安娜泛着青紫的唇。

paras.en: Kristoff tried as hard as he could to bring Anna back to him, forcing breath after breath into her.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫用尽全身力气想把安娜唤回，一口接一口地把气渡进她嘴里。

paras.en: For a long moment, nothing happened, but then Anna spat out the water she’d inhaled before drawing a surprised gulp of air. “Anna!” Kristoff pulled her into a bear hug, her hands curling around his middle. “Hey, hey, I’m okay,” she said with a shaky laugh. “A little wet and cold, though.
paras.zh: 好一阵子毫无动静，随后安娜吐出呛进的水，惊讶地猛吸一口气。“安娜！”克里斯托夫把她紧紧熊抱，她的手环住他的腰。“嘿，嘿，我没事，”她带着发颤的笑说，“就是有点湿、有点冷。”

paras.en: Where’s Elsa?” “I’m here, Anna.” Elsa reached out a hand, and Anna grasped it. “I’m guessing you saved me?” “It was a group mission,” Elsa admitted, gesturing to all the sailors and Kristoff, as well as the Water Nokk. “Are you hurt?” “A little achy, and I don’t think I’ll want to go swimming for a while.
paras.zh: “艾莎呢？”“我在这儿，安娜。”艾莎伸出手，安娜握住。“我猜是你救了我？”“这是个集体任务，”艾莎坦言，指了指所有水手、克里斯托夫，还有水马。“你受伤了吗？”“有点酸痛，而且我想我一阵子都不想游泳了。”

paras.en: It’s cold down there!
paras.zh: “底下可真冷！”

paras.en: Do we have a blanket anywhere?” One of the sailors in another boat held his hand out to Elsa. “If you’ll come aboard, milady, we’ll get you all back onto the ship and into the captain’s quarters for blankets and hot drinks.
paras.zh: “咱们有毯子吗？”另一只艇上的一名水手向艾莎伸出手。“夫人，若您上我们的船，我们就把各位送回大船，进船长室取毯子和热饮。”

paras.en: Then we can take the beast down.” “Aye!” the sailors shouted, raising their fists.
paras.zh: “然后咱们把那怪物解决掉。”“好嘞！”水手们举拳高喊。

paras.en: Elsa swam over to the other boat, her wet skirts dragging her down and her chest aching from having held her breath so long.
paras.zh: 艾莎游向另一只艇，湿裙直往下坠，胸口因憋气太久而疼痛。

paras.en: A hot drink and dry clothes sounded like the fondest dream she’d ever had.
paras.zh: 热饮和干衣，听起来宛如她做过最甜美的梦。

paras.en: The sailors reached down and helped her into the boat, and she sat on the middle seat and pushed her sopping hair out of her face.
paras.zh: 水手们伸手把她拉上船，她坐到中间座位，把湿透的头发从脸上拨开。

paras.en: She wanted to be in the other boat with Anna, but it was clearly already too full.
paras.zh: 她想上另一只艇陪安娜，可那艇明显已经太挤了。

paras.en: As soon as she was settled, the sailors began rowing back toward the frigate, where Captain Jens and General Mattias waited at the top of the rope ladder to help them back aboard.
paras.zh: 她刚坐稳，水手们便划桨返回帆船，延斯船长和马蒂亚斯将军正等在绳梯顶端，帮他们回到船上。

paras.en: Several rowboats still floated near where the Kraken lurked, including the one with the rope tied tight to a ring, the attached harpoon sunk deep into the creature far below.
paras.zh: 几只划艇仍浮在北海巨妖潜伏处附近，包括那只绳紧系在环上、鱼叉深深扎入远处巨兽的艇。

paras.en: The sailors in those boats held their own harpoons at the ready, waiting for the royals of Arendelle to find safety on the bigger ship, their eyes sparking with whatever cruel rage came over those who hunted frightening beasts and knew their impossible quarry to be near.
paras.zh: 那些艇上的水手举着各自的鱼叉严阵以待，等阿伦黛尔王室上了大船安顿好，眼中燃起一种残忍的怒意——那是猎杀可怖巨兽、明知猎物近在咫尺的人才会有的。

paras.en: The water stirred gently, the tip of a tentacle breaching the surface as if hunting for something it had lost, and the sailors raised their harpoons and shouted warnings.
paras.zh: 水面轻轻荡漾，一条触手的尖端破水而出，仿佛在找寻失去的什么，水手们举起鱼叉，发出警告的呼喊。

paras.en: Now that Anna and Kristoff were safe and Elsa’s fear and urgency were ebbing away, she could sense the disquiet of the massive creature below.
paras.zh: 安娜和克里斯托夫既已安全，艾莎的恐惧与急切渐渐退去，她便能感到水下那庞大生灵的不安。

paras.en: It wasn’t angry, it wasn’t hungry.
paras.zh: 它既不愤怒，也不饥饿。

paras.en: It was hurt and confused, its body pulsing with pain where the harpoon was stuck. “We can’t leave it,” Elsa said, to herself and to the Water Spirit paddling in the sea beside her rowboat. “It doesn’t deserve this.” The Water Nokk tossed its mane and bugled an agreement, pawing at the waves and knocking the side of the rowboat with a hoof. “Control that beast afore we’re back in the drink!” one of the men barked.
paras.zh: 它受伤而困惑，鱼叉扎入的地方随痛楚一鼓一鼓。“我们不能丢下它，”艾莎对自己、也对划艇旁水中拨弄的水之精灵说，“它不该受这罪。”水马甩了甩鬃毛，嘶鸣以示认同，用蹄拨着浪，踢了下划艇船身。“在咱们重回水里之前，把那畜生管住！”一名汉子喝道。

paras.en: Elsa looked to where Anna was climbing up the rope ladder with Kristoff just behind, helping her navigate the wet, twisting rope as it banged against the side of the ship.
paras.zh: 艾莎望向安娜正攀绳梯而上、克里斯托夫紧跟在后扶着她，帮她对付那湿滑扭曲、不停撞着船身的绳索。

paras.en: Once they were both on the deck, General Mattias beckoned to Elsa, shouting, “Please, Your Highness!
paras.zh: 两人一上甲板，马蒂亚斯将军便向艾莎招手，喊道：“求您了，殿下！”

paras.en: I can’t protect you when you’re in the middle of the ocean!
paras.zh: “您在大海中央，我护不住您！”

paras.en: The danger isn’t over!
paras.zh: “危险还没结束！”

paras.en: The men still need to kill the monster!” But Elsa looked back to the Water Spirit. “No, the danger isn’t over,” she said.
paras.zh: “弟兄们还得宰了那怪物！”可艾莎回望水之精灵。“不，危险还没结束，”她说。

paras.en: Before anyone could stop her, she stood and dove back under the waves.
paras.zh: 没等谁拦住她，她站起身，再次扎入浪下。

paras.en: This time, she was ready for the brisk bite of the sea and the salt stinging her eyes.
paras.zh: 这回，她已准备好迎接海水凛冽的啮咬与咸涩刺眼的痛。

paras.en: The Water Nokk whinnied joyously and swam under her, its confident swiftness a relief to her exhausted body.
paras.zh: 水马欢快地嘶鸣，游到她身下，那份自信的迅捷让疲惫的她松了口气。

paras.en: Again tangling her fingers in the Water Spirit’s mane, calmer this time, Elsa let the horse take her where they both knew they needed to be.
paras.zh: 艾莎再次将手指缠进精灵鬃毛，这回更从容，任由马儿带她去两人都知该去的地方。

paras.en: With her loved ones safe, it was just Elsa in her element, accompanied by a spirit that seemed to understand her, that almost read her mind as they worked in tune.
paras.zh: 所爱之人皆已安全，此刻只剩艾莎在自己擅长的领域，伴着一个仿佛懂她、几乎能读懂她心思、与她默契同行的精灵。

paras.en: She wasn’t frantic, filled with terror for her sister.
paras.zh: 她不再慌乱，不再为妹妹恐惧。

paras.en: Now she could look about with curiosity, note the silvery shoal of fish flashing in a patch of sun and the stark, jagged wood of an old shipwreck jutting out of the murk.
paras.zh: 此刻她能好奇地四下张望，留意阳光下银光闪烁的鱼群，以及从幽暗中突兀伸出的老旧沉船那嶙峋的断木。

paras.en: As the Water Nokk took her deeper and deeper, she noticed they were following the line of rope tied to the rowboat above, pulled so taut that even the current couldn’t move it.
paras.zh: 水马带她越潜越深，她注意到他们正顺着系在上方划艇的绳索而下，那绳绷得极紧，连水流都推不动。

paras.en: As the Kraken came into view, Elsa saw its large, flat eye watching her in return, an alien presence that still carried its own curiosity.
paras.zh: 北海巨妖映入眼帘，艾莎看到它那只巨大扁平的眼也正望着她，一个异类的存在，仍带着自己的好奇。

paras.en: A tentacle rose, slow and careful, and the Water Spirit slowed and hung suspended in the water as the Kraken held out its appendage like a shy stranger waiting to make friends.
paras.zh: 一条触手缓缓而谨慎地升起，水之精灵也慢下来悬在水中，北海巨妖伸出附肢，像个羞怯的陌生人等待交友。

paras.en: Elsa was a little scared, but then again, she’d once been scared of Bruni and Gale and the Earth Giants, and now they were like fond cousins.
paras.zh: 艾莎有点害怕，可话说回来，她曾怕过布伦尼、盖尔和大地巨人，如今他们却像亲近的表亲。

paras.en: Slowly, carefully, she reached out and grasped the curled tip of the Kraken’s tentacle, feeling its restrained energy in the daintiness of its response.
paras.zh: 她缓缓地、小心翼翼地伸出手，握住北海巨妖触手蜷起的尖端，从它轻柔的回应中感到它克制的力量。

paras.en: This Kraken the sailors feared—it was still a being like any other, at turns inquisitive and defensive.
paras.zh: 水手们惧怕的这头北海巨妖——它仍是和其他生灵一样的存在，时而好奇，时而戒备。

paras.en: The tentacle gently tugged, and Elsa pushed off the Water Nokk and allowed the Kraken to pull her toward it.
paras.zh: 触手轻轻一拽，艾莎便离开水马，任由北海巨妖把她拉向自己。

paras.en: With her other hand, she prepared to hurl ice if needed, but something told her that wouldn’t be necessary.
paras.zh: 她另一只手备着，必要时便掷出冰，可某种直觉告诉她不必。

paras.en: The moment she saw it, she flinched.
paras.zh: 看清的那一刻，她缩了一下。

paras.en: The sailor’s harpoon was stuck deep in the Kraken’s tender flesh.
paras.zh: 水手的鱼叉深深扎在北海巨妖柔嫩的肉里。

paras.en: For all the creature’s mass and might, it didn’t know how to fight off this supremely human affliction.
paras.zh: 尽管这生灵身躯庞大、力大无穷，却不知如何挣脱这纯粹人类带来的苦痛。

paras.en: Releasing the Kraken’s tentacle, she swam to its side and grasped the harpoon, but it was pulled too taut from above.
paras.zh: 她松开巨妖的触手，游到它身侧抓住鱼叉，可上方拽得太紧。

paras.en: With a grunt of frustration, she created a sharp ice shard and used it to saw away at the rope until finally the tension broke and the length went slack and floated harmlessly in the shifting green.
paras.zh: 她懊恼地哼了一声，凝出一片锋利的冰刃，锯起绳索，直到张力终于断掉，整条绳松垮下来，在晃动的水绿中无害地漂浮。

paras.en: The Kraken seemed, somehow, to relax, and she almost imagined it sighing in relief.
paras.zh: 北海巨妖似乎莫名地放松了，她几乎想象它在如释重负地叹气。

paras.en: Now that it was free of the rope, Elsa grasped the harpoon and worked it back and forth, gingerly pulling the metal barb from the Kraken’s rubbery flesh.
paras.zh: 既已脱绳，艾莎握住鱼叉来回活动，小心翼翼地把金属倒钩从巨妖橡胶般的肉里拔出来。

paras.en: Under her ministrations, the creature’s skin shimmered with angry reds and purples as if expressing its pain.
paras.zh: 在她的照料下，那生灵的皮肉泛起愤怒的红与紫，仿佛在表达痛楚。

paras.en: She stopped tugging and briefly put a hand to its surface, patting it as if reassuring a frightened dog.
paras.zh: 她停下拉拽，把手轻轻贴上它的表皮，拍了拍，像安抚一只受惊的狗。

paras.en: When she finally pulled the hook free, the Kraken’s skin shivered with glittering pinks, as if the creature was smiling with rosy cheeks.
paras.zh: 当她终于把钩子拔出，北海巨妖的皮肉泛起闪亮的粉红，仿佛那生灵正红着脸微笑。

paras.en: Elsa dropped the harpoon, watching it float uselessly down to the unseen depths.
paras.zh: 艾莎丢下鱼叉，看它无助地沉向看不见的深处。

paras.en: The Kraken’s tentacle again appeared, sweetly brushing across her cheek in thanks.
paras.zh: 北海巨妖的触手又出现了，温柔地拂过她的脸颊，以示感谢。

paras.en: Elsa reached out to touch it in return.
paras.zh: 艾莎伸手回抚它。

paras.en: I’m sorry , she thought, hoping the creature might understand.
paras.zh: 对不起，她心想，但愿这生灵能明白。

paras.en: The tentacle softly moved to her boots, positioning itself underneath her and then pushing her through the water at a speed she found both exciting and terrifying.
paras.zh: 触手轻轻移到她的靴子下，托住她，然后以她既觉刺激又觉可怕的速度推她穿水而行。

paras.en: She’d been so focused on solving this riddle that she’d gone too long without air, but the Kraken seemed to understand her plight and was propelling her to the surface with enormous speed.
paras.zh: 她方才太专注于解这道谜题，屏息太久，可北海巨妖似乎懂她的困境，以惊人的速度送她浮向水面。

paras.en: Of course, it didn’t fully understand physics, and thus Elsa was sent rocketing out of the water like the dolphins she’d watched earlier, the Water Nokk leaping beside her and whinnying with fierce happiness.
paras.zh: 当然，它并不全然懂得物理，于是艾莎像她早先看到的海豚一般被射出水面，水马在她身旁跃起，嘶鸣着狂喜。

paras.en: As she looked down from midair, watching the sailors gape, Elsa threw out a hand and formed a little island of ice, landing neatly on her feet as only an ice queen could. “Hurry, milady!” one of the sailors called. “The beast has broken free of its tether, and it’ll be hungering for our blood more than ever!” “No!” At her harsh word, everyone looked at her, stunned. “The Kraken won’t hurt anyone else.
paras.zh: 她从半空俯瞰，看着水手们目瞪口呆，艾莎伸出一只手凝出一座小冰岛，如只有冰之女王才能做到的那样稳稳落足。“快，夫人！”一名水手喊，“那怪物挣脱束缚了，会比以往更渴求咱们的血！”“不！”她这一声厉喝，所有人都惊愕地看向她。“北海巨妖不会再伤任何人。”

paras.en: It is not to be hunted.
paras.zh: “它不该被猎杀。”

paras.en: This is its home, where we are the trespassers.
paras.zh: “这是它的家，我们才是闯入者。”

paras.en: This is not a place we claim as our own.
paras.zh: “这里不是我们宣称归属的地方。”

paras.en: I want this area marked on a map so that no other ship might accidentally strike the beast and end up with unnecessary loss of life.” “But what will we put on the map?” a sailor asked. “Say that it is off-limits, per the queen of Arendelle,” Anna told him. “That should be enough.” Smiling her appreciation of her sister’s understanding and support, Elsa said, “Now put away your harpoons, and let’s give the poor thing a wide berth.” When the sailors didn’t immediately respond, she sent a stream of water behind her little island, pushing it over to the ship’s side.
paras.zh: “我要这片海域标在地图上，好让别的船不会意外撞上这生灵，招致无谓的伤亡。”“可我们在地图上写什么？”一名水手问。“就写：禁区，奉阿伦黛尔女王之命，”安娜告诉他，“这就够了。”艾莎为妹妹的体谅与支持报以微笑，说：“现在收起你们的鱼叉，给这可怜的家伙留足空间。”水手们没有立刻照办，她便在小冰岛后推出一股水流，把它推到船舷边。

paras.en: Before beginning her climb up to the railing, she reached out for the Water Nokk, stroking its nose in thanks.
paras.zh: 攀上栏杆前，她伸手摸了摸水马，抚着它的鼻子道谢。

paras.en: The rope ladder scratched her hands, but soon Kristoff and General Mattias were pulling her up onto the deck.
paras.zh: 绳梯磨着她的手，但很快克里斯托夫和马蒂亚斯将军就把她拉上了甲板。

paras.en: Finally she stood on the wooden boards, dripping and surrounded by her family. “With all due respect, Your Highness, we should kill it,” Captain Jens said. “It’s dangerous.” “If you don’t understand something, it will always seem dangerous.
paras.zh: 她终于站上木板，浑身滴着水，被家人围在中央。“恕我直言，殿下，我们该杀了它，”延斯船长说，“它很危险。”“若你不了解一样东西，它便永远显得危险。”

paras.en: I know that better than anyone.
paras.zh: “这点我比谁都清楚。”

paras.en: But I comprehend the Kraken better now.
paras.zh: “可我现在更懂北海巨妖了。”

paras.en: It didn’t come here for a fight.
paras.zh: “它来这里不是为了打架。”

paras.en: This is its world, not ours.
paras.zh: “这是它的世界，不是我们的。”

paras.en: There’s so much out there that we don’t know about.
paras.zh: “外面有太多我们所不知的事物。”

paras.en: It deserves to live its life just as much as we do.” “I don’t like it—” Captain Jens began. “But the queen of Arendelle does,” Anna reminded him. “But aren’t you angry, Your Majesty?
paras.zh: “它和我们一样，有权过自己的生活。”“我不乐意——”延斯船长刚开口，“可阿伦黛尔女王乐意，”安娜提醒他。“可您不生气吗，陛下？”

paras.en: Don’t you want revenge?
paras.zh: “您不想复仇吗？”

paras.en: It almost killed you!” Anna reached for Elsa’s hands. “My sister is right.
paras.zh: “它差点害死您！”安娜伸手握住艾莎的手。“我姐姐说得对。”

paras.en: Things are only dangerous when we don’t understand them.
paras.zh: “只有在我们不懂时，事物才显得危险。”

paras.en: It didn’t hurt me; it was trying to understand me.
paras.zh: “它没伤我；它只是想弄懂我。”

paras.en: And luckily, Elsa knew exactly what to do.” Frode hurried over with two blankets, rough but clean, and the sisters wrapped themselves up and took the hot tea Halima brought up from belowdecks.
paras.zh: “而且幸好，艾莎完全知道该怎么做。”弗罗德匆匆拿来两条毯子，粗糙却干净，姐妹俩裹上，接过哈利玛从下层舱端上来的热茶。

paras.en: As they sailed away, the old sea dogs shaken and the young sailors still telling tales that would only grow with time, Anna went to the front of the ship with Kristoff to wait for Liljeby to appear on the horizon.
paras.zh: 他们扬帆离去，老水手们心有余悸，年轻水手仍在讲述那些只会随岁月膨胀的传说，安娜和克里斯托夫走到船头，等待利耶比出现在地平线上。

paras.en: But Elsa turned back to gaze at the sea behind them, their fight with the Kraken unmarked, just another empty swatch of lonely water.
paras.zh: 可艾莎转过身，凝望身后的大海，他们与北海巨妖的战斗没留下任何痕迹，只是一片空寂、孤寥的水域。

paras.en: As she watched the white foam trail behind the frigate, a lone tentacle, shimmering white, emerged from the emerald-green sea as if waving goodbye.
paras.zh: 她望着帆船后拖出的白色泡沫尾迹，一条孤单的触手，泛着微光的白，从翠绿的海中升起，仿佛在挥手道别。

paras.en: Elsa smiled and waved back.
paras.zh: 艾莎微笑着，挥手回应。

paras.en: General Destin Mattias had a problem.
paras.zh: 戴斯汀·马提亚斯将军遇到了一个难题。

paras.en: To be fair, it wasn’t as big a problem as being trapped on the wrong side of an invisible magical wall of mist for thirty-four years.
paras.zh: 公平地说，这难题总比被一道无形的魔法迷雾墙困在错误的一边长达三十四年要小得多。

paras.en: But right at the moment, sitting on a dock in Arendelle’s harbor, it felt every bit as impenetrable, as insurmountable, as… “Hopeless,” said Olaf. “That’s exactly how you look right now.” The snowman plopped down on the dock next to the general. “I’m very good at reading faces,” he explained proudly. “Your face is doing a sort of everything-is-hopeless-and-things-couldn’t-be-any-worse expression.” Mattias sighed and hung his head. “Is it that obvious?” Olaf nodded. “Don’t worry,” he said. “I’ve observed that problems around here usually resolve if you sing and dance about them.” “That’s just it,” said Mattias. “I can’t dance.” “That’s silly,” said Olaf. “ Everybody can dance.” “Everybody but me ,” said Mattias.
paras.zh: 但此刻，他坐在阿伦黛尔海港的栈桥上，却觉得这难题同样难以逾越、同样无法克服，也同样……“没希望，”雪宝说，“你现在看起来就是这样。”雪人一屁股坐在将军身旁的栈桥上。“我可擅长读脸了，”他得意地解释道，“你脸上的表情分明在说：一切都完了，情况糟得不能再糟了。”马提亚斯叹了口气，垂下了头。“有这么明显吗？”雪宝点点头。“别担心，”他说，“我观察到，这附近的难题只要唱唱歌、跳跳舞，通常就能解决。”“问题就在这，”马提亚斯说，“我不会跳舞。”“那可真傻，”雪宝说，“谁都会跳舞。”“除了我，人人都会。”马提亚斯说。

paras.en: When the snowman raised his eyebrows, he continued. “I never had time to learn.
paras.zh: 雪人扬起眉毛，他便接着说：“我从来没时间学。”

paras.en: I was too busy surviving in the Enchanted Forest.
paras.zh: 我忙着在魔法森林里活下来，实在抽不出空。

paras.en: I had my soldiers to look after.” “I see,” said Olaf.
paras.zh: 我得照看我的士兵们。”“我明白了，”雪宝说。

paras.en: He considered this further and exclaimed, “But that means you can’t dance at the midsummer festival!” “Exactly.” “But won’t Halima expect you to dance with her?” “Exactly.” “Oh,” said Olaf. “I’d feel hopeless too if after waiting thirty-four years to rekindle a romance with the love of my life I disappointed her on a special occasion with everyone watching.” Olaf was attempting to be sympathetic.
paras.zh: 他进一步琢磨了一番，叫道：“可那就意味着你没法在仲夏节舞会上跳舞了！”“正是。”“可哈丽玛不指望你邀她跳舞吗？”“正是。”“噢，”雪宝说，“换作是我，等了三十四年才要和此生挚爱重续前缘，却要在众目睽睽的重要场合让她失望，我也会觉得没希望。”雪宝是想表现得有点同理心。

paras.en: Unfortunately, the snowman had a habit of stating the obvious in a way that sometimes lacked tact.
paras.zh: 不幸的是，雪人有个习惯，总把明摆着的事直说出来，有时不免缺了点分寸。

paras.en: The general was used to how Olaf spoke, but even so, he hung his head lower than before.
paras.zh: 将军早已习惯雪宝说话的方式，但即便如此，他还是把头垂得比先前更低了。

paras.en: Olaf realized he wasn’t making things better and tried to be helpful. “But couldn’t you learn to dance?” he suggested. “I’ve tried,” said Mattias. “The problem is that I’ve got two left feet.” Olaf had never heard of such a thing. “Really?
paras.zh: 雪宝意识到自己没帮上忙，便想出点力。“可你难道不能学跳舞吗？”他提议道。“我试过了，”马提亚斯说，“问题是我有‘两只左脚’。”雪宝从没听过这种说法。“真的吗？

paras.en: That’s incredible!” he exclaimed. “I didn’t know it was possible.” He peered in wonder at Mattias’s legs where they dangled over the docks.
paras.zh: 太不可思议了！”他惊呼，“我还不知道这居然可能。”他惊奇地盯着马提亚斯悬在栈桥边的双腿。

paras.en: Then a new thought occurred to him. “Do I have two left feet, too?” The snowman looked down.
paras.zh: 这时他冒出一个新念头。“我是不是也有两只左脚？”雪人低头看了看。

paras.en: He couldn’t see his own feet very well, so he leapt a little distance into the air.
paras.zh: 他看不太清自己的脚，于是轻轻一跃跳到半空。

paras.en: His snowballs all detached from one another, and he brought his feet to the front where he could see them.
paras.zh: 他的雪球身体全都散了开来，他把脚挪到眼前能看见的地方。

paras.en: For an instant, they were just two little round orbs floating free.
paras.zh: 有那么一瞬，它们只是两个自由漂浮的小圆球。

paras.en: Then Olaf reassembled and landed in one piece on the dock. “It’s disconcertingly hard to tell my feet apart,” he said in a flat voice. “I see that I don’t have any toes.
paras.zh: 然后雪宝重新拼好，稳稳落在栈桥上。“要把我的脚区分开还真是难得出奇，”他面无表情地说，“而且我发现我连脚趾头都没有。

paras.en: Perhaps I should speak to Elsa about that.” Then Olaf brightened.
paras.zh: 或许我该跟艾莎说说这事。”接着雪宝眼睛一亮。

paras.en: The left snowfoot rolled over to bump against its companion. “Now I’ve got two right feet,” he said with a giggle.
paras.zh: 左脚雪球滚过去撞了撞它的伙伴。“现在我变成两只右脚啦。”他咯咯地笑。

paras.en: However, having both feet to one side made him unbalanced.
paras.zh: 可两脚都偏在一边，让他失去了平衡。

paras.en: He tipped over to prevent himself from falling, but he swayed anyway and spun around to pitch toward the water instead.
paras.zh: 他为了不摔倒往一侧歪，却还是晃了起来，转着圈朝水边倒去。

paras.en: General Mattias reached out quickly and caught Olaf, saving him from a splash.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯将军迅速伸手接住雪宝，让他免遭落水。

paras.en: The snowman smiled and then frowned. “But it’s your feet that’re the problem.
paras.zh: 雪人先笑后皱眉。“可问题的症结在你脚上。

paras.en: Fortunately for you, I’m very good at fixing problems.
paras.zh: 幸好你运气不错，我特别擅长解决问题。

paras.en: If only we could swap your feet out with new ones.” Mattias looked back at the village, and then his gaze turned to the mountains and the waterfall that spilled down into the sea. “You know, there used to be a local legend, back when King Runeard first started construction on Arendelle Castle.
paras.zh: 要是能把你的脚换上一双新的就好了。”马提亚斯回头望了望村庄，目光又转向群山和倾泻入海的那道瀑布。“你知道吗，当年鲁内拉德国王刚开始建造阿伦黛尔城堡的时候，这里有过一个本地传说。

paras.en: About a song that people heard in the mountains that made them dance.
paras.zh: 说的是人们在山里听到一首歌，听了就会翩翩起舞。

paras.en: I could use a little of that song now.” “That’s silly,” said Olaf. “We don’t need a story from ancient days.
paras.zh: 此刻我倒真想有点那样的歌。” “那可真傻，”雪宝说，“咱们不需要什么古代的故事。

paras.en: We need a real-life solution.” The snowman removed one of his arms and used it to tap his head. “Think-think-think,” he said. “Since we can’t swap your feet out, we’ll just have to find you the right dance instructor.” “A dance instructor?” said Mattias, who wasn’t sure he liked where the conversation was going. “I’m sure in all of Arendelle, there’s someone who knows a dance that works with two left feet.” “No, Olaf, two left feet—it’s an expression,” replied Mattias, but the snowman was already bounding across the village square toward the houses, imbued with new purpose.
paras.zh: 我们需要的是现实可行的办法。”雪人卸下一条手臂，用它敲着自己的脑袋。“想想想想，”他说，“既然换不了脚，那咱们就只能给你找个合适的舞蹈老师了。”“舞蹈老师？”马提亚斯说，他不太确定这场对话会往哪儿发展。“我敢说整个阿伦黛尔，总有人懂一种适合‘两只左脚’的舞步。”“不，雪宝，‘两只左脚’——那是个比喻，”马提亚斯答道，可雪人已经朝着村庄广场上的房屋蹦跳而去，浑身充满了新的干劲。

paras.en: The general sighed again. “What am I getting myself into?” he wondered. “A dance instructor!
paras.zh: 将军又叹了口气。“我到底在掺和什么呀？”他暗想，“舞蹈老师！

paras.en: Ha!” He turned his gaze back to the mountains.
paras.zh: 哈！”他把目光转回群山。

paras.en: There had been a story.
paras.zh: 当年确有其事。

paras.en: The talk of magical music had displeased King Runeard, so he took several of his officers to investigate.
paras.zh: 关于魔法音乐的传闻惹恼了鲁内拉德国王，于是他带了几名军官前去调查。

paras.en: Mattias was a young officer candidate then and not even a lieutenant, so he wasn’t selected for the mission.
paras.zh: 那时马提亚斯还是个年轻的军官候补生，连中尉都不是，所以没被选入那支队伍。

paras.en: When Runeard came back, the king announced that they hadn’t found anything.
paras.zh: 鲁内拉德回来后，国王宣称他们什么也没发现。

paras.en: But no one heard the music after that.
paras.zh: 但从那以后，就再没人听到过那音乐。

paras.en: Olaf was right.
paras.zh: 雪宝说得对。

paras.en: It was better to keep your feet on the ground, deal with matters in real life.
paras.zh: 脚踏实地点，处理现实中的事情才是正道。

paras.en: Rising, Mattias shook himself off.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯站起身，抖了抖身子。

paras.en: He headed back toward Arendelle Castle.
paras.zh: 他朝阿伦黛尔城堡走去。

paras.en: He had things to do.
paras.zh: 他还有事情要做。

paras.en: Always a pragmatic man who put the needs of the kingdom first, he tried to shove his concern down deep inside himself where it wouldn’t get in the way of his duty.
paras.zh: 他向来是个务实的人，把王国需要放在首位，于是尽量把这份担忧深深压在心底，免得妨碍公务。

paras.en: After all, he had an important meeting with Queen Anna.
paras.zh: 毕竟，他还要和安娜女王有个重要会面。

paras.en: Sven the reindeer had just begun to enjoy a bowl of herbs and moss.
paras.zh: 驯鹿斯文刚刚开始享用一碗香草和苔藓。

paras.en: It had a pleasing garnish of lichens and fungi, which added flavor and made it nicely crunchy.
paras.zh: 碗上点缀着地衣和菌类，看着赏心悦目，还增添了风味，嚼起来脆生生的。

paras.en: Suddenly Olaf burst into his stable. “Sven,” cried the snowman, “I need your help on a matter of utmost importance!” The reindeer lifted his head in a start, accidentally tossing his vegetation into the air.
paras.zh: 忽然，雪宝冲进了他的棚屋。“斯文，”雪人喊道，“有件顶要紧的事我需要你帮忙！”驯鹿猛地抬起头，不小心把嘴里的草料甩到了半空。

paras.en: The bowl rose and fell with a crash.
paras.zh: 碗升起又落下，哐当一声摔碎了。

paras.en: Bits of his meal landed all over the ground.
paras.zh: 饭菜的碎块撒了一地。

paras.en: The reindeer widened his eyes in alarm.
paras.zh: 驯鹿惊得睁大了眼睛。

paras.en: Together with Anna, Elsa, Kristoff, and Olaf, Sven had already climbed the North Mountain and braved the Enchanted Forest, confronted angry snowmen and capricious elemental spirts, outrun Earth Giants, and faced countless other dangers.
paras.zh: 此前，斯文曾和安娜、艾莎、克里斯托夫、雪宝一起登上北山、闯过魔法森林，直面愤怒的雪人和喜怒无常的元素精灵，甩开大地巨人，还经历了无数其他险境。

paras.en: Whatever Olaf needed, the bravest reindeer of them all was ready for it. “General Mattias can’t dance!” the snowman exclaimed.
paras.zh: 无论雪宝需要什么，这群伙伴中最勇敢的驯鹿都准备好了。“马提亚斯将军不会跳舞！”雪人惊叫道。

paras.en: Sven’s eyes narrowed as if he’d been expecting something more urgent.
paras.zh: 斯文眯起眼睛，仿佛本以为会更紧急些。

paras.en: Then the reindeer looked around the floor where the remains of his lunch were scattered.
paras.zh: 接着驯鹿环顾地面，那里散落着他午饭的残骸。

paras.en: All wasted now.
paras.zh: 现在全都白费了。

paras.en: His big lips huffed a puff of air in frustration. “No, this is serious, I promise,” said Olaf.
paras.zh: 他的大嘴唇懊恼地呼出一口气。“不，这回是认真的，我保证。”雪宝说。

paras.en: Sven gave Olaf a skeptical look. “It is,” Olaf insisted. “I know.
paras.zh: 斯文用怀疑的眼神看了看雪宝。“真的是，”雪宝坚持道，“我知道。

paras.en: I am an expert when it comes to affairs of the heart.” Sven’s skeptical look deepened. “If Mattias can’t dance with Halima at the midsummer festival,” explained Olaf, “then he’ll disappoint his one true love.” That got Sven’s attention, and the reindeer forgot all about his food.
paras.zh: 论起感情的事，我可是专家。”斯文的怀疑更深了。“要是马提亚斯在仲夏节舞会上不能和哈丽玛跳舞，”雪宝解释道，“那他就会辜负他此生唯一的真爱。”这话引起了斯文的注意，驯鹿顿时把食物忘到了脑后。

paras.en: The snowman wasn’t the only expert in affairs of the heart.
paras.zh: 雪人可不是唯一一个懂感情的专家。

paras.en: After all, it had been Sven who had helped a fumbling, insecure Kristoff propose to Anna.
paras.zh: 毕竟，当初帮笨手笨脚、满心不安的克里斯托夫向安娜求婚的，正是斯文。

paras.en: And look how well that had turned out.
paras.zh: 而你看后来结果多好。

paras.en: Clearly, something needed to be done here.
paras.zh: 显然，眼前这件事得有人出手。

paras.en: Something that called for two experts in human romance.
paras.zh: 这件事需要两位恋爱专家合力。

paras.en: But what?
paras.zh: 可具体该怎么办呢？

paras.en: Olaf raced out of the door, and Sven trotted after him. “We’ve got to find the best dance instructor in Arendelle,” the snowman explained.
paras.zh: 雪宝冲出门外，斯文小跑着跟上。“咱们得找到阿伦黛尔最棒的舞蹈老师，”雪人解释道。

paras.en: Sven nodded.
paras.zh: 斯文点了点头。

paras.en: That made sense. “One who knows a dance that works with two left feet,” said Olaf.
paras.zh: 这说得通。“一位懂那种适合‘两只左脚’的舞步的老师，”雪宝说。

paras.en: That made less sense.
paras.zh: 这就没那么说得通了。

paras.en: However, Olaf was already heading across the courtyard toward the castle bridge, so Sven scooped him up in his antlers, and together they raced toward Market Square and help!
paras.zh: 不过，雪宝已经穿过庭院朝城堡桥奔去，于是斯文用鹿角把他挑起来，俩人一起朝集市广场冲去搬救兵！

paras.en: Mattias met Queen Anna in the courtyard of the castle.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯在城堡庭院里见到了安娜女王。

paras.en: He had a lot of important ideas concerning security for the upcoming midsummer festival.
paras.zh: 关于即将到来的仲夏节安保，他有一大堆重要的想法。

paras.en: Arendelle had faced its share of threats, and while things had been quiet of late, one could never be too careful.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔经历过不少威胁，虽说近来风平浪静，但小心永远不为过。

paras.en: Sometimes quiet times were just the calm before a storm.
paras.zh: 有时平静不过是暴风雨前的安宁。

paras.en: It was always good to be prepared.
paras.zh: 有备无患总是好的。

paras.en: The two of them strode across the flagstones while Mattias detailed his plans. “We will have guards in each corner of the square,” he explained. “Very good,” said Anna. “That’s in addition to the ones on the walls.” “Of course,” said Anna. “And I could put a man in the clock tower.” “If you really think it’s necessary,” said Anna. “To keep watch over the town itself from that vantage point.
paras.zh: 两人迈步走过石板路，马提亚斯细细说明他的计划。“广场每个角落都要布岗，”他解释道。“很好，”安娜说，“那是墙上哨兵之外的补充。”“当然，”马提亚斯坦然道，“我还可以在钟楼上安排一个人。”“如果你真觉得有必要，”安娜说，“从那个制高点俯瞰整座城镇。

paras.en: And of course, we’ll patrol the outer walls.” Anna stopped walking and laid a hand on the general’s arm. “General, we’re allied with Vesterland.
paras.zh: 当然，我们还会巡逻外墙。”安娜停下脚步，把手搭在将军手臂上。“将军，我们和维斯特兰是盟友了。

paras.en: Elsa is our bridge to the spirits in the Enchanted Forest.
paras.zh: 艾莎是我们与魔法森林里精灵之间的桥梁。

paras.en: We’ve made peace with the pirates.
paras.zh: 我们和海盗也讲和了。

paras.en: Arendelle is on good terms with Zaria, Chatho, and Vakretta.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔与扎利亚、查托、瓦克雷塔都关系友好。

paras.en: Even Weselton has been behaving.
paras.zh: 连韦塞尔顿都安分守己了。

paras.en: I appreciate all you and your soldiers do for me, for Arendelle, but it’s the midsummer festival.
paras.zh: 我很感激你和你士兵们为我、为阿伦黛尔所做的一切，可这毕竟是仲夏节。

paras.en: Don’t your soldiers need a break as well?
paras.zh: 你的士兵们不也需要歇一歇吗？

paras.en: Midsummer is a time to relax, to enjoy yourself, to get your knees up, as they say.” “Knees up?” said Mattias. “You know,” said Anna, lifting her feet enthusiastically. “Dancing.” Mattias turned his face away and swallowed. “Now that I think about it,” he said, “maybe I could take the post up in the clock tower myself.” “General,” said Anna. “Mattias,” she added, using his name to make sure she had his attention. “Is there a reason you don’t want to be at the midsummer festival?” “No, why would you say that?” stammered Mattias. “Why wouldn’t someone want to be there?
paras.zh: 仲夏节是用来放松、享乐、‘提起膝盖’的时光，就像人们说的那样。”“提起膝盖？”马提亚斯说。“你懂的，”安娜兴致勃勃地抬起脚，“就是跳舞嘛。”马提亚斯转过脸去，咽了口唾沫。“现在想想，”他说，“也许我可以亲自去钟楼上那个岗。”“将军，”安娜说，“马提亚斯，”她又唤了他的名字，好确保他听进去，“你是不是有什么理由不想参加仲夏节？”“没、没有，你怎么会这么问？”马提亚斯结巴道，“谁会不想去呢？

paras.en: It’s a very important tradition.
paras.zh: 这可是非常重要的传统。

paras.en: At least I think it is.
paras.zh: 至少我觉得是。

paras.en: One which I’ve not been a part of in decades, being trapped in an Enchanted Forest, not being here to partake, to learn, to…” His voice trailed off. “Right,” said Anna. “I understand.
paras.zh: 一个我因被困魔法森林几十年都没能参与的传统，没在这里分享、去学习、去……”他的声音低了下去。“明白了，”安娜说，“我懂。

paras.en: You’ve missed a lot.
paras.zh: 你错过了很多。

paras.en: You need to make up for lost time.
paras.zh: 你需要把失去的时间补回来。

paras.en: Not hide up in the clock tower away from us all.
paras.zh: 而不是躲进钟楼，远离我们大家。

paras.en: You and your staff deserve to enjoy the festival, too.” She held up a hand before the general could object. “You could implement a rotation, let your soldiers join the festival in shifts.
paras.zh: 你和你的部下也该享受这个节日。”将军还没开口反对，她便抬手制止。“你可以实行轮岗，让你的士兵分批参加节庆。

paras.en: Doesn’t Halima need a date for the big dance?” “Yes, she does,” said the general.
paras.zh: 哈丽玛不也需要个舞伴参加大舞会吗？”“是的，她需要，”将军说。

paras.en: For a second, he let his military bearing drop, and his shoulders slumped. “One who can actually dance.” Then Mattias remembered himself and stood up very straight, hardly breathing.
paras.zh: 有那么一瞬，他卸下了军人姿态，肩膀垮了下来。“一个真能跳舞的舞伴。”接着马提亚斯回过神来，挺得笔直，几乎屏住了呼吸。

paras.en: Oops.
paras.zh: 哎呀。

paras.en: Did I say that?
paras.zh: 我说出口了？

paras.en: I didn’t say that, he thought. “Oh,” said Anna.
paras.zh: 我没说，他心想。“噢，”安娜说。

paras.en: She had a quick mind and realized instantly what this was about. “I’m sure Halima will understand.
paras.zh: 她脑筋转得快，立刻明白了怎么回事。“我敢说哈丽玛会理解的。

paras.en: When you like someone, you like them for who they are inside.
paras.zh: 喜欢一个人，是喜欢他内在的那个他。

paras.en: Little things like this aren’t important.
paras.zh: 这种小事并不重要。

paras.en: And I know Halima thinks you’re wonderful.” “That’s just it.
paras.zh: 而且我知道哈丽玛觉得你很棒。”“问题就在这。

paras.en: She waited for me all those years.
paras.zh: 她等了我那么多年。

paras.en: What if I’m not as wonderful as she thinks I am?” “That’s not possible.” “If you say so,” said Mattias, but he didn’t seem convinced. “I do say so.
paras.zh: 要是我没她想的那么好呢？”“那不可能。”“既然你这么说，”马提亚斯说，可他似乎并不信服。“我确实这么认为。

paras.en: I say that as your queen… and as your friend.” “Dance instructors incoming!” Olaf’s shout rang out across the courtyard, frightening a pair of rock pigeons into the air.
paras.zh: 我是以你女王的身份这么说……也是以你朋友的身份。”“舞蹈老师来啦！”雪宝的喊声在庭院里回荡，惊得一对岩鸽飞上了天。

paras.en: Mattias and Anna turned in unison.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯和安娜齐刷刷转过头。

paras.en: In marched Sven, with Olaf riding between his antlers.
paras.zh: 斯文阔步进来，雪宝骑在他鹿角之间。

paras.en: Both reindeer and snowman puffed their chests out proudly.
paras.zh: 驯鹿和雪人都骄傲地挺起胸膛。

paras.en: They appeared very pleased with themselves.
paras.zh: 他们看起来对自己相当满意。

paras.en: Behind them came a procession of villagers. “Olaf, what is this?” asked Anna. “Oh, hi, Anna.
paras.zh: 他们身后跟着一队村民。“雪宝，这是怎么回事？”安娜问。“噢，嗨，安娜。

paras.en: Mattias told me that he can’t dance because he has two left feet.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯跟我说他不会跳舞，因为他有‘两只左脚’。

paras.en: So I rounded up a troop of villagers.
paras.zh: 所以我召集了一队村民。

paras.en: They each have a different dance to teach him.
paras.zh: 他们每人都会一种不同的舞，可以教他。

paras.en: I’m sure one of them will work no matter what kind of feet you have!” Anna looked bemused and impressed, and Mattias looked skeptical, but a determined snowman was not someone who could easily be deterred. “Instructors, present!” shouted Olaf.
paras.zh: 我敢说不管你长着什么样的脚，总有一种管用！”安娜又觉好笑又佩服，马提亚斯则一脸怀疑，可一个下定决心的雪人可不是那么容易打发的。“老师们，亮相！”雪宝喊道。

paras.en: He and Sven snapped to attention as the villagers came forward.
paras.zh: 他和斯文啪地立正，村民们走上前来。

paras.en: Olaf marched down the line as if Mattias weren’t the only general present.
paras.zh: 雪宝沿着队伍巡视，仿佛在场的将军不止马提亚斯一个。

paras.en: He pulled off one of his arms and used it as a pointing stick. “Mrs.
paras.zh: 他卸下一条手臂，拿它当指示棒。“布洛杰特夫人——

paras.en: Blodget is here to teach a traditional country dance,” the snowman explained.
paras.zh: 是来教传统乡村舞的，”雪人解释道。

paras.en: Beside him, Mrs.
paras.zh: 他身旁，布洛杰特夫人——

paras.en: Blodget curtsied politely.
paras.zh: 优雅地行了个屈膝礼。

paras.en: But when Olaf snapped his fingers on his disembodied hand, she leapt back to attention. “Anders knows a polka,” Olaf continued, indicating the fish merchant, who bowed. “Persi and Aggie will demonstrate a waltz.
paras.zh: 可当雪宝用那只离了身的手打了个响指，她又立刻绷直站好。“安德斯会跳波尔卡，”雪宝接着说，指了指那位鞠躬的鱼贩，“珀西和阿吉会展示华尔兹。

paras.en: Noa and Maja have a hora, a traditional wedding dance, in case anyone is feeling matrimonial.” Olaf brought a hand to his mouth and whispered much too loudly, “I don’t think that’s going to come up, but it’s all they know .” Then he continued in a normal tone of voice. “Tilda and Niels have a mazurka.
paras.zh: 诺亚和玛雅会跳霍拉舞，一种传统婚礼舞，万一谁有结婚的兴致呢。”雪宝把手凑到嘴边，大得离谱地小声嘀咕：“我看这用不上，可他们就会这个。”接着他用正常的嗓音继续说，“蒂尔达和尼尔斯会跳玛祖卡。

paras.en: And Oaken will demonstrate a stick dance.” The owner of Wandering Oaken’s Trading Post and Sauna stepped forward. “Ja, it can be done with sticks or canes, but I find it’s always better with swords!” Oaken produced two blades from somewhere behind himself and waved them about in the air.
paras.zh: 还有欧肯会展示棍舞。”漫游欧肯杂货店与桑拿馆的老板走上前来。“呀，可以用棍子或手杖跳，不过我发现用剑总归更好！”欧肯不知从身后何处抽出两把刀，在空中挥舞起来。

paras.en: Several villagers jumped back quickly, and Olaf’s head bounced above his torso, sparing him an accidental decapitation.
paras.zh: 几名村民慌忙后退，雪宝的脑袋在他身体上方弹了一下，免遭误伤断头。

paras.en: General Mattias held out his hands placatingly. “This really isn’t necessary.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯将军安抚地伸出双手。“这真的不必。

paras.en: Especially not the swords.” He turned to Anna. “Your Majesty, please explain to them that we have important business to discuss.” “Actually,” said Anna with a giggle, “I think we were about done.
paras.zh: 尤其是剑就免了。”他转向安娜。“陛下，请您跟他们说明，我们还有要事商议。”“其实，”安娜咯咯一笑，“我想我们刚谈完。

paras.en: I need to go supervise the dessert selection, starting with the chocolates.” She turned toward the castle doors. “Please…” said Mattias.
paras.zh: 我得去监督甜点挑选了，先从巧克力看起。”她转向城堡大门。“求你了……”马提亚斯说。

paras.en: But Anna was already halfway across the courtyard. “Have fun,” she called back over a shoulder. “That’s an order.
paras.zh: 可安娜已经走到庭院一半。“玩得开心，”她回头越过肩膀喊道，“这是命令。

paras.en: But do try to remember what I told you.” Mattias nodded, turning back to Olaf and his companions. “Go easy on me,” he said. “Easy?” said Oaken. “You know the saying: ‘A good anvil does not fear the hammer.’” Mattias looked at the wall of determined faces—young, old, furry, and frozen.
paras.zh: 但千万记得我跟你说的。”马提亚斯点点头，转回雪宝和伙伴们面前。“对我手下留情，”他说。“留情？”欧肯说，“你听过那句谚语吧：‘好铁砧不怕锤子敲。’”马提亚斯望着那面坚定的面孔墙——年轻的、年长的、毛茸茸的、冻住的。

paras.en: He thought he saw a lot of hammers in their eyes. “Wonderful,” he said with a gulp. “They say that things are supposed to look fonder in hindsight,” said Olaf. “But looking back on yesterday, I’m not so sure that’s true.
paras.zh: 他觉得在他们眼里看到了许多把锤子。“太好了，”他咽了口唾沫说。“人们说往事回看总会更美好，”雪宝说，“可回想起昨天，我不太确定那是真的。

paras.en: I’m still surprised by how badly everything went.” Sven nodded sadly.
paras.zh: 我还是对昨天一切搞砸成那样感到惊讶。”斯文难过地点点头。

paras.en: The villagers’ attempts to teach Mattias their dances had not gone as expected.
paras.zh: 村民们想教马提亚斯跳舞的尝试，并没有如预期那样顺利。

paras.en: In fact, it had nearly resulted in the general slicing off his own feet.
paras.zh: 事实上，差点让将军把自己的脚给削了。

paras.en: Oaken’s sword dancing was definitely not for beginners.
paras.zh: 欧肯的剑舞绝对不适合初学者。

paras.en: Or maybe for anyone but Oaken.
paras.zh: 或许除了欧肯，谁都不适合。

paras.en: The other dances hadn’t been as potentially life-threatening, but they hadn’t worked well, either.
paras.zh: 其他舞没那么危及性命，但同样也没教成。

paras.en: The snowman and the reindeer were trudging through the Enchanted Forest.
paras.zh: 雪人和驯鹿正步履沉重地走在魔法森林里。

paras.en: Having exhausted all potential dance instructors in Arendelle, Olaf had decided to widen their search.
paras.zh: 雪宝已经试遍了阿伦黛尔所有潜在的舞蹈老师，于是决定扩大搜索范围。

paras.en: If Arendellian dances didn’t account for two left feet, maybe someone somewhere else knew a dance that would.
paras.zh: 如果阿伦黛尔的舞步都没考虑‘两只左脚’，也许别处的某人懂一种能对付的舞。

paras.en: The trolls of the Valley of the Living Rock had been enthusiastic, but even Olaf could tell that their own dance moves involved too much rocking and rolling for a person who wasn’t made of stone to safely master.
paras.zh: 活石谷的地精们倒是热情，可连雪宝都看得出，他们自己的舞步滚来晃去太厉害，不是石头做的人根本没法安全学会。

paras.en: The midsummer festival was just days away, and they were running out of time.
paras.zh: 仲夏节只剩几天了，他们时间紧迫。

paras.en: Olaf rarely felt down for long, but he cared about his friends.
paras.zh: 雪宝很少会低落太久，可他在乎朋友们。

paras.en: Because of this, he was so preoccupied with concern that it took him a moment to realize he was humming.
paras.zh: 正因如此，他心事重重，好一会儿才意识到自己在哼歌。

paras.en: Beside him, Sven had changed his steps from a trot to a rather merry canter.
paras.zh: 身旁的斯文把步子从小跑换成了相当欢快的慢跑。

paras.en: Olaf looked at the reindeer’s hooves.
paras.zh: 雪宝盯着驯鹿的蹄子。

paras.en: There was something about the way Sven was moving that had an odd rhythm to it.
paras.zh: 斯文移动的方式里，透出一种奇怪的节奏。

paras.en: Step-step-jump.
Step-step-jump.
It was funny.
paras.zh: 真有意思。

paras.en: Then Olaf heard something.
paras.zh: 这时雪宝听到了什么。

paras.en: A faint sound, carried on the summer breeze. “Is that music?” he asked.
paras.zh: 一阵微弱的声响，乘着夏日的微风而来。“那是音乐吗？”他问。

paras.en: Beside him, the reindeer’s fuzzy ears twitched.
paras.zh: 身旁的驯鹿毛茸茸的耳朵抖了抖。

paras.en: It was music.
paras.zh: 是音乐。

paras.en: It seemed to grow louder as they listened to it, as if the notes appreciated their attention and became more confident with an audience.
paras.zh: 那音乐仿佛随着他们聆听而越来越响，好似音符感激他们的关注，有了听众便更自信了。

paras.en: The music grew stronger still.
paras.zh: 音乐愈发强劲。

paras.en: It was such a jolly, jaunty, happy tune that Olaf couldn’t help feeling elated.
paras.zh: 那是如此欢快、轻俏、喜悦的曲调，雪宝不禁心花怒放。

paras.en: He saw it was affecting his companion beside him as well.
paras.zh: 他看出这曲子也影响了身旁的伙伴。

paras.en: The reindeer’s canter had changed.
paras.zh: 驯鹿的慢跑变了样。

paras.en: He was bouncing, stamping his hooves.
paras.zh: 他蹦跳着，跺着蹄子。

paras.en: Swinging in time with the notes. “Sven!” exclaimed Olaf, “You’re… dancing!” The reindeer’s face lit with surprise as he realized this as well.
paras.zh: 随着音符的节拍摇摆。“斯文！”雪宝惊呼，“你在……跳舞！”驯鹿也意识到这点，脸上闪过惊喜。

paras.en: He stopped moving suddenly, but then his feet began to twitch on their own.
paras.zh: 他猛地停下不动，可蹄子又自己抖动起来。

paras.en: Embarrassed, Sven pulled all four hooves together in a tight bunch from the knees down.
paras.zh: 斯文难为情地四条腿从膝盖往下紧紧并拢成一团。

paras.en: But his furry back end betrayed him.
paras.zh: 可他毛茸茸的后半身出卖了他。

paras.en: His reindeer rump started swaying to the music.
paras.zh: 他的驯鹿屁股随着音乐摇了起来。

paras.en: Then his hooves all jumped at once.
paras.zh: 接着他的四蹄齐刷刷弹起。

paras.en: It was clear Sven couldn’t help himself.
paras.zh: 显然斯文控制不住自己。

paras.en: In fact, the reindeer began to pirouette.
paras.zh: 事实上，驯鹿开始原地旋转起来。

paras.en: Olaf considered his friend for a moment. “Sven is dancing,” he said. “And Sven has two left feet.
paras.zh: 雪宝端详了朋友片刻。“斯文在跳舞，”他说，“而且斯文有‘两只左脚’。

paras.en: He has two right feet as well, but that’s not really pertinent to the situation.” Olaf grabbed Sven by the muzzle to steady him, but the reindeer couldn’t stop and instead Olaf was swept into the air as Sven twirled in circles. “We’ve been searching for the right dance,” the snowman explained. “But it’s not the dance, it’s the music .
paras.zh: 他也有‘两只右脚’，不过那跟眼下的情况没啥关系。”雪宝抓住斯文的口鼻想稳住他，可驯鹿停不下来，反倒随着斯文团团转，雪宝被甩到了半空。“我们一直在找对的舞，”雪人解释道，“可关键不在舞，而在音乐。

paras.en: Just like in Mattias’s story.
paras.zh: 就像马提亚斯讲的故事里那样。

paras.en: And this music works with two left feet.
paras.zh: 而这音乐对‘两只左脚’也管用。

paras.en: We’ve got to find it and bring it back to Arendelle.” He bounced onto the reindeer’s back. “Follow the music, Sven!
paras.zh: 我们得找到它，把它带回阿伦黛尔。”他蹦到驯鹿背上。“跟着音乐走，斯文！

paras.en: Follow the music!” Sven understood.
paras.zh: 跟着音乐走！”斯文明白了。

paras.en: The reindeer took off in the direction of the sound.
paras.zh: 驯鹿朝声音的方向奔去。

paras.en: Or rather, he tried to.
paras.zh: 或者说，他想朝那个方向去。

paras.en: He was attempting to gallop in a straight line, but his newfound fancy footwork was taking him all over the place.
paras.zh: 他想笔直地飞奔，可新得的花式步法把他带得东倒西歪。

paras.en: Sven swayed and glissaded back and forth across the hills and glades of the Enchanted Forest.
paras.zh: 斯文摇摇晃晃、滑步蹿跳，在魔法森林的山丘和林间空地间来回穿行。

paras.en: He two-stepped, he four-stepped, he sashayed.
paras.zh: 他走两步、走四步、又斜步滑行。

paras.en: At one point, when his hooves had a very different idea about direction than his head, Sven even bit a branch of a tree to pull himself along.
paras.zh: 有一回，他的蹄子对方向的主张和脑袋大相径庭，斯文竟咬住一根树枝把自己拽着走。

paras.en: But slipping and sliding, stepping and shuffling, whisking and tangoing, reindeer and snowman gradually made progress.
paras.zh: 不过滑着、溜着、迈着、拖着、扫着、探戈着，驯鹿和雪人渐渐有了进展。

paras.en: The music grew louder as they followed it, until it was a full, resonant sound.
paras.zh: 他们循声而去，音乐越来越响，直到变成饱满、洪亮的声响。

paras.en: It filled the woods and shook the leaves of the cottonwood trees.
paras.zh: 它充盈了整片树林，震得棉白杨的叶子簌簌作响。

paras.en: And along with the music there was another noise, the sound of water.
paras.zh: 与音乐一同传来的，还有另一种声响——水声。

paras.en: That was when they saw it.
paras.zh: 就在那时，他们看见了它。

paras.en: A huge, roaring waterfall of clear spring water.
paras.zh: 一道巨大、轰鸣的清冽山泉瀑布。

paras.en: It spilled down a tall cliff and collected in a mirror-bright little pool.
paras.zh: 它从高高的悬崖倾泻而下，汇成一个如镜般闪亮的小水潭。

paras.en: Standing on a rock amid the spray was a very handsome and impeccably dressed young man.
paras.zh: 在飞沫中的一块岩石上，站着一位十分英俊、衣着考究的年轻男子。

paras.en: He had long flowing hair and clothes the color of the water.
paras.zh: 他长发飘逸，衣裳是水的颜色。

paras.en: The man had his eyes half-closed in intense concentration, for he was playing a hardingfele.
paras.zh: 男子半闭双眼，全神贯注，因为他正在拉一把哈丹格提琴。

paras.en: The fingers of his left hand flew across the fiddle’s strings, while his right hand moved the bow furiously. “Delightful,” said Olaf.
paras.zh: 他左手手指在琴弦上飞舞，右手则疯狂地运弓。“真悦耳，”雪宝说。

paras.en: He tipped forward into the music as if he were falling into the scent of the most fragrant flowers he’d ever smelled.
paras.zh: 他朝音乐向前倾倒，仿佛正坠入他曾闻过的最芬芳的花香里。

paras.en: Beside him, Sven was involuntarily cavorting in circles.
paras.zh: 身旁的斯文不由自主地转着圈腾跃。

paras.en: The young man’s eyes opened fully.
paras.zh: 年轻人的眼睛完全睁开了。

paras.en: They seemed to twinkle in merriment at the newcomers.
paras.zh: 那双眼似乎因新来的人而闪着欢快的光。

paras.en: But he kept playing and Sven kept dancing until the song was finished.
paras.zh: 可他继续拉着，斯文也继续跳着，直到曲终。

paras.en: Then the young man lowered his bow and nodded. “Hei, hei,” said the strange fiddler. “Good day to you fine folk.
paras.zh: 随后年轻人放下弓，点了点头。“嘿，嘿，”这位奇怪的琴师说，“祝你们这些好人日安。

paras.en: What brings you to my waterfall?” Olaf approached to the edge of the pool, stopping just short of the water. “I’m Olaf, and I like warm hugs.
paras.zh: 是什么风把你们吹到我瀑布来的？”雪宝走到水潭边，在离水一步之遥处停下。“我是雪宝，我喜欢温暖的拥抱。

paras.en: My distinguished companion is Sven, and he’s the better half of Arendelle’s ice master and deliverer.
paras.zh: 我尊贵的伙伴是斯文，他是阿伦黛尔冰雪大师兼送货员的另一半——更棒的那一半。

paras.en: But that’s not important right now.
paras.zh: 不过那现在不重要。

paras.en: We’re both experts on affairs of the heart, but we couldn’t teach Mattias to dance no matter how many dance instructors we found in the village.
paras.zh: 我们俩都是感情专家，可不管在村里找了多少舞蹈老师，就是教不会马提亚斯跳舞。

paras.en: Even if we used swords.
paras.zh: 就算用上剑也不行。

paras.en: So, you see, that’s why we’ve followed your music, because reindeers have two left feet.” Sven shot Olaf an expression that clearly said he was appalled by how poorly the snowman had summarized their predicament.
paras.zh: 所以，你瞧，这就是我们跟着你音乐来的原因，因为驯鹿有‘两只左脚’。”斯文朝雪宝递了个表情，分明在说：雪人把他们困境总结得这么糟，他感到震惊。

paras.en: But the young man didn’t seem confused.
paras.zh: 可年轻人似乎并不困惑。

paras.en: He raised his bow to his fiddle. “You say you followed my… music,” he said playing out a quick three notes.
paras.zh: 他举起弓凑近提琴。“你说你们跟着我的……音乐来的，”他说着，随手奏出三个轻快音符。

paras.en: In response, the reindeer’s feet went tap-tap-tap. “And you say you need help getting someone to… dance.” Three more quick notes and three more tappity-tap-taps from Sven. “If your music can make a reindeer dance,” said Olaf, “then it should be able to help a general.” “Oh, I can make anybody dance,” said the fiddler. “I can make everybody dance.” He played a few complete bars, and Sven began to dance automatically.
paras.zh: 驯鹿的蹄子随之嗒嗒嗒地响。“而你说你需要帮忙让某人……跳舞。”又是三个轻快音符，斯文又嗒嗒嗒地敲了三下。“如果你的音乐能让驯鹿跳舞，”雪宝说，“那它也能帮一位将军。” “噢，我能让任何人跳舞，”琴师说，“我能让所有人跳舞。”他拉了几小节完整的曲子，斯文便自动跳了起来。

paras.en: Olaf watched the reindeer move.
paras.zh: 雪宝看着驯鹿舞动。

paras.en: When he turned back to the pool, the fiddler was right next to him, so close their noses almost touched.
paras.zh: 当他转回头看水潭时，琴师已到了他身边，近得几乎鼻尖相触。

paras.en: Though how the stranger had gotten from the rock in the center of the water to the shore without getting wet was a mystery. “That’s not disconcerting,” said Olaf.
paras.zh: 至于这陌生人怎么从水中央的岩石干干爽爽到了岸上，倒是个谜。“这倒不让人不安，”雪宝说。

paras.en: He tapped his chin. “Come to think of it, a strange and very well-dressed gentleman I’ve never met before, out here all alone in a forest playing a fiddle in a waterfall without getting wet, who is immediately willing to help us with our problems should seem suspicious.” The snowman shrugged. “But I’m willing to ignore all that because it’s so coincidentally convenient.” He looked at Sven, who nodded agreement. “Will you come to Arendelle Castle for the midsummer festival and play a song so that Mattias can dance with Halima?” he asked the fiddler. “I haven’t been to Arendelle in a long time,” said the fiddler. “A very long time.
paras.zh: 他敲了敲下巴。“想想看，一位我从未谋面的陌生、衣着考究的绅士，独自在森林里的瀑布中拉琴却不沾湿，还立刻愿意帮我们解决难题，本该让人起疑才是。”雪人耸了耸肩。“可我愿意忽略这一切，因为这巧合得实在太方便了。”他看向斯文，斯文点头表示同意。“你愿意来阿伦黛尔城堡参加仲夏节，奏一支曲子，好让马提亚斯能和哈丽玛跳舞吗？”他问琴师。“我很久没去过阿伦黛尔了，”琴师说，“非常久。

paras.en: I need to ensure I’m truly welcome.
paras.zh: 我得先确认我是真的受欢迎。

paras.en: You’ll have to invite me in.
paras.zh: 你们得亲自邀请我进去。

paras.en: You must meet me at the castle gates and invite me in personally.
paras.zh: 你们必须在城堡门口见我，亲自邀请我进去。

paras.en: By name.” “But you haven’t told me your name,” Olaf pointed out. “Ah,” said the fiddler. “So I haven’t.
paras.zh: 要叫我的名字。” “可你还没告诉我你的名字呢，”雪宝指出。“啊，”琴师说，“确实还没说。

paras.en: Well, you can call me Grim.” “That sounds forbidding.” “Does it?” said the fiddler. “Then, instead, you may call me Fosse.” “Grim..
paras.zh: 那，你们就叫我格里姆吧。”“那听着吓人。”“是吗？”琴师说，“那，你们不妨叫我福塞。”“格里姆……

paras.en: Fosse,” said Olaf. “Just meet me at the gate on the day of the festival,” said Fosse, “and invite me in.
paras.zh: 福塞，”雪宝说。“节日当天在门口跟我碰面就行，”福塞说，“然后邀请我进去。

paras.en: If you do as I’ve asked, I’ll make sure your General Mattias dances.
paras.zh: 只要照我说的做，我保证让你们的马提亚斯将军跳起舞来。

paras.en: Have no fear of that!
paras.zh: 这一点你们大可放心！

paras.en: Fear anything else you want, but have no fear of that!” “There you are, Destin,” said Halima.
paras.zh: 别的随便你们怕，唯独这点不必怕！”“你在这儿啊，戴斯汀，”哈丽玛说。

paras.en: Mattias turned around as the love of his life clutched at his sleeve. “I haven’t seen you all day,” Halima continued. “If I didn’t know better, I’d almost think you were avoiding me.” “Me?
paras.zh: 马提亚斯转过身，此生挚爱正抓着他的衣袖。“我一整天都没见着你了，”哈丽玛接着说，“要不是了解你，我几乎要以为你在躲我呢。”“我？

paras.en: What?
paras.zh: 什么？

paras.en: Avoiding you?” replied Mattias. “No.
paras.zh: 躲你？”马提亚斯答道，“不。

paras.en: Not at all.
paras.zh: 完全没有。

paras.en: I’ve just had general things to do.
paras.zh: 我只是有将军该办的事要忙。

paras.en: I mean, not as in ‘things in general,’ I mean ‘being a general’ things.
paras.zh: 我是说，不是‘一般的事’，是‘当将军’的事。

paras.en: For the safety of Arendelle.” “Uh-huh,” said Halima, drawing the sound out and giving him a hard stare.
paras.zh: 为了阿伦黛尔的安全。”“嗯哼，”哈丽玛拖长声音，狠狠盯了他一眼。

paras.en: Then she smiled. “Don’t worry.
paras.zh: 接着她笑了。“别担心。

paras.en: I know you have a lot of responsibilities.
paras.zh: 我知道你担子不轻。

paras.en: You do what you need to today, and I’ll see you for the first dance when the festival starts.” “About that,” began Mattias. “You know I’m not… I mean, I can’t…” His voice trailed off.
paras.zh: 今天你忙你的，等节庆一开始，第一支舞时我再见你。”“说到这个，”马提亚斯开了口，“你知道我不太……我是说，我没法……”他的声音低了下去。

paras.en: Mattias wanted to tell her the truth, but he was afraid and embarrassed.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯想把真相告诉她，可又害怕又难为情。

paras.en: Why was it that he would rather face a dozen angry Earth Giants than risk disappointing this one woman? “It’s okay,” said Halima. “Whatever it is, you can tell me, Destin.
paras.zh: 为什么他宁愿面对一打愤怒的大地巨人，也不愿冒让这一个女人失望的风险？“没事，”哈丽玛说，“不管是什么，你都可以告诉我，戴斯汀。

paras.en: You don’t need to worry.” Searching for the right way to say what he needed to, Mattias looked around the courtyard.
paras.zh: 你不必担心。”马提亚斯寻思着该怎么把想说的说出口，环顾起庭院。

paras.en: He couldn’t find the words.
paras.zh: 他找不到合适的词。

paras.en: His eyes scanned the festive floral arrangements strung along the walls and castle eaves.
paras.zh: 他的目光扫过沿城墙和城堡檐口挂起的节日花饰。

paras.en: Through the open castle doors, he could see the banquet tables were laden with food and drinks.
paras.zh: 透过敞开的城堡大门，他能看见宴席桌上堆满了食物和饮品。

paras.en: Opposite the castle, the gates leading to the bridge were open wide.
paras.zh: 城堡对面，通向大桥的宫门大开。

paras.en: And there were Olaf and Sven.
paras.zh: 而那边是雪宝和斯文。

paras.en: Olaf was talking to a well-dressed stranger carrying a musical instrument.
paras.zh: 雪宝正和一位衣着考究、带着乐器的陌生人说话。

paras.en: The snowman saw the general and waved.
paras.zh: 雪人看见将军，挥了挥手。

paras.en: Then he came bounding over, reindeer and musician in tow. “I’ll catch up with you later,” said Halima, and she stepped away to go help with the decorating.
paras.zh: 接着他蹦跳着跑过来，身后跟着驯鹿和琴师。“我晚点再找你，”哈丽玛说，便走开去帮忙装饰了。

paras.en: Mattias was ashamed that he felt so much relief at being interrupted. “Good news, General,” said Olaf. “Sven and I have solved your problem.” “You have?” said Mattias. “But the festival starts soon.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯为自己被打断竟如释重负而感到羞愧。“好消息，将军，”雪宝说，“斯文和我已经解决了你的问题。”“你们解决了？”马提亚斯说，“可节庆马上就要开始了。

paras.en: I don’t think I’ve got time to learn a new dance.” “Oh, you won’t have to learn anything,” said the snowman.
paras.zh: 我想我都没时间学新舞了。”“噢，你什么也不用学，”雪人说。

paras.en: He gestured to the stranger behind him. “This is Fosse.” Mattias looked at the young man.
paras.zh: 他指了指身后的陌生人。“这位是福塞。”马提亚斯打量着年轻人。

paras.en: He saw that the instrument the stranger carried was a hardingfele.
paras.zh: 他看出陌生人带的是一把哈丹格提琴。

paras.en: The traditional stringed instrument was different from other fiddles in that it had twice the number of strings.
paras.zh: 这种传统弦乐器和别的提琴不同之处在于，它的弦数是别人的两倍。

paras.en: The four strings on top were played with the bow, while the remaining strings, called understrings, would resonate when the strings above were played.
paras.zh: 上面四根弦用弓拉奏，而其余被称为“低音弦”的弦，会在上面的弦被拉响时随之共鸣。

paras.en: This made for a rich, full sound. “That’s a fine-looking instrument,” said Mattias. “One that I look forward to playing for you,” said Fosse.
paras.zh: 这带来了丰富饱满的音色。“好一把漂亮的乐器，”马提亚斯说。“一把我期待为你演奏的乐器，”福塞说。

paras.en: He executed a polite bow, but Mattias thought there was something smug in this face.
paras.zh: 他优雅地鞠了一躬，可马提亚斯觉得他脸上带着几分得意。

paras.en: Something about the stranger and his fiddle seemed familiar, but Mattias was sure he’d never seen him before. “Fosse is going to join the musicians on the stage,” Olaf explained.
paras.zh: 这陌生人和他的提琴透着某种熟悉感，可马提亚斯确信自己从没见过他。“福塞要上台和其他乐师一起演奏，”雪宝解释道。

paras.en: Sven pointed with a hoof to where a small wooden platform had been set up under an awning for a group of musicians to play. “I’m sure that will be… fine,” said the general. “And when he plays, even left feet—” Fosse tapped Olaf across the mouth with his bow.
paras.zh: 斯文用蹄子指向一处：凉棚下搭起一座小木台，供一群乐师演奏。“我想那会……挺好的，”将军说，“等他一奏，就算左脚——”福塞用弓轻轻敲了下雪宝的嘴。

paras.en: The snowman’s eyes crossed at the unexpected interruption. “Let’s let it be a surprise, shall we?” said the fiddler. “Oh, a surprise!” said Olaf. “I love surprises.” Beside him, Sven nodded happily. “I’ll leave you to it,” said the general, who cast around for one of his soldiers to give orders to.
paras.zh: 雪人被这突如其来的打断弄得眼睛斗了起来。“就让它是个惊喜，好吗？”琴师说。“噢，惊喜！”雪宝说，“我最爱惊喜了。”他身旁的斯文开心地点头。“那我就不打扰了，”将军说，四下张望想找个士兵发号施令。

paras.en: He was ready for mundane duties to take his mind off personal worries.
paras.zh: 他准备好用琐碎的公务，把个人烦恼从脑中赶走。

paras.en: Whatever Olaf and his friends had planned, he didn’t expect it would be of any help.
paras.zh: 不论雪宝和朋友们谋划了什么，他都不指望会有什么用。

paras.en: Queen Elsa arrived just as the festival was ready to begin.
paras.zh: 正当节庆即将开始，艾莎女王到了。

paras.en: It was a suitably dramatic entrance.
paras.zh: 这入场堪称恰如其分的隆重。

paras.en: She rode the Water Nokk through the gap in the breakwater, and the Water Spirit leapt from the sea and onto the bridge.
paras.zh: 她骑着水马穿过防波堤的缺口，水之灵从海中一跃，跳上了大桥。

paras.en: Anna greeted her at the gates to welcome her home.
paras.zh: 安娜在宫门口迎接她，欢迎她回家。

paras.en: Inside the castle courtyard, everyone was in good spirits.
paras.zh: 城堡庭院里，人人都兴致勃勃。

paras.en: Sven had bathed, and Kristoff was looking handsome in a smart blue suit.
paras.zh: 斯文洗了澡，克里斯托夫穿一身利落的蓝色西装，帅气极了。

paras.en: He had reluctantly conceded that midsummer was one of the handful of occasions important enough for him to wear one.
paras.zh: 他不情不愿地承认，仲夏节是少数重要到值得他穿西装的场合之一。

paras.en: Even Olaf was sporting a tie, a bright green length of fabric decorated in pale yellow crocus flowers.
paras.zh: 连雪宝都系上了领带——一条亮绿色、点缀着淡黄番红花的布料。

paras.en: It was very pretty but did little to prevent a snowman from looking out of place in the middle of summer.
paras.zh: 它很漂亮，却丝毫无助于让一个雪人在盛夏里不显得格格不入。

paras.en: Taking it all in, Mattias had to admit that his concerns had been overblown.
paras.zh: 看在眼里，马提亚斯不得不承认自己的担忧有些过于夸张了。

paras.en: Everything was going very smoothly.
paras.zh: 一切进行得十分顺利。

paras.en: The people of Arendelle were going to have a great midsummer festival.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔的百姓会过一个极好的仲夏节。

paras.en: All but one of them, anyway.
paras.zh: 反正除了其中一人之外。

paras.en: His thoughts clouded when he pictured Halima and the disappointment she would surely feel when she discovered how lacking he was, unable to participate in simple, joyful traditions.
paras.zh: 当他想象哈丽玛，想象她发现他是如此欠缺、连简单欢快的传统都参与不了时定会感到的失望，他的思绪便蒙上了阴云。

paras.en: The general almost wished that an emergency would crop up, something to call him away from having to— “Destin Mattias,” said Halima, racing up to him in surprise, “you’ve begun without me!” “Begun what?” he asked. “Dancing,” she said. “What are you talking about?
paras.zh: 将军几乎希望冒出个紧急情况，好把他从不得不——的处境中叫走。“戴斯汀·马提亚斯，”哈丽玛惊讶地跑到他跟前，“你都没等我就开始了！”“开始什么？”他问。“跳舞啊，”她说，“你在说什么呀？

paras.en: Me?
paras.zh: 我？

paras.en: Dancing?” That didn’t make any sense.
paras.zh: 跳舞？”这说不通。

paras.en: But then Mattias looked down at his feet.
paras.zh: 可接着马提亚斯低头看自己的脚。

paras.en: They were moving.
paras.zh: 它们在动。

paras.en: Unconsciously.
paras.zh: 无意识地。

paras.en: All by themselves.
paras.zh: 完全自顾自地。

paras.en: He was dancing.
paras.zh: 他在跳舞。

paras.en: He was dancing well .
paras.zh: 而且跳得很好。

paras.en: That was when he heard the music.
paras.zh: 就在这时，他听到了音乐。

paras.en: On the stage, the fiddler known as Fosse was performing with the other musicians.
paras.zh: 台上，那位人称福塞的琴师正与其他乐师合奏。

paras.en: There was a nyckelharpa, a seljefløyte, and a kantele, but it was the hardingfele that somehow cut through them all and resonated across the courtyard.
paras.zh: 那里有尼古尔哈帕、柳笛和康特勒琴，可不知怎的，是那把哈丹格提琴穿透了所有乐声，在庭院里回荡共鸣。

paras.en: It was a sound that wormed its way under your skin.
paras.zh: 那声音钻进了你的皮肤底下。

paras.en: It penetrated right to your bones—and it moved your feet! “I am dancing!” Mattias exclaimed.
paras.zh: 它直抵你的骨髓——还会驱动你的双脚！“我在跳舞！”马提亚斯惊呼。

paras.en: He folded his arm across his sternum and executed a quick bow. “Madam, would you care to dance with me?” Halima smiled and took his hand. “My pleasure,” she said.
paras.zh: 他横臂胸前，迅速行了个礼。“女士，可否赏脸与我共舞？”哈丽玛微笑着牵起他的手。“荣幸之至，”她说。

paras.en: And like that, they were twirling across the flagstones.
paras.zh: 就这样，他们旋转着滑过石板地。

paras.en: Mattias laughed as he kicked up his heels. “Look, Olaf, I’m dancing!” he called to the snowman. “Another successful mission from romance experts Olaf and Sven,” replied Olaf. “I knew it would work!” “What would work?” asked Mattias, but his feet swept him away across the courtyard before he could get an answer.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯踢着脚后跟大笑。“看，雪宝，我在跳舞！”他朝雪人喊道。“又是恋爱专家雪宝和斯文的一次成功行动，”雪宝答道，“我就知道能成！”“什么能成？”马提亚斯问，可双脚已把他卷过庭院，没等来回答。

paras.en: It was strange, actually, the way the music carried him with it.
paras.zh: 说真的，音乐带着他走的样子，有点奇怪。

paras.en: But maybe that was what it felt like to be caught up in a dance.
paras.zh: 不过或许身陷舞中的感觉就是如此吧。

paras.en: Mattias didn’t have any experience with dancing.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯毫无跳舞经验。

paras.en: At any rate, the love of his life was happy.
paras.zh: 无论如何，他的此生挚爱是开心的。

paras.en: If Halima wasn’t disappointed in him, everything was right in the world.
paras.zh: 只要哈丽玛不对他失望，这世界就一切都好。

paras.en: He gave himself over to the moment.
paras.zh: 他全然沉浸于当下。

paras.en: They danced through the next song.
paras.zh: 他们跳过了下一支曲子。

paras.en: And the song after that.
paras.zh: 又跳过了再下一支。

paras.en: In fact, everyone around them was dancing.
paras.zh: 事实上，周围所有人都在跳。

paras.en: Even those who were helping with the food.
paras.zh: 连帮忙备餐的人也是。

paras.en: Even his soldiers on the walls and by the gate.
paras.zh: 连他在城墙和宫门边的士兵也是。

paras.en: He’d have a word with them when this was over.
paras.zh: 这事过后他得跟他们说道说道。

paras.en: But something wasn’t right.
paras.zh: 可哪里不太对劲。

paras.en: The faces that twirled past Mattias didn’t look as carefree as they had when the music had begun.
paras.zh: 从马提亚斯身边旋转而过的一张张脸，不再像音乐刚开始时那样无忧无虑。

paras.en: Folks were looking tired, their faces worried.
paras.zh: 人们显得疲惫，脸上挂着担忧。

paras.en: Mattias twisted his neck to glance at the stage.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯扭头瞥了一眼舞台。

paras.en: Fosse the fiddler was playing by himself.
paras.zh: 琴师福塞正独自演奏。

paras.en: The other three musicians had abandoned their instruments.
paras.zh: 另外三位乐师已经放下了乐器。

paras.en: Mattias caught a glimpse of one of them, dancing amid the crowd.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯瞥见其中一位正混在人群里跳舞。

paras.en: This was strange.
paras.zh: 这很奇怪。

paras.en: Worrisome. “Halima,” he said. “I think I need to bow out at the next song.
paras.zh: 令人忧心。“哈丽玛，”他说，“我想在下支曲子时退出。

paras.en: I think something’s not quite right.” She nodded. “I would be grateful for the break,” she said.
paras.zh: 我想有点不对劲。”她点点头。“能歇一歇我会很感激，”她说。

paras.en: But when the song ended and the next began without a pause, Mattias knew something was wrong indeed; very, very wrong. “I can’t stop dancing,” he said. “Neither can I,” said Halima.
paras.zh: 可当这支曲子结束、下支无缝接上时，马提亚斯知道确实出事了；非常、非常不对劲。“我停不下来，”他说。“我也停不下来，”哈丽玛说。

paras.en: The couple glanced around them fearfully. “No one can,” said Mattias.
paras.zh: 这对伴侣惶恐地环顾四周。“谁都停不下来，”马提亚斯说。

paras.en: It was true.
paras.zh: 的确如此。

paras.en: The entire village population was caught up in the dance.
paras.zh: 全村的人都被卷入了舞中。

paras.en: Mattias saw the same look of fear and desperation in every expression. “Follow my lead,” he asked Halima when the music shifted to a waltz.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯在每一张脸上都看到了同样的恐惧与绝望。“跟着我的步子，”当音乐转为华尔兹时，他对哈丽玛说。

paras.en: As best he could, Mattias steered them toward the fiddler. “Fosse,” Mattias cried as his steps approached the stage. “I need you to stop the music.” “Stop the music?
paras.zh: 马提亚斯尽力把他们引向琴师。“福塞，”马提亚斯边跳边靠近舞台喊道，“我要你停下音乐。”“停下音乐？

paras.en: Why on earth would I do that?” said the fiddler. “I haven’t played in Arendelle in decades.
paras.zh: 我凭什么要停？”琴师说，“我几十年没在阿伦黛尔演奏了。

paras.en: Since before this ugly old castle was here.
paras.zh: 早在这座丑陋的旧城堡立起来之前。

paras.en: I’m certainly not going to stop now that I’m back.” “Back?” called Mattias, but then something clicked into place. “It was you, all those years ago!
paras.zh: 既然回来了，我当然不会停。”“回来？”马提亚斯喊道，可随即有什么对上了。“是你，多年以前！

paras.en: You made the music in the mountains!” “I just wanted people to dance to my tunes,” said Fosse. “But nasty King Runeard said it slowed construction of his castle.
paras.zh: 是你在山里弄出那音乐！” “我只是想让人们跟着我的曲子跳舞，”福塞说，“可可恶的鲁内拉德国王说它拖慢了他城堡的建造。

paras.en: Then he banished me.
paras.zh: 于是他驱逐了我。

paras.en: A king’s word has power in his own land, and I had to stay away.
paras.zh: 国王在自己领地上说的话有魔力，我不得不远离。

paras.en: Now that Olaf has invited me back in, I’m not leaving.
paras.zh: 既然雪宝已经邀请我回来，我就不走了。

paras.en: It’s the rest of you who are!” “What do you mean?” asked Mattias, but the fiddler increased the speed of his music.
paras.zh: 要走的是你们其余人！” “你什么意思？”马提亚斯问，可琴师加快了演奏速度。

paras.en: Mattias and Halima couldn’t stop themselves from dancing away.
paras.zh: 马提亚斯和哈丽玛控制不住自己，被带着跳开了。

paras.en: The general tried to steer his footwork to bring him near the queen, who was twirling helplessly with Kristoff. “What’s happening?” said Anna. “Why can’t we stop?” “It’s the music,” Mattias explained. “Your grandfather said it was just a story.” “Grandfather Runeard?” asked Anna.
paras.zh: 将军试着挪动舞步，好靠近女王——她正和克里斯托夫无助地打着转。“怎么回事？”安娜说，“我们为什么停不下来？”“是音乐，”马提亚斯解释，“你祖父说那只是个故事。”“祖父鲁内拉德？”安娜问。

paras.en: Elsa drifted into their orbit. “The fiddler,” asked Elsa. “Who is he?” “He says his name is Fosse,” explained Mattias. “Fosse?” exclaimed Elsa. “He’s a fossegrim!
paras.zh: 艾莎飘进了他们的舞圈。“这琴师，”艾莎问，“他是谁？”“他说他叫福塞，”马提亚斯解释。“福塞？”艾莎惊道，“他是个瀑布精灵！

paras.en: A spirit of the waters that plays beguiling music.” “Are our people in danger?” asked Anna. “Not if I can help it,” said Elsa.
paras.zh: 一种弹奏迷人音乐的水之精灵。”“我们的百姓有危险吗？”安娜问。“只要我还有办法，就不会，”艾莎说。

paras.en: Spinning around, she stretched out her arm and sent a blast of ice shooting across the courtyard toward the fiddler.
paras.zh: 她旋转着伸出手臂，射出一股冰霜，横穿庭院射向琴师。

paras.en: But Fosse saw it coming and leapt to the side.
paras.zh: 可福塞早有防备，向旁一跃。

paras.en: He glared at Elsa, and his bow zigged and zagged across the strings.
paras.zh: 他瞪着艾莎，弓在弦上锯齿般左右急划。

paras.en: She sent three more bursts of ice in rapid succession, but Fosse’s music jerked her back and forth, fouling her aim.
paras.zh: 她又接连射出三股冰霜，可福塞的音乐把她拽得前仰后合，扰乱了准头。

paras.en: They all missed. “There’ll be no more of that,” he called out. “That’s the sort of bad behavior that will see you thrown out of the castle.
paras.zh: 全打偏了。“不许再来那套，”他喊道，“这种恶劣行径，足够让你们被赶出城堡。

paras.en: In fact, I’ll throw all of you out now!” Fosse leapt from the stage and began to wade through the crowd.
paras.zh: 事实上，我现在就把你们全赶出去！”福塞跳下舞台，开始穿过人群趟行。

paras.en: The dancers parted for him, then, frighteningly, they fell into his wake.
paras.zh: 舞者们给他让路，接着，令人心惊的是，他们跟在了他身后。

paras.en: As the fossegrim marched across the courtyard and out the castle gates, Anna, Kristoff, Elsa, Sven, and all the villagers danced after him.
paras.zh: 当这瀑布精灵穿过庭院、出了宫门，安娜、克里斯托夫、艾莎、斯文和所有村民都跳着跟了上去。

paras.en: It was a mad procession, but no one could resist it.
paras.zh: 这是一支疯狂的队伍，可无人能抗拒。

paras.en: Fosse led them down the bridge, across the village square, and toward the docks.
paras.zh: 福塞领着他们下桥、穿过村庄广场，朝码头走去。

paras.en: Only one person in all of Arendelle wasn’t following.
paras.zh: 整个阿伦黛尔，只有一个人没跟着。

paras.en: Oblivious to everyone and everything, Olaf danced alone in the middle of the castle courtyard. “Shooby dooby dooby do do,” he sang out.
paras.zh: 雪宝对周遭一切浑然不觉，独自在城堡庭院中央跳舞。“咕比嘟比嘟比嘟嘟，”他唱了起来。

paras.en: Then he slid to a stop and looked around. “Hello?
paras.zh: 接着他滑步停下，四下张望。“喂？

paras.en: Where did everybody go?
paras.zh: 大家都去哪了？

paras.en: Sven?
paras.zh: 斯文？

paras.en: Anna?
paras.zh: 安娜？

paras.en: Kristoff?” Olaf put a hand to the side of his head, where an ear might be if he had ears.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫？”雪宝把手贴到脑袋一侧——要是有耳朵，那儿本该是耳朵的位置。

paras.en: Listening, he caught the refrains of the fading fiddling. “The party’s moved on without me?
paras.zh: 他凝神细听，捕捉到渐远的琴声余韵。“派对抛下我继续了？

paras.en: Wait for your snowman!” Olaf ran out the gates and after the crowd.
paras.zh: 等等你们的雪人！”雪宝冲出宫门，追着人群而去。

paras.en: He caught up with castle staff members Gerda and Kai, who were straggling at the back of the pack. “We can’t stop dancing,” they explained. “That seems serious,” said Olaf. “I’ve got to find Anna. “Make way, snowman coming through!” he called.
paras.zh: 他追上了落在队尾的城堡雇员歌尔达和凯。“我们停不下来，”他们解释。“这看来严重了，”雪宝说，“我得找到安娜。”“让一让，雪人要通过！”他喊道。

paras.en: He put his head down and pounded his snowball feet on the pavement.
paras.zh: 他低下头，用雪球脚在路面上咚咚地踩。

paras.en: Olaf found Anna just as Fosse reached the edge of the docks. “Why are you doing this?” called Anna to the fiddler. “Your grandfather drove me from my home,” exclaimed Fosse, whisking his bow to point at the waterfall on the cliffs beyond the town. “Now I’m driving you from yours.
paras.zh: 雪宝找到安娜时，福塞正好到了码头边。“你为什么要这么做？”安娜朝琴师喊道。“你祖父把我从家里赶了出去，”福塞叫道，挥弓指向镇外悬崖上的那道瀑布，“现在我把你们从你们家赶出去。

paras.en: You can all take a long dance off a short pier,” he said with a laugh. “That, or you give me your word that you will all leave Arendelle forever!” “Leave Arendelle,” said Anna. “We can’t leave Arendelle!” The fiddler slid his bow across the strings.
paras.zh: 你们全都从这条短码头跳一支长舞下海吧，”他笑道，“要么，你们就发誓永远离开阿伦黛尔！”“离开阿伦黛尔，”安娜说，“我们没法离开阿伦黛尔！”琴师弓在弦上一滑。

paras.en: Anna danced right to the edge of the docks.
paras.zh: 安娜直跳到了码头边缘。

paras.en: She swayed precariously over the waters.
paras.zh: 她在海水上方危险地摇晃着。

paras.en: Olaf raced to catch her, but she danced out of his grasp. “I wonder,” said Fosse. “Can a queen swim and dance at the same time?
paras.zh: 雪宝冲过去想接住她，可她舞着从他手中溜走。“我寻思，”福塞说，“女王能边游泳边跳舞吗？

paras.en: I don’t think so.” Midway through the crowd, Mattias was thinking furiously.
paras.zh: 我看不行。”人群中间，马提亚斯急切地思索着。

paras.en: He couldn’t control his feet, not when the music played.
paras.zh: 他控制不住自己的脚，至少音乐一响就控制不住。

paras.en: And Fosse hadn’t stopped playing.
paras.zh: 而福塞始终没停。

paras.en: If only there was a way to make the fiddler not fiddle.
paras.zh: 要是有什么法子让琴师拉不成琴就好了。

paras.en: Watching Olaf, he had an idea. “Olaf!” cried Mattias. “The music doesn’t affect you.” “It’s because I am made of magic,” explained Olaf. “And snow.
paras.zh: 看着雪宝，他有了主意。“雪宝！”马提亚斯喊道，“音乐影响不到你。”“那是因为我是魔法做的，”雪宝解释，“还有雪。

paras.en: Of course.” “We have to get the fiddle away from Fosse,” Mattias said. “And I think you’re the only one who can do that!” Olaf understood.
paras.zh: 当然。”“我们得把提琴从福塞手里抢走，”马提亚斯说，“而我想只有你能办到！”雪宝明白了。

paras.en: He ran toward the fossegrim.
paras.zh: 他朝瀑布精灵跑去。

paras.en: Fosse couldn’t control him, but he had a whole village under his spell.
paras.zh: 福塞控制不了他，可他控制着整个村子的人。

paras.en: He bowed and spun two villagers into Olaf’s path.
paras.zh: 他鞠了一躬，把两名村民旋到了雪宝的去路上。

paras.en: Olaf tried again, but Oaken loomed to block his way. “Hello and apologies, little snow friend,” said the shopkeeper. “I can’t get through,” yelled Olaf. “It’s going to take strategy,” said the general. “All of us working together.” “How can we work together when we can’t stop dancing?” asked Elsa.
paras.zh: 雪宝再试，可欧肯赫然挡住去路。“你好，抱歉了，小雪人朋友，”店主说。“我过不去，”雪宝喊道。“得用计策，”将军说，“我们所有人一起配合。”“我们都停不下来，怎么配合？”艾莎问。

paras.en: That was a good question.
paras.zh: 这是个好问题。

paras.en: If they couldn’t stop dancing, Mattias had to account for the dancing in his plan.
paras.zh: 既然停不下来，马提亚斯就得在计划里把“跳舞”算进去。

paras.en: He thought back to his recent lessons, all the various dance moves the villagers had tried and failed to teach him. “I might not be a good dancer,” said Mattias. “But I bet I can choreograph!” He looked about for the reindeer.
paras.zh: 他回想起近来的“功课”——村民们试过却没教会他的各种舞步。“我也许不是个好舞者，”马提亚斯说，“但我打赌我会编舞！”他四下寻找驯鹿。

paras.en: He called out to Sven, twirling his fingers to indicate what he wanted.
paras.zh: 他朝斯文喊，转动手指示意自己的意图。

paras.en: The reindeer, always quick on the uptake, understood.
paras.zh: 驯鹿向来领会得快，一下就懂了。

paras.en: He pirouetted in a circle, caught Olaf with an antler, and hurled him over the wall of dancers.
paras.zh: 他原地旋转一圈，用鹿角钩住雪宝，把他甩过舞者组成的人墙。

paras.en: Olaf landed in a run, but Fosse scowled and sent a trio of villagers to stop the snowman. “Kristoff, you’re up!” said Mattias while gesturing instructions.
paras.zh: 雪宝落地就跑，可福塞皱眉，派出三名村民拦住雪人。“克里斯托夫，该你了！”马提亚斯一边打手势指挥一边说。

paras.en: Right before the villagers reached Olaf, Kristoff leapt in their path in a deep knee bend, then flung his arms and legs akimbo.
paras.zh: 就在村民们要够到雪宝前，克里斯托夫一个深屈膝跳到他们路上，接着把手脚大大张开。

paras.en: Olaf ran on.
paras.zh: 雪宝继续跑。

paras.en: But the fiddler danced another group of people into position. “Now, Your Majesty,” Mattias called to Anna.
paras.zh: 可琴师又舞着另一群人占了位。“现在，陛下，”马提亚斯朝安娜喊。

paras.en: She caught Olaf and sent him spinning rapidly like a top. “Wa-wa-wa-wa-wa-wah,” he cried dizzily. “Now you, Your Other Majesty,” said Mattias to Elsa. “Keep going, Olaf,” shouted Elsa.
paras.zh: 她接住雪宝，把他像陀螺般飞快旋转。“哇—哇—哇—哇—哇—哇，”他晕头转向地叫。“现在换你，另一位陛下，”马提亚斯对艾莎说。“继续冲，雪宝，”艾莎喊道。

paras.en: With split-second timing, she conjured a ramp of ice.
paras.zh: 她以分秒不差的时机，变出一道冰坡。

paras.en: Olaf hit the ramp and slid up it, launching into the air and over the villagers’ heads.
paras.zh: 雪宝撞上冰坡，顺着滑上去，腾空而起，飞过村民们的头顶。

paras.en: The snowman crashed into Fosse.
paras.zh: 雪人撞上了福塞。

paras.en: They tumbled in a jumble of limbs, not all of them attached.
paras.zh: 他们滚作一团，肢体乱成一堆，而且并非全都连着身子。

paras.en: Olaf’s arms had come off, but they still clutched at the hardingfele.
paras.zh: 雪宝的手臂脱落了，却仍死死抓着那把哈丹格提琴。

paras.en: For a minute it was touch and go, but Fosse pulled his instrument free.
paras.zh: 有那么一刻胜负难料，可福塞把乐器挣脱了出来。

paras.en: He laughed and held up his fiddle in triumph.
paras.zh: 他大笑，得意地举起提琴。

paras.en: But then his eyes went wide.
paras.zh: 可接着他瞪大了眼睛。

paras.en: Olaf’s lower half was racing away with something impaled right through the snowball. “What good is a fiddle without a bow?” said the snowman’s head from beside the fossegrim.
paras.zh: 雪宝的下半身正飞奔远去，有样东西直直插在雪球里。“没弓的提琴还有什么用？”雪人的脑袋在瀑布精灵身旁说道。

paras.en: It was true.
paras.zh: 确实如此。

paras.en: While Olaf was fighting over the fiddle, the snowman’s bottom had made off with the bow.
paras.zh: 雪宝争抢提琴时，雪人的下半身带着弓溜走了。

paras.en: Fosse plucked at his strings with a finger, but the discordant noise had no effect.
paras.zh: 福塞用手指拨弦，可那不和谐的声音毫无作用。

paras.en: Around them, the people of Arendelle began shaking off the spell.
paras.zh: 他们周围，阿伦黛尔的百姓开始抖落那道魔咒。

paras.en: They turned to advance on the fiddler. “Maybe this anvil should fear the hammers, ja?” said Oaken, smacking a meaty fist into a big palm.
paras.zh: 他们转身朝琴师逼近。“也许这块铁砧也该怕怕锤子了，呀？”欧肯说着，把厚实的大拳头拍进宽掌心。

paras.en: Fosse spun, ready to leap into the sea.
paras.zh: 福塞转身，准备跳进海里。

paras.en: But the Water Nokk rose out of it.
paras.zh: 可水马从海中升起。

paras.en: It stamped its foot and sent an angry spray to splash the fossegrim.
paras.zh: 它跺了跺脚，愤而扬起水花溅了瀑布精灵一身。

paras.en: The fiddler gulped.
paras.zh: 琴师咽了口唾沫。

paras.en: He was surrounded by a sea of angry faces.
paras.zh: 他被一汪愤怒的面孔之海包围了。

paras.en: And then the fossegrim did something very unexpected.
paras.zh: 接着这瀑布精灵做了一件出乎意料的事。

paras.en: He began to cry.
paras.zh: 他哭了起来。

paras.en: Great, big drops like a waterfall rained from his eyes and collected in a pool at his feet.
paras.zh: 大颗大颗如瀑布般的泪珠从他眼中落下，在他脚边汇成一滩水。

paras.en: Anna and Elsa looked at each other in bewilderment.
paras.zh: 安娜和艾莎困惑地对视。

paras.en: The sisters knew each other so well, they knew what the other was thinking.
paras.zh: 姐妹俩如此相知，知道对方在想什么。

paras.en: They were meant to be the bridge between people and spirits.
paras.zh: 她们本该是人与精灵之间的桥梁。

paras.en: Not the wall.
paras.zh: 而非高墙。

paras.en: Their grandfather might have built dams to divide, but they tore them down to bring folks together. “I understand you were driven out of your home,” said Anna kindly. “But things are different now,” Elsa explained. “We live in harmony with the spirits.” “We could live that way with you, if you wanted,” said Anna. “Provided you only make people dance when they want to,” added Mattias. “What do you say?” said Olaf.
paras.zh: 她们的祖父或许筑坝以分隔，她们却拆坝以聚人。“我理解你被赶出了家，”安娜温和地说，“可如今时移世易，”艾莎解释，“我们与精灵和睦共处。”“如果你愿意，我们也可以和你这样相处，”安娜说。“只要你只在人们想跳时才让他们跳，”马提亚斯补了一句。“你说呢？”雪宝说。

paras.en: His disembodied arm reached out a hand. “Friends?” Sven gave an encouraging look and a fuzzy smile.
paras.zh: 他那脱离了身体的手伸了出来。“做朋友？”斯文投来鼓励的眼神，露出自毛茸茸的微笑。

paras.en: And Fosse sniffed and stopped crying.
paras.zh: 福塞抽了抽鼻子，止住了哭。

paras.en: On the stage, Fosse played with the other musicians.
paras.zh: 舞台上，福塞与其他乐师合奏。

paras.en: This time, his tune was easy to dance to, but it wasn’t compulsory.
paras.zh: 这一次，他的曲子好跳，却不再强求。

paras.en: Queen Anna had invited the fossegrim to reoccupy the waterfall near Arendelle.
paras.zh: 安娜女王已邀请这瀑布精灵重新入住阿伦黛尔附近的瀑布。

paras.en: He wasn’t sure if he would take her up on the offer.
paras.zh: 他还不确定是否接受这提议。

paras.en: He had lived near the distant waterfall for decades, and it felt like home.
paras.zh: 他在远处的瀑布边住了几十年，那里已是他的家。

paras.en: But, as he put it, “It was nice to be welcome again.” About half the villagers were dancing.
paras.zh: 不过，正如他所说，“能再次受到欢迎，感觉真好。”约一半村民在跳舞。

paras.en: Others had had enough footwork for a night, if not for a season.
paras.zh: 其他人这一晚——即便不是这一季——的舞步也跳够了。

paras.en: They had moved inside to help themselves to the buffet table.
paras.zh: 他们已进屋去自助餐台取食。

paras.en: But a slow and pleasant waltz had tempted Anna and her friends back onto the floor. “It doesn’t matter to me if you can dance or not,” said Halima.
paras.zh: 不过一支舒缓悦耳的华尔兹，又把安娜和朋友们勾回了舞池。“你会不会跳舞，我根本不在乎，”哈丽玛说。

paras.en: She and Mattias were stepping and sliding near the center of the courtyard. “I like you for who you are, not who you aren’t.
paras.zh: 她和马提亚斯在庭院中央附近迈步滑行。“我喜欢的是本来的你，而不是那个‘你不是’的你。

paras.en: I see you, Destin Mattias.
paras.zh: 我看见你了，戴斯汀·马提亚斯。

paras.en: You’re a good man, and that’s worth risking a few feet out of place.” “I tried to tell him that,” said Anna, waltzing past with Kristoff. “Listen to your queen!” Kristoff said. “She knows what she’s talking about,” agreed Halima. “Also listen to me.” “I will,” promised Mattias. “You know,” said Olaf, twirling by with Sven, “you’re really not that bad.” The reindeer gave Mattias an approving look. “I’m not, am I?” said the general.
paras.zh: 你是个好人，这就值得冒几只脚踩错位置的风险。”“我早想跟他说这个了，”安娜和克里斯托夫跳着经过时说，“听你女王的话！”“她懂她在说什么，”哈丽玛赞同，“也听我的。”“我会的，”马提亚斯承诺。“你知道吗，”雪宝和斯文转着圈经过时说，“你还真没那么糟。”驯鹿投给马提亚斯一个赞许的眼神。“我确实不糟，对吧？”将军说。

paras.en: Whether it was a residual effect of the fossegrim, or just that his nervousness and fear were finally gone, Mattias was picking up the waltz rather quickly. “Olaf, you thought that I needed the right instructor.
paras.zh: 不知是瀑布精灵的余效，还是他的紧张与恐惧终于消散，马提亚斯学起华尔兹来相当快。“雪宝，你以为我需要的是对的老师。

paras.en: Then you thought I needed the right music.
paras.zh: 接着你以为我需要的是对的音乐。

paras.en: It turns out I just needed the right partner.
paras.zh: 到头来我需要的，不过是位对的舞伴。

paras.en: And I found her.” He turned to gaze into his love’s eyes. “Just as long as you let me lead,” said Halima. “Oh, you got that right,” said Mattias.
paras.zh: 而我找到了她。”他转头凝望挚爱的眼睛。“只要你肯让我带舞，”哈丽玛说。“噢，这点你说对了，”马提亚斯说。

paras.en: And they danced long into the night.
paras.zh: 于是他们跳啊跳，一直跳到深夜。

paras.en: Queen Anna straightened her crown and tucked an errant strand of auburn hair behind her ear.
paras.zh: 安娜女王扶正了头冠，把一缕不听话的赤褐色头发别到了耳后。

paras.en: She smiled at the looking glass and lifted her chin as a wisp sprang out on the other side of her head like a twisted pumpkin vine.
paras.zh: 她对着镜子笑了笑，扬起下巴，可另一侧的头发又像卷曲的南瓜藤一样钻了出来。

paras.en: With an exasperated sigh, she grabbed a bobby pin from her vanity and anchored the willful wave into place.
paras.zh: 她无奈地叹了口气，从梳妆台上取下一枚发卡，把那缕倔强的卷发固定住。

paras.en: She leaned toward the mirror, her reflection wide-eyed, her cheeks washed of color.
paras.zh: 她朝镜子凑近，镜中的自己睁大双眼，脸颊没有一丝血色。

paras.en: She straightened and stepped back, squaring her shoulders.
paras.zh: 她挺直身子，向后退了一步，端平了肩膀。

paras.en: In twenty minutes, she would address the kingdom at the opening of the harvest festival and tell the people of Arendelle that she had secured a trade deal with the Southern Isles that would generate jobs, increase wealth, and improve their access to a wider range of goods and services.
paras.zh: 再过二十分钟，她就要在丰收节开幕式上向全国发表讲话，告诉阿伦黛尔的百姓：她已与南境群岛达成一项贸易协定，将创造就业、增加财富，并让大家能买到更丰富多样的商品和服务。

paras.en: She had worked with the eldest prince and heir to the throne and luckily had no interaction with the dastardly Prince Hans.
paras.zh: 和她谈合作的是长王子、王位继承人，幸运的是，她没有和那个卑鄙的汉斯王子打任何交道。

paras.en: Even with the possibility of encountering the man who had nearly taken everything from her, it had been worth the risk.
paras.zh: 尽管有可能碰上那个曾差点夺走她一切的人，但这趟冒险依然值得。

paras.en: The trade agreement was something her father had worked toward his entire life.
paras.zh: 这份贸易协定，是她父亲倾尽一生都想促成的。

paras.en: And yet, her stomach felt like a snowball and her limbs like rubber.
paras.zh: 可是，她的胃却像攥着个雪球，四肢软得像橡胶。

paras.en: Not unlike during her first dance recital, when she had pirouetted so exuberantly that she’d knocked three children into the village fountain.
paras.zh: 这情形，和她第一次舞蹈演出时差不多——那回她转圈转得太起劲，一下子把三个孩子撞进了村子的喷泉里。

paras.en: Anna rubbed the back of her neck and began to pace, remembering the year after her disastrous dance, when she had studied pianoforte with a music tutor for months in preparation for a concert that she would give for her family and all the servants in the castle.
paras.zh: 安娜揉了揉后颈，开始来回踱步，想起那场糟糕的舞蹈演出之后那年，她跟着音乐老师练了好几个月钢琴，准备为家人和城堡里所有仆人办一场音乐会。

paras.en: Mama had smiled and clapped along as Anna had played Arendelle’s national anthem.
paras.zh: 安娜弹奏阿伦黛尔国歌时，妈妈笑着为她鼓掌打拍子。

paras.en: Halfway through her fourth song, Papa had been called away on urgent business.
paras.zh: 弹到第四首曲子一半时，爸爸被急事叫走了。

paras.en: Anna had suspected that his business involved an aching head more than any crucial matters of state.
paras.zh: 安娜猜，他那件“要紧事”多半是头疼，而不是什么国家大事。

paras.en: Yet that night, he had gathered her in his strong arms and assured her that she could do anything she set her mind to.
paras.zh: 可那天晚上，他用有力的双臂抱住她，告诉她：只要下定决心，她什么事都做得到。

paras.en: He’d told her he loved her music because he loved her.
paras.zh: 他说，他爱她弹的曲子，是因为他爱她。

paras.en: Tears stung the backs of Anna’s eyes.
paras.zh: 安娜的眼眶一阵发热，泛起泪意。

paras.en: She hadn’t believed him.
paras.zh: 那时她并不相信他的话。

paras.en: Mostly because she had not believed in herself.
paras.zh: 多半是因为，她连自己都不相信。

paras.en: It was so much easier to see the talents and abilities of others even as she discounted her own gifts.
paras.zh: 看得到别人的才华与能力总是容易，轮到自己的天赋，她却总把它们看轻。

paras.en: Anna sank into a chair by the window that overlooked the courtyard, decorated with cornstalk scarecrows and hay bales piled high with lemon-yellow gourds and plump pumpkins.
paras.zh: 安娜坐到靠窗的椅子上，窗外是庭院，立着玉米秆扎的稻草人，干草垛上高高堆着柠檬黄的葫芦和圆滚滚的南瓜。

paras.en: Just beyond, the village bustled with activity as the people prepared for the coming festival, and to the north, the mountains rose in a brilliant conflagration of flaming trees, a brisk wind waving their leaves in a last dance to show off their gowns of fiery foliage.
paras.zh: 再远处，村庄里一片繁忙，人们正为即将到来的节日做准备；往北望去，群山仿佛燃起一片绚烂的火光，那是变红的树木，一阵凉风拂过，吹得叶片翩翩起舞，像在炫耀它们火红的盛装，跳着最后一支舞。

paras.en: Farther up stood the icy crags.
paras.zh: 更远处，立着冰封的峭壁。

paras.en: Anna’s chest tightened with longing for her best friend and sister.
paras.zh: 安娜胸口一紧，涌起对最好朋友、也是她姐姐的思念。

paras.en: She didn’t see Elsa nearly as much as she would like.
paras.zh: 她见艾莎的次数，远远不及她所希望的。
