paras.en: Perhaps if Mama and Papa and Elsa were there, Anna would not feel so nervous about whether the people of Arendelle would embrace the new trade deal with the Southern Isles.
paras.zh: 要是妈妈、爸爸和艾莎都在，安娜大概就不会这么紧张，担心阿伦黛尔的百姓会不会接受这份与南境群岛的新贸易协定。

paras.en: With a loud sigh, she leaned against the sill and pressed her forehead to the cool glass as she peered to the east, where she could just make out the reflection of the sun on the crystalline waters of the harbor.
paras.zh: 她重重叹了口气，靠在窗台上，把额头贴上冰凉的玻璃，朝东望去，隐约能看见阳光在港口晶莹的水面上反射出的光斑。

paras.en: Father had loved the sea.
paras.zh: 爸爸曾那样热爱大海。

paras.en: A stab of grief wrenched Anna’s heart at the thought of him and Mama losing their lives in the treacherous waters.
paras.zh: 一想到他和妈妈葬身在那片凶险的海域，一阵悲痛猛地揪紧了安娜的心。

paras.en: Anna had tried hard over the years to tame her vivid imagination and not envision the ship tossed like a toy on monstrous waves, splintered to ribbons, her parents clinging to each another as they were swallowed by the fathomless deep.
paras.zh: 这些年来，安娜努力克制自己丰富的想象力，不去设想那艘船像玩具一样被巨浪抛起、撞得粉碎，父母在吞噬一切的万丈深渊中紧紧相拥的画面。

paras.en: At least they had been together, and still were.
paras.zh: 至少他们曾在一起，而且至今依然相伴。

paras.en: Her soul refused to believe otherwise.
paras.zh: 她的灵魂拒绝相信除此之外的一切。

paras.en: Anna smiled.
paras.zh: 安娜微笑起来。

paras.en: If Papa could see her now, he would be so proud.
paras.zh: 要是爸爸能看见现在的她，该有多骄傲。

paras.en: That was when it all came rushing back to her: the exact day that she had glimpsed herself through her father’s eyes… “Anna, can you play a little quieter?
paras.zh: 就在这时，一切往事涌上心头：那个她第一次透过父亲的眼睛看清自己的日子……“安娜，你能弹轻一点吗？

paras.en: I need to focus on this document,” King Agnarr asked his nine-year-old daughter.
paras.zh: 我要专心看这份文件。”国王安格瑞对他九岁的女儿说。

paras.en: Anna sat on the floor of her father’s office with dolls spread around her in various poses as she acted out a drama of adventure and romance. “But, Papa, Princess Regina has just found the location of the Devil’s Eye diamond, and it’s in Prince Handsome’s kingdom!
paras.zh: 安娜坐在爸爸办公室的地板上，周围散落着摆出各种姿势的玩偶，正演着一出冒险爱情剧。“可是爸爸，蕾吉娜公主刚找到了‘恶魔之眼’钻石的所在地，就在帅王子王国里！”

paras.en: She’s terribly excited.” The king peered over the side of his desk and lifted an amused brow. “Prince Handsome, eh?
paras.zh: 她可激动啦。”国王从桌沿探出头，好笑地挑了挑眉。“帅王子，嗯？

paras.en: Is that the best you can come up with?” Anna giggled and lifted her only male doll, brushing back the strands of his golden hair as she gazed into his blue glass eyes. “But he is quite handsome.” “Which is all well and good.
paras.zh: 你能想出的最好的名字？”安娜咯咯笑着举起她唯一的男玩偶，拨开他金色的发丝，盯着他蓝色的玻璃眼珠。“可他确实挺帅的呀。”“那当然很好。

paras.en: But you are a princess, and you’re old enough to look for other qualities in a love interest,” Papa said with mock sternness.
paras.zh: 但你是个公主，也到了该在喜欢的人身上寻找别的品质的年纪了。”爸爸假装严肃地说。

paras.en: Anna pressed her lips together in a half frown.
paras.zh: 安娜抿紧嘴唇，半皱着眉。

paras.en: In all the good fairy tales, the princes had gorgeous hair, fine eyes, and debonair charm.
paras.zh: 在所有的好童话里，王子们都长着漂亮的头发、好看的眼睛，风度翩翩，魅力十足。

paras.en: They always dressed in tailored suits befitting their station or uniforms dripping with medals. “What other qualities?” she asked. “Well”—Papa turned to face her, resting his elbows on his knees—“your future husband should be brave and kind.
paras.zh: 他们总穿着合身份的考究西装，或是挂满勋章的制服。“那还有什么品质？”她问。“这个嘛”——爸爸转过身面对她，手肘撑在膝盖上——“你未来的丈夫，应当勇敢又善良。

paras.en: He should respect your wishes and protect you with his life.” Anna set down her doll and leaned back on her hands, listening intently.
paras.zh: 他应当尊重你的心愿，并用生命保护你。”安娜放下玩偶，双手撑在身后，专心地听着。

paras.en: It felt so good to have Papa’s full attention that she wanted to soak up every moment. “Go on,” she encouraged.
paras.zh: 能得到爸爸全部的关注，感觉真好，她想把每一刻都牢牢记住。“继续说呀。”她催促道。

paras.en: The king tapped his chin. “He should be loyal and love you above all others.” “Like you love Mama?” She sighed dreamily. “Yes,” Papa answered with a decisive nod. “Shouldn’t we also like all the same things?
paras.zh: 国王轻点着下巴。“他应当忠诚，爱你胜过一切。”“就像你爱妈妈那样？”她做着美梦般地叹了口气。“是的，”爸爸坚定地点点头。“那我们是不是也该喜欢同样的东西？

paras.en: Like exploring nature and building snowmen and eating extra-tall sandwiches?” Anna spanned her arms to demonstrate all the meats and cheeses and pickles and delicious food that she could stuff between two slices of bread.
paras.zh: 比如探索自然、堆雪人，还有吃超级高的三明治？”安娜张开双臂，比划着能把多少腊肉、奶酪、酸黄瓜和各种美味塞进两片面包之间。

paras.en: Papa chuckled. “Perhaps.” He grew silent and cocked his head as he watched her. “I think, most importantly for you, he will need to have an indomitable will.” “Abominable?” Anna scrunched one eye.
paras.zh: 爸爸轻声笑了。“也许吧。”他安静下来，歪着头看她。“我觉得，对你来说最重要的是，他得有一股不屈的意志。”“可怕的？”安娜眯起一只眼。

paras.en: She had heard tales of an abominable snow monster who lived high in the mountains and liked to eat children for breakfast.
paras.zh: 她听过雪怪的传说，那怪物住在高山上，喜欢拿小孩当早餐。

paras.en: She shuddered.
paras.zh: 她打了个寒颤。

paras.en: The king laughed. “No, darling, in-dom-i-ta-ble .
paras.zh: 国王大笑。“不，亲爱的，是in-dom-i-ta-ble（不屈）。

paras.en: It means dauntless and strong.” Anna folded her legs and propped her chin on her fists. “Why do you think I need someone in-dom-it-able ?” Papa reached out and brushed aside the strand of hair that was always falling in her eyes. “Because, dear one, you need someone who can keep up with you.
paras.zh: 意思是无畏而坚强。”安娜盘起腿，用拳头托着下巴。“为什么你觉得我需要个‘不屈’的人？”爸爸伸出手，拨开那缕总落进她眼睛里的头发。

paras.en: Someone who will not cower in the face of your irrepressible spirit.” Irrepressible spirit?
paras.zh: “因为，小家伙，你需要一个能跟得上你的人。

paras.en: As in stubborn and willful as a mule?
paras.zh: 一个面对你那压制不住的活力时，不会退缩的人。”“压制不住的活力？

paras.en: She’d heard similar things uttered about her ever since she could remember.
paras.zh: 你是说像骡子一样固执、任性是吧？

paras.en: Like when Mother had taught her how to speak French, and Anna had spoken the language nonstop for a month.
paras.zh: 从她记事起，就常听人这么说她。

paras.en: Mama had complained that Anna’s pronunciation was atrocious, and Anna had insisted that she was creating her own unique dialect.
paras.zh: 比如妈妈教她说法语那回，安娜整整一个月都在不停地讲法语。

paras.en: That was when Mother had muttered something about loving her despite her inheriting her father’s bullheadedness.
paras.zh: 妈妈抱怨安娜的发音糟透了，安娜却坚持说自己是在创造一种独特的方言。

paras.en: But Anna took pride in her perseverance.
paras.zh: 那时妈妈嘀咕说，尽管她继承了她爸爸的牛脾气，自己还是爱她。

paras.en: Giving up was most definitely not her style.
paras.zh: 不过，安娜倒为自己的坚持感到骄傲。

paras.en: However, that trait in a future beau didn’t seem in the least romantic. “But, Papa—” A knock sounded on the door, and Father called for them to enter. “Your Majesty.” Anna turned to find the housekeeper wringing her hands in the open doorway. “There’s been another incident… er…” The housekeeper’s gaze shifted down to Anna, then back to the king. “Princess Elsa needs you, sir.” The king stood and rushed toward the door.
paras.zh: 放弃绝对不是她的作风。

paras.en: Anna hopped to her feet. “Papa, can I come, too?” Her father glanced back. “No, Anna, not this time.” “But I want to help!” She always wanted to help.
paras.zh: 然而，未来心上人身上的这种特质，似乎一点都不浪漫。“可是，爸爸——”敲门声响起，爸爸叫人进来。“陛下。”安娜转过头，看见管家站在敞开的门口，双手不安地绞在一起。“又出事了……呃……”管家的目光先落到安娜身上，又回到国王脸上。“艾莎公主需要您，陛下。”国王站起身，朝门口冲去。

paras.en: Instead, she always seemed to be in someone’s way.
paras.zh: 安娜一下子跳起来。“爸爸，我也能一起去吗？”爸爸回头看了一眼。“不行，安娜，这次不行。”“可我想帮忙！”她总想帮忙。

paras.en: She could prove that she could be helpful!
paras.zh: 可她似乎总在碍别人的事。

paras.en: She rushed forward and grabbed Papa’s large hand.
paras.zh: 她能证明自己是有用的！

paras.en: Time with her father was so rare.
paras.zh: 她冲上前，抓住爸爸的大手。

paras.en: He was always busy running off to solve some problem or help others. “I promise I won’t get in the way.” Papa looked down at her, and Anna stared up at him with wide eyes.
paras.zh: 和爸爸相处的时光太难得了。

paras.en: His gaze softened upon her, and a tiny smile tugged up the corner of his mouth.
paras.zh: 他总是忙着去处理问题、帮助别人。“我保证不挡路。”爸爸低头看她，安娜睁大眼睛仰望着他。

paras.en: Certain that she had won, Anna offered her biggest grin.
paras.zh: 他的目光在她身上柔和下来，嘴角泛起一丝笑意。

paras.en: But then Papa’s brows lowered. “Not this time, darling.” “When will you be back?” Anna asked, her lip jutting out in a pout. “I don’t know.
paras.zh: 安娜确信自己赢了，咧开嘴露出最大的笑容。

paras.en: You should go find your mother.
paras.zh: 可接着爸爸眉头一皱。“这次不行，亲爱的。”“你什么时候回来？”安娜噘着嘴问。“我不知道。

paras.en: I’m sure she can give you something useful to do.” Anna squeezed his hand harder, silently begging him not to go.
paras.zh: 你该去找你妈妈。

paras.en: Carefully he tugged his fingers out of her grasp. “I must go help your sister.
paras.zh: 我肯定她能给你找点有用的事做。”安娜更用力地攥紧他的手，无声地恳求他别走。

paras.en: I’ll see you at dinner.” Anna’s shoulders drooped as she watched him walk out the door.
paras.zh: 他小心地把手指从她手里抽出来。“我得去帮你姐姐。

paras.en: Anna raced down the corridor on her bike, the breeze blowing back her hair as she broke through shafts of golden sunlight that shimmered like dancing fairies.
paras.zh: 晚饭时见。”安娜看着他走出门，肩膀耷拉下来。

paras.en: If she made it to the kitchen in time, there might be waffles left over from breakfast.
paras.zh: 安娜骑着自行车冲下走廊，风把她的头发吹到脑后，她穿过一道道金色阳光，那些光柱像跳舞的小精灵般闪烁。

paras.en: She passed a set of open doors, the sound of melodic humming drifting through the air.
paras.zh: 要是能赶在厨房收拾前到，说不定还有早餐剩下的华夫饼。

paras.en: Anna swung her bike around and skidded to a halt, setting one foot on the marble floor as she stared into her mother’s sewing room.
paras.zh: 她经过一组敞开的门，空气中飘来悠扬的哼唱声。

paras.en: Mama sat near the hearth, chestnut hair pinned back in a messy bun as she worked knitting needles through azure-colored yarn.
paras.zh: 安娜掉转车头，一个急刹停住，一只脚踩在大理石地板上，朝妈妈的缝纫室里望去。

paras.en: Anna had heard the furious clacking all the way down the hall.
paras.zh: 妈妈坐在壁炉旁，栗色头发随意挽成一个乱蓬蓬的发髻，正用织针穿梭在蔚蓝色的毛线间。

paras.en: Mama spent most every day making blankets and mittens and clothing for the elderly and the sick.
paras.zh: 那一连串急促的“嗒嗒”声，安娜在走廊那头就听见了。

paras.en: She always said it was the best way to use her talents to care for others while the castle was shut off to visitors.
paras.zh: 妈妈几乎每天都给老人和病人织毯子、手套和衣物。

paras.en: A situation Anna had stopped asking questions about long ago.
paras.zh: 她总说，在城堡闭门谢客的日子里，这是用自己的才华关怀他人最好的方式。

paras.en: Sometimes Father and Mother went out.
paras.zh: 这种情况，安娜早就不再追问了。

paras.en: But besides their few loyal servants, no one ever came in.
paras.zh: 有时爸爸妈妈会出门。

paras.en: Anna’s gaze darted to rolls of fabric, tissue paper patterns, scissors, and measuring tapes on a table near her mother’s elbow.
paras.zh: 但除了那几个忠心的仆人，从没人进来过。

paras.en: There were baskets heaped full of yarn balls and a wooden rack that contained thread in every color of the rainbow.
paras.zh: 安娜的目光扫向妈妈手边桌上的一卷卷布料、纸样、剪刀和软尺。

paras.en: Sweaters embroidered with tiny reindeer, kissing birds, and rows of snowflakes hung on a rod, ready for delivery.
paras.zh: 那里有堆满毛线团的篮子，还有一个木架子，上面挂着彩虹里每一种颜色的线。

paras.en: Three sewing machines sat unused against the wall.
paras.zh: 绣着小驯鹿、亲嘴小鸟和一排排雪花的毛衣挂在杆子上，准备送出去。

paras.en: Mama didn’t have as much help in her charitable efforts since they had dismissed half the servants.
paras.zh: 三台缝纫机靠墙摆着，无人使用。

paras.en: It seemed she would never finish all the work she had laid out for herself.
paras.zh: 自从辞退了一半仆人，妈妈做慈善活计时帮手就少了。

paras.en: Papa had said to find something useful to do.
paras.zh: 她似乎永远也做不完自己给自己揽下的活。

paras.en: Anna should really help Mama.
paras.zh: 爸爸说过，找点有用的事做。

paras.en: She’d already lapped the first floor of the castle four times, and her stomach growled.
paras.zh: 安娜真该帮帮妈妈。

paras.en: But luncheon was more than an hour away!
paras.zh: 她已经绕着城堡一层转了四圈，肚子也咕咕叫了。

paras.en: Anna lifted her foot back onto the bike pedal.
paras.zh: 可离午饭还有一个多小时！

paras.en: She could grab a waffle and bring her mother one, too.
paras.zh: 安娜把脚重新踩回自行车踏板。

paras.en: But as she started to ride, she found herself pedaling toward Mama instead of away.
paras.zh: 她可以抓块华夫饼，也顺便给妈妈带一块。

paras.en: Visions of Mama singing her praises to Father at dinner propelled Anna into the sewing room. “Hello, dear.” Mama beckoned. “Come in!” Anna grinned and rode inside.
paras.zh: 可刚骑起来，她发现自己踩着踏板，是冲着妈妈去了，而不是离开。

paras.en: Perhaps she was needed after all.
paras.zh: 脑海里浮现出妈妈在晚饭时向爸爸夸奖自己的画面，这念头推着安娜进了缝纫室。“你好呀，亲爱的。”妈妈招招手。“进来！”安娜咧嘴一笑，骑了进去。

paras.en: She leaned her bike against the wall, ran over, and gave her mother a hug.
paras.zh: 也许她终究是被需要的。

paras.en: Then she stood straight as a soldier and clicked her heels. “Princess Anna reporting for duty!” “Duty?” her mother chuckled. “Yes, I’m here to help.
paras.zh: 她把车靠在墙上，跑过去给了妈妈一个拥抱。

paras.en: Put me to work!” Anna didn’t miss that her mother nibbled on her top lip.
paras.zh: 接着她像士兵一样站得笔直，鞋跟一并。“安娜公主前来报到！”“报到？”妈妈忍俊不禁。“对，我是来帮忙的。

paras.en: It was something Mama did when she needed time to think.
paras.zh: 给我派活吧！”安娜没漏看妈妈轻咬着上嘴唇。

paras.en: Anna’s heart dropped.
paras.zh: 那是妈妈需要思考时会做的动作。

paras.en: She didn’t have the best sewing skills.
paras.zh: 安娜的心一沉。

paras.en: But she was willing to learn.
paras.zh: 她的缝纫技术可不怎么样。

paras.en: Maybe she would find that she was amazing at sewing.
paras.zh: 但她愿意学。

paras.en: The best in the land!
paras.zh: 或许她会发现自己缝纫方面出奇地拿手。

paras.en: There had to be something she was good at. “I’ll listen, Mama.
paras.zh: 全国第一！

paras.en: I promise!” “All right.” Her mother offered a gentle smile and patted the sofa cushion. “Sit next to me and I’ll show you what to do.” After a flurry of instructions, Anna began sewing together soft woolen fabric to create a sock. “Make the stitches as small and close to the edges as possible.
paras.zh: 总该有她擅长的事吧。“我听您的，妈妈。

paras.en: Once you’re finished, we will turn the sock inside out so those stitches will be on the inside.” “Got it!” Anna stuck her tongue out to the side and screwed up one eye, focusing all her attention on her work. “When I’m finished, can I give these stockings to Papa?” “There’s a slight problem with that,” Mama said pragmatically.
paras.zh: 我保证！””好吧。”妈妈温和地一笑，拍了拍沙发垫。“坐我旁边，我教你怎么做。”一阵飞快的指点后，安娜开始把柔软的羊毛布料缝在一起，做一只袜子。“针脚要尽可能又小又靠边。

paras.en: Anna clamped the needle between her teeth and raised the attached pieces of fabric. “Oh!” she said out of the side of her mouth. “These would never fit Papa.
paras.zh: 做完后，我们把袜子翻过来，针脚就藏里面了。”“明白！”安娜把舌头歪向一边，眯起一只眼，全神贯注地做活。“等我做好了，能把这袜子给爸爸吗？”“这事有个小问题，”妈妈务实地说。

paras.en: His feet are as big as shovels!” Her mother’s laughter sounded like light skipping across a babbling stream.
paras.zh: 安娜用牙齿咬住针，举起连着的布片。“哦！”她从嘴角漏出声。“这根本套不进爸爸的脚。

paras.en: Anna stopped to stare at her beautiful mama, praying one day she might become a tenth as lovely.
paras.zh: 他的脚大得像铲子！”妈妈的笑声，像光点在潺潺溪水上跳跃。

paras.en: When Mama’s mirth had subsided, she wrapped an arm around Anna and squeezed her close. “You are the delight of my life, little one.
paras.zh: 安娜停下手，盯着美丽的妈妈，暗暗祈祷有一天自己能有她十分之一的动人。

paras.en: But let’s not tell your father the part about the shovels.” “Yes, Mama,” Anna said with a contented sigh.
paras.zh: 等妈妈的笑意平息，她用一只手臂搂住安娜，把她紧紧贴向自己。“你是妈妈生命中的欢乐，小家伙。

paras.en: She could’ve stayed tucked against her mother’s warm side, breathing in her powdery scent, for the rest of the day.
paras.zh: 不过铲子那句，咱们别告诉你爸爸。”“好的，妈妈，”安娜满足地叹了口气。

paras.en: But the socks would not sew themselves, so she set about her task with singular focus.
paras.zh: 她本可以整日都偎在妈妈温暖的身侧，嗅着她身上那股粉香。

paras.en: Maybe if she finished quickly enough, Olina would make her a fresh waffle.
paras.zh: 但袜子不会自己缝好，于是她带着一股专注劲儿干起活来。

paras.en: After what felt like hours, Anna finished stitching the edges of the fabric together. “Ta-da!” But when she lifted the completed sock, the blanket her mother was knitting rose with it.
paras.zh: 或许要是做得够快，奥丽娜会给她现做一块华夫饼。

paras.en: Realizing that she had accidentally sewn the sock to her mother’s beautiful creation, Anna shrieked and jumped to her feet.
paras.zh: 仿佛过了好几个小时，安娜终于把布边缝在了一起。“当当！”可当她举起做好的袜子，妈妈正在织的毯子也跟着升了起来。

paras.en: As she did, her foot caught in a loop of yarn and she tumbled to the side, knocking her mother’s sewing kit into the air.
paras.zh: 安娜意识到自己不小心把袜子缝到了妈妈漂亮的作品上，尖叫着跳了起来。

paras.en: Anna reached out to catch it too late as dozens of needles, straight pins, and bobbins of thread flew into the air, then crashed to the floor, rolling in all directions. “Oh no!” When the cacophony of plinking sounds finally stopped, Mother frowned and shook her head.
paras.zh: 这一跳，她的脚绊进一圈毛线，朝旁边摔倒，把妈妈的针线盒撞飞到了半空。

paras.en: Anna’s throat squeezed.
paras.zh: 安娜伸手去接，已经太迟——几十根针、大头针和线轴飞向空中，又哗啦摔到地上，滚向四面八方。“哦不！”当那片叮叮当当的杂乱声响终于停息，妈妈皱起眉，摇了摇头。

paras.en: Mama painted on a smile and sighed. “It’s fine, dear.
paras.zh: 安娜的喉咙一紧。

paras.en: Just pick everything up and I’ll work on detaching your sock.” “I’m sorry, Mama.” Anna’s shoulder’s slumped.
paras.zh: 妈妈挤出一个笑容，叹了口气。“没事，亲爱的。

paras.en: So much for being the best seamstress in the land. “It’s fine, dear.
paras.zh: 把东西都捡起来，我来把你的袜子拆下来。”“对不起，妈妈。”安娜的肩膀垮了下来。

paras.en: No harm done.” On hands and knees, Anna crawled around the floor cleaning up the enormous mess she’d made.
paras.zh: “全国第一缝纫师”算是没戏了。“没事，亲爱的。

paras.en: It was a common predicament she found herself in—making up for the chaos she seemed to create everywhere she went.
paras.zh: 没造成什么伤害。”安娜趴在地上，爬来爬去收拾自己弄出的这一大片狼藉。

paras.en: Apologizing for some tangle or another.
paras.zh: 这已是她常见的处境——为她走到哪儿都似乎会惹出的混乱善后。

paras.en: She picked up a needle and accidentally pricked her finger.
paras.zh: 为这样那样的乱子道歉。

paras.en: Her eyes stung as she sucked away the drop of blood.
paras.zh: 她拾起一根针，不小心扎破了手指。

paras.en: Yet it wasn’t the pain of the stick but the throb in her chest that hurt; the disappointment that she had discovered another thing she wasn’t good at.
paras.zh: 她吮掉那滴血，眼睛一阵发酸。

paras.en: Anna trudged down the corridor toward her bedroom.
paras.zh: 可刺痛她的不是针扎的疼，而是胸口那阵闷痛——是她又发现自己有一件事做不好的失落。

paras.en: After lunch her mother had suggested that Anna take a rest.
paras.zh: 安娜拖着步子沿走廊朝自己卧室走去。

paras.en: Not a nap , although Anna was certain that was what she’d meant.
paras.zh: 午饭后，妈妈提议安娜去歇一会儿。

paras.en: Not as a punishment, Mama had clarified—although being banished from the sewing room felt like a direct result of her clumsy mistake.
paras.zh: 不是小睡，尽管安娜确信那正是她的意思。

paras.en: If Anna had crafted the most beautiful sock, and not sewn it to her mother’s blanket, and not knocked the sewing kit into the air and watched it explode like fireworks, Mama would still want her help.
paras.zh: 不是惩罚，妈妈特意说明——尽管被“驱逐”出缝纫室，感觉正是她笨手笨脚犯错的直接后果。

paras.en: Elsa had always been good at dancing and playing the piano and sewing.
paras.zh: 要是安娜做出了最漂亮的袜子，没把它缝到妈妈的毯子上，没把针线盒撞飞、看着它像烟花一样炸开，妈妈还是会要她帮忙的。

paras.en: Her sister’s calm and focus allowed her to master any skill she set her mind to.
paras.zh: 艾莎一向擅长跳舞、弹钢琴和缝纫。

paras.en: At least that was how she used to be.
paras.zh: 姐姐的沉着和专注，让她能掌握任何下定决心去学的本事。

paras.en: Ever since Elsa had gotten sick, Anna had not been allowed to see her.
paras.zh: 至少从前是这样。

paras.en: She didn’t know for certain what was wrong with Elsa—Mama and Papa would never say—but what other explanation could there be?
paras.zh: 自从艾莎生病，安娜就不被允许见她了。

paras.en: Anna had imagined all sorts of horrid illnesses that Elsa could have: pox that covered her from head to toe in enormous welts, a virus that turned her skin purple and her hair blue, a wasting disease, the putrid throat, or the worst of the lot, hippofanatitis .
paras.zh: 她并不确切知道艾莎怎么了——妈妈和爸爸从来不说——可还能有什么别的解释呢？

paras.en: She’d overheard a delivery boy talking about it in the courtyard one afternoon.
paras.zh: 安娜想象过艾莎可能得的种种可怕病：让她从头到脚长满大脓疱的天花、让皮肤变紫头发变蓝的病毒、消耗性疾病、烂喉咙，还有最要命的一种——河马咽喉炎。

paras.en: He’d sworn that when he had spied Elsa through the window, she’d grown an enormous snout and her ears had migrated to the top of her head.
paras.zh: 有一天下午，她无意中听见一个送货小哥在庭院里说起这种病。

paras.en: Anna shuddered at the thought.
paras.zh: 他信誓旦旦地说，自己从窗口偷看艾莎时，她长出了一个大鼻子，耳朵还挪到了头顶上。

paras.en: But what was she supposed to think when her parents refused to discuss it?
paras.zh: 安娜想到这打了个寒颤。

paras.en: It had to be something so horrendous that they didn’t want to frighten Anna with the details.
paras.zh: 可父母都不肯谈论这事，她还能怎么想？

paras.en: Anna let out a hard sigh and stopped in front of Elsa’s locked doors.
paras.zh: 那一定是可怕到了极点，他们才不愿把细节说出来吓到安娜。

paras.en: At first, she’d visited her sister every day, sometimes sitting outside her room for hours or sleeping there at night.
paras.zh: 安娜重重叹了口气，停在艾莎紧锁的房门前。

paras.en: She would sing, tell stories, beg Elsa to come out even if they didn’t tell their parents.
paras.zh: 起初，她每天都去看姐姐，有时在门外一坐几小时，有时夜里就睡在那儿。

paras.en: She had insisted that whatever disease Elsa had, she wanted it, too.
paras.zh: 她会唱歌、讲故事，求艾莎出来，哪怕不告诉父母也行。

paras.en: Once, Anna had wrapped her entire body in strips of leather fabric with only tiny holes for her nose and eyes.
paras.zh: 她坚持说，不管艾莎得的是什么病，她也要得。

paras.en: She’d looked like a mummy and walked like one, too.
paras.zh: 有一次，安娜用一条条皮革把自己全身裹起来，只给鼻子和眼睛留了小孔。

paras.en: Anna had figured if she covered every bit of her skin, she would not catch whatever Elsa had.
paras.zh: 她看起来像木乃伊，走起路来也像。

paras.en: She had assured Elsa that it would be safe for her to come in.
paras.zh: 安娜盘算着，只要把皮肤全盖住，就不会被艾莎的病传染。

paras.en: Unfortunately, Papa had come along before Anna could convince Elsa to open the door.
paras.zh: 她向艾莎保证，进来是安全的。

paras.en: Anna knocked three times. “Elsa?
paras.zh: 可惜，安娜还没说服艾莎开门，爸爸就来了。

paras.en: It’s me, Anna.” “I know who it is,” Elsa answered gravely.
paras.zh: 安娜敲了三下。“艾莎？

paras.en: Anna jumped at her sister’s voice and then rushed forward, pressing her mouth to the hairline crack between the doors. “How did you know I was out here?” “You were stomping your feet as you walked.” As usual, Elsa sounded older than her twelve years. “Was not!” Anna insisted with a pout. “What’s wrong, Anna?” Elsa asked with a long sigh.
paras.zh: 是我，安娜。”“我知道是谁，”艾莎严肃地答道。

paras.en: Anna leaned her forehead against the door. “I was worried about you.
paras.zh: 安娜被姐姐的声音吓了一跳，随即冲上前，把嘴贴在门缝上。“你怎么知道我在外面？”“你走路时跺着脚呢。”一如往常，艾莎听起来比她十二岁的年纪成熟。“才没有！”安娜噘着嘴不服。“怎么了，安娜？”艾莎长叹一声问。

paras.en: Papa rushed off earlier.…” Anna heard a thump and knew Elsa was leaning against the other side.
paras.zh: 安娜把额头抵在门上。“我担心你。

paras.en: Anna could almost smell her sister’s fresh scent, like crystallized vanilla and crisp winter winds. “I’m fine,” Elsa huffed.
paras.zh: 爸爸刚急匆匆走了……”安娜听见“咚”的一声，知道艾莎也正靠在门的另一侧。

paras.en: Anna could feel her sister’s frustration.
paras.zh: 安娜几乎能嗅到姐姐清新的气息，像结晶香草和凛冽冬风。“我没事，”艾莎闷声说。

paras.en: It hurt, being shut out by her best friend.
paras.zh: 安娜能感觉到姐姐的沮丧。

paras.en: But she got the feeling it was out of Elsa’s control. “I miss you, Elsa.
paras.zh: 被最好的朋友拒之门外，很伤人。

paras.en: You’re like the peanut butter to my jelly.
paras.zh: 但她觉得，这并非艾莎所能左右。“我想你，艾莎。

paras.en: The ham to my cheese.” Was that a laugh Anna heard through the door?
paras.zh: 你就像我果酱里的花生酱。

paras.en: She pressed her face to the gap.
paras.zh: 你就像我奶酪里的火腿。”门后传来的，是笑声吗？

paras.en: When she only heard silence, she whispered, “I’m lost without you.” “No, Anna.
paras.zh: 她把脸贴上缝隙。

paras.en: You’re better off without me.… I would only—” “You would only what?
paras.zh: 当只听见沉默，她轻声说：“没有你，我就像丢了魂。”“不，安娜。

paras.en: Elsa, talk to me!” An icy chill permeated the wood, and Anna stepped back.
paras.zh: 没有我你反而更好……我只会——”“你只会怎样？

paras.en: Elsa must have walked away and opened a window.
paras.zh: 艾莎，跟我说！”一股寒意渗过木门，安娜退后了一步。

paras.en: Anna hung her head and spoke into the silence. “At least when we were together, I could cheer you up.
paras.zh: 艾莎一定是走开了，打开了窗。

paras.en: It was the one thing I was good at.” “What are you good at, dear one?” a deep voice asked, making Anna whirl to find her father approaching, head cocked to the side, eyes searching as he awaited her reply.
paras.zh: 安娜垂下头，对着沉默开口。“至少我们在一起时，我能让你开心起来。

paras.en: Anna supposed it wouldn’t hurt to tell the truth. “I could always make Elsa happy.
paras.zh: 那是我唯一拿手的事。”“你拿手什么呢，小家伙？”一个低沉的声音问。安娜猛地转身，看见爸爸正走来，头微微歪着，目光探寻，等着她回答。

paras.en: Make her laugh, even when she was sad.” Papa smiled but his eyes were far away as he said, “You could make a polar bear laugh, Anna.” He looked at her, then, “I’ve come to ask if you would accompany me to the harbor.
paras.zh: 安娜想，说实话也无妨。“我总能让艾莎开心。

paras.en: There’s a bit of business I need to take care of with a merchant captain.” Anna’s heart cartwheeled in her chest. “Me?
paras.zh: 让她笑，哪怕她正难过。”爸爸笑了，可眼神飘向远方，说：“你连北极熊都能逗笑，安娜。”他看向她，“我来是想问，你愿不愿意陪我去港口。

paras.en: You want me to come with you?” Bemused, the king replied, “Yes, Anna.
paras.zh: 有个商人船长那儿，我得去办点事。”安娜的心在胸口翻了个跟头。“我？

paras.en: Your mother and I think it would do you good to get out of the castle.
paras.zh: 你想让我一起去？”国王有些好笑地答道：“是的，安娜。

paras.en: Would you like to come?
paras.zh: 你妈妈和我都觉得，让你出城堡透透气对你有好处。

paras.en: I have a horse saddled for you.” Anna jumped up and pumped her fist in the air. “Yes, yes, yes!” The harbor had always felt like a magical place to Anna.
paras.zh: 你愿意来吗？

paras.en: She rode beside her father through the courtyard, past the castle gates, and up to a landscape of glittering blue water and crisscrossing bridges.
paras.zh: 我给你备好马了。”安娜跳起来，朝空中挥了挥拳头。“要要要！”在安娜心里，港口一直像个魔法之地。

paras.en: Sailors in short pants and caps, some with ink circling their arms, bustled around the docks unloading heavy crates of cargo and piling them into wagons.
paras.zh: 她骑马跟在爸爸身边长廊庭院，穿过城堡大门，来到一片波光粼粼的蓝水和纵横交错的桥前面。

paras.en: Fishermen hefted buckets of fresh fish to sell at the market, and others scurried to load supplies onto a glorious ship tied to the longest pier.
paras.zh: 穿着短裤和帽子、有些人手臂上纹着圈圈的水手们在码头穿梭，卸下一箱箱沉重货物，堆上马车。

paras.en: The ship had three masts, with billowing white sails reaching as high as the nearest tower of the castle.
paras.zh: 渔夫扛着一桶桶鲜鱼去集市卖，另一些人则忙着把补给搬上停在最长栈桥边那艘气派的船。

paras.en: The boat was enormous, larger than five cottages stacked side by side. “How many people live on such a boat, Papa?” “That depends, but usually at least twenty.
paras.zh: 那船有三根桅杆，鼓胀的白帆高得几乎够到城堡最近的塔楼。

paras.en: It takes a skilled crew to manage such a vessel.” The briny air pushed Anna’s hair off her face.
paras.zh: 船大得惊人，比五座并排的农舍还大。“这么大一艘船上住多少人呀，爸爸？”“看情况，但通常至少二十个。

paras.en: She breathed deeply.
paras.zh: 驾驭这样的船需要熟练的船员。”咸湿的海风把安娜的头发从脸上吹开。

paras.en: She’d never minded the scents of sea and fishes. “How exciting it would be to sail the open ocean and discover new lands and peoples and languages and food!” Anna sighed dreamily.
paras.zh: 她深深吸了口气。

paras.en: The king chuckled. “Yes, I imagine it would seem romantic to one such as you.” Anna turned to stare at him. “What do you mean, ‘such as you’?
paras.zh: 她从不讨厌海和鱼的味道。“在开阔的大海上航行，去发现新陆地、新人群、新语言和新食物，该多让人兴奋啊！”安娜出神地叹道。

paras.en: Do you mean someone who is always getting in the way?” Her shoulders slumped. “Mama told you what happened in the sewing room.” “Anna, I meant nothing of the sort.
paras.zh: 国王轻笑。“是啊，我想对像你这样的人，那会显得很浪漫。”安娜转头盯着他。“‘像我这样的人’是什么意思？

paras.en: You are never in the way.
paras.zh: 你是说那种总在碍事的人？”她肩膀一垮。“妈妈把缝纫室的事告诉你了。”“安娜，我绝不是那个意思。

paras.en: And yes, your mother explained that you’d tried to help but had a mishap in the process.
paras.zh: 你从不会碍事。

paras.en: That’s why I thought it would do you good to get outside and expend some energy.” A large man in suspenders and high boots with a wicked-looking ice pick strapped to his back stomped past, shouting, “Kristoff!
paras.zh: 是的，你妈妈说了，你是想帮忙，只是过程中出了点岔子。

paras.en: Where could that boy have gotten to now?” Anna’s gaze caught on a shaggy blond head peaking up behind a stack of boxes as he stuffed a krumkake into his mouth and smeared chocolate up one side of his face.
paras.zh: 所以我才想，让你出来活动活动、消耗点精力挺好。”一个穿背带裤、高筒靴，背后挎着一把凶相毕露的冰镐的大个子跺着脚走过，喊道：“克里斯托夫！

paras.en: Their eyes met, and he raised a finger to his lips as if asking her not to reveal his location.
paras.zh: 那小子现在会跑到哪儿去了？”安娜的目光被一个乱蓬蓬的金发脑袋吸引——他从一摞箱子后探出头，正把一块卷心酥塞进嘴里，巧克力糊了半边脸。

paras.en: Then a young reindeer stomped up beside him and nudged his shoulder with his crown of antlers. “Not now, Sven!” The boy pushed the animal away. “I’ll get you another cookie, I promise.” Was this the boy the ice harvester was searching for?
paras.zh: 两人的目光碰上，他竖起一根手指贴在嘴唇上，像是在求她别暴露自己的位置。

paras.en: Anna glanced back just as the reindeer’s enormous tongue engulfed the boy’s face and licked the chocolate off his cheek. “EEK!” The boy laughed and playfully slapped the reindeer away.
paras.zh: 接着一只小驯鹿跺着蹄子走到他身边，用头顶的鹿角蹭他的肩膀。“现在不行，斯文！”男孩把动物推开。“我再去给你拿块饼干，我保证。”这男孩，就是那个采冰人找的人吗？

paras.en: Anna giggled even as longing unfurled in her chest.
paras.zh: 安娜刚回头，就见驯鹿的大舌头把男孩的脸整个盖住，把脸颊上的巧克力舔掉了。“呀！”男孩大笑，调皮地把驯鹿拍开。

paras.en: What she wouldn’t give to have such companionship.
paras.zh: 安娜咯咯笑起来，可胸口却悄然漾开一阵渴望。

paras.en: A few moments later they reached the end of the pier, and Anna stared up and up and up into the snapping canvas sails, mesmerized by their dance.
paras.zh: 她多么渴望能有这样的陪伴啊。

paras.en: Father dismounted and then reached to help Anna down.
paras.zh: 片刻后，他们到了栈桥尽头，安娜仰头、再仰头、拼命仰头，望着啪啪作响的帆布船帆，看它们起舞看得入了迷。

paras.en: He held her under her arms, and she placed her hands on his shoulders, eye to eye for once. “Papa, may I please go on board the ship?
paras.zh: 爸爸先下了马，然后伸手扶安娜下来。

paras.en: Please? ” She puffed out her bottom lip and stared at him with puppy eyes. “No, dear.
paras.zh: 他托着她的腋下，她把手搭上他的肩膀，难得地和他平视。“爸爸，我能上船看看吗？

paras.en: It isn’t safe for one as curious as yourself,” Father said as he set her onto the boards of the dock. “Stay close while I speak with this gentleman, and then I’ll take you to Blodget’s Bakery and buy you a whole bag of rosettes.” Rosettes were her very favorite cookie: sweet batter shaped like flowers, fried, and topped with powdered sugar.
paras.zh: 求你了？”她撅起下嘴唇，用小狗般的眼神望着他。“不行，亲爱的。

paras.en: Anna’s mouth watered just imagining the first bite as it melted on her tongue. “Yes, Papa.” Father strode off to speak with a rotund man in a tall feathered hat, and Anna wandered over to the edge of the dock and stared out at the fjord speckled with silver shards of sunlight.
paras.zh: 对像你这么好奇的孩子不安全，”爸爸说着把她放到栈桥的木板上。“我同这位先生说话时你待在附近，然后我带你去布洛杰特面包房，给你买一整袋玫瑰花酥。”玫瑰花酥是她最爱的点心：甜面糊做成花形，炸过再撒上糖粉。

paras.en: The trail of sparkles led through craggy gray mountains to the open sea beyond.
paras.zh: 光想象第一口在舌尖化开，安娜就流口水了。“好的，爸爸。”爸爸大步去和一位戴高羽毛帽的胖男人说话，安娜溜达到栈桥边，望着点缀着银色阳光碎片的峡湾。

paras.en: And to adventure.
paras.zh: 那道闪光的小径穿过灰色的嶙峋群山，通向远方的开阔大海。

paras.en: Anna exhaled slowly.
paras.zh: 也通向冒险。

paras.en: Perhaps her destiny lay beyond the boundaries of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 安娜缓缓吐了口气。

paras.en: What if she possessed the talent for sailing and discovery and such?
paras.zh: 也许她的命运，就在阿伦黛尔边界之外。

paras.en: How would she ever know if she didn’t try?
paras.zh: 万一她有航海、探索之类的天赋呢？

paras.en: She stared at the looming hull of the ship as it bobbed up and slapped back down in the gentle waves.
paras.zh: 不试一试，她又怎么知道？

paras.en: The sides were carved with the shapes of blooming flowers, and blue and green scrolling designs marked the vessel as Arendellian.
paras.zh: 她盯着那艘船高耸的船身，它在温柔的波浪里上下浮沉，拍打着水面。

paras.en: She stood near the bow, and the eyes of a wooden puffin figurehead perched there watched her, inviting her to come aboard.
paras.zh: 船舷上雕着绽放的花朵，蓝绿相间的卷曲花纹标明这是艘阿伦黛尔的船。

paras.en: Anna glanced back to where Papa spoke with the captain, their heads bent in deep concentration.
paras.zh: 她站在船头附近，那儿一只木制海鹦船首像的眼睛正望着她，像在邀请她上船。

paras.en: She had told her father she would stay nearby.
paras.zh: 安娜回头望向爸爸和船长说话的地方，两人正低着头，专注地谈着。

paras.en: It wasn’t honorable to break a promise.
paras.zh: 她答应过爸爸会待在附近。

paras.en: Her feet tingled, energy coursing up her legs imploring her to move.
paras.zh: 违背诺言可不算光彩。

paras.en: To go!
paras.zh: 她的脚一阵发麻，一股劲从腿上窜起，催她迈步。

paras.en: A ramp led from the dock to the ship.
paras.zh: 去呀！

paras.en: Wide and sturdy, it didn’t appear dangerous at all. “Help!” Anna’s eyes jerked up to the deck of the ship. “Stop.
paras.zh: 一道跳板从栈桥连到船上。

paras.en: Help!” The voice sounded young.
paras.zh: 又宽又结实，看起来一点也不危险。“救命！”安娜的目光猛地抬起，落到甲板上。“住手。

paras.en: Anna took several steps back and shielded her eyes as she searched for the person in distress.
paras.zh: 救命！”那声音听上去是个孩子。

paras.en: A boy, no older than herself, hung upside down from the mainmast, his ankle caught in a rope.
paras.zh: 安娜后退几步，手搭凉棚，寻找那个遇险的人。

paras.en: Red hair hung straight down from his head, and his green eyes darted as a couple of teenage sailors poked him, cackling as they watched him swing.
paras.zh: 一个不比她大的男孩头朝下吊在主桅杆上，脚踝卡在绳里。

paras.en: Hands on her hips, Anna did her best to imitate her mother’s queen voice as she demanded, “Release that boy this instant!” The boy’s tormentors whirled to face Anna.
paras.zh: 红头发笔直垂下，绿眼睛慌乱转动，两个十来岁的水手戳着他，看他晃来晃去，咯咯直笑。

paras.en: A lanky young man with braided brown hair scoffed, “And why should we do that?” “Yeah,” the round one chimed in. “We don’t answer to little girls .” “Yeah,” the lanky sailor said as he stepped toward her with a menacing frown. “You might want to listen to her, chaps,” the boy hanging upside down said. “That be the princess.” “And how would ye know that?” the shorter sailor asked as he gave the boy another shove, sending him in dizzying circles.
paras.zh: 安娜叉起腰，尽力模仿妈妈当女王时的嗓音，喝道：“立刻放了那个男孩！”欺负他的男孩们猛地转过身面对安娜。

paras.en: Even as he spun, the boy said, “’Cause I just watched her ride up next to the king, ye dimwits!” The lanky sailor froze mid-stalk, and the round one paled even as he pulled a cutlass from his belt and swung it toward the dangling boy. “Wait, stop!” Anna flung herself forward as the knife sliced through the rope and the redheaded boy fell to the deck with a smack.
paras.zh: 一个棕色辫子的瘦高青年嗤笑道：“我们凭什么听你的？”“就是，”圆脸的那个附和，“我们可不听小丫头的话。”“就是，”瘦高水手皱着威胁的眉，朝她逼近一步。“你们最好听她的，伙计们，”倒吊的男孩说，“那是公主。”“你咋知道？”矮个水手又推了男孩一把，把他转得晕头转向。

paras.en: Anna ran over and knelt beside him. “Are you okay?” The boy lay curled on his side, and when Anna touched his arm, he glanced up with wet green eyes. “I’m fine.” Up close, Anna could see that he was younger than her by a few years.
paras.zh: 即便转着，男孩仍说：“因为我刚看见她骑马跟在国王旁边，你们这群笨蛋！”瘦高水手僵在半步，圆脸的则脸色发白，却已从腰间抽出短弯刀，朝吊着的男孩挥去。“等等，住手！”刀划断绳索，红发男孩“啪”地摔在甲板上，安娜猛地扑上前。

paras.en: What was such a young child doing on a ship? “Are you a sailor?” she asked. “Of a sort.” “He ain’t no sailor,” one of the tormentors spat. “He ain’t nothing but a nuisance.” The other bully laughed. “Only reason he’s here is ’cause he’s the quartermaster’s son and his mama don’t want him!” The boy swallowed hard, and Anna could see he was fighting against his tears. “What’s your name?” she asked. “Ebbe,” he muttered. “Ebbe,” Anna began. “Are you injured?” “I don’t think… think so.” Ebbe sat up and cradled the arm he’d landed on, his chin trembling. “Would serve the little pest right!” the lanky sailor spat.
paras.zh: 安娜跑过去，跪在他身旁。“你没事吧？”男孩侧身蜷着，安娜碰到他手臂时，他抬起湿漉漉的绿眼睛看她。“我没事。”近看，安娜才发现他比自己小几岁。

paras.en: Ebbe hung his head and whispered, “I only get in the way.” Anna took the boy’s hand and tugged him to his feet. “My papa says that if you square your shoulders and lift your chin, you always feel stronger.” Ebbe’s head snapped up. “The king says that?” “Yep.
paras.zh: 这么小的孩子跑船上干啥？“你是水手吗？”她问。“算是吧。”“他算哪门子水手，”一个欺负人的啐道，“他就是个讨人厌的麻烦精。”另一个坏小子笑说：“他在这就因为他是舵长的儿子，他妈不要他！”男孩用力咽了口唾沫，安娜看得出他在强忍眼泪。“你叫什么？”她问。“埃贝，”他嘟囔。“埃贝，”安娜开口，“你受伤了吗？”“我想……想没有。”埃贝坐起来，护着落地时撑的那条胳膊，下巴发颤。“那小惹祸精活该！”瘦高水手啐道。

paras.en: And my mother tells me that everybody is good at something.
paras.zh: 埃贝垂下头，小声说：“我就是碍事。”安娜拉住男孩的手，把他拽起来。“我爸爸说，只要端平肩膀、抬起下巴，你就会觉得自己更有力气。”埃贝猛地抬头。“国王说的？”“嗯。

paras.en: It just takes some of us longer to find our gifts.” The round sailor stepped forward. “The queen says that?” Anna gave a nod.
paras.zh: 而且我妈妈告诉我，每个人都有自己的长处。

paras.en: The lanky young man propped his hands on his hips. “I ain’t got no talents.
paras.zh: 只是有些人要花更久才找得到自己的天赋。”圆脸水手上前一步。“王后说的？”安娜点点头。

paras.en: That’s why my ma kicked me out at seventeen.
paras.zh: 瘦高青年叉起腰。“我可没啥天赋。

paras.en: Swabbin’ decks is the only job I could find.” “And that’s only because my pa felt sorry for you and took ye on,” Ebbe fired back, his tears replaced by anger.
paras.zh: 所以我妈在我十七岁那年把我赶出了门。

paras.en: The lanky sailor lunged.
paras.zh: 擦甲板是我唯一找得到的工作。”“那还因为我爸可怜你，才收留你，”埃贝反击道，眼泪变成了怒气。

paras.en: Anna stepped between them and flung her hands out. “Stop!
paras.zh: 瘦高水手扑了过来。

paras.en: If you quit squabbling and feeling sorry for yourselves, you could help one another.” The bickering boys stilled. “How’s that?” Ebbe scratched his head. “Treat others the way you wish to be treated.” Anna repeated something her mother was fond of saying. “How’s that?” the thin one asked. “For one,” Anna said, “if you work together, you can accomplish much more.” “Like what?” the shorter sailor asked. “You can do whatever you set your mind to!” Anna gestured to the magnificent ship, their vessel to the world. “And me, too?” A teenage sailor Anna had never seen before stepped into view.
paras.zh: 安娜挡在两人中间，张开双手。“住手！

paras.en: Then another young man and a boy of around twelve, until Anna was surrounded by scruffy sailors. “You’re all like Vikings of old, sailing the fjords to find treasure!” Anna cleared her suddenly dry throat and lifted her chin. “I mean, all of you have gifts and a bigger destiny.” An adolescent with inked-up arms said, “I don’t fulfill any destiny.” His words were gruff, yet Anna could see the longing in his eyes.
paras.zh: 如果你们别再斗嘴、别再自怜，就能互相帮忙。”吵闹的男孩们安静了。“怎么说？”埃贝挠挠头。“你希望别人怎样待你，就怎样待别人。”安娜重复着妈妈爱说的一句话。“啥意思？”瘦的那个问。“比方说，”安娜说，“你们合作，能做成的事多得多。”“比如呢？”矮水手问。“只要下定决心，你们什么都能做到！”安娜朝那艘壮观的船一指，那是他们驶向世界的船。“那我也能？”一个安娜从没见过的十来岁水手凑上前来。

paras.en: Anna straightened her spine and asked, “What do you do on the ship?” “Trim the sails and care for the rigging.
paras.zh: 接着又来一个青年和一个十二岁左右的男孩，直到安娜被一群邋遢水手围住。“你们都像古代的维京人，航行峡湾去寻找宝藏！”安娜清了清突然发干的嗓子，抬起下巴。“我是说，你们每个人都有天赋，都有更宏大的命运。”一个满臂纹身的小伙子说：“我可担不起什么命运。”话虽生硬，安娜却看得到他眼里的渴望。

paras.en: Ain’t no destiny in that.
paras.zh: 安娜挺直脊背问：“你在船上做什么？”

paras.en: Except pinched fingers and sunburn!” the tattooed sailor scoffed.
paras.zh: “修剪船帆、照管索具。

paras.en: Several of the boys laughed. “When you sail through a storm,” Anna said, projecting her voice, “do you lower the sails to keep the boat from blowing off course?” “Yes…” “Then you are responsible for every life on this ship.” The young man’s eyes widened.
paras.zh: 这可没什么命运可言。

paras.en: Anna turned as she spoke to the entire group. “Each of you brings goods to Arendelle that enrich our land.
paras.zh: 除了夹痛的手指和晒伤的皮！”纹身水手嗤道。

paras.en: Books for education.
paras.zh: 几个男孩笑了。“当你们在风暴里航行，”安娜提高声音说，“是不是要降下船帆，免得船被吹偏航？”“是……”“那这条船上每一条命，都系在你身上。”小伙子睁大了眼。

paras.en: Rice that feeds those who are less fortunate.
paras.zh: 安娜转向全体人说：“你们每个人，都给阿伦黛尔带来丰富这片土地的商品。

paras.en: Just last week, I heard about a cargo that brought metals used to repair a broken waterwheel that supplies fresh water to the entire village!” Anna turned back and faced Ebbe. “Everybody is important, and my papa says we all have a purpose.” “She’s right,” someone with a deep voice said as the crowd parted for the king.
paras.zh: 书籍，用于教育。

paras.en: Immediately every sailor dropped to one knee.
paras.zh: 大米，养活那些不那么幸运的人。

paras.en: Anna gaped up at her father, his green eyes shining down on her with pride. “You should all listen to Princess Anna.
paras.zh: 就上周，我还听说一船货运来了修水车的金属，那水车给全村供清水！”安娜转回来，面对埃贝。“人人都重要，我爸爸说我们都有存在的意义。”“她说得对，”一个低沉的声音说，人群为国王让开一条路。

paras.en: She is wise beyond her years,” Papa said without taking his eyes off Anna’s face. “If you are fortunate, you will have the gift of leadership like my daughter, and you can inspire others to be part of something greater than themselves.” Anna couldn’t speak through the tightness in her throat as Papa led her by the hand through the crowd of burly men who each bowed their heads to her.
paras.zh: 水手们立刻齐刷刷单膝跪下。

paras.en: Once they were off the ship, Papa stooped to Anna’s level and took her face in his hands. “That, my darling, is what it means to be a fearless leader.” “Was I indom-itable?” Papa laughed as he stood and then helped her onto her horse. “Yes.
paras.zh: 安娜仰头呆望着爸爸，他绿色的眼睛带着骄傲俯视着她。“你们都该听安娜公主的。

paras.en: And brave and inspiring and—” “And irrepressible?” Anna asked hopefully. “You are all of those things, and more, Anna.” Papa sat in his saddle and helped lead her horse around.
paras.zh: 她比同龄人睿智得多，”爸爸目不转睛地看着安娜的脸说。“如果有幸，你们会像我女儿一样拥有领导的天赋，能激励他人去成就比自身更伟大的事。”安娜喉咙发紧，说不出话，爸爸牵着她的手，领她穿过那群壮汉，每个人都向她低头致意。

paras.en: As they entered the empty bridge that connected the harbor to the boardwalk, Papa spoke over the squawks of seabirds and the clomp of the horses’ hooves. “Anna, I never want you to doubt yourself and your value.
paras.zh: 一下船，爸爸弯下身，与安娜平视，双手捧住她的脸。“亲爱的，那就是无畏的领袖意味着什么。”“我‘不屈’了吗？”爸爸站起来，扶她上马，笑着说：“是的。

paras.en: You have a natural empathy for others that allows you to see from their point of view.
paras.zh: 还勇敢、还鼓舞人心，而且——”“还有‘压制不住’？”安娜满怀希望地问。“你全都具备，而且不止这些，安娜。”爸爸坐上马鞍，牵着她的马转了个圈。

paras.en: To identify the very thing that will encourage them the most.
paras.zh: 当他们走上连接港口和步道的空桥，爸爸压过海鸟的鸣叫和马蹄的嗒嗒声说：“安娜，我永远不要你怀疑自己、怀疑自己的价值。

paras.en: It is a rare gift to leave people better than you found them.
paras.zh: 你对他人有一种天然的共情，能站在他们的角度看问题。

paras.en: But you are more than the sum of your parts.” Anna gazed up at her father, wanting to take in every word, every nuance of his voice, even the glint of the sun off his burnished hair.
paras.zh: 能找准最能鼓舞他们的事。

paras.en: She swallowed the lump in her throat and asked, “What do you mean, Papa?” Father tugged their horses to a stop. “Anna, you make me proud just by being yourself.
paras.zh: 让人因你而变得更好，是种难得的天赋。

paras.en: You never have to do anything to earn my approval.
paras.zh: 但你远不止是各部分的相加。”安娜仰头望着爸爸，想把他的每句话、每个语气的细微差别，甚至阳光在他光泽头发上的闪烁，都记在心里。

paras.en: I love you just the way you are.” Anna’s heart ballooned until she felt like she was floating. “Truly, Papa?” He smiled wide. “Always and forever, dear one.” Queen Anna looked out at the crowd, hundreds of eyes gazing up at her with varying expressions of anticipation and hope.
paras.zh: 她咽下喉咙里的哽咽，问：“这是什么意思，爸爸？”爸爸勒马停下。“安娜，光是做你自己，就让我骄傲。

paras.en: She saw Oaken, head and shoulders above the rest, hands clasped in front of him as he bounced on his toes.
paras.zh: 你从不需要做任何事来换取我的认可。

paras.en: Then, on the edge of the front row, her Kristoff smiled and gave a nod that sent a swath of unruly blond hair over his eyes.
paras.zh: 我爱你本来的样子。”安娜的心像充了气般膨胀，简直要飘起来。“真的吗，爸爸？”他开朗地笑了。“永远，亲爱的，永远。”安娜女王望向人群，数百双眼睛带着或期待或希冀的神情仰望着她。

paras.en: Next to him, Olaf waved a tiny arm, and she could hear his little voice calling out, “Queen Anna!
paras.zh: 她看见奥肯，高出旁人一头一肩，双手在身前交握，踮着脚一蹦一蹦。

paras.en: I know her!
paras.zh: 接着，在前排边上，她的克里斯托夫笑了笑，点了下头，一缕不羁的金发滑落到眼睛上。

paras.en: She’s my friend!” Anna gave a discreet wave in his direction and searched through the faces again.
paras.zh: 他身旁，雪宝挥着小胳膊，她能听见那细细的嗓音喊着：“安娜女王！

paras.en: She’d sent Elsa an invitation and asked her to come and celebrate the day with them.
paras.zh: 我认识她！

paras.en: But her sister couldn’t always get away.
paras.zh: 她是我的朋友！”安娜朝他那边悄悄挥了下手，又去人群中搜寻。

paras.en: Elsa was tied to the Enchanted Forest in ways that Anna didn’t quite understand.
paras.zh: 她给艾莎发了邀请，请她来和他们一起庆祝这一天。

paras.en: Still, a tiny part of her had hoped.
paras.zh: 但姐姐并不总是能抽身。

paras.en: The band finished playing their lively rendition of the national anthem, and nerves balled like wet yarn in Anna’s gut.
paras.zh: 艾莎与魔法森林之间，有着安娜不太理解的牵绊。

paras.en: Would the citizens see this new agreement with the Southern Isles as a step forward for their country, or would some allow old resentments to cloud their perception?
paras.zh: 可她心底，仍有一丝希望。

paras.en: Anna took a deep breath, and a voice spoke so loudly in her mind that she nearly jumped.
paras.zh: 乐队奏完欢快版的国歌，安娜的胃里像攥着一团湿毛线，紧张成一团。

paras.en: If you are fortunate, you will have the gift of leadership like my daughter, and you can inspire others to be part of something greater than themselves.
paras.zh: 百姓们会把这份与南境群岛的新协定看作国家向前的一步，还是有人会让旧怨蒙蔽了他们的判断？

paras.en: Inspire them to be part of something greater than themselves… Anna could do that.
paras.zh: 安娜深吸一口气，一个声音在脑海里响得她几乎跳起来。

paras.en: Anna squared her shoulders and lifted her chin. “Good afternoon, citizens of Arendelle!” The crowd cheered, and Anna smiled. “We have been given an unprecedented opportunity to bring two nations together.
paras.zh: “如果有幸，你们会像我女儿一样拥有领导的天赋，能激励他人去成就比自身更伟大的事。”

paras.en: A partnership that my father, King Agnarr, dreamed of solidifying has come to fruition.
paras.zh: 激励他们去成就比自身更伟大的事……安娜能做到。

paras.en: Arendelle now has a free trade agreement with the Southern Isles!” As Anna spoke, detailing all the benefits of the arrangement she had painstakingly negotiated, the people hung on her every word, some nodding, smiling, or whispering excitedly to one another.
paras.zh: 安娜端平肩膀，抬起下巴。“下午好，阿伦黛尔的公民们！”人群欢呼，安娜笑了。“我们获得了一个前所未有的机会，让两个国家走到一起。

paras.en: Heart near bursting, Anna spotted the one face she most hoped to see.
paras.zh: 我父亲安格瑞国王梦想缔结的伙伴关系，如今终于成真。

paras.en: Elsa!
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔现在与南境群岛达成了自由贸易协定！”安娜讲话时，细细列举她费心谈判达成的各项好处，人们全神贯注地听着她的每句话，有的点头、有的微笑，或兴奋地彼此低语。

paras.en: Her sister stood beside Olaf, tears brimming in her eyes as she nodded her encouragement. “In conclusion, it is with great joy and optimism that I see Arendelle moving into a new era.
paras.zh: 心几乎要炸开，安娜瞥见了她最想见的那张脸。

paras.en: An era of growth and expansion that will positively impact us individually and as a nation.
paras.zh: 艾莎！

paras.en: I invite you to join me in becoming part of this incredible opportunity!” Cheers and applause erupted, and Olaf rushed the stage, with Elsa and Kristoff not far behind. “Queen Anna!
paras.zh: 姐姐站在雪宝身旁，眼里闪着泪光，点头给她鼓励。“最后，我怀着巨大的喜悦与乐观，看到阿伦黛尔正迈入一个新时代。

paras.en: Do you think the Southern Isles would be interested in adopting some snowgies?” The little snowman cupped a hand around his mouth and stage-whispered, “There are way too many of them.” Anna laughed.
paras.zh: 一个成长与扩张的时代，将对我们每个人、对整个国家产生积极影响。

paras.en: She happened to know that Olaf and the snowgies had a complicated relationship. “Let’s go, little man,” Kristoff said as he herded Olaf away. “There’s a pumpkin-spice snow cone with Sven’s name on it.” “Okay!” Olaf hopped from foot to foot. “Did you know that pumpkins are the biggest fruit in the world?
paras.zh: 我邀请你们与我一同，成为这不可思议机遇的一部分！”欢呼和掌声骤起，雪宝冲上舞台，艾莎和克里斯托夫紧跟在后。“安娜女王！

paras.en: They can weigh up to a ton, and I read a story about a carriage made from…” Anna met the eyes of her sister, but before they could speak, Oaken strode onto the stage. “Queen Anna!
paras.zh: 你觉得南境群岛会有兴趣领养一些小雪灵吗？”小雪人把手拢在嘴边，像说悄悄话似的说：“它们实在太多了。”安娜笑了。

paras.en: I would like to speak to you about my Hygge for Home products.
paras.zh: 她恰好知道，雪宝和小雪灵的关系挺复杂。“走吧，小家伙，”克里斯托夫把雪宝往旁边赶，“有个南瓜香料刨冰，上面写着斯文的名字呢。”“好耶！”雪宝两只脚跳来跳去。“你知道南瓜是世界上最大的水果吗？

paras.en: I believe the Southern Isles would buy in bulk, ja?
paras.zh: 它们能重达一吨，我还读过一篇讲用南瓜做马车的故事……”安娜与姐姐目光相遇，可还没来得及开口，奥肯大步走上台。“安娜女王！

paras.en: I’d also like to create franchises of Wandering Oaken’s Sandwiches and Sauna Shoppes.” As Anna opened her mouth to respond, Elsa stepped forward. “You may set up a meeting with Anna next week, Oaken.
paras.zh: 我想跟您说说我的‘Hygge居家’产品。

paras.en: But for now, let’s all enjoy the festival.” Elsa placed a delicate hand on the big man’s arm and steered him back toward the celebration.
paras.zh: 我相信南境群岛会成批采购，对吧？

paras.en: When Elsa returned, she embraced Anna in a warm huge. “I’ve never been more sure that you were born for this role.
paras.zh: 我还想开几家‘流浪奥肯三明治与桑拿店’的连锁。”安娜正要答话，艾莎上前一步。“你下周约安娜开个会就好，奥肯。

paras.en: Father would be so proud of your accomplishments.” Anna pulled back and held her sister’s hands. “I know.” Elsa’s eyes fluttered in surprise before her lips slid into a smile. “There’s the confidence I like to see.” Anna grinned. “Papa once told me I was stubborn as a mule and indomitable as a yeti.” Elsa reared back. “He did?” “Well, not in those words exactly.
paras.zh: 不过现在，咱们都先好好享受节日。”艾莎把纤纤玉手搭在大个子手臂上，把他引回庆祝的人群。

paras.en: But you can hardly disagree.” “No.” Elsa snickered. “No, I can’t.” Anna took Elsa’s arm and led her down toward the market. “Can I interest you in a dozen or so snowgies to take to the Enchanted Forest?
paras.zh: 艾莎回来后，给了安娜一个温暖的拥抱。“我从未像现在这样确信，你生来就是担当这个角色的人。

paras.en: Olaf says they’ve become a plague, but he can’t bring himself to smite a single one.” Elsa’s bright, clear laughter lightened Anna’s heart.
paras.zh: 爸爸会为你的成就无比骄傲。”安娜退后一步，握住姐姐的手。“我知道。”艾莎惊讶地眨了眨眼，随后嘴角漾开微笑。“这才是我乐意看到的自信。”安娜咧嘴笑。“爸爸曾说我倔得像骡子，又坚不可摧得像雪怪。”艾莎往后一仰。“他说过？”“嗯，不完全是这几个字。

paras.en: When they reached the statue of their parents, they both stopped and placed a hand upon the stone pedestal, as they always did.
paras.zh: 但你总不能反驳吧。”“不能。”艾莎窃笑。“不，我不能。”安娜挽住艾莎的胳膊，带她往集市走。“要不要带一打左右的小雪灵去魔法森林？

paras.en: But this time, as Anna stared up at her father’s sculpted face, she was almost certain she saw him smile down upon her.
paras.zh: 雪宝说它们都成灾了，可他下不了手去消灭哪怕一只。”艾莎清亮明快的笑声，让安娜的心轻松起来。

chapters.title: Wandering Oaken and the Not-So-Hygge Day

paras.en: “Hoo-hoo!” The big man smiled at his last customer of the day.
paras.zh: 「呼——嗬！」大个子男人冲今天最后一位顾客微笑着。

paras.en: His large steepled hands opened, fingers wiggling spiritedly as he exclaimed, “Big anniversary blowout!
paras.zh: 他双手十指相对搭成尖塔状，随即张开，手指欢快地摆动着，大声宣布：“周年庆大促销！

paras.en: Half off locally carved troll statues, gooseberry lip balm of my own invention, and everything in our new Hygge for Home section, ja?” The young lady stood in the doorway blinking.
paras.zh: 本地雕刻的地精雕像、我自己研制的醋栗润唇膏，还有我们全新『居家Hygge专区』里的所有商品，统统半价，对吧？”年轻姑娘站在门口，眨巴着眼睛。

paras.en: She was Arendellian.
paras.zh: 她是阿伦黛尔人。

paras.en: Oaken could see that much from her clothes.
paras.zh: 奥肯从她的衣着就能看出这一点。

paras.en: She needed sturdier boots and a heavier cloak—both of which he could supply for a reasonable cost.
paras.zh: 她需要更结实的靴子和更厚实的斗篷——这两样他都能以公道的价格提供。

paras.en: Most of all, she was an opportunity to practice his pitch for his latest venture one last time.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，她是个机会，让他能最后一次演练新事业的推销词。

paras.en: While her face had yet to react, Oaken took heart in the fact she remained in the shop.
paras.zh: 尽管她脸上还没什么反应，但奥肯想到她还留在店里，便有了信心。

paras.en: He’d dealt with tough sells before.
paras.zh: 难缠的客人他以前也应付过。

paras.en: No matter the reason for her visit on this most fortuitous of days, she would leave an ambassador for his growing enterprise. “You are in luck,” he said. “Tomorrow is the grand opening of Oaken’s Family-Friendly Cozy Cottages and Sauna.
paras.zh: 不管她今天这么走运的日子来店里所为何事，她离开时都会成为他蒸蒸日上事业的代言人。“你真走运，”他说，“明天『奥肯家庭温馨小屋与桑拿房』就要盛大开业了。

paras.en: I am happy to give you an exclusive sneak peek into this new and one-of-a-kind opportunity for the families of Arendelle.” Oaken stood slowly.
paras.zh: 我很乐意让你抢先一睹这个专为阿伦黛尔家庭打造、独一无二的新机会。”奥肯缓缓站起身。

paras.en: Having been large all his life, he knew his size could be off-putting to strangers.
paras.zh: 他一生都是大块头，知道自己这般体型可能会让陌生人望而却步。

paras.en: But eventually everyone discovered, as his family always said, he was a gentle, hardworking soul.
paras.zh: 但最终大家都会发现，正如他家人常说的，他是个温和又勤恳的人。

paras.en: When the woman didn’t so much as flinch as he stepped around the counter, his heart leapt in excitement.
paras.zh: 当他把柜台绕到她身边，那女人连眼睛都没眨一下时，他兴奋得心里一跳。

paras.en: Gesturing toward the area in the back, separated by partially open sheer curtains, he said, “The trading post has been expanded to include a reception space for guest check-in.
paras.zh: 他朝后方一处用半开的薄纱帘隔开的角落比了比手，说：“杂货铺已经扩建，新增了供客人登记的接待区。

paras.en: Come, come!” Holding back the drapery, he gestured proudly to the room beyond.
paras.zh: 来，来！”他撩开帘子，自豪地朝里间的屋子比了比手。

paras.en: To the right stood a gleaming, natural wood desk facing one of the coziest places Oaken and his family had ever created.
paras.zh: 右边立着一张锃亮的原木书桌，正对着奥肯和家人打造过的最温馨的角落之一。

paras.en: Deep blue chairs and a yellow velvet love seat surrounded three sides of a thick, white shaggy rug.
paras.zh: 深蓝色的椅子和一张黄色丝绒双人沙发，围住了厚实白色长毛地毯的三边。

paras.en: Natural wood end tables were interspersed around the sitting area, and the entire space had been decorated with colorful knitted pillows and throw blankets.
paras.zh: 原木小茶几散落在这片休息区周围，整个空间还用五彩编织靠垫和盖毯装点起来。

paras.en: The cocoa table, situated between the furniture, showcased picture books in artfully arranged shapes.
paras.zh: 摆在家具之间的热可可桌上，精巧地叠放着一本本图画书，造型别致。

paras.en: It also contained a tray of one of Oaken’s Family-Friendly Cozy Cottages’ signature amenities: warm, freshly baked walnut cookies, which infused the air with the pleasing aroma of sugar and cinnamon.
paras.zh: 桌上还有一盘『奥肯家庭温馨小屋』的招牌供应品：温热刚出炉的核桃饼干，空气中弥漫着糖与肉桂的怡人香气。

paras.en: Oaken’s favorite feature, however, was the shelves of merchandise lining the walls.
paras.zh: 不过，奥肯最中意的，还是沿墙而立的一排排商品货架。

paras.en: Directly opposite the reception desk, shelves offered select items from his Hygge for Home line: wool-scented candles, mugs with take-home cocoa mix, cozy picture books, and the like.
paras.zh: 正对着接待台的货架上，摆着他『居家Hygge系列』的精选好物：羊毛香味的蜡烛、附赠外带热可可粉的马克杯、温馨图画书等等。

paras.en: All with smartly printed labels featuring the Oaken family logo.
paras.zh: 全都贴着印有奥肯家族徽标的精致标签。

paras.en: There were sections for Oaken’s ointments, Oaken’s anti-ailment remedies, and Oaken’s beauty balms—each of his own invention.
paras.zh: 这里还分区陈列着奥肯的软膏、奥肯的疗愈偏方和奥肯的美容香膏——全是他自己研制的。

paras.en: The shelves on the wall directly across from the curtains contained his newest line of offerings, souvenirs that he called Oaken’s Tokens.
paras.zh: 正对着帘子的那面墙上的货架，放着他最新推出的系列——他称为“奥肯纪念品”的各式小玩意。

paras.en: They contained snow globes, carvings of snowgies, baskets containing the awkwardly revealing yet tastefully traditional towels his family was so fond of wearing, and many other items intended to surprise and delight. “Oaken’s Family-Friendly Cozy Cottages are all inclusive and come with unlimited lutefisk and sauna use.
paras.zh: 里面有雪景球、小雪宝的木雕、盛着那种全家都爱穿、虽略显暴露却考究传统的毛巾的篮子，以及许多让人又惊又喜的小物件。“奥肯家庭温馨小屋一价全包，还附赠无限量碱渍鱼和桑拿使用。

paras.en: We have a continuous supply of heated towels, warm cookies, and cocoa.” Brows meeting in the middle of her forehead like caterpillars, the woman opened her mouth to speak.
paras.zh: 我们随时供应加热毛巾、温饼干和热可可。”那女人眉头拧紧，像两条毛毛虫在额头中央交汇，张嘴想说话。

paras.en: A firm believer in seizing every opportunity to wow and delight, Oaken waved a freshly baked cookie under her nose. “Care for a treat?” She paused in confusion before taking the cookie and nibbling politely. “Good, ja?” When she nodded, he continued with his pitch. “In addition to such amenities, each guest gets fleecy slippers and a soft, signature towel to wear during their stay that they take home afterward.
paras.zh: 奥肯坚信要抓住每个让人惊喜开心的机会，便在她鼻尖下晃了晃一块刚出炉的饼干。“来块尝尝？”她困惑地顿了顿，才接过饼干，礼貌地小口咬着。“好吃吧，对不对？”她点头后，他继续推销。“除了这些设施，每位客人还会获赠毛绒拖鞋和一条柔软的招牌毛巾，住宿期间穿着，走时带回作纪念。

paras.en: Guests can choose whether they want to take meals communally in the sauna or in the coziness of their private cabin.” Continuing his spiel, he pivoted and pointed back toward a windowed wooden door situated halfway between the reception area and the trading post counter. “On the board over there is a list of nightly sauna activities.
paras.zh: 客人可自行选择是在桑拿房里集体用餐，还是在私密小屋的温馨中享用。”他滔滔不绝地转过身，指向接待区与杂货柜台之间一扇带窗的木门。“那边板子上列着每晚的桑拿活动。

paras.en: Each evening we offer something different: charades, trivia, sing-alongs, storytelling, and my favorite—the family dance party.
paras.zh: 每晚内容都不同：你比划我猜、趣味问答、合唱、讲故事，还有我最爱的——家庭舞会。

paras.en: Storytelling nights will feature rotating themes, such as spooky speculations, traditional tales, and comedic amusements called Oaken’s Jokens.
paras.zh: 讲故事之夜会轮流变换主题，比如惊悚猜测、传统故事，还有叫作『奥肯笑话』的搞笑段子。

paras.en: Guests will also receive a gift bag of assorted all-natural, locally obtained Oaken products, and the kiddies get to select one free item from Oaken’s Wall of Tokens as a treasured keepsake of their magical visit.” Grabbing a colorful, hand-knitted satchel from beneath the registration desk, Oaken thrust the bag into the woman’s arms. “Since you are getting this very special preview, the Oaken family wants you to have this bag of complimentary cozy items as you consider booking your next getaway with us.” There he paused.
paras.zh: 客人还会收到一袋由本地天然奥肯产品组成的礼包，小朋友则能从『奥肯纪念品墙』免费挑选一样，作为这次奇妙之旅的珍贵纪念。”奥肯从登记台下抽出一只五彩手编小挎包，一把塞进女人怀里。“既然你享受了这次特别预览，奥肯一家想送你这袋免费温馨好物，等你考虑下次来我们这儿度假时再用。”说到这儿他停了下来。

paras.en: That was the pitch in its entirety.
paras.zh: 整段推销词到此结束。

paras.en: He waited, blinking down at the woman, whose expression had not changed in the slightest since she had walked through the door.
paras.zh: 他眨着眼低头等着那女人，而她进门以来，脸上的表情丝毫未变。

paras.en: After a moment, she replied, “I have a delivery.
paras.zh: 过了一会儿，她才回答：“我是来送货的。

paras.en: It’s on the porch.
paras.zh: 货在门廊上。

paras.en: Sign, please.” As soon as Oaken signed the slip, she turned to leave.
paras.zh: 请签字。”奥肯一签完单子，她就转身要走。

paras.en: No matter that she was a delivery person.
paras.zh: 可她是个送货员又怎样。

paras.en: Everyone was a potential customer.
paras.zh: 人人都可能是潜在顾客。

paras.en: People who toted packages up and down the mountains for a living had families, too.
paras.zh: 那些靠在山上山下搬货谋生的人，也有自己的家人。

paras.en: Following her out the door, he watched as she climbed into her sled. “Remember.
paras.zh: 他跟出门，看着她爬上雪橇。“记住。

paras.en: Make your hassle-free reservations at Oaken’s Cloakens and Sauna, or Oaken’s Hus of Hygge tiny beauty salon in the village.
paras.zh: 预订就找奥肯斗篷坊与桑拿，或村里那家奥肯Hygge美容小屋，省心又方便。

paras.en: Tell your friends!
paras.zh: 告诉你的朋友！

paras.en: Bye-bye.” Oaken waved as the nice lady disappeared down the lane, then turned his attention to the parcels on his porch.
paras.zh: 再见啦。”奥肯挥着手，看着这位好心的姑娘消失在小路上，这才把注意力转向门廊上的包裹。

paras.en: In addition to a bag of walnuts for the cottages’ signature cookies, his delivery included a fresh supply of jars and labels from the printer in Arendelle for his latest invention: a carrot-balm beauty face mask.
paras.zh: 除了做小屋招牌饼干用的一袋核桃，这次送货还带来了阿伦黛尔印刷厂为他最新发明——胡萝卜香膏美容面膜——送来的一批新罐子和标签。

paras.en: The mask could be used with or in place of the sauna, to give you a fresh, moist glow when you had no time for a good sweat.
paras.zh: 这面膜可以和桑拿搭配用，也可替代桑拿，让你没空好好流汗时，也能拥有清新水润的光彩。

paras.en: Humming to himself, he turned the sign on the door from OPEN to CLOSED and carried the parcels into the store.
paras.zh: 他哼着小调，把门上的牌子从“营业中”翻成“打烊了”，抱着包裹进了店。

paras.en: Soon Wandering Oaken’s would become a multi-kingdom destination, more famous than Wes-Lee’s, a beloved string of Weselton traveler-respite and goods-of-convenience posts.
paras.zh: 很快，漫游奥肯就会成为跨王国打卡地，名气盖过韦斯利之家——那是一连串深受喜爱的韦塞尔顿旅客歇脚与便民商店。

paras.en: Of course, Wes-Lee’s possessed an iconic mascot.
paras.zh: 当然，韦斯利之家有个标志性吉祥物。

paras.en: Weslee the Wolverine’s likeness greeted weary travelers from large signs along the main trading routes of Weselton.
paras.zh: 狼獾韦斯利的形象，从韦塞尔顿主要商道旁的大招牌上，迎接疲惫的旅人。

paras.en: But Arendelle had cute, furry animals, too.
paras.zh: 可阿伦黛尔也有毛茸茸的可爱小动物。

paras.en: Oaken hurried to the counter to set down his parcels.
paras.zh: 奥肯快步走到柜台放下包裹。

paras.en: He grabbed a pencil and his list of ideas for his ever-expanding enterprise.
paras.zh: 他抓起铅笔，还有那张为不断扩张的事业列的点子清单。

paras.en: Below Wandering Oaken’s Annual Winterfest: frozen snowground, ice rink, and sliding sleigh adventure ride, he scrawled Get adorable mascot .
paras.zh: 在“漫游奥肯年度冬庆：冰冻雪地、溜冰场与雪橇滑行探险”下面，他潦草地写上：找个可爱吉祥物。

paras.en: Setting the paper on the countertop, he turned his attention to the jars and labels.
paras.zh: 把纸摊在柜台上，他把注意力转向那些罐子和标签。

paras.en: Tomorrow he and the family would package the rest of the balm for guests.
paras.zh: 明天他和家人会给客人把剩下的香膏装罐。

paras.en: Right now, he only needed enough for himself.
paras.zh: 眼下，他只需要给自己留够用的量。

paras.en: As was his tradition on the eve of every new venture, Oaken liked to take time to simulate the customer experience to ensure maximum coziness.
paras.zh: 按照每次新事业前夜的传统，奥肯喜欢花时间模拟顾客体验，确保达到最极致的温馨。

paras.en: A moment of hygge awareness and appreciation.
paras.zh: 这是一段hygge式的体悟与欣赏时光。

paras.en: Today he would sample the carrot face mask while eating warm cookies and practicing his jokes during some well-deserved sauna time.
paras.zh: 今天，他要在应得的桑拿时光里，一边吃温饼干、练段子，一边试用胡萝卜面膜。

paras.en: That way he could personally ensure the cookies and towels were at the perfect temperature, the jokes would flow smoothly, and the carrot balm would give his face a fresh-sweat radiance that would last for days.
paras.zh: 这样他就能亲自确保饼干和毛巾温度恰到好处，段子讲得顺溜，而胡萝卜香膏能让他脸上焕发出仿佛刚出一身汗般的新鲜光彩，连日不褪。

paras.en: Making a quick things-to-do list in his head, he headed to the cold storage off the stockroom and grabbed the vat of carrot balm.
paras.zh: 在脑中快速列了张待办清单，他走向储藏室旁的小冷库，拎起那一大桶胡萝卜香膏。

paras.en: Next he headed into the changing annex of the reception space to shed his rather constricting clothes for a heated, brightly colored towel.
paras.zh: 接着他走进接待区的更衣隔间，脱下紧绷的衣服，换上一条加热过的亮色毛巾。

paras.en: He had gotten the idea from Olaf, who came asking about holiday traditions.
paras.zh: 这主意是跟雪宝那儿得来的——当时雪人跑来打听节日传统。

paras.en: The inquisitive little snow person had asked for a towel to take home as a souvenir of his visit.
paras.zh: 那个好奇的小雪人想要一条毛巾带回家，作为来访的纪念。

paras.en: Oaken had been so pleased by the request that he’d given Olaf his favorite towel as a memento.
paras.zh: 奥肯对这个请求高兴坏了，干脆把自己最爱的毛巾送给了雪宝作纪念。

paras.en: He liked to think of the little fellow wearing it around the castle.
paras.zh: 他喜欢想象小家伙在城堡里围着那条毛巾的模样。

paras.en: Towels were so much cozier than everyday clothes.
paras.zh: 毛巾可比日常衣服惬意多了。

paras.en: Plus, it was good advertising, ja?
paras.zh: 再说，这也是不错的广告，对吧？

paras.en: On his way back through the guest area, he picked up the tray of cookies.
paras.zh: 回程穿过客人区时，他顺手端起了那盘饼干。

paras.en: While fresh, they were no longer warm.
paras.zh: 饼干虽新鲜，却已经不温了。

paras.en: He set them on top of the wood-burning stove.
paras.zh: 他把盘子搁在烧柴的炉子顶上。

paras.en: Allowing the tray to warm while he filled one jar of balm would allow the tasty treats to heat to the perfect temperature.
paras.zh: 趁他装一小罐香膏的工夫让盘子回回温，美味零食就能热到最完美的温度。

paras.en: Placing the wooden vat on the counter, he proceeded to fill one tiny jar, affixing it with a dainty label front and center.
paras.zh: 把木桶搁在柜台上，他便往一只小罐里装香膏，再在正中贴上一枚精致标签。

paras.en: He and the family would take care of the rest of the jars in the morning.
paras.zh: 剩下的罐子他留到明早和家人一起弄。

paras.en: And shell the walnuts.
paras.zh: 还要剥核桃。

paras.en: He glanced over toward the nuts.
paras.zh: 他朝那堆坚果瞥了一眼。

paras.en: Huh?
paras.zh: 咦？

paras.en: Oaken scratched his head.
paras.zh: 奥肯挠了挠头。

paras.en: He could have sworn he’d left the walnuts on the counter next to the jars.
paras.zh: 他发誓明明把核桃放在罐子旁的柜台上。

paras.en: But they were no longer there.… Perhaps he’d accidentally taken the bag into the storage room or the changing annex and absentmindedly set it down.
paras.zh: 可那袋核桃不见了……也许他不小心把袋子带进了储藏室或更衣间，又心不在焉地撂下了。

paras.en: He did that sometimes.
paras.zh: 他偶尔会这样。

paras.en: No matter.
paras.zh: 无所谓。

paras.en: They would turn up eventually.
paras.zh: 总会找到的。

paras.en: Intent on returning the carrot balm to cold storage, he picked up the vat and made his way across the store.
paras.zh: 他一心要把胡萝卜香膏送回冷库，便拎起木桶穿过店铺。

paras.en: Pausing at the stove, he inhaled the heavenly aroma of freshly baked cookies.
paras.zh: 在炉边停下时，他深吸一口刚出炉饼干的天堂般香气。

paras.en: Nearly ready, they would be perfect to eat while having a good, steamy sweat.
paras.zh: 差不多好了，正好趁痛快地蒸出一身汗时吃。

paras.en: Remembering he needed to prep the sauna for maximum steam, he set down the vat and backtracked to add water to the sauna stones.
paras.zh: 想起得给桑拿备好足量的蒸汽，他放下木桶折回去，往桑拿石上加水。

paras.en: Typically, entering Oaken’s sauna was like stepping into a tropical oasis.
paras.zh: 平时走进奥肯的桑拿房，就像踏入热带绿洲。

paras.en: Steamy moisture and the scent of burning cedar tickled the senses.
paras.zh: 氤氲的水汽和燃烧雪松的香气撩动着感官。

paras.en: But not this time.
paras.zh: 可这次不是。

paras.en: The place was as cold as Elsa’s ice palace.
paras.zh: 这地方冷得像艾莎的冰宫殿。

paras.en: The fire that heated the sauna had gone out, and the extra wood was gone.
paras.zh: 加热桑拿的火灭了，多余的柴也不见了。

paras.en: Strange; he could have sworn his family had restocked it earlier that day.
paras.zh: 怪了；他明明记得家人当天早些时候补过柴。

paras.en: Nothing, however, was burning—except the cookies!
paras.zh: 然而，此刻没什么是烧着的——除了那些饼干！

paras.en: With no cedar aroma to distract, he could clearly smell them.
paras.zh: 没了雪松香气的干扰，他能清清楚楚闻到它们。

paras.en: Rushing out of the sauna, he raced to the stove and carefully lifted the tray using the corner of his towel to protect his fingers.
paras.zh: 他冲出桑拿房，跑到炉子前，用毛巾角护着手指，小心端起盘子。

paras.en: The cookies had definitely exceeded optimal warmth.
paras.zh: 饼干绝对已经过了最佳温热度。

paras.en: No matter.
paras.zh: 无所谓。

paras.en: A moment on the porch while he collected more wood for the sauna would be just the right amount of time to cool them off.
paras.zh: 把盘子搁在门廊上，趁他去捡桑拿用的柴，这点时间正好让饼干凉一凉。

paras.en: He had just set the tray on the porch railing and turned toward the woodpile when a familiar high-pitched squeak echoed from inside.
paras.zh: 他刚把盘子搁在门廊栏杆上、转身朝柴堆走去，里面就传来一声熟悉的高亢尖叫。

paras.en: Oofta!
paras.zh: 哎呀！

paras.en: Not again.
paras.zh: 又来。

paras.en: The sauna door slammed shut just before he reached it.
paras.zh: 桑拿门在他够到之前“砰”地关上了。

paras.en: Peering through the window confirmed his fears—three ecstatic snowgies, led by that scoundrel William, had barricaded themselves in the sauna and were building a fort out of wood and colorful towels.
paras.zh: 透过窗户一看，印证了他的担忧——三个乐疯了的小雪宝，在那个捣蛋鬼威廉带领下，把自己反锁在桑拿房里，正用木柴和彩色毛巾搭堡垒。

paras.en: Did Marshmallow know William was causing mischief down the mountain?
paras.zh: 棉花糖知道威廉在山下捣乱吗？

paras.en: How had he and the others gotten all the way to the trading post?
paras.zh: 他和其他小雪宝是怎么一路跑到杂货铺来的？

paras.en: BANG!
paras.zh: 砰！

paras.en: Rattling outside led Oaken to deduce the three snowgies weren’t alone.
paras.zh: 外面的哗啦声让奥肯推断，这三个小雪宝并非单独行动。

paras.en: Creeping to the front door, Oaken listened to the noises coming from the porch.
paras.zh: 他蹑手蹑脚走到前门，听着门廊传来的动静。

paras.en: Convinced that whatever was making the racket was complicit in the snowgies’ coup, the shopkeeper threw open the door, coming nose to nose with a most unexpected accomplice.
paras.zh: 店主确信那制造喧闹的也是小雪宝政变的同伙，便猛地拉开门，正和一位最出人意料的同伙撞了个面对面。

paras.en: Mouth stuffed full of cookies, the creature swallowed with a resounding gulp.
paras.zh: 那家伙嘴里塞满饼干，咕咚一声响亮地咽了下去。

paras.en: A second later, its mouth opened wide as steam from the flaming-hot snack rose from its throat.
paras.zh: 一秒后，它张大了嘴，滚烫零食冒出的热气从喉咙里升腾而起。

paras.en: Sucking in a lungful of air, the animal let out a huge yawn to cool its brain. “Sven!” Oaken reprimanded. “What have we talked about?
paras.zh: 它深吸一口气，打了个大大的哈欠给脑子降温。“斯文！”奥肯训斥道，“我们说过什么来着？

paras.en: You can’t just eat things that belong to someone else.
paras.zh: 你不能随便吃别人的东西。

paras.en: You need to ask permission first, ja?” “Bwrahf.” Sven brayed out an apology and nosed the tray with its two remaining cookies toward the shopkeeper.
paras.zh: 你得先征得同意，对吧？”“布饶夫。”斯文叫着道歉，用鼻子把还剩两块饼干的盘子拱向店主。

paras.en: Thankfully these were a test batch and not needed for guests.
paras.zh: 幸好这只是试验批次，客人用不上。

paras.en: But still, the animal needed to respect the boundaries they’d drawn.
paras.zh: 但即便如此，这动物也该尊重他们划下的界限。

paras.en: Sven’s other companion—the big blond ice boy—was fond of saying reindeers were better than people.
paras.zh: 斯文的另一位伙伴——那个金发大块头冰小子——总爱说驯鹿比人强。

paras.en: But people didn’t tend to eat everything not nailed down.
paras.zh: 可人通常不会把没钉死的东西都吃光。

paras.en: The reindeer brayed again, batting his long lashes.
paras.zh: 驯鹿又叫了一声，扑闪着长睫毛。

paras.en: At least Sven seemed sorry for his actions.
paras.zh: 起码斯文好像为自己的行为感到抱歉。

paras.en: His tiny menace of a buddy was another story entirely.
paras.zh: 他那小捣蛋伙伴又是另一码事了。

paras.en: William had no respect for anyone’s authority.
paras.zh: 威廉谁的话都不听。

paras.en: And this time, the rebellious snowgie had brought reinforcements. “As payment for your snack, Sven, please go get Olaf.
paras.zh: 而且这次，这个叛逆的小雪宝还带来了援军。“作为你这顿零食的补偿，斯文，去把雪宝叫来吧。

paras.en: Tell him William is loose again, ja?” The reindeer hesitated for an instant, and Oaken had to make the stern face with the eyebrows before Sven grunted in agreement and headed down the lane.
paras.zh: 告诉他威廉又跑出来了，对吧？”驯鹿犹豫了一瞬，奥肯不得不摆出皱眉的严肃表情，斯文才咕哝着答应，顺着小路去了。

paras.en: If not for his insatiable appetite, Sven might make a good mascot for his latest franchise.
paras.zh: 要不是贪吃得没完，斯文倒能当他最新连锁店的好吉祥物。

paras.en: Oaken would have a think on that while he shelled some nuts for a new batch of cookies.
paras.zh: 奥肯边剥坚果准备新一批饼干，边琢磨这事。

paras.en: Where did that bag of walnuts go? “Hoo-hoo!” As he reentered the store in search of nuts, the sauna door nudged open and a voice called out.
paras.zh: 那袋核桃跑哪儿去了？“呼——嗬！”他重新进店找坚果时，桑拿门被轻轻顶开，一个声音喊了起来。

paras.en: Lunging forward, Oaken leapt hands-first into the opening, just in time to prevent the door from slamming shut. “Got you!” He grabbed for William, and the sauna went dark.
paras.zh: 奥肯猛地前扑，双手抢先堵住门缝，刚好拦住门“砰”地关上。“抓到你了！”他伸手去抓威廉，桑拿房却一下黑了。

paras.en: One of the snowgie cohorts had pulled his hat over his eyes.
paras.zh: 一个小雪宝同伙把他的帽子拉下来盖住了眼睛。

paras.en: Not one to be bested by balls of snow, Oaken removed the hat and stood to his full height.
paras.zh: 奥肯可不会被雪球欺负，他扯下帽子，挺直高大的身躯。

paras.en: When he reached down to pick up the nearest snowgie, another hopped across his back, causing enough of a distraction for the first one to slip his grasp.
paras.zh: 他弯腰去抓最近的小雪宝时，另一个跳到他背上，分散了注意，让第一个从手里溜走。

paras.en: All three chuckled like it was the funniest trick ever.
paras.zh: 三个小雪宝咯咯直笑，仿佛这是天底下最好玩的把戏。

paras.en: He reached out again with the same results.
paras.zh: 他又伸手，结果还是一样。

paras.en: This game of leap-over-the-frog went on for a few rounds before Oaken got tired of being the frog.
paras.zh: 这“跳青蛙”的游戏玩了几回合，奥肯腻了当青蛙。

paras.en: Oofta!
paras.zh: 哎呀！

paras.en: Olaf could deal with them.
paras.zh: 雪宝能对付他们。

paras.en: Throwing his hands in the air, he abandoned the sauna and resumed the hunt for his bag of nuts.
paras.zh: 他双手一摊，放弃桑拿房，继续找那袋坚果。

paras.en: Forgotten next to the hot stove, the vat of carrot balm had turned to liquid.
paras.zh: 被忘在热炉旁的那桶胡萝卜香膏已经化成了液体。

paras.en: No worries.
paras.zh: 别急。

paras.en: He would set it outside and it would be solid again in no time.
paras.zh: 放到外面，一会儿就重新凝固。

paras.en: After placing the vat on the porch, he retraced his steps through the reception area.
paras.zh: 把桶放到门廊后，他顺原路穿过接待区。

paras.en: Sometime during the chaos, a display of all-natural pastes for the teeth had clattered to the floor.
paras.zh: 混乱中不知何时，一排全天然牙膏的展示架哗啦倒在了地上。

paras.en: He’d tested many flavors over the years, but to date only three variations earned family approval: minty, no flavor for the sensitive of mouth, and family-favorite Arctic Bramble Berry.
paras.zh: 这些年他试过许多口味，但迄今只有三种得到家人认可：薄荷味、给口腔敏感者的无口味，以及全家最爱的北极莓果味。

paras.en: Oaken restacked the tins next to the gifting baskets for all ages and every occasion.
paras.zh: 奥肯把那些罐子重新码好，放在适合各年龄段、各种场合的礼篮旁。

paras.en: Next he surveyed the changing annex, again without success.
paras.zh: 接着他查看更衣隔间，依旧一无所获。

paras.en: Walking to the reception desk, he caught a flash of movement out of the corner of his eye.
paras.zh: 走到接待台时，他眼角瞥见一道动静。

paras.en: When he turned toward the shelves, nothing seemed amiss.
paras.zh: 可他转向货架时，一切又似乎正常。

paras.en: Except the tins of pastes for the teeth were once again on the ground.
paras.zh: 除了那排牙膏罐又躺在了地上。

paras.en: Moving slowly, he carefully inspected the shelves of merchandise, starting with the products and progressing to the souvenirs.
paras.zh: 他缓缓移动，仔细查看商品货架，从产品看到纪念品。

paras.en: All seemed in order.
paras.zh: 一切看似井然有序。

paras.en: Shelves gleamed with snow globes, replicas of the North Mountain, and carved figurines.
paras.zh: 货架上闪着光：雪景球、北山的微缩模型，还有雕刻小像。

paras.en: But somewhere between the troll-like dolls, carvings of snowgies, and cloth animals stuffed with fluff, two eerily realistic statues on the top shelf caught his attention. “Hoo-hoo!
paras.zh: 可就在那些地精模样玩偶、小雪宝木雕和塞满棉絮的布偶之间，顶层货架上有两尊逼真得诡异的雕像吸引了他的目光。“呼——嗬！

paras.en: What are you?” They each looked like a cross between a preserved squirrel and a nutcracker.
paras.zh: 你们是什么？”它们看起来像风干松鼠和胡桃夹子的混合体。

paras.en: One wore a tiny knitted topplue, identical to Oaken’s own hat.
paras.zh: 一个戴着顶小针织帽，和奥肯自己的帽子一模一样。

paras.en: The other donned a doll-sized troll souvenir sweater.
paras.zh: 另一个套着件娃娃尺寸的地精纪念毛衣。

paras.en: He recognized both items from his miniature mementos display.
paras.zh: 这两样东西他都认得，出自他的迷你纪念品展。

paras.en: The one with the sweater had excessively bushy red ears that reminded him of his granduncle Hugo.
paras.zh: 穿毛衣的那只红耳朵毛太过蓬松，让他想起叔祖父雨果。

paras.en: The other possessed a droopy sort of mustache reminiscent of Cousin Lars.
paras.zh: 另一只耷拉着种垂头丧气的胡子，像极了表兄拉尔斯。

paras.en: Between their paws, each held a death grip on a walnut.
paras.zh: 两只爪子间，各自死死攥着一颗核桃。

paras.en: Fragments of shells littered the space around them.
paras.zh: 碎壳散落在一圈地上。

paras.en: Oaken stared at the unmoving beady eyes while inching closer.
paras.zh: 奥肯盯着那对不动的芝麻眼，一点点凑近。

paras.en: Suddenly one of the figures blinked.
paras.zh: 忽然其中一个雕像眨了下眼。

paras.en: With a screech, they both came to life.
paras.zh: 一声尖叫，两只都活了过来。

paras.en: Before he could even process what was happening, a walnut whizzed past his head.
paras.zh: 他还没反应过来发生了什么，一颗核桃就嗖地从他头顶飞过。

paras.en: Calling back and forth in a chirpy trill that sounded almost like a woodpecker, the squirrels scampered along the shelf in an effort to get away.
paras.zh: 它们用几乎像啄木鸟般的啁啾声彼此呼应，顺着货架飞奔想逃走。

paras.en: At least he’d figured out what had happened to the walnuts. “Come here, you!” He chased Hugo and Lars—now that he had noticed the resemblances, he couldn’t think of them as anything else—to the far corner of the reception area.
paras.zh: 起码他搞清楚核桃的去向了。“过来，你们俩！”他把雨果和拉尔斯——既然看出了那几分相似，他再也想不出别的叫法——追到了接待区最远的角落。

paras.en: As he closed the distance between them, Hugo lobbed another walnut at Oaken’s face.
paras.zh: 他逼近时，雨果又朝奥肯的脸砸来一颗核桃。

paras.en: He ducked, but his elation was short-lived as Lars’s walnut bonked him in the noggin. “Oof,” he grunted, as the bell over the shop’s front door chimed. “Hello?” called a familiar voice. “I’ve come for my little brothers.” He would deal with Hugo and Lars after he helped Olaf get rid of those little snowgie terrors. “Olaf.
paras.zh: 他一低头躲开，喜悦却没持续多久——拉尔斯的核桃“咚”地敲在他脑门上。“哎哟，”他哼了一声，这时店门前的铃铛响了。“有人吗？”一个熟悉的声音喊，“我来接我的弟弟们。”得先帮雪宝打发掉那几个小雪宝恐怖分子，再收拾雨果和拉尔斯。“雪宝。

paras.en: William and his friends have taken over my sauna again , ja?” The little snowfellow wobbled in on his little snowball feet. “Sorry, Mr.
paras.zh: 威廉和他朋友又占领我的桑拿了，对吧？”小雪人踩着小雪球脚丫摇摇晃晃进来，说道：“抱歉，先生。

paras.en: Fuzzy Oaken Man-Bear.
paras.zh: 毛茸茸的奥肯熊人大叔。

paras.en: Sometimes William tumbles down the mountain before anyone can stop him.
paras.zh: 有时候威廉还没等谁拦住，就顺着山滚下来了。

paras.en: He doesn’t mean to cause trouble—he’s just packed that way.
paras.zh: 他不是故意惹麻烦——他天生就这副模样。

paras.en: But don’t worry, I’ll get him out.” The snowman turned toward the sauna, then abruptly swung back around. “A night of sauna trivia!” he exclaimed with huge eyes. “Can I be the host?
paras.zh: 不过别担心，我会把他弄出去。”雪人转向桑拿房，又猛地转回来。“桑拿趣味问答之夜！”他瞪大眼睛喊，“能让我当主持吗？

paras.en: Pleeeease.” “Oh, I’m not so sure about that.” Oaken recalled the last time Olaf had visited his sauna.
paras.zh: 求求你啦。”“哦，这我可不太确定。”奥肯想起上次雪宝来桑拿房。

paras.en: Even if the little snowman didn’t become an instant puddle, his permafrost presence in the sultry sauna could be a source of anxiety for his guests.
paras.zh: 即便小雪人不会瞬间化成水洼，他在闷热桑拿里那冰封般的存在，也会让客人焦虑。

paras.en: But the frosty font of facts would make the perfect trivia host given the right circumstances.
paras.zh: 不过，这位冷冰冰的“知识泉”只要条件合适，倒能当完美的问答主持。

paras.en: Not one to quit easily, Oaken had a flash of inspiration. “Tell you what.
paras.zh: 奥肯不轻易认输，灵光一闪。“这样吧。

paras.en: You get those brothers of yours back up the mountain and keep them away, and you can be the special trivia host at our first annual outdoor event: Wandering Oaken’s Annual Winterfest and Holiday Market.
paras.zh: 你把那几个弟弟弄回山上、看住别让他们下来，就能当咱们首届户外活动的特别问答主持：漫游奥肯年度冬庆暨节日集市。

paras.en: Ja?” “Thank you so much!” Olaf blinked and added, “Did you know turtles can breathe through their butts?” “Oh, ja?
paras.zh: 怎样，对吧？”“太感谢啦！”雪宝眨着眼补了一句，“你知道吗，乌龟能用屁股呼吸？”“哦，是吗？

paras.en: Did you know elephants sweat through their toenails?” “ What?
paras.zh: 你知道吗，大象是从脚趾甲出汗的？”“什么？

paras.en: That’s great!” WHOMP!
paras.zh: 太厉害了！”砰！

paras.en: A snowball hit Olaf square in the face, followed by a second and a third.
paras.zh: 一个雪球正砸雪宝脸上，接着是第二个、第三个。

paras.en: With his nose poking through the back of his snow head, Olaf looked at Oaken. “Whoa!
paras.zh: 雪宝的鼻子从雪脑袋后头戳出来，看着奥肯。“哇！

paras.en: Head rush.
paras.zh: 头晕。

paras.en: Could you… ?” “Ja.” Oaken carefully pushed the carrot into its rightful place.
paras.zh: 你能……？”“好。”奥肯小心地把胡萝卜推回原位。

paras.en: He caught a flurry of white before a snowball disintegrated against his massive chest and the sauna door slammed shut.
paras.zh: 他瞥见一团白色飞舞，随即一个雪球在他宽阔的胸口碎开，桑拿门“砰”地关上。

paras.en: Properly motivated, Olaf faced the sauna. “William!
paras.zh: 这下动力十足，雪宝面向桑拿房。“威廉！

paras.en: Crystal!
paras.zh: 克里斯特尔！

paras.en: Fridge!
paras.zh: 弗瑞吉！

paras.en: Marshmallow has been looking all over for you.
paras.zh: 棉花糖到处找你们呢。

paras.en: Stop causing pandemonium and yield presently, you little rapscallions.” “Ooh.
paras.zh: 别再闹得天翻地覆，赶紧投降，你们这群小捣蛋。”哦。

paras.en: Someone has been reading their word-a-day calendar and top gift pick for the holidays.” Oaken had given one to all his best customers.
paras.zh: 有人在看每日一词日历，还买了节日热门礼物。”奥肯把这礼物送给了所有好顾客。

paras.en: Olaf nodded. “Indubitably, my uninhibited, congenial hirsute acquaintance.” The sauna door opened a crack and Oaken’s list of ideas sailed out.
paras.zh: 雪宝点头。“无疑，我这位无拘无束、亲切又多毛的熟人。”桑拿门开了一条缝，奥肯的点子清单飞了出来。

paras.en: As it landed facedown, Oaken saw the crude drawing of a rounded figure with buckteeth, four crooked lines sprouting from above its overly large brows, stick arms, three dark buttons, and a grossly disproportionate carrot nose.
paras.zh: 清单面朝下落地，奥肯却看到上面画着个圆滚滚的小人：龅牙、过宽的眉毛上方冒出四条歪线、棍子似的手臂、三颗黑纽扣，还有个比例失调的大胡萝卜鼻子。

paras.en: The caricature had a circle around it with a line through the middle. “No Olafs allowed!” the snowman interpreted. “That’s not very amicable.” Oofta.
paras.zh: 漫画周围画了个圈，中间一道斜杠。“禁止雪宝入内！”雪人解读道，“这可不太友好。”哎呀。

paras.en: It was not.
paras.zh: 确实不友好。

paras.en: But it did give Oaken an idea. “Hoo-hoo!” he called. “Little snow rapscallions, if you come out now, mind your big brother, and stop turning the sauna into a snow fort, I will give you complimentary passes to Wandering Oaken’s Annual Winterfest, including unlimited ice-skating and all the snow cones you can wear.” If it kept them and their antics away from his guests, it would be worth it.
paras.zh: 但这倒让奥肯有了主意。“呼——嗬！”他喊，“小捣蛋们，要是你们现在出来、听大哥的话，别再把桑拿变成雪堡垒，我就送你们漫游奥肯年度冬庆的免费通行证，含无限溜冰和你穿得下的所有雪花冰。”只要能让他们和恶作剧离客人远点，就值了。

paras.en: Plus, they would be rainbow-colored for weeks, all the more easily spotted coming his way.
paras.zh: 再说，他们好几周都会是彩虹色，朝他这儿来时更好认。

paras.en: A commotion rose from inside the sauna.
paras.zh: 桑拿房里传来一阵骚动。

paras.en: After a few moments, the door opened wide and the three contrite snowgies toddled out.
paras.zh: 片刻后门大开，三个知错的小雪宝摇摇晃晃走了出来。

paras.en: In the space beyond, Oaken could see they’d tidied up their mess.
paras.zh: 里面那片空间，奥肯能看见他们已收拾好乱摊子。

paras.en: The used towels were piled in a basket, and the wood was returned to its spot.
paras.zh: 用过的毛巾堆进篮子，木柴也归了位。

paras.en: William extended Oaken’s hat as a peace offering.
paras.zh: 威廉递出奥肯的帽子，算是赔礼。

paras.en: With a nod of approval, Oaken said, “Very good.
paras.zh: 奥肯赞许地点点头：“很好。

paras.en: I will see you all at the winterfest, ja?” “Unquestionably, my substantial, genial, ruddy-faced Homo sapiens compatriot.” With his little brothers in tow, Olaf herded them out of the trading post.
paras.zh: 冬庆见，对吧？”“毫无疑问，我这位壮实、和善、红脸膛的人类同胞。”雪宝带着弟弟们，把她们赶出了杂货铺。

paras.en: Grabbing the basket of soiled towels, Oaken carried it into the reception area.
paras.zh: 奥肯抓起那篮脏毛巾，拎进接待区。

paras.en: He listened as the front doorbell chimed; confirmation that his unwanted guests were, indeed, gone.
paras.zh: 他听着前门铃响，确认那些不速之客确实走了。

paras.en: Just before the door shut behind the snowman, he heard, “Thank you again, Sven.” Oaken experienced a moment of what Olaf would call trepidation that the rapacious reindeer had devoured the remaining two cookies.
paras.zh: 雪人出门前，他听见一句“再次谢谢啦，斯文”。奥肯心头掠过雪宝口中的“忐忑”——生怕那贪吃的驯鹿把剩下两块饼干也吞了。

paras.en: Glancing at the reception desk, he confirmed the signature treats were safe.
paras.zh: 他瞥了眼接待台，确认招牌零食安然无恙。

paras.en: The carrot balm, however— SCHLURHP!
paras.zh: 可那胡萝卜香膏——咂噜噗！

paras.en: The animal’s tongue swirled around his entire mouth twice.
paras.zh: 那动物的舌头在嘴边绕了两整圈。

paras.en: It looked like a red waterspout—all circular motion and drops of moisture.
paras.zh: 像红色的喷水柱——全是转圈的动作和飞溅的水珠。

paras.en: Instead of looking contrite, the reindeer grinned.
paras.zh: 驯鹿非但没显出愧疚，反而咧嘴笑了。

paras.en: Large eyes gleaming, he bobbed his head and chuckled as if to say, Good stuff, ja?
paras.zh: 大眼睛闪着光，他点头咯咯笑，仿佛在说：好东西，对吧？

paras.en: The vat was completely empty.
paras.zh: 那桶彻底空了。
