paras.en: Henry put his arm around Clemet’s shoulders and gave him a hug. “You see, when I was your age, my grandfather told me a secret.” Clemet smiled. “You mean my great-grandfather?” “No, my child, your great-great-grandfather.
paras.zh: 亨利搂住克莱梅特的肩膀，给了他一个拥抱。“你看，在我像你这么大的时候，我的爷爷告诉我一个秘密。”克莱梅特笑了。“您说的是我的曾祖父？”“不，孩子，是你的高祖父。

paras.en: And his name was Clemet, too.” The little boy couldn’t believe his ears. “Just like me?” Grandpa smiled and nodded slowly. “You are named after him.
paras.zh: “而且他的名字也叫克莱梅特。”小男孩简直不敢相信自己的耳朵。“和我一样？”爷爷微笑着缓缓点头。“你就是以他命名的。

paras.en: I was on a fishing trip with him, just like this one, when I heard a cuckoo sing.
paras.zh: “当时我和他一起出来钓鱼，就像现在这样，听见了布谷鸟歌唱。

paras.en: He told me to wish three things for myself.” The little boy wanted to know what his grandpa had wished for, and whether those wishes had come true or not.
paras.zh: “他让我为自己许下三个愿望。”小男孩想知道爷爷当时许了什么愿，那些愿望又有没有成真。

paras.en: Henry explained that the wishes that you wished on the cuckoo were secret—you must not tell them to anyone.
paras.zh: 亨利解释说，对着布谷鸟许下的愿望是秘密——绝不能告诉任何人。

paras.en: Clemet’s face fell and Grandpa could tell he was disappointed.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特的脸垮了下来，爷爷看得出他很失望。

paras.en: He patted his grandson on the head and said, “But everything came true, my child.
paras.zh: 他拍拍孙子的头说：“可每一件都成真了，孩子。

paras.en: Everything came true.” A yellow-beaked, brown-feathered cuckoo flew over them and landed on a tree, singing its happy song.
paras.zh: “每一件都成真了。”一只黄嘴棕羽的布谷鸟从他们头顶飞过，落在一棵树上，唱起欢快的歌。

paras.en: Grandpa and the little boy were fascinated by the bird that promised to grant all the wishes from the forest. “Now it’s your turn to make three wishes.
paras.zh: 爷爷和小男孩都被这只据说能实现森林中所有愿望的鸟迷住了。“现在轮到你许三个愿望了。

paras.en: Not too loud.
paras.zh: “别太大声。

paras.en: Close your eyes, my child, and give it a go.” The little boy’s dark eyes snapped shut and he began to whisper into the wind, quietly so his grandfather couldn’t hear him: “Please give me a dog for my very own, a silver coin on a chain, and true love.” At that exact moment, the cuckoo took off into the sky as if it had heard the wishes.
paras.zh: “闭上眼睛，孩子，试试看吧。”小男孩乌黑的双眼猛地合上，开始对着风低语，声音轻得让爷爷听不见：“请赐我一只完全属于自己的狗、一枚挂在链子上的银币，还有真爱。”就在此刻，布谷鸟振翅飞向天空，仿佛听见了那些愿望。

paras.en: It circled around them in the air, as though in their honor, before flying away. • • • Years went by, and Clemet grew up to be a handsome young man.
paras.zh: 它在他们上空盘旋一圈，仿佛致以敬意，随后飞走了。• • • 多年过去，克莱梅特长成了英俊的青年。

paras.en: And over time he found that the wishes that he had whispered to the cuckoo were coming true.
paras.zh: 渐渐地，他发现当年向布谷鸟低声许下的愿望，正在一一成真。

paras.en: First, he got his own dog that followed him everywhere he went.
paras.zh: 首先，他有了一只自己的狗，走哪儿都跟着他。

paras.en: He named her Tinka.
paras.zh: 他叫她廷卡。

paras.en: They even slept in the forest together whenever they were out exploring.
paras.zh: 每当外出探险，他们甚至一起睡在森林里。

paras.en: She was very special to him, and special in general.
paras.zh: 对他而言，她格外特别，而她本就是一只不寻常的狗。

paras.en: His people, the Aljel, said that Tinka was a “four-eyed dog.” That meant that she could see more than other dogs—she could even see spirits and warn Clemet when they were near.
paras.zh: 他的族人——阿尔耶尔人——说廷卡是只“四眼狗”。意思是她比别的狗看得更多——甚至能看见精灵，并在它们靠近时向克莱梅特发出警告。

paras.en: Next, Clemet received his silver coin on a chain, which he always kept around his neck.
paras.zh: 接着，克莱梅特得到了那枚挂在链子上的银币，他时刻都戴在脖子上。

paras.en: It was well known from his people in Aljel that it would serve as protection against the spirits—the silver metal blinded them.
paras.zh: 阿尔耶尔的族人尽人皆知，银币能抵御精灵——银质的金属会让精灵目眩。

paras.en: The coin was also special to the Northuldra people.
paras.zh: 这枚银币对北地人也意义非凡。

paras.en: The elders said that if you were a young sky-people man who was lucky enough to meet a girl from the Northuldra people, then you could throw your silver coin over her to win her love, but you needed to be careful.
paras.zh: 长老们说，如果你是个年轻的天族男子，有幸遇见一位北地姑娘，就可以把银币抛过她头顶来赢得她的芳心，但你必须小心。

paras.en: Very careful.
paras.zh: 非常小心。

paras.en: After you did that, you would need to marry her.
paras.zh: 这么做之后，你就得娶她为妻。

paras.en: The young man and his beloved tan-and-white Tinka had been walking through the forest for what felt like ages.
paras.zh: 青年和他心爱的黄白相间的廷卡，在森林里走了仿佛整整一个世纪那么久。

paras.en: Finding the perfect spot for a break, Clemet sat and drank from his cup while he stroked the dog lovingly. “You know, it was somewhere around here that I heard the cuckoo and wished for a dog for myself, and here you are, my four-eyed best friend.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特找了个绝佳的地方歇脚，一边坐着用杯子喝水，一边疼爱地抚摸着狗。“你知道吗，我就是在附近这片地方听见布谷鸟、许愿要一只狗的，而你就在我身边了，我四眼的好朋友。

paras.en: Tinka, I love you.” The dog licked her owner’s hand as if to say that she loved him, too.
paras.zh: “廷卡，我爱你。”狗舔了舔主人的手，仿佛也在说爱他。

paras.en: Feeling himself in a very good mood, Clemet stood and took a stick from the ground.
paras.zh: 心情大好，克莱梅特站起身，从地上捡起一根树枝。

paras.en: Looking at Tinka with a smile, he threw the stick as far as he could. “Come on, now.
paras.zh: 他微笑着看向廷卡，把树枝用力远远掷出。“来吧。

paras.en: Go get it and bring it back to me.” But Tinka grabbed the stick and ran away from him instead of to him.
paras.zh: “去把它叼回来给我。”可廷卡衔起树枝，却朝反方向跑开了，而不是奔向他。

paras.en: With a laugh, Clemet ran after her.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特大笑着追了上去。

paras.en: He tried many times to grab the stick, but the dog would not let it go that easily.
paras.zh: 他好几次想抢回树枝，可狗没那么轻易松口。

paras.en: Out of breath but happy, Clemet lay down on the ground and looked up at the sky, watching the clouds move slowly. “I give up, Tinka.
paras.zh: 上气不接下气却满心欢喜，克莱梅特躺倒在地，仰望天空，看着云朵缓缓飘移。“我认输，廷卡。

paras.en: You win,” he declared as he listened to the leaves rustle and the birds sing.
paras.zh: “你赢了，”他宣告道，耳边是树叶沙沙、鸟儿的歌唱。

paras.en: There was a sudden silence in the forest.
paras.zh: 森林里忽然安静下来。

paras.en: Frowning, Clemet sat up and looked around.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特皱起眉，坐起身四下张望。

paras.en: Tinka sat nearby, still with the stick in her mouth.
paras.zh: 廷卡坐在不远处，嘴里还叼着那根树枝。

paras.en: He could see that she was also listening, her head tilted to the side.
paras.zh: 他看得出来，狗也在倾听，脑袋歪向一边。

paras.en: Then the sound of laughter floated around them on the breeze.
paras.zh: 接着，笑声随风在他们周围飘荡。

paras.en: Tinka stood up.
paras.zh: 廷卡站了起来。

paras.en: They both looked at each other, wondering if the other had heard it. “It’s so quiet, so quiet,” said Clemet to himself.
paras.zh: 他们彼此对望，想知道对方是否也听见了。“太静了，太静了，”克莱梅特自言自语。

paras.en: Suddenly a stick sailed through the air.
paras.zh: 忽然，一根树枝从空中飞来。

paras.en: And Tinka couldn’t just stand still.
paras.zh: 廷卡可静不下来了。

paras.en: Her tongue lolling out of her mouth as she dropped her own stick, she ran to retrieve the new one and started playing with it.
paras.zh: 她吐出自己的树枝，舌头耷拉在嘴外，跑去叼起那根新树枝，玩了起来。

paras.en: Clemet was confused.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特一头雾水。

paras.en: Where did the stick come from?
paras.zh: 树枝是从哪儿来的？

paras.en: He shouted into the air, “Come here so I can see you.” But no one answered his call.
paras.zh: 他对着空中大喊：“过来，让我看看你。”可没人回应他的呼唤。

paras.en: All he could hear was a child laughing.
paras.zh: 他只听见一个孩子的笑声。

paras.en: Curious, Clemet ran after his dog, trying to see who it was.
paras.zh: 出于好奇，克莱梅特追着狗跑去，想看清那是谁。

paras.en: But Tinka soon returned to him and now had a good grip on the stick.
paras.zh: 可廷卡很快回到他身边，这回紧紧叼住了树枝。

paras.en: She tried to play with Clemet, but he wasn’t in the mood, the invisible laughter on his mind. “Tinka, not now.
paras.zh: 她想和克莱梅特玩，可他没那个心情，心里惦记着那听不见身影的笑声。“廷卡，现在不行。

paras.en: Do you hear?” But the dog still wanted to play and ran away with the stick.
paras.zh: “你听见了吗？”可狗还是想玩，叼着树枝跑开了。

paras.en: Clemet called after her, not wanting her to leave his side.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特在后面喊她，不想让她离开自己身边。

paras.en: The laughter came again and he turned toward the voice.
paras.zh: 笑声再次响起，他循声转过头去。

paras.en: He could see a silhouette, a little boy, but the child ran so fast that Clemet had no chance to catch up.
paras.zh: 他看到一个身影，是个小男孩，可那孩子跑得飞快，克莱梅特根本追不上。

paras.en: Now when Clemet looked around, he realized that he was lost.
paras.zh: 这时克莱梅特环顾四周，才发觉自己迷路了。

paras.en: He could hear something rustling in the bushes, but then he saw it posed no danger.
paras.zh: 他听见灌木丛里有什么在窸窣作响，随即看出那并无危险。

paras.en: It was only a female fox with her kits.
paras.zh: 那不过是一只母狐带着它的幼崽。

paras.en: The fox was scurrying around, trying to get her babies deeper into the forest. “Oh, mummy fox, I wish you could tell me if you saw something—” he started.
paras.zh: 母狐匆忙奔走，想把孩子们往森林更深处带。“哦，狐妈妈，真希望你告诉我有没有看到什么——”他开口道。

paras.en: But before he finished the sentence, a new stick flew by him.
paras.zh: 可话没说完，一根新树枝从他身边飞过。

paras.en: Clemet took off in the direction that it had come from in pursuit of the child, whom he could finally see more clearly.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特朝着树枝飞来的方向追去，终于把那孩子看得更清楚了些。

paras.en: The little boy had dark hair, and a big smile crossed his face. “Hey, you.
paras.zh: 小男孩一头黑发，脸上绽开大大的笑。“嘿，你。

paras.en: Come back here!” Clemet called after him.
paras.zh: “回来！”克莱梅特在身后喊。

paras.en: But the boy, Fally, ran quickly.
paras.zh: 可那叫法利的男孩跑得飞快。

paras.en: In fact, in his language, his name meant “fast runner.” Fally knew he could easily outrun the young sky man and escape to the Northuldra village.
paras.zh: 事实上，在他的语言里，他的名字意为“飞毛腿”。法利知道自己轻易就能甩开这个年轻的天族男子，逃回北地人的村庄。

paras.en: When he tried to open the way, though, he couldn’t remember the key words. “Skång-skång-lay,” said the little Northuldra boy, but nothing happened.
paras.zh: 可当他想打开通路时，却记不起那句咒语。“斯康-斯康-莱，”小北地男孩念道，却什么也没发生。

paras.en: Clemet was now very close by, but he couldn’t see as clearly in the forest as Fally and the Northuldra could.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特现在已离得很近，可他在森林里的眼力，远不及法利和北地人那般敏锐。

paras.en: Clemet tried to grab for him, but Fally skirted away, and Clemet fell.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特伸手想抓他，法利一闪躲开，克莱梅特摔了一跤。

paras.en: When Clemet got up from the ground, he was irritated.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特从地上爬起，心里有些恼火。

paras.en: He started walking.
paras.zh: 他迈步走开。

paras.en: But in the chaotic situation, he didn’t notice that his silver coin had fallen from around his neck. “Oh, that boy… just wait and see, I’ll find you.” Then Clemet heard something else.
paras.zh: 可慌乱之中，他没注意到脖子上的银币掉了。“哦，那小子……等着瞧，我会找到你的。”接着克莱梅特听见了别的动静。

paras.en: He bent down. “All right, let’s see now,” he said as he lay down by some bushes, trying to hide himself.
paras.zh: 他弯下腰。“好吧，现在看看，”他边说边在灌木丛边躺下，想把自己藏起来。

paras.en: But he saw only the hats of three people.
paras.zh: 可他只看见三个人的帽顶。

paras.en: He realized that in order to see better, he would have to stand up.
paras.zh: 他意识到，要想看得更清楚，就得站起来。

paras.en: And when he did, he could hardly believe what was before his eyes—it took his breath away. “Northuldra.
paras.zh: 当他站起身，眼前的一切让他几乎不敢相信——美得让他屏住了呼吸。“北地人。

paras.en: Oh my gosh,” he whispered to himself as he saw the three women—one old and two young.
paras.zh: “我的天，”他望着那三个女人——一老两少——低声自语。

paras.en: The one with long black hair, Lejla, took his breath away.
paras.zh: 那位长着一头乌黑长发的姑娘莱拉，让他看呆了。

paras.en: She had a red scarf with flowers on it draped around her neck, and she held a wooden walking stick.
paras.zh: 她颈间围着一条带花纹的红围巾，手里拄着一根木杖。

paras.en: Without warning, Fally ran up to the women, and Lejla’s sister, Ristin, clapped her hands in surprise. “What are you doing out here alone?” she asked.
paras.zh: 毫无预兆，法利朝女人们跑去，莱拉的妹妹丽斯汀惊讶地拍起手来。“你一个人跑出来干什么？”她问。

paras.en: Biret, the oldest of the three women, leaned on her own walking stick and wiped sweat off her forehead. “Now, Fally, do you want to tell us?” “I’m sorry, but I ran really fast, and he couldn’t reach me,” answered the boy as he stared at the ground.
paras.zh: 三个女人中最年长的比雷特，倚着自己的木杖，擦了擦额头的汗。“好了，法利，你想跟我们说说吗？”“对不起，我跑得特别快，他追不上我，”男孩盯着地面答道。

paras.en: His face was red, but whether it was from exertion or shame was anybody’s guess.
paras.zh: 他涨红了脸，可没人说得清那是累的还是羞的。

paras.en: Lejla glanced around at the trees of the forest surrounding them, but she didn’t see anyone.
paras.zh: 莱拉环视周围林立的树木，却没看到任何人。

paras.en: She wondered who Fally was talking about.
paras.zh: 她纳闷法利说的是谁。

paras.en: Ristin gave the little boy a hug. “I can’t even think about losing you.” Their mother shook her head.
paras.zh: 丽斯汀给了小男孩一个拥抱。“我连想都不敢想会失去你。”她们的母亲摇了摇头。

paras.en: She looked at Fally with love in her eyes.
paras.zh: 她眼里满是爱意地望着法利。

paras.en: Kicking a rock almost bashfully, Fally told them that he couldn’t remember the key words to get back inside the Northuldra village. “Listen, child, we will always let you in, but promise me that next time you will ask me first, because you know the rules.
paras.zh: 法利几乎害羞地踢了踢石子，告诉他们自己记不起回北地人村庄的咒语。“听我说，孩子，我们永远会让你进来，但答应我下次先问过我，因为你懂规矩。

paras.en: Don’t you?” Fally nodded. “You have to use the key words.
paras.zh: “对吧？”法利点点头。“你得出那句咒语。

paras.en: You shouldn’t go to the sky people’s world without an adult with you.
paras.zh: “没有大人在身边，你不该去天族人的世界。

paras.en: If you go out too many times, you will lose your memory of the Northuldra.” Biret saw that Fally was really sorry for what he had done, and he promised not to do it again.
paras.zh: “要是出去太多次，你就会忘了北地人的事。”比雷特看出法利真心悔过，他保证不再犯。

paras.en: She placed her hand on his head as if to say he was forgiven for his mistake.
paras.zh: 她把手放在他头上，像是在说他的过错已被原谅。

paras.en: Then she looked around carefully to make sure they were alone before she raised her wooden walking stick and said the key words: “Skongally, skongally, please let the Northuldra in.” The sun shone down through a parting in the trees, illuminating a path that hadn’t been apparent before. “Don’t you stand there, boy.
paras.zh: 随后她谨慎地四下张望，确认只有他们几人，才举起木杖念出咒语：“斯康加利，斯康加利，请让北地人进来。”阳光穿透树木的缝隙倾泻而下，照亮了一条先前并不明显的路。“别傻站着，孩子。

paras.en: Go home now!” Fally gave the older Northuldra woman a big smile and then disappeared down the path.
paras.zh: “快回家！”法利冲年长的北地女子灿烂一笑，随即沿路消失。

paras.en: Lejla shook her head before voicing her concern about how Fally had gotten out of the Northuldra village.
paras.zh: 莱拉摇了摇头，道出了对法利如何溜出北地人村庄的担忧。

paras.en: The older woman looked toward the opening and shook her head. “I don’t know, but we need to talk with him,” she said.
paras.zh: 年长的女子望向那处开口，也摇了摇头。“我不知道，但我们得找他谈谈，”她说。

paras.en: Clemet saw and heard everything from his hiding place in the bushes.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特在灌木丛的藏身之处，把这一切看了个清、听了个明。

paras.en: He couldn’t believe his eyes as the women walked away from the sunlit path and it disappeared into the darkness of the underbrush. • • • Not long after, Ristin, Lejla, and their mother, Biret, followed a very old, difficult path strewn with roots and stones.
paras.zh: 女人们离开被阳光照亮的小路、小路隐没在灌木丛的暗影中时，他简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。• • • 不久后，丽斯汀、莱拉和她们的母亲比雷特，走上一条古老而难行、满是树根与碎石的小路。

paras.en: The two young women played and laughed, teasing each other as they continued on their journey.
paras.zh: 两个年轻姑娘边走边嬉戏欢笑，互相打趣。

paras.en: The older woman stopped by a beautiful lake fed by waterfalls and looked around. “Girls, girls, take it easy now,” she said, and waved in the air with her walking stick.
paras.zh: 年长的女子在一处由瀑布补给的秀美湖泊旁停下，环顾四周。“姑娘们，姑娘们，慢着点，”她说着，用木杖在空中挥了挥。

paras.en: Lejla began to dance happily while her sister Ristin squealed.
paras.zh: 莱拉欢快地跳起舞来，妹妹丽斯汀则兴奋地尖叫。

paras.en: They were thrilled to be out in the land of the people of the sky.
paras.zh: 能来到天族人的土地上，她们兴奋极了。

paras.en: The two of them held hands and ran among the trees on the banks of the lake.
paras.zh: 两人手牵手，在湖岸的树林间奔跑。

paras.en: Biret looked at her beautiful daughters and smiled, feeling the love for them flood her heart. “Can we swim now?” Lejla asked her mother, and Ristin nodded her head in agreement. “That’s fine, but not so long this time.
paras.zh: 比雷特望着美丽的女儿们，微笑着，爱的暖流涌入心头。“我们现在能游泳吗？”莱拉问母亲，丽斯汀点头附和。“行，不过这次别游太久。

paras.en: Remember to rinse your hair, girls,” the older woman instructed.
paras.zh: “记得把头发冲一冲，姑娘们，”年长的女子嘱咐道。

paras.en: That night was when the midnight sun turned over to autumn, so to keep their vibrant hair color, according to legend, all the daughters of the Northuldra needed to rinse their hair in waterfalls.
paras.zh: 那一夜正值午夜太阳换季入秋之时，因此传说中，为了保持鲜亮的发色，北地人的所有女儿都需在瀑布里冲洗头发。

paras.en: The young women shed some of their outer layers of clothing while the older Northuldra woman sat down on a rock by the water.
paras.zh: 年轻姑娘们脱去部分外衣，年长的北地女子则在岸边石头上坐下。

paras.en: She took her wooden cup off her belt and scooped up the water from the waterfalls to have a drink.
paras.zh: 她从腰带上取下木杯，舀起瀑布的水喝了一口。

paras.en: She relaxed to the sound of her daughters’ laughter and splashing while she looked up to the sky and saw clouds shaped as hearts. • • • Hidden nearby behind some bushes was Clemet.
paras.zh: 她惬意地听着女儿们的笑声与水花声，仰望天空，看见形似爱心的云朵。• • • 克莱梅特藏在附近的灌木丛后。

paras.en: He watched the two sisters play in the water, and he felt something that surprised him when he looked at Lejla.
paras.zh: 他看着两姐妹在水中嬉戏，而当目光落在莱拉身上时，一种令他惊讶的感觉涌上心头。

paras.en: Somehow and in some way, he had fallen in love.
paras.zh: 不知为何，他竟坠入了爱河。

paras.en: The older woman shivered, feeling a sensation wash over her skin.
paras.zh: 年长的女子打了个寒颤，感到一种异样的感觉掠过肌肤。

paras.en: What it was she didn’t know, but it was enough to worry her.
paras.zh: 那是什么她说不清，但足以让她感到不安。

paras.en: A sense of urgency gripping her, she called out, “Ristin, Lejla, come here a moment.” Lejla swam to her mother and came out of the water.
paras.zh: 一阵紧迫感攫住她，她喊道：“丽斯汀，莱拉，过来一下。”莱拉游向母亲，从水里出来。

paras.en: Her long black hair was shining.
paras.zh: 她长长的黑发闪着光。

paras.en: She stepped up and wrung the water from it.
paras.zh: 她走上前，拧干头发上的水。

paras.en: Clemet felt his breath escape him.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特只觉呼吸一滞。

paras.en: There was just something about this young woman that he found utterly mesmerizing.
paras.zh: 这位年轻女子身上，有种让他彻底着迷的气质。

paras.en: With nary a moment’s thought, he decided to throw his silver coin over her as he heard the elders’ advice ringing in his ears.
paras.zh: 他想也没想，便决意把银币抛过她头顶——长老们的叮嘱在耳畔回响。

paras.en: His grandfather’s words came through loud and clear in his memory: If you see a Northuldra girl, and you fall in love, then you must use your silver coin to get her to love you in return.
paras.zh: 祖父的话在记忆中清晰回响：若你遇见北地姑娘并坠入爱河，就必用银币让她也爱上你。

paras.en: Clemet reached to his neck to grab his silver coin, but all his hand found was an empty spot where it used to be.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特伸手去摸脖子上的银币，掌心却只触到原本戴币的空处。

paras.en: His heart began to race, and he felt panic take hold of him.
paras.zh: 他的心骤然狂跳，恐慌攫住了他。

paras.en: Where has it gone? “Girls, I don’t feel safe here,” the older woman said. “Go on and rinse your hair as well as you can and we will go.” Even though they still wanted to swim, Lejla and Ristin heard something in their mother’s tone and didn’t argue.
paras.zh: 它去哪儿了？“姑娘们，我在这儿觉得不安，”年长的女子说。“快把头发冲干净，我们这就走。”尽管还想游，莱拉和丽斯汀听出母亲语气里的异样，便没争辩。

paras.en: They finished with their hair, and just as Lejla moved to emerge from the water, she turned her face to the bushes where Clemet hid.
paras.zh: 她们洗好了头发，就在莱拉准备出水时，她把脸转向克莱梅特藏身的灌木丛。

paras.en: But she didn’t see anything.
paras.zh: 可她什么也没看见。

paras.en: It was as if she had been staring straight into his heart.
paras.zh: 仿佛她直直望进了他的心里。

paras.en: Clemet was sold.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特彻底沦陷了。

paras.en: He needed to follow the old ones’ advice, but with the loss of his silver coin, what could he do?
paras.zh: 他必须听从长老们的忠告，可银币丢了，他能怎么办？

paras.en: He found himself wishing for the beautiful melody of the cuckoo so he could make more wishes.
paras.zh: 他不由得盼望听见布谷鸟美妙的啼鸣，好再许下愿望。

paras.en: But alas, there were no bird sounds to be had.
paras.zh: 可惜，四周听不到一丝鸟鸣。

paras.en: Instead, he simply closed his eyes and whispered to himself, “Please don’t go away.
paras.zh: 于是他只是闭上眼，对自己低语：“请别离开。

paras.en: Please let me get to know you, Lejla.” A sudden happy barking made his eyes fly open.
paras.zh: “请让我认识你，莱拉。”一阵突如其来的欢快狗吠让他猛地睁开眼。

paras.en: Tinka had found him, but she had also revealed his hiding place.
paras.zh: 廷卡找到了他，却也暴露了他的藏身之处。

paras.en: All three women turned and stared, finally seeing the young man. “Hurry,” Biret urged as her daughters quickly threw on their outer clothes.
paras.zh: 三个女人齐齐转身盯住，终于看清了那个年轻人。“快，”比雷特催促道，女儿们慌忙套上外衣。

paras.en: Tinka was happy to see Clemet, but Clemet was frustrated and angry at the dog for giving him away.
paras.zh: 廷卡见到克莱梅特很高兴，可克莱梅特却因狗出卖自己而懊恼生气。

paras.en: She tried to jump up on him and lick his face, but he didn’t have time for her antics.
paras.zh: 她想扑到他身上舔他的脸，可他没空理会她的胡闹。

paras.en: He needed to get to Lejla.
paras.zh: 他必须赶到莱拉身边。

paras.en: But by the time he could escape from Tinka, there was no one left at the water.
paras.zh: 可等他挣脱廷卡，水边已空无一人。

paras.en: Clemet felt his heart sink, and he pushed Tinka away when she prodded him with a stick. “Not now,” he groused, stepping back from her, no longer in a playful mood.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特心头一沉，当廷卡用树枝戳他时，他把狗推开。“现在不行，”他抱怨着退后，再没心思玩耍。

paras.en: He hoped to catch any glimpse, any sign, of where the three women had gone.
paras.zh: 他盼望能捕捉到那三个女人离去的一丝踪迹、一点迹象。

paras.en: But it was almost like they had vanished into thin air.
paras.zh: 可她们几乎像凭空消失了一样。

paras.en: Clemet, frustrated, finally took Tinka’s stick and threw it as far out into the water of the lake as he could.
paras.zh: 沮丧的克莱梅特，终于拿起廷卡的树枝，尽力远远掷向湖心。

paras.en: Where did they go?
paras.zh: “她们去了哪儿？”

paras.en: Confused and unhappy, he sat down on the rocks by the water.
paras.zh: “满心困惑又不快，他在水边岩石上坐下。

paras.en: It was then that a big stick caught his eye.
paras.zh: 就在这时，一根大树枝引起了他的注意。

paras.en: It was lying at the ground near his feet.
paras.zh: 它躺在脚边的地上。

paras.en: Taking it in hand, he frowned and then looked at it more closely.
paras.zh: 他拾起树枝，皱起眉，凑近细看。

paras.en: Then he suddenly realized—it was a Northuldra walking stick!
paras.zh: 随即他猛然醒悟——这是一根北地人的木杖！

paras.en: With a happy bark, Tinka emerged from the lake and wanted to trade the stick she’d retrieved for the one he was holding. “Behave yourself now,” he scolded the dog.
paras.zh: 廷卡欢叫一声从湖里钻出，想用叼回的树枝换他手里的那根。“规矩点，”他训了狗一句。

paras.en: Along the stick he felt something, and he turned it to investigate.
paras.zh: 他顺着木杖摸到了什么，便翻过来看个究竟。

paras.en: There were letters carved into the wood: ALJEL.
paras.zh: 木头上刻着字母：ALJEL。

paras.en: Clemet didn’t understand why the name of his town was written on a Northuldra walking stick.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特不懂，为何自己镇子的名字会刻在一根北地人的木杖上。

paras.en: There were other letters, too, but they made no sense to him.
paras.zh: 还有别的字母，可他完全看不懂。

paras.en: Standing up with the walking stick in his grasp, he saw something else on the ground that had been left behind—a beautiful handmade wooden cup.
paras.zh: 他握着木杖站起身，看见地上还落着别的东西——一只精美的手制木杯。

paras.en: Clemet picked up the cup and examined it.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特捡起杯子端详。

paras.en: With one last look around the area, he decided to return home, taking the two found items with him. • • • Clemet’s grandparents were older now, and they still lived out in the forest in the tiny house where they’d lived their whole lives.
paras.zh: 最后环顾四周，他决定带着这两件拾得之物回家。• • • 克莱梅特的祖父母如今年事已高，仍住在森林里那栋他们住了一辈子的简陋小屋里。

paras.en: As Clemet walked down the path, he saw his grandpa outside fixing the fence.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特沿小路走来，看见爷爷正在屋外修补栅栏。

paras.en: When the older man heard Tinka barking, he stood up and waved to them.
paras.zh: 老人听见廷卡吠叫，站起身朝他们挥手。

paras.en: Tinka ran happily to Grandpa, who stroked her lovingly and laughed. “Oh, you wish to play, do you?” Clemet looked at them with a smile.
paras.zh: 廷卡欢快地跑向爷爷，爷爷疼爱地抚摸她，笑道：“哦，你想玩了，是吧？”克莱梅特微笑着看他们。

paras.en: But then he sighed as his eyes traveled back to the forest, back the way he had come.
paras.zh: 可随后他叹了口气，目光回到森林，回到自己来时的方向。

paras.en: He couldn’t help wondering if he would see Lejla again.
paras.zh: 他不禁猜想，自己能否再见到莱拉。

paras.en: His grandmother, Eleha, opened the window of the small cottage. “Clemet!
paras.zh: 他的祖母埃莱哈推开小屋的窗。“克莱梅特！

paras.en: Clemet!
paras.zh: 克莱梅特！

paras.en: So nice to see you.
paras.zh: 见到你真好。

paras.en: How are you, child?” Clemet loved his grandparents a lot, and he was really happy to see his grandma.
paras.zh: “你好吗，孩子？”克莱梅特很爱祖父母，见到奶奶格外高兴。

paras.en: He went to her and gave her a big hug as she came out of the house with a pitcher of juice in her hands. “Good to see you, too, Grandma.
paras.zh: 她端着一壶果汁从屋里出来，他迎上去给了她一个大大的拥抱。“我也很高兴见到您，奶奶。

paras.en: I’m fine.” But she noticed that her grandson was not smiling. “Did Grandpa say something to you, child?” she asked, concern on her face. “Don’t listen to what he tells you.
paras.zh: “我挺好的。”可她注意到孙子没有笑。“爷爷跟你说什么了吗，孩子？”她脸上露出关切。“别听他说的那些。

paras.en: He is an old, silly guy now.” As Clemet looked over to where Henry and Tinka were playing, he told her that his grandpa had nothing to do with his bad mood.
paras.zh: “他现在是老糊涂了。”克莱梅特望向亨利和廷卡玩耍的地方，告诉她自己心情不好与爷爷无关。

paras.en: Eleha shook her head and laughed. “Look at them.
paras.zh: 埃莱哈摇着头笑了。“瞧他们。

paras.en: He loves that dog as much as he loved his own dog.” Tinka turned and started to bark at the forest.
paras.zh: “他爱这条狗，就像当年爱他自己那条狗一样。”廷卡转过身，冲着森林吠了起来。

paras.en: But none of them could see what she was fussing at. “Lie down,” Clemet called to her. “It’s enough now.” But at the same time, Clemet tried to see something at the forest line, wishing a certain young woman would suddenly, yet impossibly, appear.
paras.zh: 可谁也看不出她在冲什么叫。“趴下，”克莱梅特冲她喊。“够了。”与此同时，克莱梅特努力朝林线张望，盼着某位年轻女子会突然——尽管不可能——出现。

paras.en: Eleha led them to the outdoor table, where they all sat around and begin to sip juice.
paras.zh: 埃莱哈领他们到户外桌旁，大家围坐，喝起果汁。

paras.en: No one spoke as they listened to the sounds of the forest.
paras.zh: 无人说话，只听着森林的声响。

paras.en: Henry looked over at Clemet and said, “You can tell us, you know.” Clemet’s grandparents were so focused on him and what was upsetting him that nobody seemed to notice Tinka.
paras.zh: 亨利看向克莱梅特，说：“你瞒不过我们的，你知道的。”祖父母一心关注他和让他心烦的事，似乎谁都没留意廷卡。

paras.en: She was now playing with the Northuldra’s walking stick.
paras.zh: 她这会儿正玩着那根北地人的木杖。

paras.en: Clemet hesitated, but then he said, “Let me show you something.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特犹豫了一下，然后说：“让我给你们看样东西。

paras.en: I found it in the forest.” He took out the cup—the one he had found by the rocks of the waterfall.
paras.zh: “我在森林里找到的。”他掏出那只杯子——在瀑布岩石边拾到的那只。

paras.en: Eleha put on her glasses while Clemet held the cup up so she could see it better.
paras.zh: 埃莱哈戴上眼镜，克莱梅特把杯子举高让她看得更清。

paras.en: Henry became serious.
paras.zh: 亨利严肃起来。

paras.en: He took his glasses off and looked at his grandson.
paras.zh: 他摘下眼镜，注视着孙子。

paras.en: Grandma came over to her husband and stood behind his chair, placing her hand on his shoulders as the smile faded from her face. “My child, you need to return the cup.
paras.zh: 奶奶走到丈夫身边，站到椅后，把手搭在他肩上，脸上的笑容褪去。“孩子，你要把这杯子还回去。

paras.en: It belongs to the people of the sun.” “She was so beautiful,” Clemet said.
paras.zh: “它属于太阳的子民。”“她真美，”克莱梅特说。

paras.en: Grandpa frowned. “What are you talking about?
paras.zh: 爷爷皱起眉。“你在说什么？

paras.en: Who was beautiful?” “I don’t like this at all.
paras.zh: “谁美了？”“我一点都不喜欢这样。

paras.en: Not at all,” said Grandma.
paras.zh: “一点都不喜欢，”奶奶说。

paras.en: She was really worried for her grandson.
paras.zh: 她着实为孙子担忧。

paras.en: Then Clemet told them about Lejla.
paras.zh: 接着克莱梅特向他们讲起莱拉。

paras.en: How beautiful she was, and how she had been out swimming with her sister.
paras.zh: 讲她多么美丽，讲她怎样和妹妹一起出来游泳。

paras.en: The grandparents looked at each other, worry in their eyes.
paras.zh: 祖父母对视一眼，眼中写满担忧。

paras.en: Then his grandfather stood up and spoke loudly. “Listen, you need to return the Northuldra cup back to exactly where you found it.
paras.zh: 随后祖父站起身，大声说：“听好，你得把这北地人的杯子还到当初发现它的原处。

paras.en: Whoever it belongs to will die if it is not returned.” Grandpa’s raised voice brought Tinka over with the walking stick in her mouth.
paras.zh: “它的主人若收不回去，就会死。”爷爷提高的嗓门把衔着木杖的廷卡也引了过来。

paras.en: But still, no one paid the dog any attention. “Why didn’t you use your silver coin?
paras.zh: 可依旧没人理会狗。“你为何没用你的银币？

paras.en: Where is it, by the way?” he asked, his hands tightly clenched on the tabletop.
paras.zh: “对了，它在哪儿？”他问，双手紧紧攥着桌面。

paras.en: Clemet touched the empty spot on his neck and said that he must have dropped it somewhere.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特摸了摸脖子上的空处，说自己定是掉在哪儿了。

paras.en: Tinka nudged Clemet, trying to get his attention.
paras.zh: 廷卡用鼻子拱克莱梅特，想引起他注意。

paras.en: Finally, he noticed what she was playing with and immediately tried to take it from her.
paras.zh: 他终于注意到狗在玩的东西，立刻想从她嘴里夺下。

paras.en: But it wasn’t as easy as he expected.
paras.zh: 可这没他想的那么容易。

paras.en: Eleha found another stick and threw it for the dog.
paras.zh: 埃莱哈另找了根树枝扔给狗。

paras.en: Tinka dropped the walking stick and went after the new piece of wood.
paras.zh: 廷卡丢下木杖，去追那根新树枝。

paras.en: Henry picked up the walking stick before Tinka could return and looked at it carefully.
paras.zh: 廷卡还没回来，亨利已拾起木杖仔细端详。

paras.en: Clemet told them that he had tried to read the words on the stick. “No, you couldn’t because this is the Northuldra’s language,” Grandma said to him. “The only way you can read it properly is by looking at it in a mirror.” Clemet frowned, thinking it was strange that she knew about it, but she didn’t explain.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特告诉他们，自己试着读过杖上的字。“不，你看不懂，因为这是北地人的文字，”奶奶对他说。“要看懂，唯有借镜子反照。”克莱梅特皱起眉，觉得奶奶竟懂这些很奇怪，可她没有解释。

paras.en: At that moment, Eleha took off her necklace made of reindeer horn and hung the amulet around her grandson’s neck.
paras.zh: 就在此时，埃莱哈摘下自己那串驯鹿角做的项链，把护符挂到孙子脖子上。

paras.en: Clemet opened his mouth to say something, but his grandmother shook her head as a sign that it was not the time for questions.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特张口想说什么，奶奶却摇头示意此刻不是提问的时候。

paras.en: Clemet nodded, somehow knowing he was going to get no more information from his grandparents. “Tinka, come here!
paras.zh: 克莱梅特点点头，莫名地明白从祖父母这儿问不出更多了。“廷卡，过来！

paras.en: Let’s go, girl.” With that, Tinka and Clemet started back to the forest to return the two items they had found. • • • At home with her daughters, Biret was shaken up, but she didn’t want Lejla and Ristin to be upset.
paras.zh: “我们走吧，姑娘。”说罢，廷卡和克莱梅特动身回森林，去归还那两样拾得之物。• • • 比雷特和女儿们在家，仍心有余悸，却不想让莱拉和丽斯汀不安。

paras.en: She asked them to not show how shaken they were so they wouldn’t scare the children in the village. “I feel much better now, Mother,” said Ristin. “We are home and we are safe.” The three women held hands as they walked by some of the children of their village, who sat around and sang a beautiful song about seven blackbirds drinking water.
paras.zh: 她让她们别显出惊惶，免得吓着村里的孩子。“我现在好多了，母亲，”丽斯汀说。“我们到家了，平安了。”三姐妹手牵手走过村里一些孩子身边，孩子们围坐着，唱着一首关于七只黑鸟喝水的动听歌曲。

paras.en: They clapped their hands in rhythm and sang together in that happy, disjointed way that all children do.
paras.zh: 他们打着拍子齐声歌唱，带着所有孩子都有的那种快乐又不成调的劲儿。

paras.en: Nearby, some of the adults listened to the song as they continued about their daily lives, feeling the magic of the word seven .
paras.zh: 附近，几个大人一边继续着手头的活计，一边听着歌，感受着“七”这个字的魔力。

paras.en: Biret just didn’t understand why that young man had been so deep in the forest and far away from any of the villages of the sky people.
paras.zh: 比雷特就是想不通，那个年轻人怎会深入森林、远离任何天族人的村庄。

paras.en: She knew for a fact that water had a very good memory, and it didn’t seem that any of the waters she had encountered remembered the young man of the sky people who had been watching them.
paras.zh: 她确知水的记性极好，而她遇到的那些水域，似乎都不记得那个曾注视着他们的天族年轻人。

paras.en: She even said as much to her daughters as they continued through the Northuldra camp.
paras.zh: 穿过北地人营地时，她甚至把这话对女儿们说了。

paras.en: Lejla and Ristin didn’t answer, but Ristin tugged on Lejla and whispered to her, “Oh my gosh, he was so handsome, and he kept staring at you.
paras.zh: 莱拉和丽斯汀没答话，可丽斯汀扯了扯莱拉，低声说：“我的天，他好帅，而且一直盯着你看。

paras.en: I think he likes you.” Lejla didn’t find her sister’s words funny. “No, he does not!” Now Ristin started teasing her sister. “Oh, yes, he does!” Biret shook her head at their arguing.
paras.zh: “我觉得他喜欢你。”莱拉觉得妹妹的话不好笑。“才没有！”这下丽斯汀开始逗姐姐。“哦，他明明就是！”比雷特对她们拌嘴摇了摇头。

paras.en: At least they were home now.
paras.zh: 好在她们现在到家了。

paras.en: It felt so good.
paras.zh: 这感觉真好。

paras.en: She took a look over the Northuldra village.
paras.zh: 她眺望整个北地人村庄。

paras.en: The tents that they lived in were called lavvoes, and they clustered throughout the camp, declaring it home.
paras.zh: 他们住的帐篷叫“拉沃”，一顶顶聚在营地里，宣示着这里是家园。

paras.en: The crackling campfires added to the coziness, and the herds of reindeer stamped and snorted.
paras.zh: 噼啪作响的篝火更添暖意，成群的驯鹿跺着蹄、喷着鼻息。

paras.en: Some young people were having fun, playing and singing “Turn on the Ring.” The game was about how to get the right person to be your sweetheart.
paras.zh: 几个年轻人在嬉戏欢唱，玩着“转圈圈”的游戏。这游戏讲的是如何找到对的人做心上人。

paras.en: Lejla and Ristin, still bickering, joined them.
paras.zh: 还在斗嘴的莱拉和丽斯汀也加入了。

paras.en: One of their friends greeted them. “You are back home!
paras.zh: 一个朋友迎上来。“你们回来啦！

paras.en: Come play with us.” Their mother joined them, too.
paras.zh: “来跟我们玩。”她们的母亲也来了。

paras.en: She wanted her people to listen as she began to warn them about the sky man they had encountered.
paras.zh: 她想让族人们听她说话，便开始警告他们当心那个遇见的天族男人。

paras.en: Fally quickly came up to the group as well.
paras.zh: 法利也飞快跑到人群里。

paras.en: He told the story, as fast as he ran, of the sky man he had met—and how he had secretly left the village again to follow him. “He watched them swimming at the sky people’s waterfalls, and he took a Northuldra walking stick.” The village people murmured in shock.
paras.zh: 他讲起遇见天族男人的经过——语速和他奔跑一样快——讲自己怎样又偷偷溜出村去跟着他。“他在天族人的瀑布那儿盯着她们游泳，还拿走了一根北地人的木杖。”村民们震惊地低语。

paras.en: Fally also told them that the young man from the sky people had been about to throw his silver coin over Lejla. “It’s good that didn’t happen.
paras.zh: 法利还告诉他们，那天族年轻人本要把银币抛过莱拉头顶。“幸好没成。

paras.en: Otherwise, we would lose our dear Lejla,” said the old Northuldra man. “She would have had to live with the sky people forever.” Biret turned to Fally with a frown. “It all started when you ran away.” Fally hung his head, feeling guilty.
paras.zh: “否则，我们就要失去亲爱的莱拉了，”一位年长的北地男子说。“她就得永远和天族人生活了。”比雷特皱眉转向法利。“一切都是你逃跑惹出来的。”法利羞愧地低下头。

paras.en: He promised that he would never do it again.
paras.zh: 他保证再也不这样了。

paras.en: Not ever.
paras.zh: 绝不再犯。

paras.en: Suddenly, he remembered something that he thought might make the village forgive him. “I know where the sky person’s silver coin is.
paras.zh: 忽然，他想起一件事，觉得或许能让村里原谅他。“我知道那天族人的银币在哪儿。

paras.en: He dropped it.” He mentioned it was right outside of the forest path.
paras.zh: “他弄丢了。”他说银币就在森林小路边上。

paras.en: The older Northuldra woman wanted to know if Fally had seen her cup with the missing walking stick, too.
paras.zh: 年长的北地女子想知道，法利是否也见到了她那连同木杖一起不见的杯子。

paras.en: Fally nodded. “The man had both of them.
paras.zh: 法利点头。“那男的两样都有。

paras.en: He found them by the waterfall.” Biret considered this. “Then we will see whether he comes to give them back.
paras.zh: “他在瀑布边捡到的。”比雷特思忖道。“那就看他会否送来归还。

paras.en: If he does, we will know he is a friend.” • • • With his grandparents’ words ringing in his ears, Clemet returned to where he had seen Lejla.
paras.zh: “若送来，便知他是朋友。”• • • 祖父母的叮嘱在耳边回响，克莱梅特回到了当初见到莱拉的地方。

paras.en: With the cup in one hand and the walking stick in the other, he moved around the lake, hoping to see some sign of Lejla and her family.
paras.zh: 他一手拿杯、一手握杖，在湖边走动，盼望能看到莱拉和她家人的一丝踪迹。

paras.en: His walk had been a long one, and he decided to use the cup to get a drink of the clear water from the waterfall.
paras.zh: 走了许久，他决定用杯子舀些瀑布的清水喝。

paras.en: But when he stood up, it seemed that the forest was cast in a different light and looked much clearer.
paras.zh: 可当他站起身，森林仿佛被别样的光照亮，显得清晰许多。

paras.en: Out of the corner of his eye he saw the young boy who had been throwing sticks for Tinka.
paras.zh: 眼角余光里，他瞥见那个曾给廷卡扔树枝的小男孩。

paras.en: He was almost hidden behind a bush. “Hello, boy, you can come out now.
paras.zh: 他几乎藏在灌木丛后。“你好，孩子，现在可以出来了。

paras.en: I see you,” Clemet called.
paras.zh: “我看见你了，”克莱梅特喊道。

paras.en: Even though the sunlight was changing, the midnight sun was rising, and Clemet could clearly see the forest.
paras.zh: 尽管天光在变，午夜太阳正在升起，克莱梅特把森林看得清清楚楚。

paras.en: Fally took a few steps out from the bushes. “That cup doesn’t belong to you.
paras.zh: 法利从灌木丛里走出几步。“那杯子不是你的。

paras.en: If you want to see her, you better bring the cup back to the Northuldra,” he said. “See who?” “The girl you were staring at,” Fally answered.
paras.zh: “你想见她，最好把杯子送回北地人那儿，”他说。“见谁？”“你一直盯着看的那姑娘，”法利答道。

paras.en: Clemet ignored his answer. “Who are you, boy?” “I am your neighbor.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特没理会他的回答。“你是谁，孩子？”“我是你的邻居。

paras.en: My name is Fally,” he said with a smile.
paras.zh: “我叫法利，”他笑着说。

paras.en: Clemet frowned.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特皱起眉。

paras.en: It seemed odd that a young boy was alone in the forest.
paras.zh: 一个年幼的男孩独自在森林里，显得怪异。

paras.en: Was it possible that he was Northuldra, like the women he had seen? “I live here,” Fally explained. “I want you to come to my home village with me.” Fally told him that they had to hurry up now, because of the time of the midnight sun.
paras.zh: 难道他像见过的那些女子一样，是北地人？“我住这儿，”法利解释。“我要你跟我回我的村子。”法利告诉他现在得抓紧，因为正值午夜太阳的时令。

paras.en: Clemet shielded his eyes from it as he asked, “Why is it shining so bright?
paras.zh: 克莱梅特抬手遮眼，问道：“它怎么亮得这么刺眼？

paras.en: It almost hurts.” Fally explained that the Northuldra people used special sunglasses in emergencies like this—sunglasses made from reindeer bones. “You can take mine, but we need to hurry now.” Putting the sunglasses on, Clemet was grateful. “I live near Arendelle.
paras.zh: “简直晃眼。”法利解释说，北地人在这类紧急情况会用特制的墨镜——用驯鹿骨做的墨镜。“你戴我的，可我们得赶紧了。”克莱梅特戴上墨镜，心怀感激。“我住在阿伦黛尔附近。

paras.en: A little place named Aljel.” Fally didn’t answer.
paras.zh: “一个叫阿尔耶尔的小地方。”法利没有答话。

paras.en: He just started moving through the trees and waving at Clemet to follow him. “I saw them, you know, the Northuldra,” Clemet admitted, feeling warm.
paras.zh: 他只管拨开树林往前走，招手让克莱梅特跟上。“我见过他们，你知道的，北地人，”克莱梅特坦言，心里暖暖的。

paras.en: When they stopped, Clemet took off the sunglasses and recognized the area from earlier in the day where he had seen the sunlit path.
paras.zh: 停下时，克莱梅特摘下墨镜，认出这正是白天见过那条被阳光照亮的小路的地方。

paras.en: He was confused. “Tell me, now, where are you from?” The boy explained that they had arrived at his home.
paras.zh: 他困惑了。“告诉我，现在，你到底是哪儿人？”男孩说他们已到了他的家。

paras.en: Clemet started laughing. “Out here?
paras.zh: 克莱梅特笑起来。“这儿？

paras.en: We are nowhere.
paras.zh: “我们什么都不是。

paras.en: Are you serious?” But Fally stared at him without answering the question.
paras.zh: “你认真的？”可法利只是盯着他，不答这话。

paras.en: Instead he asked Clemet if he knew the words that the older Northuldra woman had spoken that morning. “Yes, I heard the words.
paras.zh: 反而问他是否知道那天早上那位年长北地女子念的词。“是的，我听见了。

paras.en: But why would I use them?” Clemet asked.
paras.zh: “可我为何要用？”克莱梅特问。

paras.en: Fally tapped his foot on the ground in irritation. “Well, sky boy.
paras.zh: 法利不耐烦地用脚点地。“好吧，天族男孩。

paras.en: It’s up to you.
paras.zh: “随你。

paras.en: Do you or do you not want to see Lejla again?” Clemet startled, then quickly repeated the words he had heard the older Northuldra woman say: “Skongally, skongally, please let the Northuldra in!” Out of the shadows, a path of light slowly appeared.
paras.zh: “你到底还想不想再见莱拉？”克莱梅特一惊，随即飞快重复那年长北地女子念过的词：“斯康加利，斯康加利，请让北地人进来！”光影之中，一条光路缓缓浮现。

paras.en: Fally cheered and started to happily run along it.
paras.zh: 法利欢呼着，欢快地沿路跑起来。

paras.en: But seeing Clemet standing in one place, Fally ran back and took Clemet’s hand to pull him along.
paras.zh: 可见克莱梅特站着不动，法利跑回来拉住他的手，拽着他走。

paras.en: Together, they walked toward the village in the distance. • • • Northuldra children surrounded them, laughing in a melodic way. “Look, look, a sky boy inside our village, and his eyes are searching for the beautiful Lejla.” They took turns running around Clemet and teasing him.
paras.zh: 两人一起朝远处的村庄走去。• • • 北地人的孩子们把他们围住，笑着唱似的说：“看哪看哪，天族男孩进了咱村，眼睛直找漂亮的莱拉呢。”他们轮流绕着克莱梅特跑，逗他玩。

paras.en: Fally shooed them away.
paras.zh: 法利把他们轰走。

paras.en: But Clemet paid them no mind.
paras.zh: 可克莱梅特没理会他们。

paras.en: He looked around the village in awe. “Oh my gosh, your village is Northuldra.
paras.zh: 他惊奇地环顾村庄。“我的天，你们的村庄是北地人的。

paras.en: You are Northuldra.
paras.zh: “你们是北地人。

paras.en: This place is amazing.” A young man with brown hair and a big smile approached. “You are so welcome here, neighbor.
paras.zh: “这地方太不可思议了。”一个棕发、笑容灿烂的小伙子走上前。“你在这儿太受欢迎了，邻居。

paras.en: My name is Aimo.” He shook hands with Clemet. “Let me show you around.” He motioned for Clemet to follow him.
paras.zh: “我叫艾莫。”他和克莱梅特握了手。“我带你转转。”他示意克莱梅特跟上。

paras.en: The two young men started walking across the Northuldra village.
paras.zh: 两个年轻人开始穿过北地人村庄。

paras.en: The first person they saw was an old woman who looked like she was playing a game with her fingers—a game that created shadows.
paras.zh: 他们最先见到的，是一位仿佛用手指玩着某种戏法、变出影子的老妇人。

paras.en: Clemet was filled with curiosity about what she was doing. “She is our oldest, and she is teaching the young ones how to get bad spirits out from our village,” Aimo explained. “Don’t worry about her.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特对她在做什么满是好奇。“她是我们中最年长的，正教小辈如何把恶灵赶出村庄，”艾莫解释。“别管她。

paras.en: Come on.” On the other side of the village, Lejla watched them from her family’s tent.
paras.zh: “走吧。”村庄另一头，莱拉从自家帐篷里望着他们。

paras.en: As the two walked toward her, she ducked inside, the butterflies in her stomach flittering nonstop.
paras.zh: 两人朝她走来时，她缩回帐内，心里七上八下，扑腾个不停。

paras.en: She couldn’t help herself. “Sky boy, sky boy, why is my heart beating so fast when I see you?” she muttered under her breath.
paras.zh: 她忍不住了。“天族男孩，天族男孩，为何一见你，我的心就跳得这样快？”她低声喃喃。

paras.en: Finally Clemet and his guide arrived at the big tent.
paras.zh: 终于，克莱梅特和向导来到大帐篷前。

paras.en: Clemet noticed smoke curling up into the sky from a pipe that came out of the top of the roof. “Someone is home,” Aimo said.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特注意到烟从帐顶的管子袅袅升向天空。“有人在家，”艾莫说。

paras.en: Clemet felt a bit apprehensive.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特有点局促。

paras.en: He looked around for Fally, feeling as if the little boy would help calm his nerves now as he had earlier. “Who lives here?” Clemet asked, although he was sure he already knew the answer.
paras.zh: 他四下找法利，觉得这小男孩此刻会像之前那样帮他定神。“谁住这儿？”克莱梅特问，尽管他确信自己已知道答案。

paras.en: Biret emerged from the tent with a much younger woman by her side.
paras.zh: 比雷特从帐篷里出来，身旁跟着一位年轻许多的女子。

paras.en: The young woman took one look at Clemet and stepped forward with a smile.
paras.zh: 那年轻女子看了克莱梅特一眼，笑着上前。

paras.en: Clemet recognized her immediately. “That’s Ristin,” Aimo said softly. “Well, sky boy, we are impressed.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特立刻认出了她。“那是丽斯汀，”艾莫轻声说。“好了，天族男孩，我们倒挺佩服你的。

paras.en: What do your people call you, and what brings you here?” Ristin asked him.
paras.zh: “你的族人怎么称呼你，你来此何事？”丽斯汀问他。

paras.en: Clemet looked at Aimo, who nudged him with his elbow.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特看向艾莫，艾莫用胳膊肘轻轻碰了碰他。

paras.en: At the encouragement, Clemet took a step forward and cleared his throat. “No particular reason.
paras.zh: 受到鼓励，克莱梅特上前一步，清了清嗓子。“没什么特别的事。

paras.en: I was nearby and thought I’d like to visit you.” Aimo added, “Fally brought him here, and see what he carries?” Ristin looked to the walking stick and nodded. “And what do your people call you?” Clemet told her his name, and the history behind it, and then, looking guilty, he offered the walking stick to the older Northuldra woman. “I’m so sorry I took it,” he apologized, his chin down to his chest and his hands clasped in front of him. “I didn’t realize it belonged to you.” She held the walking stick lightly in her hands and then passed it back to Clemet.
paras.zh: “我就在附近，想着来拜访你们。”艾莫补了一句：“法利带他来的，看他还带着什么？”丽斯汀看向木杖，点点头。“那你的族人怎么称呼你？”克莱梅特告诉她自己的名字和名字的由来，随后带着歉意，把木杖递给那位年长的北地女子。“很抱歉我拿了它，”他道歉道，下巴垂在胸前，双手交握身前。“我没想到它属于你。”她轻轻握住木杖，又把它递还给克莱梅特。

paras.en: Not understanding what was happening, the young man took it. “Please read the letters you see on it,” she said.
paras.zh: 年轻人不明所以，接过了。“请念出你看见杖上的字母，”她说。

paras.en: Clemet glanced from Biret to Aimo to Ristin, not sure why they were asking him to do that.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特从比雷特看到艾莫，又看向丽斯汀，不明白他们为何要他这么做。

paras.en: But Ristin requested that he give it a try. “A-L-J-E-L,” he read aloud, again wondering why it spelled out the name of his city.
paras.zh: 可丽斯汀请他试一试。“A-L-J-E-L，”他念出声，再次纳闷它为何拼出自己城镇的名字。

paras.en: Biret and Ristin shared a knowing smile.
paras.zh: 比雷特和丽斯汀会心一笑。

paras.en: He looked at the two Northuldra women as if waiting for an answer. “We always put our names on our belongings,” Ristin explained. “But we write our words backward.
paras.zh: 他望着两位北地女子，似乎在等答案。“我们总在自己的物件上刻名字，”丽斯汀解释。“但我们是反着写字的。

paras.en: So that stick belongs to my sister, Lejla.” Clemet stared at Ristin in dumbfounded silence. “I will go get her,” Aimo offered.
paras.zh: “所以那根杖属于我姐姐莱拉。”克莱梅特目瞪口呆地望着丽斯汀，说不出话。“我去叫她，”艾莫主动说。

paras.en: But the older Northuldra woman held up her hand. “I will do it.
paras.zh: 可年长的北地女子抬起手。“这事我来。

paras.en: She is my daughter.” Ristin asked the two young men to sit down with her at the campfire and wait while Lejla was brought to them.
paras.zh: “她是我女儿。”丽斯汀请两个年轻人随她在篝火旁坐下等候，莱拉会被带来。

paras.en: Northuldra children were playing around and singing the song about seven beautiful blackbirds drinking water.
paras.zh: 北地人的孩子们在一旁玩耍，唱着那首七只美丽黑鸟喝水的歌。

paras.en: Clemet asked about their song, which was unfamiliar to him.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特问起这首歌，他对它很陌生。

paras.en: Ristin explained that the number seven was a powerful number for the Northuldra people.
paras.zh: 丽斯汀解释，“七”对北地人是个充满力量的数字。

paras.en: And if one of the sky people like Clemet wanted to marry one of the Northuldra, they needed to wash their face with seven kinds of water.
paras.zh: 而若像克莱梅特这样的天族人想娶北地人为妻，需用七种水洗脸。

paras.en: Clemet didn’t understand.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特没听懂。

paras.en: But then Ristin got up and spread her arms to encompass the nature all around them. “What do you see?” she asked.
paras.zh: 可随即丽斯汀站起身，张开双臂，把周围的自然尽揽其中。“你看见了什么？”她问。

paras.en: Clemet stood and didn’t say a word, because walking toward him were Biret and Lejla.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特站起身，一言不发，因为朝他走来的，是比雷特和莱拉。

paras.en: The children stopped playing and the Northuldra people followed the two women as if they were following their leader.
paras.zh: 孩子们停了玩耍，北地人跟在两位女子身后，仿佛追随首领。

paras.en: But the only thing Clemet noticed was Lejla.
paras.zh: 可克莱梅特眼里只有莱拉。

paras.en: He was utterly enchanted.
paras.zh: 他完全被迷住了。

paras.en: Half of her face was hidden behind a curtain of her ebony hair. “Listen, Northuldra, his name is Clemet.
paras.zh: 她半张脸藏在如瀑的黑发后。“听好，北地人，他叫克莱梅特。

paras.en: He is named after his great-great-grandfather.
paras.zh: “他以高祖父的名字命名。

paras.en: He found my daughter’s walking stick, and he was able to spell her name in our language.
paras.zh: “他找到了我女儿的木杖，还能用我们的文字拼出她的名字。

paras.en: You all know what that means.
paras.zh: “你们都明白这意味着什么。

paras.en: Don’t you?” It felt as if every eye in the village was on Clemet.
paras.zh: “对吧？”仿佛全村人的目光都落在克莱梅特身上。

paras.en: Ristin smiled, seeming to be satisfied.
paras.zh: 丽斯汀微笑着，似乎很满意。

paras.en: The older Northuldra woman started to sing, and slowly everyone joined her.
paras.zh: 年长的北地女子开始歌唱，慢慢所有人随之唱和。

paras.en: Together, with their hands touching the shoulder of the person next to them, they formed a ring. “What are they singing?” Clemet asked. “A blessing song,” Ristin responded. “The words talk about how Lejla came from a cuckoo’s dream.
paras.zh: 他们手搭身旁之人的肩膀，围成一圈。“他们在唱什么？”克莱梅特问。“一首祝福歌，”丽斯汀答。“歌词讲莱拉如何来自布谷鸟的梦境。

paras.en: A sky boy came and found her walking stick.
paras.zh: “一位天族男孩前来，找到了她的木杖。

paras.en: Our beautiful Northuldra daughter.
paras.zh: “我们美丽的北地女儿。

paras.en: Her song is the cuckoo’s cry that tells that the people of the sun love their daughter so much that they want to give her wings to fly.” Then the singing stopped and the Northuldra moved apart to create space in the ring.
paras.zh: “她的歌便是布谷鸟的啼鸣，诉说太阳的子民多么爱女儿，恨不得给她翅膀去飞翔。”随后歌声停了，北地人散开，在圈中腾出空地。

paras.en: Not sure what to do, Clemet looked at Aimo, who gestured to him to move forward.
paras.zh: 不知如何是好，克莱梅特看向艾莫，艾莫示意他上前。

paras.en: And so the son of the sky people moved into their circle and stood there, holding the walking stick.
paras.zh: 于是这天族之子走进他们的圈子，握着木杖站在那里。

paras.en: Ristin motioned for Lejla, and the two women joined him in the circle.
paras.zh: 丽斯汀招手唤莱拉，两位女子也进到圈中与他同立。

paras.en: Ristin then took the walking stick and held it up. “Now you can tell us, Clemet.
paras.zh: 丽斯汀接过木杖，高高举起。“现在你可以告诉我们了，克莱梅特。

paras.en: What do you see?” But Clemet only had eyes for Lejla. “I see the most beautiful…” The children started laughing.
paras.zh: “你看见了什么？”可克莱梅特眼里只有莱拉。“我看见了最美的……”孩子们笑了起来。

paras.en: But Biret smiled and said, “No, children, not now.” Forgetting her shyness, Lejla stepped forward to Clemet. “They mean, you have to read the words on the walking stick.” Clemet cleared his throat and he read, “Northuldra, Biret…” The children laughed again.
paras.zh: 可比雷特微笑着说：“不，孩子们，现在不行。”莱拉忘却羞涩，上前对克莱梅特说。“他们的意思是，你得念出木杖上的字。”克莱梅特清了清嗓子，念道：“北地，比雷特……”孩子们又笑了。

paras.en: But everyone was friendly.
paras.zh: 可大家都很友善。

paras.en: Lejla smiled as she put her finger on the walking stick. “Not those names… but this one.” Clemet looked at her. “Lejla.” Children began to yell over one another. “What?” “What does the sky man say?” “We can’t hear you!” Clemet said it louder this time, with laughter in his voice. “Lejla.
paras.zh: 莱拉微笑着，手指点在木杖上。“不是那些名字……是这一个。”克莱梅特看向她。“莱拉。”孩子们开始七嘴八舌。“什么？”“天族男人说了什么？”“我们听不见！”这回克莱梅特抬高了声音，带着笑意。“莱拉。

paras.en: Lejla is her name.” The Northuldra people cheered. “Thank you for getting it back for me,” Lejla said.
paras.zh: “莱拉是她的名字。”北地人欢呼起来。“谢谢你替我找回它，”莱拉说。

paras.en: Clemet could tell by looking in her eyes that she was grateful.
paras.zh: 克莱梅特看她的眼睛便知她心怀感激。

paras.en: He was about to give the walking stick to her, but the older Northuldra woman wanted him to read the letters of Lejla’s name in the sky people’s language. “Aljel.
paras.zh: 他正要把木杖交给她，可年长的北地女子想让他用天族人的文字念出“莱拉”的名字。“阿尔耶尔。

paras.en: It’s Aljel…” he started. “The name of my hometown.
paras.zh: “是阿尔耶尔……”他开口。“我家乡的名字。

paras.en: How can it be?” Ristin gave him a hug. “Nothing is strange, sky boy.
paras.zh: “怎么可能？”丽斯汀给了他一个拥抱。“没什么奇怪的，天族男孩。

paras.en: We believe in destiny.” • • • Later as they all sat around the campfire together, Aimo was busy searching for something. “What are you looking for?” Clemet asked. “Biret’s cup.
paras.zh: “我们相信命运。”• • • 后来大家围坐在篝火旁，艾莫忙着找什么。“你在找什么？”克莱梅特问。“比雷特的杯子。

paras.en: If she cannot find it, she cannot drink, and if she doesn’t drink, she will die,” Aimo explained.
paras.zh: “她若找不到杯子，就没法喝水；不喝，就会死，”艾莫解释。

paras.en: Fally immediately pointed at Clemet. “He has it.
paras.zh: 法利立刻指向克莱梅特。“在他那儿。

paras.en: I saw him drinking from it by the waterfalls.” Clemet nodded.
paras.zh: “我见他在瀑布边用它喝水。”克莱梅特点点头。

paras.en: He told the others where he had found it. “I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 他告诉大家自己在何处找到。“对不起。

paras.en: I forgot all about it when I was returning the walking stick.” Clemet walked over to Biret and held out the cup.
paras.zh: “还木杖时，我把它全忘了。”克莱梅特走到比雷特面前，递出杯子。

paras.en: She took it in her hand and gave a big smile when she saw her name carved into it.
paras.zh: 她接过去，看到杯上刻着自己的名字，露出了大大的笑容。

paras.en: Grateful for its return, she made him an offer. “What can I do for you, Clemet, son of the sky people?” Clemet looked back at Lejla, who was staring at him. “It’s such a pleasure for me to be here.
paras.zh: 感激物归原主，她向他发问。“我能为你做些什么呢，克莱梅特，天族之子？”克莱梅特回望正盯着他的莱拉。“能来这儿，我十分荣幸。

paras.en: Perhaps you would let me know your daughter a bit better?” Biret and the older Northuldra women were smiling. “Thank you for not using your silver coin against us,” the woman says. “Clearly you didn’t need to.
paras.zh: “或许您能让我多了解令爱一些？”比雷特和年长的北地女子都微笑着。“谢谢你没用银币对付我们，”那女子说。“显然你并不需要。

paras.en: I think Lejla likes you just fine.” Then Biret saw the amulet that Clemet had around his neck.
paras.zh: “我看莱拉挺喜欢你的。”这时比雷特看到了克莱梅特脖子上的护符。

paras.en: She motioned to him, and he took it off, handing it to her as he told her that it belonged to his beloved grandmother. “I would like you to meet my grandparents, Lejla,” he said quickly.
paras.zh: 她示意他取下，他摘下递给她，告诉她那是心爱祖母的护符。“莱拉，我想让你见见我的祖父母，”他急忙说。

paras.en: The Northuldra village became quiet.
paras.zh: 北地人的村庄安静下来。

paras.en: Biret looked at the young couple as she held the amulet in her hand. “It is Eleha’s amulet you wear,” Biret confirmed. “I knew her well, once.” • • • In the clearing near where the path to the Northuldra village appeared, Clemet’s grandparents, with Tinka by their side, searched around for him.
paras.zh: 比雷特手握护符，望着这对年轻人。“你戴的是埃莱哈的护符，”比雷特确认道。“我曾与她相识。”• • • 在北地人村庄入口附近那片空地，克莱梅特的祖父母带着廷卡，四处寻找他。

paras.en: Tinka whined and barked, but there was nothing there.
paras.zh: 廷卡呜咽着吠叫，可那里空无一人。

paras.en: All of a sudden, Grandpa saw the glint of something flashing in the light of the midnight sun. “Look,” he said as he bent down. “It’s Clemet’s silver coin.” “He has my amulet,” Eleha responded, patting Henry on the arm. “He is protected, and he is in love.
paras.zh: 忽然，爷爷看见午夜太阳的光里有什么在闪。“看，”他弯腰说。“是克莱梅特的银币。”“他带着我的护符，”埃莱哈轻拍亨利的胳膊回应。“他受了庇护，也陷入了爱河。

paras.en: Don’t you worry about a thing.” Suddenly a wooden stick flew through the air.
paras.zh: “你什么都不必担心。”忽然，一根木棍从空中飞来。

paras.en: Tinka immediately ran after it, her tongue lolling out of her mouth. “Is that you, Clemet?” Grandpa called out.
paras.zh: 廷卡立刻追了上去，舌头耷拉在嘴外。“是你吗，克莱梅特？”爷爷喊道。

paras.en: But there was no answer—just the voice of a child laughing loud and happy.
paras.zh: 可没有回应——只有孩子响亮欢快的笑声。

paras.en: Out of the bushes ran a young boy with black hair and a big smile on his face.
paras.zh: 灌木丛中跑出一个黑发、满脸灿烂笑容的小男孩。

paras.en: Eleha could hardly believe her eyes.
paras.zh: 埃莱哈简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

paras.en: The boy ran faster than Tinka.
paras.zh: 那男孩跑得比廷卡还快。

paras.en: And he carried something in his hands. “What do you have there?” asked Eleha.
paras.zh: 他手里还拿着什么。“你拿着什么？”埃莱哈问。

paras.en: Fally’s fingers uncurled to show an amulet made from reindeer bones. “I think that the amulet belongs to me.
paras.zh: 法利展开手指，露出一枚驯鹿骨做的护符。“我想那护符是我的。

paras.en: Where did you get it?” Eleha continued.
paras.zh: “你从哪儿得来的？”埃莱哈追问。

paras.en: The boy told them that Clemet had given it to him because he was a fast runner and was able to bring a message. “Message?
paras.zh: 男孩告诉他们，克莱梅特把护符交给他，因为他跑得快，能送口信。“口信？

paras.en: What do you mean?” Henry asked, confused.
paras.zh: “什么意思？”亨利困惑地问。

paras.en: But before Fally could answer, Eleha took the amulet and held it lovingly. “The message is clear,” she said. “He sent the amulet back to us.
paras.zh: 可法利还没答，埃莱哈已接过护符，珍爱地捧着。“口信很清楚，”她说。“他把护符送回给了我们。

paras.en: He is planning to stay there, with the Northuldra.
paras.zh: “他打算留在那儿，留在北地人那里。

paras.en: Isn’t that so?” Fally nodded, hugging Tinka around her neck.
paras.zh: “是不是？”法利点点头，搂住廷卡的脖子。

paras.en: Henry sighed.
paras.zh: 亨利叹了口气。

paras.en: He had been worried that something like that would happen.
paras.zh: 他早担心会出这样的事。

paras.en: He patted the dog on her head. “It’s okay, Tinka.
paras.zh: 他拍拍狗的头。“没事，廷卡。

paras.en: You can go to your owner.
paras.zh: “你可以去找主人了。

paras.en: Go and find Clemet.” Then he took his wife’s hand and they waved goodbye to Fally and Tinka.
paras.zh: “去找到克莱梅特。”随后他牵起妻子的手，向法利和廷卡挥手道别。

paras.en: It was hard for them, but they were pleased to know that Clemet was doing fine and was happy with his Lejla.
paras.zh: 离别虽难，但得知克莱梅特安好、与莱拉在一起很快乐，他们由衷欣慰。

paras.en: When the man finished his tale, the group was silent—the only sounds the crackling of the fire. “I can’t believe he left his family behind to live with Lejla,” one young girl said loudly. “You wouldn’t do anything you could to be with someone you loved?” the man asked. “I love the forest and the reindeer and my family.
paras.zh: 故事讲完，人群陷入沉默——唯有篝火噼啪作响。“真不敢信他抛下家人，去和莱拉同居，”一个年轻女孩大声说。“若是为了和所爱之人在一起，你会什么都不做吗？”那男子问。“我爱森林、爱驯鹿、爱我的家人。

paras.en: I don’t think I could love anyone as much as all of them,” she responded. “You may change your mind when you get older, Iduna,” he said with a quick pat to her head.
paras.zh: “我想我没法像爱他们那样去爱任何人，”她答道。“等长大些，你或许会改变想法，伊杜娜，”他轻拍她的头说。

paras.en: You’re Invited to Berit’s 10th Birthday Date: March 16 Time: 11 a.m.
paras.zh: 诚邀您参加贝丽特十岁生日派对｜日期：3月16日｜时间：上午11点

paras.en: Place: 46 Agder Street, Arendelle Dear Queen Anna, Please come to my party.
paras.zh: 地点：阿伦黛尔阿格德街46号 亲爱的安娜女王，请来参加我的派对。

paras.en: We just moved to Arendelle and I don’t have any friends.
paras.zh: 我们刚搬到阿伦黛尔，我一个朋友都没有。

paras.en: I’m scared no one will come.
paras.zh: 我好怕没人会来。

paras.en: My mom says you’re too busy, but I’ve heard you’re really nice.
paras.zh: 妈妈说您太忙了，但我听说您人特别好。

paras.en: From, Berit “Oh!” Anna rubbed the sleep from her eyes and looked around her bedchamber at the people anxiously waiting for her to wake up.
paras.zh: 贝丽特 敬上 “噢！”安娜揉了揉惺忪的睡眼，环顾寝宫，看到众人正焦急地等着她醒来。

paras.en: She was sleeping in the same carved wooden bed she’d had since she was a little girl, sporting the same tangled bed head.
paras.zh: 她睡的还是小时候那张雕花木床，顶着同一头乱蓬蓬的睡发。

paras.en: She wiped her face: the same line of drool, too. “Um, good morning.” Anna wasn’t a little girl anymore.
paras.zh: 她擦了擦脸：连口水流的那道印子都还在。“呃，早上好。”安娜不再是小女孩了。

paras.en: She was the queen of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 她是阿伦黛尔的女王。

paras.en: She had been for a few months now, since her sister, Elsa, moved to the Enchanted Forest to bring balance to the spirits of nature.
paras.zh: 几个月前，她姐姐艾莎搬去魔法森林，去调和自然之灵，从那以后她便成了女王。

paras.en: Sometimes that idea still baffled her.
paras.zh: 有时这个念头仍让她觉得难以置信。

paras.en: Anna didn’t have time to be baffled, though, because Kai, the castle steward, was holding a tray of papers.
paras.zh: 不过安娜没空去发愣，因为城堡管家凯正端着一托盘文件。

paras.en: The cook, Olina, held a tray of breakfast treats.
paras.zh: 厨娘奥丽娜端着一托盘早餐点心。

paras.en: Though, judging by the worried expression Gerda, her lady’s maid, wore, Anna didn’t have time for Olina’s famous hot chocolate or steaming chocolate porridge.
paras.zh: 不过，从她的贴身侍女格尔达那担忧的神情来看，安娜这会儿可没空享用奥丽娜著名的热可可或冒着热气的巧克力粥。

paras.en: She probably needed to prioritize unsnarling her copper hair and putting on the purple gown with teal rosemaling Gerda had draped over her arm.
paras.zh: 她大概得先把铜红色的头发理顺，再穿上格尔达搭在臂弯里的那件饰有青绿色洛丝梅林花纹的紫色礼裙。

paras.en: Kai cleared his throat. “Good morning, Your Majesty.
paras.zh: 凯清了清嗓子。“早上好，陛下。

paras.en: Did you hear me go over the day’s events?
paras.zh: 方才一天的安排，您可听进去了？

paras.en: Or should I begin again?” Oh.
paras.zh: 还是要我从头再说一遍？”噢。

paras.en: So apparently this wasn’t her first wake-up call.
paras.zh: 看来这已经不是她第一次被叫醒了。

paras.en: Anna yawned and sat up straighter.
paras.zh: 安娜打了个哈欠，坐直了身子。

paras.en: She was not a morning person—but she was trying.
paras.zh: 她可不是爱早起的人——但她正在努力。

paras.en: It felt like something a queen should do: greet the day cheerfully and be up and at ’em, et cetera.
paras.zh: 这似乎是女王该做的事：愉快地迎接晨光，精神抖擞地开始一天，诸如此类。

paras.en: Elsa had been great at that when she ruled Arendelle.
paras.zh: 艾莎统治阿伦黛尔时，这一点做得极好。

paras.en: She’d be halfway through her to-do list before the sun was halfway up the sky.
paras.zh: 太阳还没爬到半空，她的待办清单就已经划掉一半了。

paras.en: The only thing Anna ever accomplished before breakfast was an epic case of bed head.
paras.zh: 安娜在早饭前唯一能搞定的，就是一头堪称史诗级的乱发。

paras.en: But different scenes for different queens!
paras.zh: 不过，每位女王各有各的做派！

paras.en: She and Elsa had their own ways of doing things.
paras.zh: 她和艾莎各有各的处事方式。

paras.en: Anna liked to be awake when the sky was, when the Northern Lights painted a symphony of colors over the stars.
paras.zh: 安娜喜欢在天色将明时醒来，那时北极光正为星辰绘上一曲色彩的交响。

paras.en: Since she was now queen—and doing it well was exhausting—shouldn’t she get to sleep in occasionally? “Nope,” she said in answer to her own question as well as Kai’s, because if she was running late, she was probably making all of them late, too.
paras.zh: 如今她已是女王——而想把女王当好着实累人——难道她就不能偶尔赖个床吗？“不行，”她这样回答自己，也回答凯，因为若她迟了，多半也会连累大家跟着迟到。

paras.en: They worked hard to make Arendelle the wonderful place it was; delaying them was definitely not queenly behavior.
paras.zh: 他们辛勤付出，才让阿伦黛尔如此美好；耽误他们绝非女王应有的风范。

paras.en: She stifled another yawn. “The schedule.
paras.zh: 她又憋住一个哈欠。“日程表啊。

paras.en: I’ve got it.
paras.zh: 我心里有数。

paras.en: Great.
paras.zh: 挺好。

paras.en: Don’t let me keep you.
paras.zh: 别因为我耽搁你们。

paras.en: I’m on it.” Kai looked a little dubious but nodded. “Very good, Your Majesty.
paras.zh: 这就开工。”凯略显怀疑，但还是点了点头。“遵命，陛下。

paras.en: I’ll set this tray on your desk.” “Wait.” She pointed to a red piece of paper that stood out among the white envelopes and formal documents on his tray. “What’s that?” Queen Anna was written at the top in careful lopsided print. “It came with the mail, Your Majesty, from a village child.” Kai handed it to her. “It’s an invitation!” Anna sat up more fully, grinning as she read. “To a child’s party,” said Kai. “I’ll draft a letter wishing her a joyous birthday and expressing your regrets.” “What?
paras.zh: 我把这托盘放到您书桌上好了。”“等等。”她指着他托盘上那张在白色信封和公文间格外醒目的红纸。“那是什么？”顶端用工整却歪歪扭扭的字体写着“安娜女王亲启”。“陛下，这是随邮件送来的，出自村里一个孩子之手。”凯把它递给她。“是一份请柬！”安娜完全坐直了，边读边咧嘴笑。“是去参加孩子的生日派对，”凯说，“我来起草一封贺信，祝她生日快乐，并代为致歉。”“什么？

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 不。

paras.en: I have to go.” She crushed the invitation to her chest, remembering all her own birthdays after the castle gates had been shut when she was five.
paras.zh: 我一定要去。”她把请柬紧紧按在胸前，想起五岁宫门紧闭后自己那一个个孤单的生日。

paras.en: On every birthday candle, she’d wished for friends.
paras.zh: 每吹灭一岁生日蜡烛，她许的愿望都是能有朋友。

paras.en: Anna couldn’t let that happen to Berit. “I have to.” “But your schedule—” said Gerda. “I’ve got it right here.” Anna swiped a lock of hair out of her face so she could tap her forehead. “It’s going to be a great day.
paras.zh: 安娜绝不让贝丽特重蹈覆辙。“我必须去。”“可您的日程——”格尔达说。“我记着呢。”安娜把垂落脸颊的一缕头发拨开，好腾出手敲了敲额头。“今天会是很棒的一天。

paras.en: Thanks!” Kai hesitated at the door, with Gerda and Olina pausing behind him. “Are you sure we cannot be of more help, Your Majesty?” “We’re happy to assist in any way we can,” added Gerda.
paras.zh: 谢啦！”凯在门口迟疑着，格尔达和奥丽娜在他身后也停下脚步。“陛下，您确定我们不需要再多帮些忙吗？”“我们乐意在任何方面效劳。”格尔达补充道。

paras.en: Olina nodded. “We’re worried you’ve overcommitted.” Anna straightened her shoulders.
paras.zh: 奥丽娜点头道：“我们担心您揽的事太多了。”安娜挺直了肩膀。

paras.en: She could do this.
paras.zh: 她能行。

paras.en: Sure, there were a lot of Arendellians and only one of her, but still… she was queen. “Thanks.
paras.zh: 没错，阿伦黛尔人多，她只有一人，可话说回来……她是女王。“谢了。

paras.en: I appreciate the offer, but I’ve got it.” “Don’t forget the earrings,” Gerda called as she followed Kai and Olina out.
paras.zh: 好意我心领了，不过我心里有数。”“别忘了戴耳环，”格尔达一边跟着凯和奥丽娜往外走，一边回头喊道。

paras.en: Earrings?
paras.zh: 耳环？

paras.en: Anna glanced at the beautiful amber jewels set beside her crown on the vanity table.
paras.zh: 安娜瞥了眼梳妆台上王冠旁那对精美的琥珀耳饰。

paras.en: They were important somehow, but she couldn’t remember why.
paras.zh: 它们似乎很重要，可她想不起为何了。

paras.en: Olaf squeezed in through the door as the others exited.
paras.zh: 其他人退出时，雪宝从门缝里挤了进来。

paras.en: He went straight to the chair where Gerda had draped the gown. “Ooh, is this the dress you’re wearing to your meeting with one of the princes from the Southern Isles?
paras.zh: 他直奔格尔达搭着礼裙的那张椅子。“哦，这就是你要穿去见南岛某位王子的那条裙子吗？

paras.en: I like it.
paras.zh: 我喜欢。

paras.en: I like it.
paras.zh: 我喜欢。

paras.en: It says, ‘I’ve forgotten all about your lying youngest brother who pretended to love me and then tried to kill me.’” “Wait, what?” Anna groaned and yanked on the hairbrush she was using to tame and braid her hair.
paras.zh: 它在说：'我已把那个撒谎的最小弟弟忘得一干二净，他假装爱我，后来又想杀了我。'”“等等，你说什么？”安娜叹了口气，拽了拽正用来梳理编发的发刷。

paras.en: There were few things she liked less than being reminded of the very brief period when she’d thought she should marry the evil Prince Hans of the Southern Isles.
paras.zh: 没几件事比被提醒那段短暂往事更让她反感——那时她竟以为该嫁给南岛那个邪恶的汉斯王子。

paras.en: To be fair, Hans had been the first guy her own age she’d talked to in thirteen years, so maybe it made sense that he’d spun her head a bit.
paras.zh: 平心而论，汉斯是她十三年来头一个同龄的说话对象，所以他对她稍微有些迷惑也情有可原。

paras.en: She was pretty sure that his twelve older brothers were not evil, but some of them delighted in reminding her of her almost-fatal infatuation. “That meeting is today ?” Ugh.
paras.zh: 她相当确信他十二个哥哥并非坏人，可其中几位总爱拿她那段险些致命的迷恋来打趣。“那个会就在今天？”哎呀。

paras.en: That was why the earrings were important.
paras.zh: 难怪那对耳环如此重要。

paras.en: They’d been a gift from the king of the Southern Isles to her mother. “The meeting is before the seed dedication,” said Olaf. “Do you think they’ll have snacks?” “That’s also today?” Anna groaned again.
paras.zh: 它们是南岛国王送给她母亲的礼物。“会议在种子供奉仪式之前，”雪宝说，“你觉得会有点心吗？”“也是今天？”安娜又叹了一声。

paras.en: Farmer Niels had been so excited when he invited her, and she was excited about attending, but her schedule was more snarled than her hair.
paras.zh: 尼尔森农夫邀她时兴奋得不得了，她也很期待出席，可她的日程比她的头发还要乱。

paras.en: She definitely should’ve asked Kai to repeat the agenda. “Do you know when the delegation arrives?” “It starts…” Olaf raised a stick arm and frowned. “I don’t wear a watch, but I’m pretty sure it’s now.
paras.zh: 她真该让凯把议程再说一遍。“你知道代表团什么时候到吗？”“开始了……”雪宝抬起树枝做的胳膊，皱起眉头。“我不戴表，但我相当确定就是现在。

paras.en: The carriages were arriving while I was waiting in the hall.” Anna jammed her crown on top of her hastily braided hair.
paras.zh: 我在大厅等着的时候，马车就已经到了。”安娜把王冠往匆忙编好的头发上一扣。

paras.en: As she quickly changed into her gown, she wondered, not for the first time, how Elsa had done it all.
paras.zh: 她匆忙换上礼裙时，不禁又一次思忖：艾莎究竟是怎么把这一切都应付下来的。

paras.en: She knew her sister was amazing—literally magical—but still.
paras.zh: 她知道姐姐了不起——简直是魔力非凡——可仍觉难以想象。

paras.en: Sometimes Anna felt like she needed two of herself so she could be in more places at once.
paras.zh: 有时安娜觉得，她需要两个自己，才能同时出现在更多地方。

paras.en: Like right now.
paras.zh: 比如此刻。

paras.en: Should she call for Kai and confess she’d double-booked the meeting and the seed ceremony?
paras.zh: 她该不该叫来凯，坦白自己把会议和种子仪式排在了同一时间？

paras.en: Ask him to contact Farmer Niels and reschedule?
paras.zh: 让他去联系尼尔森农夫改期？

paras.en: And what about Berit?
paras.zh: 那贝丽特怎么办？

paras.en: At her own tenth birthday, she’d pretended the paintings on the wall were party guests just to feel a little less lonely.
paras.zh: 在她自己十岁生日时，她曾假装墙上的画是派对宾客，好让自己少些孤单。

paras.en: Anna rubbed her damp eyes and blinked down at the invitation.
paras.zh: 安娜揉了揉湿润的眼角，眨着眼低头看那张请柬。

paras.en: It wasn’t right for a child in Arendelle to have to celebrate her birthday alone.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔的孩子不该孤零零地独自庆生。

paras.en: Not if Anna could do something about it.
paras.zh: 只要安娜能帮上忙，就不该如此。

paras.en: And she could!
paras.zh: 而她办得到！

paras.en: The best part of being queen was the opportunities it gave her to make people’s lives better. “Olaf,” she said, “I’m going to do it.
paras.zh: 当女王最棒的一点，便是能有机会让人们的生活变得更好。“雪宝，”她说，“我决定去做。

paras.en: I’m going to the meeting, the seed dedication, and a ten-year-old’s birthday party.” “That’s the spirit!” Olaf cheered. “But how?” “We’re going to need some help.” She shoved the invitation into her pocket, scooped the amber earrings from her vanity, and slipped them on as she burst out of her bedroom, already calling her fiancé’s name. “Kristoff!” Anna glanced up and down the hallway.
paras.zh: 我要去开会、去参加种子供奉仪式，还要去参加一个十岁孩子的生日派对。”“这才对嘛！”雪宝欢呼道。“可怎么去？”“我们得找人帮忙。”她把请柬塞进口袋，从梳妆台抓起琥珀耳环戴上，冲出卧室时已经喊起了未婚夫的名字。“克里斯托夫！”安娜上下打量着走廊。

paras.en: The suit of armor next to her door seemed to be missing its head… and its feet.
paras.zh: 门边的那套盔甲，似乎少了脑袋……也少了脚。

paras.en: Kristoff popped out from behind it—wearing both the helmet and the metal shoes.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫从它后面钻了出来——头盔和金属靴都穿在身上。

paras.en: At least, she assumed it was Kristoff.
paras.zh: 至少，她以为那是克里斯托夫。

paras.en: The person was the right height, had broad shoulders, and was wearing Kristoff’s fur-lined leather tunic.
paras.zh: 那人高矮合适、肩宽体阔，身上正是克里斯托夫那件毛衬皮外套。

paras.en: He took a clanking step forward. “I’m here.
paras.zh: 他铿锵地向前迈了一步。“我来了。

paras.en: What do you need?” Anna nestled against the front of his tunic.
paras.zh: 你需要什么？”安娜依偎到他的外套前襟上。

paras.en: He always smelled like moss and reindeer; it was an unusual combination, but the scent calmed her nerves and made her smile. “Have I told you this morning that I love you and you’re the best?” Kristoff’s brown eyes were shining behind the visor of the helmet, which he flipped up so he could plant a kiss on her cheek. “You haven’t even told me ‘good morning’ yet.” Anna laughed. “Good morning.” Then her frown returned. “Now, do you have any advice on how to do eight things at once?” “Eight?” Olaf asked. “I can only think of…” He started to count on the twiggy fingers of one hand, then gave up when he ran out. “Less than eight.” “Okay, it’s just three.
paras.zh: 他身上总有股苔藓与驯鹿的味道；这组合虽特别，却安抚了她的神经，让她忍不住微笑。“今天早上我有没有说过，我爱你，你最棒了？”克里斯托夫棕色的眼睛在头盔面甲后闪闪发亮，他掀开面甲，在她脸颊上印下一吻。“你连'早上好'都还没说呢。”安娜笑了。“早上好。”可她又皱起了眉。“那么，对于如何一心八用，你有什么建议吗？”“八个？”雪宝问，“我只能想到……”他在一只树枝手上数起来，数到没指头了便放弃。“不到八个。”“好吧，其实就三件。

paras.en: But what am I going to do?
paras.zh: 可我该怎么办？

paras.en: I have no birthday present.
paras.zh: 我连生日礼物都没有。

paras.en: I’m late to meet the delegates from the Southern Isles.
paras.zh: 我赴南岛代表团的约已经迟了。

paras.en: I know nothing about seeds.
paras.zh: 我对种子一窍不通。

paras.en: And—” “Whoa, whoa, whoa.” Kristoff’s metal shoes clanged as he took a step forward to put his hands on her shoulders. “Take a deep breath.
paras.zh: 还有——”“哇，哇，哇。”克里斯托夫向前一步，双手按住她的肩膀，金属靴当当作响。“深呼吸。

paras.en: We’ve got this.
paras.zh: 我们搞得定。

paras.en: What is it that you and Grand Pabbie always say?
paras.zh: 你和皮比长老总说的话是什么来着？

paras.en: Do the…” “Do the next right thing.” Anna exhaled slowly.
paras.zh: 做……”“做当下该做的事。”安娜缓缓吐了口气。

paras.en: She could do hard things if she took them one step at a time.
paras.zh: 只要一步一步来，再难的事她也能做成。

paras.en: She had done much harder things than handling a snarled schedule. “Yes.
paras.zh: 她做过的难事，可比理顺一团乱的日程难多了。“对。

paras.en: You’re right.
paras.zh: 你说得对。

paras.en: I’ll just…” Anna took a brief moment to think. “Go get Sven.
paras.zh: 我就……”安娜略一思索。“去把斯文叫来。

paras.en: We have things to do.” “Sure.” Metal crashed to the ground as Kristoff stripped off the armor. “But can you tell me what things?” “Simple.” Anna was already turning toward the library, mentally rehearsing what she was going to say to the Southern Isles delegation. “You’re going to help me sneak out of a royal meeting and to a kid’s birthday party in the village without being seen.” Olaf paused from attaching the armor’s left foot to its right leg. “And to the seed ceremony,” he said.
paras.zh: 我们有事要办。”“当然。”克里斯托夫扯下盔甲，金属哗啦落地。“可你能告诉我是什么事吗？”“简单。”安娜已转身朝藏书室走去，心里默默排练要对南岛代表团说的话。“你要帮我神不知鬼不觉地从王宫会议溜出去，去村里参加孩子的生日派对。”雪宝停下手里给盔甲接左脚的活儿，插嘴道：“还有种子仪式呢。

paras.en: Anna nodded at Olaf. “Right.
paras.zh: 安娜朝雪宝点点头。”对。

paras.en: And that.” “You got it.” Kristoff tugged off the helmet and tossed it to Olaf. “Phew.
paras.zh: 没错。“”明白。“克里斯托夫扯下头盔抛给雪宝。”呼。

paras.en: I thought it was going to be something tough, like running away from wolves or a snow monster, or tricking the Earth Giants into breaking a dam and almost flooding a village.” Anna laughed and called over her shoulder, “There’s always tomorrow!” Unless, of course, tomorrow’s schedule was also bursting at the seams.
paras.zh: 我还以为是什么硬骨头呢，比如从狼群或雪怪手里逃命，或者骗大地巨人撞毁水坝、差点淹了村子。“安娜笑着，回头喊道：”总还有明天嘛！“当然，除非明天的日程也塞得满满当当。

paras.en: But, no, Anna wouldn’t think about that right now.
paras.zh: 不过，不，安娜现在可不想操心那个。

paras.en: She was doing the next right thing—which was to greet the delegation from the Southern Isles and hope they liked her earrings.
paras.zh: 她正在做当下该做的事——去迎接南岛代表团，并盼着他们喜欢她的耳环。

paras.en: When Anna rushed into the library, she found Prince Lars of the Southern Isles and his wife, Princess Helga, seated at a long table between two giant stacks of books.
paras.zh: 安娜冲进藏书室时，看见南岛的拉尔斯王子与妻子赫尔加公主坐在一张长桌旁，两侧堆着高高的书堆。

paras.en: Her shoes skidded on the polished wooden floor as she came to a stop above the inlaid design.
paras.zh: 她鞋底在打磨光亮的木地板上打滑，停在镶嵌花纹的上方才刹住脚。

paras.en: Queens were probably not supposed to skid.
paras.zh: 女王大概不该打滑。

paras.en: Or be late.
paras.zh: 也不该迟到。

paras.en: Or get in dubious engagements with men they’d just met.
paras.zh: 更不该和刚认识的男人定下荒唐的婚约。

paras.en: Stupid Hans!
paras.zh: 该死的汉斯！

paras.en: He wasn’t even here and he was still making things awkward. “Good morning,” Anna said. “Oh, please.
paras.zh: 他压根不在这儿，却还在叫人尴尬。”早上好，“安娜说。”哦，快别。

paras.en: Stay seated.
paras.zh: 坐着就好。

paras.en: There’s no need to get up.” The other royals stood and bowed anyway.
paras.zh: 不必起身。“可两位王室成员还是站起身鞠了躬。

paras.en: Prince Lars was a tall, round man with a warm smile and large spectacles.
paras.zh: 拉尔斯王子高个子、圆脸庞，笑容温和，戴着一副大眼镜。

paras.en: Helga was shorter and rounder, with bigger glasses and a bigger smile.
paras.zh: 赫尔加更矮更圆，眼镜更大，笑容也更灿烂。

paras.en: Anna gave a quick curtsy. “I’m so sorry to have kept you waiting.” “No problem at all.” Lars gestured to the bookshelves around them. “We’ve been perusing your wonderful library and collecting books.
paras.zh: 安娜匆匆屈膝行礼。”让您二位久等，万分抱歉。“”一点都不碍事。“拉尔斯朝四周的书架一指。”我们一直在欣赏您这美妙的藏书室，顺便收罗些书。

paras.en: Have I told you how much we enjoy studying history?” “Yes, you—” Anna hoped to change the subject, but it was too late.
paras.zh: 我有没有说过，我们多爱钻研历史？“”说过，您——“安娜想岔开话题，可惜为时已晚。

paras.en: Lars plunged into describing a book he’d found on ice harvesting through the ages.
paras.zh: 拉尔斯便滔滔不绝地讲起他找到的一本关于历代采冰的书。

paras.en: She liked Lars—of the thirteen Southern Isles princes, he might have been her favorite—but he and his wife were the most likely to bore her to sleep with historical facts.
paras.zh: 她挺喜欢拉尔斯——十三位南岛王子中，他或许最合她心意——可他和妻子最爱拿史实把她讲到睡着。

paras.en: When he finally paused to breathe, Anna quickly jumped in. “Do you know who’d really like this conversation?
paras.zh: 他终于停下来喘口气时，安娜赶紧插话。”您知道谁会真正喜欢这场谈话吗？

paras.en: My fiancé, Kristoff, since he’s an ice aficionado.
paras.zh: 我的未婚夫克里斯托夫，他可是个冰迷。

paras.en: Or Elsa, since… ice .” “Will she be joining us?” asked Helga. “I’ve heard so much about her wonderful powers.” “My country so enjoyed working with your sister, if only from afar,” added Lars. “Oh.
paras.zh: 还有艾莎，毕竟……冰。“”她会来和我们会合吗？“赫尔加问，”我听过太多关于她神奇能力的传闻了。“”我国虽只是远隔千里，却很乐于与您姐姐合作，“拉尔斯补充道。”哦。

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 不。

paras.en: Sorry.
paras.zh: 抱歉。

paras.en: It’s just me.” Anna glanced out the north window toward Ahtohallan and the Enchanted Forest. “Elsa really is the best.” “Indeed,” said Helga, nodding enthusiastically. “We appreciate the invitation to your home and hope we enjoy working with you just as much.” “Do you think you won’t?” Anna wished she could gulp the words back in.
paras.zh: 就我一人。“安娜望向朝北的窗户，目光落向阿图蕴和魔法森林。”艾莎真的是最棒的。“”的确，“赫尔加点着头，热切地说，”我们很感激您邀我们到府上，也希望与您合作得同样愉快。“”您莫非觉得不会？“安娜恨不得把话吞回去。

paras.en: Was she messing this up already?
paras.zh: 她已经把事情搞砸了？

paras.en: Before lunch was even served? “I’m not normally late—or, well, sometimes I am, but I try not to be.” “Oh!” Lars exchanged panicked looks with his wife. “We didn’t mean to sound critical of your punctuality, Your Majesty.
paras.zh: 午饭都还没上就搞砸了？”我平时并不常迟到——呃，好吧，有时也会，但我尽量不迟到。“”噢！“拉尔斯与妻子交换了一个慌乱的眼神。”陛下，我们绝无意对您的守时加以批评。

paras.en: Helga was just expressing our gratitude for your hospitality and your willingness to make sure that, er, bit of unpleasantness with Hans doesn’t impact the long friendship between Arendelle and the Southern Isles.” “Unpleasantness?
paras.zh: 赫尔加只是想表达我们对您款待的感激，以及您愿意确保——呃——汉斯那点不愉快不会影响阿伦黛尔与南岛长久的友谊。“”不愉快？

paras.en: Oh, you mean that time your youngest brother tried to kill me and my sister?” Anna had tried to make it sound like a joke, but the prince and princess winced. “That would be it,” he said.
paras.zh: 哦，您是说您那最小的弟弟企图杀害我和我姐姐那回？“安娜本想说得像玩笑，可王子和公主都缩了缩。”正是那回事。“他说。

paras.en: Anna probably wasn’t supposed to mention that.
paras.zh: 安娜大概不该提这个。

paras.en: Hadn’t she hoped that they wouldn’t mention it?
paras.zh: 她不是还指望他们别提吗？

paras.en: There was a long, uncomfortable silence while they stared at the floor, the doors, the bookshelves.
paras.zh: 一阵漫长而尴尬的沉默中，他们盯着地板、房门和书架。

paras.en: Lars reached for a book from his stack.
paras.zh: 拉尔斯从书堆里抽出一本书。

paras.en: Anna was blowing this!
paras.zh: 安娜把局面彻底搞黄了！

paras.en: She almost wished Lars would resume telling her about the history of ice, just to break the quiet.
paras.zh: 她几乎盼着拉尔斯继续讲采冰史，好打破这片死寂。

paras.en: Even the footmen at the doors seemed to be giving her do something looks.
paras.zh: 连门边的侍从都向她投来”快做点什么“的眼神。

paras.en: Anna fiddled with a loose piece of hair until inspiration struck. “Oh!
paras.zh: 安娜拨弄着一缕散落的头发，直到灵光一闪。”哦！

paras.en: Did you notice these earrings?
paras.zh: 您注意到这对耳环了吗？

paras.en: Your father gave them to my mother when she became queen.” “A lovely gift for a lovely queen.” Helga exhaled her relief and dabbed at her forehead. “We have heard wonderful things about your mother.
paras.zh: 您父亲在她登基时把它们赠予了我母亲。“”送给美丽女王的美丽礼物。“赫尔加松了口气，轻轻拭了拭额头。”我们听过许多关于您母亲的佳话。

paras.en: And the earrings suit you, Queen Anna.” “They were a symbol of the strong bond between our kingdoms.” Anna tried to make her voice firm and regal.
paras.zh: 这对耳环也很衬您，安娜女王。“”它们象征着我们两国之间牢固的纽带。“安娜努力让声音坚定而威严。

paras.en: She lowered her tone even more when she added, “I wore them today as a reminder of that history.” “Do you need to be reminded?” Lars looked at his wife with concern. “What?
paras.zh: 她压低嗓音补了一句：”我今天戴上它们，正是为了铭记那段历史。“”您还需要特意提醒自己吗？“拉尔斯忧心忡忡地望向妻子。”什么？

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 不。

paras.en: I just meant…” Anna glanced at the door.
paras.zh: 我只是说……“安娜瞥了眼门口。

paras.en: Where was Olaf when she needed him?
paras.zh: 她正需要雪宝时，他在哪儿？

paras.en: As if on cue, there was a knock. “Sorry.
paras.zh: 仿佛收到暗号，传来一声敲门。”失陪。

paras.en: I need to check on that.” She pushed back her chair so forcefully that Helga’s book tower wobbled.
paras.zh: 我得去查看一下。“她推开椅子用力过猛，晃得赫尔加的书塔直摇。

paras.en: Anna pointed to a plate on the table. “Help yourself to some cookies and enjoy the library.
paras.zh: 安娜指了指桌上的盘子。”请随意用些饼干，也请尽情看书。

paras.en: I’ll be back soon.” Anna didn’t stop running when she reached the hallway, where Olaf was pointing a twig arm to the left. “Sven and Kristoff are waiting this way.” He did a little jig on the carpet as he trotted to keep up with her. “So, how’s it going in there?” She rubbed her temples.
paras.zh: 我很快回来。“安娜跑到走廊也没停下，雪宝正用树枝胳膊指向左边。”斯文和克里斯托夫在那边等着呢。“他一路小跑跟上她，在地毯上蹦跶着。”那么，里面进展如何？“她揉了揉太阳穴。

paras.en: Sometimes the crown gave her a headache. “Well, I somehow managed to make them think I was wearing these earrings as a sort of diplomatic threat?
paras.zh: 有时这顶王冠真让她头疼。”呃，我不知怎的竟让他们以为，我戴这对耳环是在搞某种外交威胁？

paras.en: Not quite sure how that happened.
paras.zh: 也不大清楚怎么会变成这样。

paras.en: Why couldn’t this have been a meeting with the Baron of Snoob?
paras.zh: 怎么不是和斯努布男爵开会呢？

paras.en: He and I get along great.
paras.zh: 我跟他可投缘了。

paras.en: You know what?
paras.zh: 你说呢？

paras.en: Let’s not talk about it.
paras.zh: 不提这个了。

paras.en: Let’s just get to the party as quickly as possible, focus on making Berit feel fully welcomed to Arendelle, then get back before they notice I’m gone.” “Great idea, great idea,” said Olaf. “But let’s not talk about it that way.” He pointed to a door behind them. “Because we just ran by Sven.” The address on the invitation belonged to a red house on a cozy street in the center of the village.
paras.zh: 咱们尽快赶到派对，专心让贝丽特感受到阿伦黛尔的热烈欢迎，然后在他们发现我溜走之前赶回去。“”好主意，好主意，“雪宝说，”不过别这么说。“他指了指身后的门。”因为咱们刚从斯文身边跑过。“请柬上的地址，是村里中心一条温馨小街上的一栋红房子。

paras.en: Its steeply peaked roof lined up with a row of others, like a mini mountain range.
paras.zh: 它那陡峭尖顶与一排房屋连成一线，像一道迷你山脉。

paras.en: Its windows sparkled like its neighbors’; its porch was clean swept.
paras.zh: 窗户像邻居们的一样闪闪发亮；门廊扫得干干净净。

paras.en: Despite this, there were a few clues that Berit’s family was newly moved in.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，仍有几处迹象表明贝丽特一家是新搬来的。

paras.en: The window boxes on either side of the door were still empty, while the neighboring houses had filled theirs with fresh dirt, ready to plant bulbs that would become the spring and summer’s lush crocuses.
paras.zh: 门两侧的花箱还是空的，而邻家早已填好新土，只待种下球茎，待春夏长出繁茂的藏红花。

paras.en: There weren’t curtains hung on the windows yet, and there weren’t any sounds of friendly chatter coming through the open front door. “How nice it must be to have a house all snuggled up to your neighbors’,” Anna mused. “Can you imagine all those playmates right next door and down the street?” Olaf, sitting beside her on the wagon’s bench, nodded.
paras.zh: 窗户上还没挂窗帘，敞着的前门里也听不到邻里闲谈的声响。”紧挨着邻居有座房子，该多好啊，“安娜若有所思，”你能想象隔壁和街那头全都是玩伴吗？“坐在她身旁的雪宝在马车长凳上点了点头。

paras.en: Sven, wearing his harness, snorted, still catching his breath from the run across town.
paras.zh: 斯文套着挽具，打了个响鼻，方才穿城奔跑还没喘匀气。

paras.en: Kristoff turned around in the driver’s seat, shrugged, and said, “Don’t look at me.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫在车夫座上转过身，耸了耸肩说：”别看我。

paras.en: I was raised in the woods.” Anna mussed his hair and hopped down from the wagon. “Can you stay nearby?
paras.zh: 我是在林子里长大的。“安娜揉了揉他的头发，跳下马车。”你们能在附近等着吗？

paras.en: I’m going to want to stay all day, but I need to get back to the castle and the meeting.” “Seeds,” said Olaf. “Don’t forget about the seed ceremony.” “Right!” Anna said, trying not to panic. “And that!” Kristoff pointed to a water trough at the corner of the street. “We’ll wait right there.
paras.zh: 我本想待上一整天，可我得回城堡去开会。“”种子，“雪宝说，”别忘了种子仪式。“”对！“安娜强作镇定。”还有那个！“克里斯托夫指向街角的饮水槽。”我们就等在那儿。
